author: lovelle-cardoso
body:
## Summary

Triage now counts a repeat report whose `Skill and section` names the same skill as the saved problem, even when the section or wording differs; a repeat naming a different skill stays intact with a reason that quotes the saved target to copy.

Closes #976

## Motivation

A repeat names its problem by ID, but `fold` compared the full normalized target (`keyOf`) at `.agents/skills/triage-skill-feedback/triage-skill-feedback.mjs:175`, so a repeat reworded as `review-pr section 4` or with an added reference file was left unparsed and its session went uncounted. The last triage left sixteen such comments, understating counts for F-5773769269, F-5789457733, F-5752190271, F-5764183462 and F-5797692962. The refusal also gave no hint how to fix the report.

## Changes

- `triage-skill-feedback.mjs`: new `skillNameOf` (the first word of the normalized target, before any comma or whitespace); a repeat matches when its skill name equals the saved problem's. The refusal now ends with `copy the saved target verbatim: <saved target>`. The legacy-table identity check and duplicate detection keep the stricter `keyOf`.
- `references/records.md` and `references/feedback-reporting.md` state the rule.
- The table-budget half of the ticket already shipped in PR #949 (#947), as the ticket notes; nothing further here.

Rejected: fuzzy matching of sections. The problem ID is the identity, so only a skill mismatch signals a likely wrong ID.

## Type of change

Type: build/tooling/CI, documentation

## Testing and verification

- New test `a repeat whose target names the saved skill in other words is counted` in `.agents/skills/triage-skill-feedback/triage-skill-feedback.test.mjs`, plus an assertion on the refusal wording in the existing changed-skill test.
- Red on base: `node .agents/skills/triage-skill-feedback/triage-skill-feedback.test.mjs` failed with `The input did not match the regular expression /copy the saved target verbatim: review-pr, section 3/`.
- Green on fix: `All 37 triage checks passed.`
- CI on head `c06b1dcb0`: Hook Tests standalone checks passed on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest (run 36288124327), and the Test Suite `test-suite` gate passed with its package jobs skipped because nothing under `packages/` changed (run 36288122294). The typecheck passed too (run 36288122288).
- Review round 1 on `9bad19ebe`: undirected gpt-5.6-terra found nothing; blast-radius claude-sonnet-5 raised one optional nit (an unused export), fixed in `c06b1dcb0` without changing behavior. The adjudication is in the PR comments.

## Checklist

Tests run: triage-skill-feedback test file, red then green.

Visual check: not applicable, tooling only.

Docs: records.md and feedback-reporting.md updated.

Body read back: yes.

## Notes for reviewers

Applied feedback: #976 (F-5849970348, repeat-matching half). The sixteen already-unparsed intake comments are counted on the next triage run with no edits needed, as long as they name the same skill.

body:
## What

Implementation plan for i18n stage 3, wave (d) `web-finance`: translating the web finance surface (transaction ledger, transaction detail, drop finance, create/edit/validate dialogs, payout/settlement dialogs, income-compliance statistics `stats.tsx`, and the web part of invoices) to `uk`/`en`. Plan only — no product code touched.

New file: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-27-crm-i18n-stage3d-web-finance.md`.

## Perimeter (measured on origin/main `5c477321f`, #728)

- **30 product files, 744 non-comment Cyrillic lines** (audit counted 34 files / 569 visible fragments + 174 comment lines — consistent; `KpiCards`/`api.ts`/`sort.ts`/`usePaginatedFilter` carry no non-comment Cyrillic).
- Includes the finance components wave 3c deliberately left untouched (`TransactionRow`, `TransactionDetailDialog`, `fmtUsd`, `ExchangeRates`) — they live in `finance/**` and are native here, not pulled cross-slice.
- Two files already partially migrated (`AdminEditTransactionDialog`, `CascadeImpactPanel`) — the plan finishes them, does not restart.

## Structure

Mirrors the 3b/3c plan format: header, Global Constraints with lessons #700–#728, wave term canon (`uk`/`en`), migration templates A–L (+ finance-specific G-fin/J-fin/K-fin/L-fin), shared E2E-sweep step, Task 1–4 with Files/Interfaces/dangers/AC/steps, audit-findings traceability (21 `web-finance` findings), out-of-perimeter list, assumptions, wave-readiness check.

**4 PRs, merged serially** (shared `.po` + shared hub `finance/constants.ts`):
1. `constants.ts` hub (label maps → message-maps, formatters) + transaction ledger + cross-slice consumer `FinanceTab`
2. transaction detail, drop finance, validation, receipts
3. create/edit transaction dialogs + `EXPENSE_CATEGORIES`
4. payouts/settlements, statistics, invoices + deletion of the deprecated string maps

## Money/RBAC on surface → security-reviewer mandatory on every PR

The whole slice is in `pm.md` critical-path zones (transactions, payouts, drop/senior share, company account, dividends, `mapTx(viewer)` amount masking). The plan marks `security-reviewer` as a required AC on **all four** PRs, alongside spec + code + copy (uk/en) + designer (Mode B, all widths).

## Contested decisions (recommendations in the plan)

- **`EXPENSE_CATEGORIES` / `receiver_label` (data-at-rest):** the Russian category strings are stored in `transactions.receiver_label`, so this is a data migration, not a UI translation. Recommendation: a separate api+shared+prod-DDL PR (stable codes `SERVICE`/`BANK_FEE`/`OTHER` + value migration) as a precondition of PR3 — flagged as an A2 owner decision (irreversible prod finance data). Interim fallback documented.
- **Cross-slice imports:** `FinanceTab.tsx` (web-people) is the only external consumer of the finance label maps → PR1 updates its lookup. `fmtUsd` keeps its signature so `$projectId.tsx` (web-projects) needs no edit. `lib/format-amount.ts` (ru-RU/en-US root) is cross-slice → A2, locale-awareness coordinated with web-core.
- **`localeCompare('ru')`:** not present in finance (verified); the only reference is a comment in `documents-filter-sort.ts` noting it was replaced by `Intl.Collator` in stage 2. Recorded as already-done.
- **Server error codes (#704):** already migrated — consumed via `getApiErrorMessage`/`translateZodCode`, not duplicated.

Not to be merged — planning artifact for review.

author: omar16100
body:
Follows #1 (media download fix, REST guard, drafts), now merged. Lets one checkout and binary serve several WhatsApp accounts.

## Env config
| Variable | Used by | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `WHATSAPP_STORE_DIR` | bridge | `store` |
| `WHATSAPP_PORT` | bridge | `8080` (bound to `127.0.0.1`) |
| `WHATSAPP_API_URL` | MCP server | `http://127.0.0.1:8080/api` |
| `WHATSAPP_DB_PATH` | MCP server | `whatsapp-bridge/store/messages.db` |

- An explicit invalid `WHATSAPP_PORT` or a busy port stops the bridge at startup (the port is bound before connecting to WhatsApp), so a typo cannot put a second account on the first one's port.
- `WHATSAPP_STORE_DIR` containing `?`, `#` or `%` is refused (SQLite URI syntax).
- MCP server: all `print()` calls go to a stderr logger, because stdout is the MCP stdio channel.

## Pairing helpers
`whatsapp-bridge/qr_server.py` (`BRIDGE_LOG`, `QR_PORT`) and `whatsapp-bridge/regen_qr.sh` (`BRIDGE_DIR`, `BRIDGE_LOG`, `QR_OUT`, `STATUS_OUT`) render the pairing QR from the bridge log. Paths resolve relative to the script directory. Both only look at the current bridge session and ignore a QR code once a login or logout followed it. `qr_server.py` answers only loopback `Host` headers.

## Docs
README fork note (upstream is lharries/whatsapp-mcp), clone URL for this fork, upstream author's newsletter line marked as upstream's, multi-account section. `docs/index.md`, `docs/c4model.md`, plans, `todo.md` change log.

## Tests
Go: 21 tests. Python: 14 tests in `whatsapp-mcp-server`, 6 in `whatsapp-bridge/test_qr_server.py` (`uv run --with segno --with pytest pytest whatsapp-bridge/test_qr_server.py`). Nothing talks to a running bridge.

author: bbambaaamm
jacob-lasky
body:
Closes #223
Closes #224

Found while verifying the 1.30.0 deploy on the live instance: two not-yet-started NC State recordings had been cancelled overnight.

## Root causes

Determined 2026-09-26 from the live instance, and fixed on that basis.

- **#224:** the cancel rule treated "this game is not in the current slate" as "this recording is no longer wanted". One refresh got `NCAA Football: 0 games` from a one-off CFBD failure; the API answered normally an hour later, with 275 games for week 6. That emptied the sport and deleted the Oct 3 NC State football recording.
- **#223:** `_scheduler_loop` read settings at the top of its loop, slept until the next `scheduled_times` slot, and ran with that snapshot. Recorded teams, saved at 5:48 PM, was therefore ignored by the 7 PM run: every row got `recorded_matched=[]`, and the Oct 2 soccer recording was cancelled.

## Fix

- **Missing-game rule:** a recording whose game is missing from the whole cache (applied games and bench) is cancelled only when its stored reason no longer holds. A game still in the cache but unplanned is cancelled as before.
- **Stored reason:** each recording now stores why it exists: `team` plus the game's home and away teams, re-checked through the same `match_favorites` refresh uses, so fixing a typo in the list doesn't look like removing the team; or `ranked` plus its league. Older rows get the reason backfilled, and a stale one refreshed, on the next apply (not-yet-started rows only).
- **Scheduler:** re-reads settings after waking, and skips the run if auto-refresh was switched off meanwhile.
- **Locked re-reads:** writes and cancels re-read the row with `select_for_update` inside the apply transaction. So the DVR's own status write can't be overwritten, and a recording that has just started can't be deleted.
- **Test rot, in a separate commit:** removes the unused imports and dead bindings pyflakes reported across 12 test files. The test count is unchanged.

**Known limit:** a game that really is cancelled upstream keeps its recording. The recording fires, captures nothing useful, and the normal cleanup archives it. That's the deliberate price of not deleting a recording on missing evidence.

## Tests

- 22 new tests in `tests/test_autorecord_resilience.py`.
- On the old code, 12 of them failed as assertions and none failed on a missing symbol.
- Suite: **4636 passed**.

## Live verification

Run inside a rolled-back transaction on the running instance, against the real Oct 2 recording (id 39):

```
1_reason_backfilled: reason=team, teams=[NC State], league=NCAAMSOC
2_outage_cancelled: 0      (game removed from games + bench, team still listed; recording kept)
3_team_removed_cancelled: 1 (same outage, Recorded teams changed to Duke; recording cancelled)
rolled_back_clean: true
```

## Review

`codex-dg`, `gpt-6-sol`, high effort, read-only. 5 findings:

- **Fixed (4), each with a test:**
  - a stale reason kept on KEEP;
  - a renamed list entry looking like a removed team;
  - a status race between the re-read and the save;
  - the cancel step deciding on a stale row.
- **Documented as designed (1):** a game that really is cancelled keeps its recording.

## Release

1.30.0 (#222) was deployed to the maintainer's instance but never published. This release carries it to the public listing.

author: mattias800
body:
## Problem

Every headless agent run of `prosper-app` uses `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=offscreen` (Linux). SDL's offscreen
driver creates its Vulkan surface with `VK_EXT_headless_surface`, but the shared renderer instance
only enabled the window-system surface extensions (xlib/xcb/wayland). So the app could not create a
surface on the renderer's instance, logged

```
GPU present: surface on shared instance failed (VK_EXT_headless_surface ... not enabled); using own device
```

and never adopted GPU present. Every offscreen frame therefore took the CPU readback path, and every
offscreen F8 capture or fps figure described that fallback rather than the shipped renderer.
Measured 2026-09-27 on Sonic Frontiers at one anchor: offscreen 15.34 guest flips/s vs windowed
16.34/s, and the SDL main thread at 22.7% CPU offscreen vs 4.1% windowed (memmove of every frame).

## Change

Add `VK_EXT_headless_surface` to the Linux/other-Unix list of surface extensions enabled on the
shared instance. It is add-if-available like the others, so a loader that does not advertise it
behaves exactly as before.

## Verification

- 45 s offscreen run of The Messenger (`PPSA24651`), `prosper-app`, this head:
  `[app] GPU present: adopted the renderer's device (shared present queue)`.
- Caveat now visible in the log: the headless surface offers only FIFO, so
  `--present-mode immediate` falls back to `fifo` and the *presented* rate of an offscreen run is
  paced to 60. Distinct-frame rates of titles below 60 fps are unaffected; quote `distinct`.
- `ctest --no-tests=error -R 'multidraw_render|indexed_render$|gpu_execute|present_blit|vk_object|command_pool'`:
  8/8 passed (RADV, Linux).

## Risk

Instance creation only; the extension is enabled only when advertised. Windows/macOS lists unchanged.

Refs #3873

author: jay3332
body:
mac-claude-a subagent (mac-m1max-a). The owner's 21-242 proof-practice worksheet, **slice A**: everything in its diagnostics except the fixed-height minipages and `\vfill`, which slice B (#1121) covers.

## What was wrong (CLI on main, `bb853342f`)
`flashtex build` gave 55 pages, **118 errors, 442 warnings**. The fancy pages had **no running head or foot at all**, because the exact route never modelled `\pagestyle{fancy}`. `\pdfbookmark` printed its arguments as text (`[1]1. Fields…topic1`). `\ruled`'s rules were black and 19.5pt apart. The first `center` lost 3pt.

## Changes
**compiler / tex-expansion** (`8ce64135d`)
- **Fields expand at shipout.** fancyhdr stores a field unexpanded and expands it when the page ships. The field commands are now recorded unexpanded (`expansion::FANCY_PRELUDE`) and re-expanded at `\begin{document}`, at every body field command, and after every body (re)definition of a control sequence that a field names. A new tex-expansion primitive `\flashtex@watch` does this: a watched name's definition inserts `\flashtex@watchfired` after the assignment. The parser turns each re-expansion into `Parsed::fancy` or an `Inline::FancyFields` marker, and each page takes the last marker before it. As a result:
  - `\fancyhead[R]{…\topicshort}` before `\newcommand{\topicshort}` is no longer an unknown command;
  - every page shows its own `\renewcommand`.
- **Body `\parskip=` and `\baselineskip=`** (TeX assignments and `\setlength`) are now scoped by groups. They set `ParStart::parskip_sp` and an Explicit `ParLeading`. Size declarations still reset `\baselineskip`.
- **Bookmark commands.** `\pdfbookmark`, `\currentpdfbookmark`, `\subpdfbookmark` and `\belowpdfbookmark` read their arguments and typeset nothing. Without hyperref/bookmark they raise an error, as in pdflatex.
- **mathtools.** `\usepackage{mathtools}` with the default options (`fixamsmath`, `disallowspaces`) no longer warns. The unimplemented commands are each diagnosed where they are used (checked: `\DeclarePairedDelimiter`, `\prescript`, `\cramped`, `\smashoperator`, `\splitfrac`, `\adjustlimits`, `\overbracket`, `\lparen`, `multlined`). This document uses none of them.
- **3pt page-1 offset.** A fancy field's words no longer leave the parser in horizontal mode. That had made the first `\begin{center}` read as opened in horizontal mode and lose `\partopsep` (3pt) from its closing skip. The same offset is on main. Isolated: with only `\pagestyle{fancy}` page 1 matched, and adding `\fancyhead[L]{X}` reproduced the shift.

**render-pipeline** (`0de55194e`)
- **fancyhdr chrome on the exact route** (`fancy_page_chrome`, fancyhdr 5.2 geometry):
  - the `[b]` head parboxes sit the `\strut` depth above the `\headrulewidth` rule, whose top is the class head baseline;
  - the `[t]` foot sits at the class foot baseline, with `\footrule`/`\footruleskip`;
  - left, centre and right fields are placed as in fancyhdr;
  - microtype protrudes the first character into the left margin. There is no right protrusion, because the trailing strut box stops it: page numbers 1 and 7 would otherwise move 1.09 and 0.55bp.
- `Paragraph::parskip_pt` applies a body `\parskip`.
- A text `\rule` is painted in the colour in force, so `black!17` gives `0.83 g`.
- **Re-pin.** vendor `compiler` and `tex-expansion` are now `git archive 8ce64135d:crates/<name>`, and math-layout's PIN moves with them (content unchanged). `VENDORING.md` is updated. `check-vendor-pins.sh` exits 0 and `check-generated.py` reports 15 files ok.
- **Fixture.** `fixtures/real-world/proof-practice-21242` holds the owner's source and PDF (TL 2023, kept byte-immutable) and a MacTeX 2026 regeneration. Their words agree within 0.011bp.

## Measured (pdflatex TL 2026, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0 FORCE_SOURCE_DATE=1`, `tools/visual-oracle/pdftext.py`)
| | main | this PR | this PR + #1121 (trial merge, not pushed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| errors / warnings | 118 / 442 | **108 / 225** | **0 / 8** (font-resource notes only) |
| head/foot words (55 pages) | none drawn | **647/647, max 0.005bp** | same |
| words within 0.5bp of the owner's PDF | 368 / 4799 matched | 1396 / 5323 | **4998 / 5431** |
| rules (head rules + 756 `\ruled` rules) | — | — | **813/813 within 0.006bp**, grey 0.83 |

What remains in this PR alone is slice B's: 108 `\linewidth` errors from the unimplemented minipage's arguments, 108 minipage warnings and 109 `\vfill` warnings. The trial merge also closes the 20.32bp first-rule offset slice B saw, because `\baselineskip=17pt` now reaches the rules.

## Merging with #1121
Both PRs re-pin `vendor/compiler`. Whoever lands second merges main and re-pins again. The source code merges cleanly, but there is one semantic conflict: #1121 adds `fill_before`/`fill_after` to `pagebuild::VBlock`, so `Context::fancy_line`'s literal needs `fill_before: pagebuild::Fil::NONE, fill_after: pagebuild::Fil::NONE`. The trial build confirmed exactly that fix.

## Not done
- **PDF outline.** `\pdfbookmark` emits no outline entry. `crates/pdf` can write outlines, but the render pipeline has no producer, not even for `\section`. That is a separate feature.
- **Words that undo a watched redefinition at a group end** keep the local definition's text, because the engine's restores are silent (documented in `FANCY_PRELUDE`).
- **Word x drift** of up to about 0.6bp on some lines (math operators and microtype font expansion) is outside this slice.

## Tests
- compiler + tex-expansion: 170/170 test binaries in debug and 171/171 in release, including `--test supported_latex`.
- render-pipeline: 212/212 in both profiles.
- flashtex-cli: release green.
- `parity --tier fixtures --check-baseline`: no document below its recorded level (83 measured, L3 72.3%).
- New tests: `compiler/tests/fancyhdr_deferred_fields.rs`, `compiler/tests/proof_practice_constructs.rs`, the tex-expansion watch test, and `render-pipeline/tests/fancyhdr_chrome.rs` (pdflatex numbers).

body:
## Summary

This is the bottom of a three-layer stack that moves the admin console's reader, member, and access ticket actions from public IDs to internal IDs. `AdminReader`, `TenantMember`, and `AdminAccessTicket` now carry the record's primary key, and the requests that change one of these records accept it beside the existing public ID field, so the console can switch to the internal ID (the next layer) before the public ID fields are removed (the layer after it). Each layer passes CI on its own.

The reader writes and the access ticket revoke are now keyed by primary key; a request that still names its record by public ID only has it resolved to the row first. The shared `tenantmembers` package takes a `UserID` beside `UserPublicID` in the same shape the platform tenant stack gives it, so the two stacks meet without a conflict.

Fixes #3145

## Changes

- `AdminReader.id`, `TenantMember.user_id`, `AdminAccessTicket.id`, and `RemoveTenantMemberResponse.user_id` / `DeleteReaderResponse.reader_id` carry the primary key.
- `SuspendReaderRequest`, `UnsuspendReaderRequest`, `SetReaderBirthDateRequest`, and `DeleteReaderRequest` take `reader_id`; `UpdateTenantMemberRoleRequest` and `RemoveTenantMemberRequest` take `user_id`; `RevokeAccessTicketRequest` takes `access_ticket_id`. Each takes precedence over the public ID, and a malformed one is `invalid_argument`.
- New `GetTenantReaderByID` and `GetAccessTicketIDByPublicIDForTenant`; `SuspendTenantReader`, `UnsuspendTenantReader`, `SetTenantReaderBirthDate`, `DeleteTenantReader`, and the access ticket read and revoke (`GetAccessTicketForTenant`, `RevokeAccessTicketForTenant`) are keyed by `id`.
- The audit log keeps recording a reader's and a ticket's public ID as the target, as before.
- Handler and integration tests address readers, members, and tickets by ID, with one test each still covering the public ID path this layer keeps.

## How to Test

- `task gen` (no diff), `sqlc diff`, `task server:lint`, `task server:test-short`, `task server:test`
- `pnpm preflight` (the generated TypeScript only adds fields; nothing under `apps/` changes)

- [x] I tested my changes locally.
- [x] I updated docs if needed.

Follow-up to omniclaude#2378. #2378 gave the public-repo hygiene gate an added-lines scope and enforced four content classes (private-repo-name, internal-kb-prose, lab-config, person-name), but deliberately left `private-network` unenforced ("Adding it would be a separate decision"). `private-network` (lab addresses and host nicknames) is already a fully implemented, NEVER-EXEMPTABLE content class in `scripts/public_repo_hygiene_gate.py` — it was simply not in omniclaude's own `enforce_classes` — so a pull request adding a lab IP or hostname still passed.

## Changes

- `.public-repo-hygiene.yaml`: adds `"private-network"` to `enforce_classes` (still under `enforce_scope: added-lines`, inherited from #2378), and updates the comment's residue count.

author: rusholme
body:
Tests only; `rapidpipe/` is unchanged. Closes three test-enforcement gaps that the Codex review of c10d95c7..d4ca5484 confirmed. None is a runtime defect.

**Caller-side manifest write (gap 1).** `test_compose_inputs_makes_one_call_to_the_primitive` now monkeypatches `runctl._Storage.write_manifest` on the class to append to a log. It asserts the log is empty in all four cases. An aliased bound call such as `publish = storage.write_manifest; publish(...)`, or an unbound call, lands in the spy even though the static text guard cannot see it.

**Commit-before-write on real PostgreSQL (gap 2).** In `test_inputs_commits_bindings_before_the_manifest_write_and_recovers_after_a_write_failure`, `flaky_write_manifest` now queries the consumer's `unit_inputs` through the independent autocommit `db` connection before it raises. The test asserts the set seen at the failing write equals `{ref_instance_id}`, and that the retry's write saw the same set. A commit made during failure cleanup can no longer satisfy the test. The after-return assertions stay.

**Eager composition in the loop (gap 3).** `test_the_loops_three_sites_each_make_one_call_per_consumer` now replaces `loop.crossmatch_inputs` and `loop.input_set_manifest` with recorders and asserts neither ran, in both the absent and existing cases. The recording primitive never calls `compose`, so the maintain lambda, the crossmatch lambda and the alerts site's local `compose` must not run either. The test also adds a class-level `write_manifest` spy on the fake storage. The instance wrapper already caught aliases taken inside `process_date`, but it did not catch an unbound class call that rewrites the same object.

Mutation probes, each reverted with `git checkout` afterwards:
- An aliased write after the primitive in `compose_inputs` fails all four CLI recorder cases.
- An eager `crossmatch_inputs` before the primitive in `process_date`, passed as `compose=lambda: precomputed`, fails both the absent and existing loop cases.
- Moving `conn.commit()` after the write in `binding.py` fails the fake-order unit tests. The new in-write DB query depends on that same line, `binding.py`'s step 7 commit. That probe can run only in CI, because there is no local PostgreSQL.

`pytest tests/unit -q` gives 1419 passed.

author: danieljoppi
body:
Closes #121.

## What changed
- **`build-drift.py`, check 6.** Every template `test/*.test.js` must exist in the site and match the template **outside its `// >>> ADOPT` regions**, which hold the site's dataset name and allowlists by design. A site that must change a shared test declares it under `"tests"` in `.template-drift.json`, with a reason and a `base` hash. It gets the same MISSING, DRIFT, STALE and UNUSED-DECLARATION findings as functions. `--hash <name>.test.js` prints a test's hash.
- **`tools/adopt-tests.py <site>`** writes the template's shared tests into a site. It carries the site's ADOPT region contents across by label and leaves declared customisations alone.

## A departure from the ticket's suggestion
The suggestion was to make feature tests self-skip. The survey showed that isn't needed: the shared tests run against the **example fixture**, not the site's data. On a simulated wave across all 23 sites (adopt the tests, port #74, vendor the missing template support files `chronology.example.json`, `src/latam.svg` and `glossary-terms.json`), **17 sites pass with no declarations.**

The other six have specific causes, which the wave handles:

| site | failing | cause | resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| tl, lagrimas | data-invariants | extra page routes (figure pages, subpages) | declare |
| olavo | i18n-completeness | its own translation-cache layer | declare |
| rcc, fsspx | viz-renderers | their customised `renderPage` | declare |
| perennialism, rcc | link-health (`deriveUserAgent`) | check in the wave | port or declare |
| fsspx | i18n-completeness | **real missing translations**; fsspx never had the test | translate |

The survey also found untracked drift nobody knew about:
- 22 sites never received the template's BCE-year fix to `data-invariants`;
- 4 sites run an older `link-health`.

## Tests
New unit tests cover:
- the in-step case (ADOPT content differs);
- drift outside ADOPT;
- a missing test;
- declared, stale and unused declarations;
- `adopt-tests` merging regions by label.

The tools suite is OK.

## Что сделано

`DELETE /api/v1/me/children/{id}/` → `204`. Удаление мягкое: у `Student` появилось поле `archived_at`. Физически удалить ребёнка с историей нельзя, потому что `enrollment.student` защищён `PROTECT`, а записи и оплаты нужны для учёта.

- Удалённый ребёнок скрыт из `children` профиля, для него `PATCH` → `404`, в чекауте → `403 FORBIDDEN_RESOURCE`. В админке и в истории покупок (`/me/subscriptions`, `/me/trials`) он остаётся виден.
- Удаление запрещено, пока есть живая запись: абонемент (`HELD`/`ENROLLED`), неоплаченная бронь пробного или оплаченное пробное с датой сегодня или позже. Ответ `409 CHILD_HAS_ACTIVE_ENROLLMENTS`, список мешающих записей в `extensions.active_enrollments`. Прошедшее пробное удалению не мешает.
- Уникальность «родитель + ФИО + дата рождения» проверяется только среди неудалённых (`uq_student_active_per_parent_name_dob`), поэтому удалённого ребёнка можно добавить заново.
- Гонка «удаление против покупки» закрыта: и `archive_child`, и чекаут берут `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` на строку ребёнка. Порядок блокировок: ребёнок → слоты → депозит.
- Попутно исправлено: `PATCH /me/children/{id}/` при совпадении с другим ребёнком теперь отвечает `422 VALIDATION_ERROR`, а не `500`.
- Обработчик ошибок добавляет в ответ `exc.extensions`.
- В админке появились колонка и фильтр «Удалён родителем». Восстановить ребёнка — очистить это поле.

## Решения бизнеса

- `health_issues` при удалении пока не стираются, пересмотрим вместе с юристом (`docs/personal-data.md`).
- Лазейку «удалил и добавил заново → снова доступно пробное» пока принимаем.
- Восстановить удалённого ребёнка может только администратор в админке.

## Миграция `users/0007`

Колонка nullable без default, поэтому таблица не переписывается. Партиальный уникальный индекс создаётся до удаления старого. Стоит `lock_timeout = 5s` в обе стороны. Откат упадёт, если после наката того же ребёнка удалили и добавили заново: полный уникальный индекс в таком случае не построится. Это ожидаемое поведение.

## Проверки

`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy`, `pytest` — 478 passed, из них 20 новых тестов. Миграция проверена на локальной базе: накат, откат и снова накат.

Документация: `api-core-contracts.md` (ручка, код ошибки, `extensions`), `schema.md`, `auth-flow.md`, `personal-data.md`.

## O que este PR faz e por quê

Este PR atualiza o status das 14 User Stories do Macro2PR de `Draft` para `Ready`, após o tema ter sido aprovado pelo professor.

As regras das US01–US14 já haviam sido definidas durante a fundação do produto (Atividade 04), incluindo critérios de aceite, regras de negócio associadas, tamanhos e prioridades MoSCoW. Elas permaneceram em Draft enquanto aguardávamos o aceite formal do professor para confirmar a viabilidade do tema.

Este PR altera somente o campo Status de cada história, de `⚪ Draft` para `🟡 Ready`. Não houve mudança de escopo, critérios de aceite, regras de negócio, tamanhos ou prioridades em nenhuma das 14 histórias.

O status Ready significa que estas histórias agora podem ser transformadas em Issues no GitHub pela Atividade 05, permitindo a criação do backlog rastreável no GitHub Projects/Kanban.

Arquitetura, código, implementação e decisões técnicas não fazem parte deste PR. O repositório continua sem alterações de produto durante toda a transição entre fases.

author: mgoldsborough
body:
Closes #1283 ## The defect On a phone, `AppWithChat` skipped rendering its `SlotRenderer` whenever the chat sidebar was open (`hideMobileApp = isMobile && isSidebar`). That destroyed the app's iframe and bridge while `AppWithChat` stayed mounted and kept the app focused. The app lost its local UI state and reloaded when the chat closed. And because app state lives only as long as the view that pushed it (#1284), a message sent from the sidebar carried the focused app's briefing with no state, at the moment the user opened chat to ask about what they were looking at. ## The rule Covering an app is presentation, not lifetime. The app area now renders in every panel state; only unmounting `AppWithChat` or a new placement tears the view down. No conditional render and no `key` change touches the `SlotRenderer`. ## Layout, as it is today - **Mobile (< 768px, `useIsMobile`)**: the chat panel is a `fixed top-0 right-0 h-full` overlay at 100% width (`ChatChrome.tsx` `resolvePanelWidth` and the panel div). `
` gets no `marginRight` on mobile (`ShellLayout.tsx` `mainMarginRight`). So the sidebar never takes layout space from the app; it covers it. - **Desktop sidebar**: `
` is pushed over by `panelWidth`; the app stays visible and interactive beside the panel. Unchanged. - **Fullscreen (both)**: the app area stays mounted at `opacity-30 blur-sm pointer-events-none`. Unchanged. - **Closed**: the app area renders normally. Unchanged. Other mount sites checked for the same shape: `SettingsAppPanel`, `InlineAppView` (in `BlockTimeline`), and the `AppWithChat` routes in `App.tsx` all unmount only on a real route or message change. None has this defect. ## Hiding method While the mobile sidebar covers the app, the app area gets `visibility: hidden` (Tailwind `invisible`), `inert`, and `aria-hidden="true"`, the same `inert` + `aria-hidden` pair `ArtifactPanel` uses for its closed state. `visibility: hidden` rather than `display: none` so the iframe keeps its size and the app sees no resize (and no layout collapse) while covered. Interaction with the on-screen preference in `web/src/bridge/bridge.ts`: `IntersectionObserver` ignores `visibility`, occlusion, and opacity, so the covered view still counts as on screen and `getAppState` returns its latest push. That is the right answer: it is the view the user just opened chat to ask about. Had it reported off-screen (as `display: none` would), `getAppState` falls back to the latest push among off-screen views, so the state would reach the prompt either way. `bridge.ts` is unchanged. ## Tests `web/src/__tests__/AppWithChat.test.tsx` mounts the real `ChatProvider` → `ChatPanelProvider` → `AppWithChat` at a 375px viewport and wraps (does not replace) `createBridge`: - opening and closing the sidebar keeps the same iframe element and the same bridge, and `destroy()` is never called; - with the sidebar open, `getAppState` for the focused app returns what the view pushed, and a push while covered still lands; - while covered, the app area is `inert`, `aria-hidden`, and invisible, and all three clear on close; - on desktop, opening the sidebar leaves the app area interactive. Against `main`'s `AppWithChat` all four fail (the first three on the defect; the desktop guard because `main` has no test id on the area). On this branch all four pass. `bun run verify` is green. ## In a browser (390×844, mobile emulation, `bun run dev:worktree`) Steps: open Conversations, type into its search box, open the chat sidebar, close it. | | App before opening chat | After closing chat | |---|---|---| | **main** | | search cleared, iframe rebuilt | | **this branch** | | search kept | On `main` the page has 0 iframes while the chat is open. On this branch the same iframe element stays in the DOM throughout (`inert`, `aria-hidden`, `visibility: hidden`, still 390×844) and the typed text survives. Out of charter, filed separately: #1295 (the closed chat panel stays focusable and exposed to assistive tech), #1296 (workspace-tree links leave the mobile nav drawer open).

author: jonclegg
body: ## What changed **No Python on the host.** `cloakroom` is now a bash dispatcher. The Python `cli/` package is deleted, so the README and installer no longer tell anyone to run `xcode-select --install`. - `cloakroom start` / `stop` run `start.sh` / `stop.sh`, as before. - `cloakroom share` / `unshare` run the new `share.sh`. It starts a `cloudflared` quick tunnel to the viewer only and keeps the same `~/.cloakroom/share.json` state file. - `cloakroom status` uses `docker inspect` plus a `curl` to `/json/version`. - `lib.sh` holds the ports, the state paths, the container health check, and the share-state helpers, so they aren't duplicated. - The `--json` output for `status`, `share`, and `unshare` has the same shape as before. **README is a short quickstart (about 50 lines).** It covers the problem, what Cloakroom is, a one-line proof point, the install one-liner, `cloakroom start`, the viewer, pointing your agent at the folder, and `cloakroom share` for the phone. It keeps short "Good to know" notes and the license. The Settings table is still gone; `.env.example` is unchanged and holds the optional settings. **Details for agents moved to `skills/cloakroom/SKILL.md`:** - The architecture diagram and the full CDP example. - The commands table. - What the installer does. - A pointer to `.env.example` for optional settings. - Limits (the old "What Cloakroom doesn't promise" list). - Security notes. - The troubleshooting table. - The Windows steps. - Internals: the container, volumes, extra identities, the stealth test, pinning a CloakBrowser version, and plain Compose. - Links. `AGENTS.md` now says the skill is the full reference. The error messages in `start.sh`, `start.ps1`, and `install.sh` that pointed at the README now point at the skill. Main is merged in; there are no conflicts. ## Testing On Linux, I ran `cloakroom status`, `share`, `share stop`, and `unshare`, in both `--json` and text mode, against stub `docker`, `curl`, and `cloudflared` binaries. Their output matched the old Python CLI. I haven't run it on a real Mac with OrbStack yet.

body:
**Description**

Fixes Dependabot security alert #271 (asyncssh), and clears the other Python advisories `pip-audit` finds in `uv.lock` that already have a fix.

| Package | From | To | Advisory | Path |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| asyncssh | 2.23.1 | 2.24.0 | GHSA-rw4j-r22c-9gc3 / CVE-2026-62949: a peer can freeze the asyncio event loop with a maximum packet size of `0` in `SSH_MSG_CHANNEL_OPEN` / `OPEN_CONFIRMATION` | direct (SSH save sync) |
| click | 8.2.1 | 8.5.0 | GHSA-47fr-3ffg-hgmw / CVE-2026-7246: command injection in `click.edit()` | transitive (rq, uvicorn, apprise) |
| requests | 2.32.5 | 2.34.2 | GHSA-gc5v-m9x4-r6x2 / CVE-2026-25645: predictable temp path in `extract_zipped_paths()` | transitive (apprise, OTLP exporter) |
| pygments | 2.19.2 | 2.21.0 | GHSA-5239-wwwm-4pmq / CVE-2026-4539: ReDoS in the GUID regex | dev/test only |

- `pyproject.toml`: `asyncssh ~= 2.23` → `~= 2.24` so the resolver can't pick a vulnerable release.
- `uv.lock`: only the four packages above change. It was regenerated with `uv lock --upgrade-package` using the pinned uv 0.12.13, and every new version is older than the 7-day `exclude-newer` window.

Still open: `mariadb` 1.1.14 (GHSA-pv9p-5w55-55jm) has no fixed release yet.

body:
## Summary

This is the middle of a three-layer stack. The layer below returns the internal IDs of readers, members, and access tickets and accepts them in the requests that change those records; this layer makes the admin console send them, so the layer above can remove the public ID fields.

The reader page still resolves its reader by the public ID `/readers/[reader_id]` carries, and the access ticket list keeps filtering by the public IDs its `?user=` and `?episode=` parameters carry. Everything the console sends to change one of these records is now the internal ID it read back.

Fixes #3118

## Changes

- Reader page: the suspend, unsuspend, change-birth-date, and delete forms post `reader_id` (the reader's internal ID) for the RPC. They keep posting `public_id` only so the action can redirect back to `/readers/[reader_id]`.
- Members: `TenantMemberItem` carries `userId` instead of `userPublicId`, and the role change and removal forms post `user_id`. No member URL carries an ID, so nothing on this screen needs the public ID any more.
- Access tickets: each row carries the ticket's `id`, and the revoke form posts `access_ticket_id`. The row still shows the ticket's public ID, as before.
- Unit test fixtures carry the internal IDs.

## How to Test

- `pnpm preflight`
- `task e2e`. `admin.readers`, `admin.tenant-members`, and `admin.access-tickets` exercise suspend, unsuspend and delete, role change and removal, and revoke against a running stack.

## Checklist

- [x] I used a Conventional Commits style PR title.
- [x] I tested my changes locally.
- [x] I updated docs if needed.

body:
Auto placement for movable floor parts, with a manual override in the Inside stage.

- Drives can turn a quarter and move to another row the layout allows: layout A battery row or board row; layout B front, beside the board, or beside the battery; layout C side bay or beside the battery. Batteries and speakers can turn in place.
- The solver tries each auto slot's zones and turns, one slot at a time from the best so far (two passes), and keeps the plan with the smallest footprint that needs no more width or depth than the layout's own. The best few are then solved in full and must not be thicker or bring more problems, so auto never needs more room than before.
- Inside stage: Place (Auto or a named row) and Turn (Auto, 0°, 90°) chips for each movable part. Pins are stored in `build.place.parts`; old saves load as auto.
- The 3D view builds a turned part at its own size and turns it.
- Rivals keep their stored sizes (sized with auto off). 267 rivals and 4 samples now need a smaller minimum; none needs more and none gains a problem.

## Summary With `prependOnFirst=false`, legacy `paginationLinks()` stripped `Len(arguments.prependToPage)` characters from the start of the page window. But the first page is not preceded by the raw argument. It gets the **sanitized** `prependToPage` (numeric entities decoded, `on*` handlers stripped), or its `active ` variant when that page is the current one and `addActiveClassToPrependedParent=true`. Whenever the lengths differ, the first link is mangled. The sibling `appendOnLast` branch already uses the sanitized length. **Fix:** the per-page prefix logic moves into a new public helper, `$paginationPrependForPage()`, which the window loop and the strip now share. The strip works out the first page in the window (`Max(1, currentPage - windowSize)`, matching the loop's lower bound). It then removes that exact prefix, and only if `Left()` actually matches it. ## Related Issue None filed. author: tobocop2
body:
Stacked on #325. Merge that first.

## Commas inside parentheses

The markdown rewrite ended a srcset descriptor at the next comma, even inside parentheses, so `a.png 1x (x, y), b.png 2x` became three candidates and the rewrite turned `y)` into an address a browser never requests.

## Commas in image discovery

Image discovery split the list on every comma. It cut a URL at its own comma (`a,b.png` became `a`), returned nothing when the list began with commas, and emitted a truncated `data:` address.

## The spec's splitter

Both readers now use one splitter that follows the HTML spec, including the parentheses rule. It separates only at the spec's five whitespace characters, so the rewrite keeps a no-break space in a descriptor and image discovery keeps a leading no-break space in the URL. Image discovery skips a `data:` first candidate in any letter case.

## Checked

The splitter agrees with a reference written from the spec text on every list of up to six characters over an eight-character alphabet (299,593 lists). An independent reference also agreed on 1,003,917 generated lists.

Closes #271

author: stefanmaron
body:
Closes #4767

Corpus-NA: needs several source app groups declaring one object id in a single runner invocation; a corpus run is one app on one service tier, so a real BC tier never has two declarations of one id to choose between

## What changed

This is the runtime half of #4767, the part #4776 left open (issue comment 5848903217). When two source app groups in one run declare the same table, page, report or query id, the runtime metadata objects are now resolved per executing group. The mechanism is the one #4764 used for xmlports. `AppGroupScopeFor(kind, id)` names the executing group when it is one of several declaring the id. Two helpers are new in `RecordPatches.AppGroupObjectVisibility.cs`:

- `AppGroupCacheScope(kind, id)`: that group, or `Guid.Empty`. The empty answer keeps every other caller on the one process-wide entry.
- `GetOrAddInAppGroupScope(processWide, byAppGroup, kind, id, factory)`.

A run where no two groups share an id answers from `_appGroupsSharingAnId.Count` alone.

Each kind had several id-keyed stores. All of them now take the group term:

| kind | stores now per executing group |
|---|---|
| all | the emit-captured documents: `AlPageMetadataRegistry`, `AlReportMetadataRegistry`, `AlObjectMetadataRegistry` (a per-app copy beside the last-wins one, as #4764 did). BC's `MetaObjectCache` also has one loader per group (`RunnerMetaApplicationObjectLoader.For`). That cache keys on (package id, object id), and the runner supplies no package id, so the first group's parsed page or table definition answered every group. |
| table | `NCLMetaTable` (`GetOrBuildNCLMetaTable`, built from the group's own parsed table and document). Also scoped: the `Record{id}` type (`FindRecordType`), field-trigger wiring (`_fieldTriggersWiredByAppGroup`), the table-subscriber injection ledger (`EventSubscriberPatches.InjectedLedgerFor`, for the lazy per-table injection only), the AutoIncrement field registry (`_aiFieldIds`), and every by-id and by-name `_parsedTables` read on the runtime path. A group's own instance is never put into BC's `metadataCacheEntries`, which holds one entry per id. Every lookup goes through our Cecil-rewritten `GetMetaTableById` first. |
| page | `NCLMetaForm` (`GetOrBuildMetaForm`), `EnsureRealPageMetadata`'s loaded, negative and retake bookkeeping (now keyed `(group, id)`), the `Page{id}` type cache, and the runtime `_parsedPages` readers in `AlPageParser` (control map, source table, member names, and so on). |
| report | `NCLMetaReport`, `NavReportSync`'s `MetaReport` cache, the Report Metadata document cache (`_bcReportDocuments`), and the `Report{id}` type cache. |
| query | `EnsureQueryInMetadataCache`'s and `BuildRealNCLMetaQuery`'s caches, and the `Query{id}` type cache. |

**Cache-HIT fix:** the page and report sidecars were written with `TryGet(id)`. With `TryGet` now scoped, that read returned the previous group's document, because that group's test assembly is still the current one when the next group's sidecar is written. The sidecar and `--watch` readers now use `TryGetForCompile`, which reads the compiling app's own copy. The warm-run test below pins this.

## RED -> GREEN

`AppGroupObjectVisibilityTests`' dupX/dupY fixture gains four tests per group, one per kind. Each group now also declares:

- a field `OnValidate` trigger and an `AutoIncrement` field (X only) on the shared table 62680;
- an `OnAfterInsertEvent` subscriber codeunit (62690 in X, 62691 in Y; the fixture's idRanges are now 62680-62699);
- an `OnPreReport` that raises its own letter;
- page controls and properties named per group.

The four tests:

- `SharedTableRuntimeMetadataIsThisGroupsOwn`: the `Field` row, `RecordRef` name and field name, the group's own `OnValidate`, its subscriber, and its AutoIncrement.
- `SharedQueryMetadataIsThisGroupsOwn`: the Query Metadata name.
- `SharedReportRunsThisGroupsOwn`: `Report.Run(62686)` runs this group's report, and Report Metadata `UseRequestPage` is read from this group's document.
- `SharedPageTestPageIsThisGroupsOwn`: TestPage controls by this group's control names, its caption, and the Page Metadata `DelayedInsert` / `RefreshOnActivate` columns.

A new `Cli_SharedIds_ColdThenWarmOnOneCacheRoot_EachGroupStillReadsItsOwn` runs the fixture twice on one `--cache` root. The CLI assertion now prints the whole runner output when it fails.

Measured with BC 28.1.49838.53910, Debug build:

- Merge-base runner (`AlRunner/` from `origin/main`) with the new fixture: `Tests: 23 passed 18 failed 5`. xUnit `AppGroupObjectVisibilityTests`: `Failed: 3, Passed: 9, Total: 12` (Cli, warm and Server). The failures: `Field name for 62680/2 in Y is OnlyX`; `AutoIncrement Seq of the second row of 62680 in X is 0`; `Query Metadata name for 62688 in X is Dup Y Query`; `Report Metadata UseRequestPage for 62686 in X is Yes`; `NavTestFieldNotFoundException: The field with ID = 848534563 is not found on the page` (X's control on Y's page).
- This branch: `Tests: 23 passed 23 failed 0`, xUnit `Failed: 0, Passed: 12, Total: 12`.

## Mutations

Each was applied with `tools/apply-mutation.py`, rebuilt, run through the Cli tests, and restored. The four kind mutations use one anchor: `AppGroupCacheScope` answers `Guid.Empty` for that kind only. Each one reds exactly its own kind's test.

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| table unscoped | 21/23: X `AutoIncrement Seq ... is 0`, Y `Field name ... is OnlyX` |
| page unscoped | 22/23: X `TestPage caption of 62687 in X is Dup Y Page Cap` |
| report unscoped | 22/23: X `Report Metadata UseRequestPage for 62686 in X is Yes` (before the UseRequestPage assertion was added: both groups' `Report.Run` red) |
| query unscoped | 22/23: X `Query Metadata name for 62688 in X is Dup Y Query` |
| `RunnerMetaApplicationObjectLoader.For` always returns `Instance` | 21/23: Y `Field name ... OnlyX` and Y `TestPage caption ... Dup X Page Cap` |
| subscriber ledger always the process-wide set | 21/23: `own OnAfterInsert subscriber on 62680 did not fire` in X and Y |
| `FindRecordType` scoped branch disabled | 22/23: Y `field OnValidate of 62680 in Y set Mark to VX` |
| `BuildNCLMetaTable` keeps the process-wide parsed table | 22/23: X `AutoIncrement Seq ... in X is 0`. The first fixture did not catch this one: the table builds from BC's document, and only the runner-side field wiring reads the parsed table. The AutoIncrement assertion was added for this. |
| AutoIncrement registry keyed by `Guid.Empty` | 22/23: Y `AutoIncrement Seq ... in Y is 2` |
| report document cache process-wide | 22/23: Y `Report Metadata UseRequestPage for 62686 in Y is No` |
| page sidecar written with `TryGet` | warm test only: Y `TestPage caption of 62687 in Y is Dup X Page Cap` (cold run green) |
| report sidecar written with `TryGet` | warm test only: Y `Report.Run(62686) in Y ended with: Exception has been thrown...` |

## Other runs

- **Whole `AlRunner.Tests` suite, Release** (the CI configuration), in partitions on head `0c95006`: 7018 run, 59 failed, 4 skipped. All 59 failures are `MetadataGroundTruthStaleException`: this box's ground-truth bundles were written by an older generator. That is environmental, and the tests fail the same way before measuring anything.
- In **Debug**, `BuildNclMetaTableFailureAttributionTests.TheTwoAbsentReturns_SitOutsideTheTry...` went red. It passes in Release. It looks for a raw `0x2A` byte before the first try, and in Debug the early returns are `br` to a shared `ret`. Added static fields shift token bytes, and the coincidental `2a` disappears. Filed as #4822. Nothing here changes the method's control flow.
- `tools/test_*.py`, `.github/scripts/test_*.sh` and `.github/scripts/test_*.py`: all green.
- **Cold then warm on one cache root**: a scratch copy of the fixture and the new xUnit test are both green on both runs.

author: d-martian
body:
Implements the plan's phase 2 item "24 h ledger and the three monthly rates".

## Tray
```
⛏ Mining gently · 6 of 8 threads
   3.42 kH/s now · 3.10 30 min · 2.87 24 h
   ≈ 0.0102 · 0.0093 · 0.0086 XMR/month
   …
   Shares  4 found · 100% of the payout window · next in ≈ 6h
```
- The three hashrates share the unit of the largest.
- The monthly figures share one precision, three significant digits on the largest.
- A rate the ledger can't vouch for yet shows "—".

## The ledger (`internal/stats/ledger.go`)
- **Why our own record:** XMRig's 10 s/60 s/15 m windows stop while it's suspended, so a throttled miner's averages describe only the moments it was allowed to run. The scheduler records a paused tick as zero, which is the truth.
- **Resolution:** one-minute buckets (sum of samples, count) for 24 hours, 1,440 at most. A window's rate is Σsum ÷ Σcount, so every 2 s tick weighs the same. Time kind-miner wasn't running has no samples and doesn't count.
- **Honest windows:** a rate is quoted only once the ledger covers at least half its window. A fresh start shows "—" for 24 h until 12 hours of history exist, rather than a "24 h" number computed from minutes.
- **Persistence:** `ledger.json` next to p2pool's data, written atomically (temp file and rename) every 10 minutes and at shutdown (after the scheduler's last tick). On load it keeps the last 24 h. A missing file is simply empty; a corrupt, wrong-version, out-of-order or future-dated one is logged and discarded. Losing averages is no reason not to mine.

## Formulas
- XMR/month = H × 2,629,800 s × R ÷ D (`P2PoolStats.EstimatedXMRPerMonth`).
- Next share = sidechain difficulty ÷ the 30-minute rate (`ShareIntervalAt`). p2pool's 15-minute figure only counts hashes it received, so it overstates a throttled miner's pace too.

## Dashboard
- The hashrate details swap "Since start" for 30 min and 24 h, and income gains "Est. per month".
- The income estimate uses the longest rate the ledger can vouch for (24 h, else 30 min, else now).
- `kvList.Set` silently drops keys a list wasn't built with, so the new rows are declared, with a test guarding them.

## Testing
- `stats`: rates over mixed mining, pauses and gaps; the half-window rule; the 24 h bound; save and restore across a "reboot"; stale data dropped after two days; forgiving loads.
- `engine`: monthly estimate arithmetic; `ShareIntervalAt` against p2pool's figure.
- `core`: the timed save writes and stops with shutdown, and a restore brings the minute back.
- `gui`: rate and monthly line formatting (including the plan's exact example), next share from the 30-minute rate, longest-rate choice, dashboard rows.
- `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` pass; `-race` on stats, core and scheduler.
- Not tested live: a day of real mining.

🎯 **What:** Moved hardcoded trip data from `DataSeeder.java` into an external `trips.json` file. Refactored `DataSeeder` to use Jackson `ObjectMapper` to parse this JSON configuration.
💡 **Why:** Hardcoding data in Java classes mixes logic with configuration, violating separation of concerns. Moving this data to a JSON file improves maintainability, making it much easier to add, modify, or remove initial trip data without needing to edit Java code or recompile the application.
✅ **Verification:** Verified by checking that `backend/src/main/resources/data/trips.json` was correctly created, `DataSeeder.java` and `DataSeederTest.java` were updated successfully, and running `mvn clean test` which successfully passed all 74 unit tests, including the updated Seeder tests.
✨ **Result:** The `DataSeeder` is now cleaner and agnostic to the actual trip data it populates, while the configuration is highly readable in standard JSON format.

## Summary

This PR removes the last two users of qwen3:8b and stops ollama-host from keeping it loaded. The model stays pulled on disk.

- `mtrace.env.j2` drops `OLLAMA_HOST` and `MEDIA_CONTROL_MODEL`. mtrace routes by keyword only (media-control PR, PET-525).
- The `lab-digest` role prints its fact sections and drops the narration paragraph. `lab_digest_ollama_url` and `lab_digest_model` are gone.
- `ollama_resident_models` no longer lists qwen3:8b. `ollama_base_models` still does, so the model stays on disk.
- The `ollama-models` role unloads every model an instance holds but does not declare for that port. It reads `/api/ps` back and fails if one remains. The instances run with `OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1`, so removing the list entry would not free VRAM on its own.
- `lab-verify.sh` reports a loaded but undeclared model as BAD.

The branch has no `pet-525-` prefix on purpose. The done-when checks need playbook runs after the merge, so `plane-sync` must not close the item.

## Merge order

Merge this PR before the media-control PR. media-control's deploy runs `configure-media-dash.yml` from iac `main`, so this merge removes the env lines first.

## Deploy (Pedro runs these)

- The lab digest: `configure-pete-pi.yml --tags lab-digest`.
- The unload: `playbooks/ollama-models.yml`.

## Verification

- `ansible-lint roles/ollama-models roles/lab-digest` passes on the production profile.
- `--syntax-check` passes for `ollama-models.yml`, `configure-pete-pi.yml` and `configure-media-dash.yml`.
- The rendered digest script passes `bash -n`.
- A local playbook run on sample `/api/ps` data selects `qwen3:8b@11434` for the unload and skips the declared embed model.

It also shows that :11435 holds 0 loaded models, so the embed model isn't resident either. The same playbook run loads it.

author: ghigog
body:
Server and client errors are now tracked with secrets redacted, and error
spikes, smoke-test failures, and `/api/health` returning `ok: false` all
alert through an optional webhook.

- `src/lib/observability/error-tracking.ts`: `trackThrown`/`trackError` log a
  redacted, structured error (route, commit from `VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA`,
  digest, source) via `console.error`, reusing `src/lib/secrets/redact.ts`.
  A rolling counter alerts once 10+ errors land within 5 minutes (15-minute
  cooldown so it doesn't spam).
- `src/lib/observability/alerts.ts`: `sendAlert` redacts and POSTs to the new
  optional `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` (Slack-compatible JSON body); without it, it
  logs a warning instead of throwing, matching how every other optional
  credential in this app degrades.
- `src/instrumentation.ts`: added `onRequestError`, which Next.js calls for
  every server-side route/render/action error, wired to `trackThrown`.
- `src/instrumentation-client.ts` (new): catches `window` `error` and
  `unhandledrejection`, redacts client-side too (defense in depth), and
  forwards to the server.
- `.github/workflows/smoke-test.yml`: added an `alert()` helper that posts to
  a new `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` secret (skips quietly if unset). It fires on the
  existing "never became healthy" and "/ returned non-200" failures, and now
  also fires immediately the first time `/api/health` reports `ok: false`
  on the deployed commit, rather than waiting out the full 20-minute
  deploy-wait window.
- `src/lib/secrets/env.ts`: added `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` (validated as a URL) so
  server code reads it through the existing typed config, like every other
  optional credential, instead of raw `process.env`.
- `.env.example`: documented `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL`.

Verified the acceptance criterion directly: a route handler that throws now
produces a structured `console.error` line with `route`, `commit`, and the
error message/stack with secrets redacted (covered by
`src/lib/observability/error-tracking.test.ts`).

Outside the ticket's listed file scope: added
`src/app/api/observability/client-error/route.ts` (plus its test). Client
error tracking has no other way to reach the server — the browser can't
write to server logs or call `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` directly without exposing
that URL to every visitor — so `instrumentation-client.ts` POSTs redacted
error details here, and the route re-redacts and calls `trackError`. Also
touched `src/lib/secrets/env.ts` and its test, for the reason above.

Left `next.config.ts` and `package.json` (both in the listed scope)
unchanged: no dependency was needed (no external error-tracking SDK — this
follows the app's existing pattern of a self-hosted, credential-optional
integration rather than requiring a paid service), and Next.js 16 picks up
`instrumentation.ts`/`instrumentation-client.ts` and `onRequestError`
without any config flag.

  (any Slack- or Discord-compatible incoming webhook URL) and add the same
  value as a repository secret named `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` for the
  `smoke-test.yml` workflow. Without it, alerts still log to the server
  console / Action run log, just without paging anyone.

Plan:
- [x] Explore repo structure: redact.ts, instrumentation, observability, next.config, package.json, smoke-test workflow
- [x] Add ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL to src/lib/secrets/env.ts
- [x] Create src/lib/observability/alerts.ts (sendAlert, redacted, posts to ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL)
- [x] Create src/lib/observability/error-tracking.ts (trackError/trackThrown, redaction, commit+route, spike alert)
- [x] Wire src/instrumentation.ts onRequestError to trackThrown
- [x] Add src/instrumentation-client.ts capturing window errors, redacting, posting to new API route
- [x] Add src/app/api/observability/client-error/route.ts (outside file scope, needed as the client->server transport)
- [x] Update .github/workflows/smoke-test.yml: alert on smoke-test failure and explicit ok:false
- [x] Document ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL in .env.example
- [x] Write unit tests for observability modules and the client-error route
- [x] Run lint, typecheck, and test suite

Closes #35.

## AUD-10 — Error tracking and alerting

**User story:** As a operator, I'd like to hear about a failure before a beta user reports it, so that I can fix it first.

### Context
There is no error tracking or alerting; failures are only seen if someone reports them.

### Description
Server and client error tracking with alerts.

### Requirements
- Server and client error tracking with secrets redacted (reuse src/lib/secrets/redact.ts).
- Alerts on smoke-test failure, health ok: false, and error spikes.

### Acceptance criteria

- Given error tracking is configured, when a route throws, then the error appears with the route and commit, and no secrets.

### File scope

`.env.example`, `.github/workflows/smoke-test.yml`, `next.config.ts`, `package.json`, `src/app/api/observability/client-error/route.test.ts`, `src/app/api/observability/client-error/route.ts`, `src/instrumentation`, `src/instrumentation-client.ts`, `src/lib/observability`, `src/lib/secrets/env.test.ts`, `src/lib/secrets/env.ts`

No verification command was run.

### For you

Steps outside the repository no agent can take. The Epic's showcase lists them again once everything has merged.

- [ ] To get alerts, set `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` in Vercel's environment variables

author: kylepatrickhodge26-png
body:
Adds the Dashboard on top of Scheduling and Crew (kylepatrickhodge26-png/ecoscapeops#3). It follows the prototype's Home screen, because `SPEC.md` isn't in the repo. Weather, routing, expenses and billing are out of scope.

## What's included

**Home page**
- `/dashboard` is everyone's home: signup, sign-in and `/` land there.
- A new **Home** nav item for owners and crew.

**Job counts**
- Today (completed / remaining), Tomorrow, and This week (today plus the next 6 days).
- Cancelled visits never count, and all dates use the business's time zone.

**Revenue (owners only)**
- Every non-cancelled visit booked this month at its price, completed or not — not just invoiced-and-paid, as the spec calls out.
- A "completed so far" line underneath.

**Estimated profit (owners only)**
- Revenue minus expenses, labeled "no expenses tracked yet" until Expenses exists.

**Invoice totals**
- Outstanding and overdue totals stay hidden until Invoicing exists, rather than showing a misleading $0.

**Quick actions (owners)**
- Add customer, book a job, manage crew, needs attention.

**Today's jobs**
- Owners see the business's list, with a crew column when there's a crew.
- Crew members see their own jobs, with the usual crew actions and no money.

## Database change
- New migration: `ecoscape-ops/supabase/migrations/20260928000000_dashboard.sql`.
- It adds `dashboard_summary()`, which scopes by role:
  - owners get business-wide numbers, including money;
  - crew get counts of only their own assigned jobs, and the money fields are null.
- Hosted Supabase needs the migration applied. There are no new environment variables.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 30 unit tests.
- `npm run test:db`: 84 tests against local Supabase, run as real signed-in users. The dashboard tests check:
  - exact owner numbers against an independent calculation;
  - that each crew member's numbers include only their own jobs, with no money;
  - that other crew members and another business are never counted;
  - that removed crew, users without a business, and anonymous visitors get nothing;
  - that "today" follows the business time zone.

  I deliberately broke the crew filter and the owner-only money check, and the 3 leak tests failed as expected.
- `npm run test:e2e`: 81 Playwright runs across desktop and mobile. Dashboard coverage: new-business zeros and quick actions; numbers after booking, completing and cancelling; crew dashboards scoped with no money; a crew action updating counts; another business's crew; home routing. Older tests were updated for the new home page.
- `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` are clean.

author: profjsb
body:
## Summary
- **New talk page** `content/talk/pepperdine-hcai-2026/` (#127). It's a keynote at the Human-Centered AI Conference 2026, Pepperdine University (Malibu, Sat Sep 26, 2026, 10:30–11 AM per the official program). Topics are astronomy, industry, and ai-ml. No public recording exists yet.
- **Embedded slide viewer** (new, reusable for any talk). The deck shows inline on the talk page as rendered slide images, so **the PDF is never published** and there's no download button. The viewer supports click/tap zones, arrow keys, swipe, full screen, and a progress line. It preloads neighbouring slides, and right-click, drag, and long-press saving are suppressed on the slide. That deters casual copying; screenshots can't be prevented.
- `talks.py slides --slug <slug> --pdf <deck>` renders a deck into `content/talk/<slug>/slides/NNN.webp` (2400 px WebP; Ghostscript + cwebp). This deck comes to 28 slides, 4.4 MB total, loaded a few at a time.
- On the talk page, the viewer replaces the Slides button. On the list page, the Slides button jumps to `/talk/<slug>/#slides`, and arriving there hands the keyboard to the viewer. Talks with external `url_slides` are unchanged.
- `validate` counts embedded slides as a link and warns about any PDF inside a talk bundle, since this repo is public. `SKILL.md` documents the workflow.

This branch was force-pushed to drop an earlier commit that self-hosted the PDF, so the deck never enters `master`'s history.

## Verification
- `talks.py validate`: 127 pages, 127 ledger entries, 0 errors. `linkcheck`: the new talk's links pass; the 7 dead links are older rot also on `master`.
- The `slides` subcommand renders 28 slides at 2400×1350. It errors cleanly on a missing talk or PDF, and the PDF warning fires and clears as expected.
- The viewer was tested in a local Hugo build of the real talk templates, including a copy spliced into the live site's theme shell (Academic CSS/JS). Checked there: navigation by click, arrow keys, Home/End, and the bar buttons; synthetic swipes (left, right, vertical, and tiny moves); neighbour preloading; disabled states at the ends; right-click blocked; the full-screen layout; dark mode via the theme toggle; a 375 px phone layout; and the list-page Slides button (anchor offset under the navbar, focus handoff). Real full-screen entry couldn't be exercised because the test browser denies the Fullscreen API.
- Still to check on the deploy preview: that Hugo 0.60 renders the partial and publishes `slides/*.webp`.

body: WebKit rejects the redundant unique directions on key-only IndexedDB object-store cursors. Use ordinary forward and reverse directions; object-store primary keys are already unique. A browser regression covers empty, prefix, seek, reverse, and unbounded-prefix traversal.

body:
## Summary

This is the top of a three-layer stack. The admin console now sends the internal ID for every reader, member, and access ticket action (the layer below), so this layer removes the public ID fields those requests still took and the handlers' resolution of them. Each removed field's number and name are reserved.

Fixes #3112

## Changes

- `SuspendReaderRequest`, `UnsuspendReaderRequest`, `SetReaderBirthDateRequest`, `DeleteReaderRequest`: `public_id` removed and reserved; `reader_id` is required.
- `UpdateTenantMemberRoleRequest`, `RemoveTenantMemberRequest`: `user_public_id` removed and reserved; `user_id` is required.
- `RevokeAccessTicketRequest`: `public_id` removed and reserved; `access_ticket_id` is required. `GetAccessTicketIDByPublicIDForTenant` is gone.
- Tests that still named a reader by public ID through the admin API (including the public API's reader-moderation integration test) name it by ID. The tests of the fallback the layer below kept are removed.

Requests that keep a public ID, because a URL names the record:

- `GetReaderRequest.public_id`: `/readers/[reader_id]`.
- `ListAccessTicketsRequest.user_public_id` / `episode_public_id`: the `?user=` and `?episode=` filters of `/access-tickets`.
- `ListAuditLogsRequest.actor_user_public_id`: the `?actor=` filter of `/audit-logs`.

Moved out of #3112 into their own Issues:

- `IssueAccessTicketRequest.user_public_id` / `episode_public_id`: the ticket form has the operator type the reader's public ID, so it needs a way to choose the reader and the episode before it can send internal IDs. #3164, #3165, and #3166 cover it.
- `CreateAnnouncementRequest.target_user_public_ids`: announcements are tenant-wide notices, so the per-user target is removed rather than moved to an internal ID, by #3162 and #3163.

## How to Test

- `task gen` (no diff), `sqlc diff`, `task server:lint`, `task server:test`
- `pnpm preflight`

- [x] I used a Conventional Commits style PR title.
- [x] I tested my changes locally.
- [x] I updated docs if needed.

author: ctoth
body:
**Security: this fixes a real privilege escalation.** A non-wizard verb could gain wizard authority by catching the E_MAXREC raised when it called a wizard-owned verb (or `pass()`ed to one) at the activation-depth limit. After the catch it ran with the wizard verb's programmer and wizard flag. The conformance test shows it setting `.wizard = 1` on an object.

## Cause
`startVerbCall` and `executePass` (`vm/op_verb.go`) did several things before calling `checkFrameLimit()`:
- switched `vm.Context` to the callee (ThisObj, ThisValue, Verb, Programmer, IsWizard, ThreadMode)
- allocated the callee's locals
- took a frame from the pool

When the limit check then raised E_MAXREC, none of that was undone. A caller that caught the error kept running with the callee's context, and the locals slots and frame struct were leaked.

Toast's `call_verb2` (`execute.cc`) checks `push_activation()` right after the verb lookup and "does not change the vm in case of any error".

## Fix
Move the frame-limit check in both functions to just after the verb resolves and compiles, before any state changes. The other early exits (E_TYPE, E_INVIND, E_VERBNF, compile error, the pass() E_INVIND/E_VERBNF/E_INVARG paths) already returned before the mutation, so they were never affected.

## Evidence
Conformance: MongooseMoo/moo-conformance-tests#111 (`vm/max_recursion_caller_context.yaml`)
- Toast (managed WSL oracle, with capability admission): 3 passed
- Barn master: both new tests fail with `['maxrec', 0, 1, 1, 1, 1]` (expected `['maxrec', 1, 1, 0, 'denied', 0]`)
- Barn with this fix: 3 passed

Gates:
- gofmt clean; `go vet ./...`, `staticcheck ./...` and `go build ./...` pass.
- `go test ./... -count=1`: one failure, `builtins TestDivergenceRuntimeIntrospection` (`memory_usage()` returns E_QUOTA on Windows). It fails the same way on unchanged master, so this PR did not cause it.
- `go test -race ./vm ./engine`: ok.
- Full managed conformance suite on Barn (linux build, canonical `-m "admission or conformance"` form): 12642 passed, 420 skipped, exit 0.
- `TestRejectedVerbCallDoesNotLeakTaskActivationFrame` now also asserts that the caller's context is unchanged. It fails without the fix: `this 0 programmer 0 wizard false thread mode true`.

_Requested by **Dan** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_014fZXCJJ4gu2vWGDRf37rfw?thread=cmsg_014fZXCJJ4gu2vWGDRf37rfwRePJ9u9f3cNCcBDzYHC7Wg)_

Before: while a turn was running, the right panel just said "Waiting for response…", and then everything showed up at once. The panel was one long scroll: the whole conversation came first, then the answer, sources, raw tool-call JSON and response JSON. The turn's status was packed into one monospace line. Jev's routing only showed up in the raw JSON. On a phone, the question list got hidden under the panel.

After: while the Brain works, the panel shows what it's doing right now ("Looking up campus data · dinner menu · Sep 27"), a color bar of the steps so far, and the draft answer marked "not checked yet". The pending question in the list shows the current step too. The panel now opens with a summary strip: outcome, time, model, a Jev badge (green if Jev handled it, amber if it handed off to GPT) and a copyable request id. Under that are tabs: **Answer**, **Sources**, **Trace**, **Request** and **Raw**. The picked tab stays picked as you step between turns. Trace shows where the time went, what Jev picked, how sure it was and why it handed off, and each tool call with readable arguments and results. It also has model call counts, fallback and failed checks. On a phone, the list, composer and panel stack and the page scrolls.

The Brain already streams these steps when asked with `Accept: text/event-stream`, so the Brain doesn't change. Sources and tool calls still arrive with the final answer, because that's the only place the Brain sends them.

How: the chat proxy passes the stream request through. It forwards the Brain's `cache-control: no-transform` so Next's gzip doesn't hold events back. `lib/chat-stream.ts` reads the events onto the pending turn. A failure inside the stream is described the same way as a plain HTTP failure, using `lib/brain-failure.ts`, which is shared with the proxy. A stream that ends with no answer says so. The panel is split into `TurnInspector.tsx` (the header, tabs, Answer, Request and Raw) and `TraceView.tsx` (the timeline, Jev, tool calls and details).

Tested with typecheck, lint and `next build`. I also clicked through every tab in Chromium against a stand-in Brain that streams the real frame format, under `next start` with gzip on. That covered a normal answer, Jev handling a turn, Jev handing off to GPT, a failed result, a stream cut off halfway, and phone width. It has not been run against a real Brain yet.

author: agentydragon
body:
Removes `augur`, `augur-frontend`, `augur-evidence` and `budget-exporter` from `devinfra/ci/image_targets.json`, so `push-images` stops testing, building and pushing them to `git.allegedly.works/ducktape-ci/`. Their deployments are parked, yet every devel commit that changes one still costs a push job and mints a tag: the downstream `augur` `ImagePolicy` resolved `devel-20260927004506-97d7154` (#8075) on 2026-09-27.

## They are parked

- **augur API + frontend, budget-exporter**: deployed from `gaffer-private` into the `augur` namespace (the exporter CronJob "runs alongside augur", `tf/gitops/budget-ledger/main.tf`). `gaffer-private`'s augur manifests sit under `k8s/parked/augur/` (`finance/augur/frontend/BUILD.bazel`, `cluster/docs/agent_rbac.md`), and `cluster/docs/decisions.md` § Parked application manifests records the namespace as absent.
- **augur-evidence**: parked in #7206 and unwired from the Flux root in #7530; `finance/README.md` records the scraper's cluster pipeline as parked.

## Nothing active consumes them

- **Repo**: no reference to the four repositories (Forgejo or GHCR path), no `$imagepolicy` marker for them, no entry in `cluster/cdk8s/forgejo_image_automation.py`, nothing in `.github/`.
- **Live cluster** (read-only, 2026-09-27): namespace `augur` is NotFound. A scan of all 1673 Pods, Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, CronJobs, Jobs and ReplicaSets finds no container running one of these images; the same scan finds `ducktape-ci/airlock` in 14 objects. The only things still watching them are four `ImageRepository`/`ImagePolicy` pairs owned by the downstream `gaffer-private-image-automation` Kustomization.

## No companion edits

`plan_image_pushes.py` is the roster's only reader and computes the push matrix at run time, so nothing generated changes. `test_every_checked_in_image_declares_a_usable_target` checks an invariant over the roster, not a copy of it, and `cluster/docs/container-images.md` describes the mechanism without listing images.

## Deliberately left out

- **The `oci_image` targets and their tests stay.** None is `manual`, so the `//...` sweep keeps building and testing them; only publishing stops. Reviving a deployment re-adds its roster entry.
- **Deleting the augur, scraper or beancount-export code**: a separate owner decision. Augur is under active development.
- **Downstream image-automation cleanup**: the four `ImageRepository`/`ImagePolicy` pairs belong to `gaffer-private` and are removed there. Until then they keep scanning and hold their last tag; nothing breaks.
- **Already-published tags** stay in the Forgejo registry.

## Checks

- `bbr test //devinfra/ci:test_plan_image_pushes`: passed ([invocation](https://app.buildbuddy.io/invocation/afff74bd-921b-459f-9d89-9f9e48a3eb64)).
- `pre-commit run --files devinfra/ci/image_targets.json` under `nix shell .#precommit`: passed.
- The planner's strict `load_images` parses the roster: 52 images, down from 56.

Not yet observed: a post-merge `push-images` run. Its plan step should cover 52 images, none of them these four.
