author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an open chat becoming empty or staying on an old branch after another browser tab switches branches or rewinds the conversation.

## User Impact

Open chats follow the selected conversation history while retaining unsent drafts. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two ordering gaps affected the same flow. Branch switching and rewind evicted cached history using the notification that retires a live transcript, which could erase messages after replacement history had already loaded. These actions now use the existing cache-eviction reason; destructive reset and deletion retain their existing behavior.

Separately, a replacement event can arrive before the canonical session list admits its new physical session. Rejecting that early event is correct, but later row admission only rebound metadata and never refreshed history. The pane observation now requests history when that accepted binding changes. A captured event owns its own matching session refresh; if another listener has already admitted a newer session, the observation refreshes the newer one. Existing history loading retains displayed messages until the replacement is ready and coalesces overlapping requests.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the empty chat through two real browser tabs. The first candidate's live replay then exposed stale follower history in both branch directions and after rewind; that incomplete result was kept as a draft and repaired.
- Regressions cover cache invalidation before and after replacement history, delayed canonical admission for branch switch and rewind, and a newer session admitted during delivery of an older event. Each newly identified ordering gap was observed failing before its correction.
- The final correction passed 92 focused and sibling tests: six owning cases in 4.228 seconds wall time and 86 sibling cases in 11.593 seconds. Delayed branch/rewind cases took 293/104 ms; the reentrant newer-session case took 53 ms. Lint, formatting, and styles passed, and independent review found no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Final candidate `9c71b2d0ac0` incorporates main `3a68ec05f92`. Eight affected files passed 155 tests in 22.260 seconds wall, including the new immutable-array rendering and async-question owners. The complete selected changed check passed in 472.962 seconds, including six consumer type graphs, UI typing, dead exports, lint, formatting, and styles. Fresh whole-PR review was clean through P2. An earlier wrapper was interrupted with exit 143 and is not counted as passing; this integrated run completed normally.
- Exact-head full build passed in 455.623 seconds; strict UI performance check passed. The rebuilt isolated Gateway passed all 35 pre/post-update continuity groups, and the eight served startup assets matched the build.
- Real two-tab replay on that build passed: 140 → 145 messages, reverse 145 → 140 while the follower was scrolled into older history, rewind to the retained 39-message prefix, and restore to 140. The follower converged without a reload after each action; all three unsent Unicode drafts survived. Rewind restored the initiating prompt in the writer as expected. Before/after captures below show the actual browser state.
- A fresh live OpenAI follow-up completed in 31 seconds on the rebuilt Gateway, reading the two retained fixture files and verifying both calculations, Unicode content, and the prior browser editor change.
- Exact-head CI [36289851543](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36289851543) passed: 65 successful checks, 20 skipped. Changed test module timings in hosted UI shard 3/3: history observation 2.808 seconds and successor events 1.855 seconds (reporter module time, not process wall time). The test step took 242 seconds.

Before: the lower-right conversation became empty while its unsent draft remained.

![Before: another tab’s branch switch clears the open conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b6b5b6e-7a92-49a2-8a9a-5c93177d9d21)

Before the second correction: the writer selected the 140-message branch, but the follower remained on the 145-message branch.

![Before: follower remains on the previous branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6337aa3-041c-4b3e-a7bd-f4e551c8699e)

After: the follower reaches the selected 140-message branch without reloading, retaining all three drafts.

![After: follower displays the selected branch and retains drafts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a926386a-2bb8-40e5-b8df-c460a0197d79)

After rewind in the other tab: the follower shows the retained conversation prefix, with its draft unchanged.

![After: follower reflects rewind and retains its draft](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e424046-9471-4808-a5df-6055fab5eb0a)

body: Shared Audible titles currently appear once per owning account in Get books. This combines each Audible product into one row, shows every account tag, and counts unique books. Account filters and download status continue to work across all owners; different Audible editions remain separate. Downloads try the first owner, then each other known owner on failure, stopping after success. The job stays running through fallback and reports failure only after all attempts fail. Saved ownership is used for catalogue recovery and fallback discovery. Reader access grants require a fresh scan of the selected legacy account; expired ownership and unavailable accounts cannot authorize access from saved records. ### Before and after Browser captures of the original and updated application with identical sample data at a 360 × 1400 viewport. Six ownership rows become three unique books; Dad, Marge, and Veterans remain visible. These are sample titles and accounts, not live Audible data. | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | ### Verification - Server tests after the ownership fix: 486 passed, 5 ignored. - Web tests for the original UI change: 475 passed; the feedback fix changes only the server. - Server formatting and Clippy with warnings denied passed. - Web typecheck, lint, and production build passed. - Browser check: three unique rows; filtering to Marge shows her two books with all ownership tags intact. - Regression coverage includes explicit download errors, a successful process exit with no downloaded book, every owner failing, stopping at the first success, and excluding unrelated accounts. Ownership regression coverage exercises direct and approved reader requests against both original-owner and switched-owner exports, with expired ownership, unavailable accounts, and successful revalidation. The regression failed before the fix and passes afterward. Live Audible downloads and device testing were not performed.

## Summary

Update `actions/github-script` from v7 to v8 in the CI Test Gate workflow to fix the Node 24 runner incompatibility that caused the "Comment on PR" step to fail with `403 Resource not accessible by integration`.

## Problem

GitHub Actions runners now default to Node 24, but `github-script@v7` targets Node 20. When forced to run on Node 24, the step fails to authenticate the `createComment` API call. All other steps (checkout, setup-python, install, analyze) pass successfully.

## Changes

- `actions/github-script@v7` → `@v8`

This is a minimal one-line change that updates only the version pin. No other workflow logic changes.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes on this branch (all steps including Comment on PR)
- [ ] Comment appears on PR #88 once this workflow runs against it

Closes #71

author: shiwaku
body:
## 概要

D2(#37、設計 `docs/sumo-design.md` §13.6・§13.17)。JARTIC 車両感知器(断面交通量 typeB、5 分値)の位置を特定し、センサスと同じ形式の時間帯別観測値にする。D4(需要推定の補正と照合)の観測値になる。

## 変更

- **`network/jartic.py`**: 交差点制御情報(typeC)の定義と交差点座標の読み込みを `scripts/12` から共通化(12 の出力は変わらないことを確認)
- **`calib/detectors.py`**: 地点名称の進行方向・条丁目の住所の解釈、進行方向で道路を選ぶ処理
- **`cases/sapporo.grid_address_xy`**: 条・丁目の住所 → 街区の中心の座標
- **`scripts/42_jartic_detectors.py`**(`make detectors`): typeB(1.09 GB)を一度読んで平日の時間帯別平均交通量にし(キャッシュ)、位置を特定して `data/processed/detector_counts.json` を書き出す

## 進行方向の意味

地点名称の末尾 2 文字(「東西」「北南」など)の **2 文字目が進行方向**。交差点制御情報で区間と向きが確定する 114 地点で、札幌の格子の向き(約 11 度傾く)で東西南北に分けた進行方向と約 8 割が一致した(北北・南北 → 北、北南・南南 → 南、東東・西東 → 東、東西・西西 → 西)。

## 位置の特定

| 方法 | 地点 |
|---|---|
| 交差点制御情報: 交差点 X の流出かつ Y の流入(区間が確定) | 41 |
| 交差点制御情報: Y の流入 → Y に入る道路のうち進行方向の合うもの | 117 |
| 交差点制御情報: X の流出 → X から出る道路のうち進行方向の合うもの | 126 |
| 地点名称の条・丁目の住所 → 街区の中心から 120 m 以内で進行方向の合う最寄りの道路 | 309 |
| 特定できない(大半は区域外。「琴似 1-7」のような町名 + 条丁目は位置参照情報が無いので保留) | 966 |

→ 区域内の **564 Edge** に観測値。センサスの独立な観測点(区域内 71)の約 8 倍。

## 検査

- **センサスとの比較**: センサスと同じ Edge にある 209 地点で、朝 8 時の交通量の比(感知器 / センサス)は中央値 **0.94**(四分位 0.75〜1.16)。時期の違い(2026 年 6 月 / 2021 年秋)があっても水準はよく合う
- **方法による差は小さい**: 比の中央値は 住所 0.89・流入 0.92・区間確定 1.03・流出 0.98、±30% 以内はどれも 6 割前後。住所と交差点制御情報で決めた位置は中央値 228 m 離れるが、同じ道路の隣の区間に寄せただけで交通量としては同じものを見ている

テスト 57 件通過(進行方向・住所の解釈、進行方向による道路の選択、格子の向きの方位、街区の中心を追加)。

Refs #37

author: pierrevieira
body:
Screen transitions now follow each platform's guidelines. Before, Android relied on Navigation 3's defaults (a slow 700 ms cross-fade, and a predictive back that shrank the screen to 70%), and tab switches cross-faded on every platform.

**Android and desktop (Material motion)**
- Opening and closing screens uses the Material *shared axis* pattern: a 30 dp slide combined with a fade, over 300 ms.
- Predictive back follows the Android spec: the leaving screen shrinks to 90% and shifts toward the swipe; the screen underneath scales from 110% to 100%, with a fade-through at 35% of the gesture.
- Switching tabs is a quick 150 ms cross-fade. The navigation bar is now a shared element between tabs, so it stays still instead of fading along with the content.

**iOS**
- Opening and closing screens keeps Navigation 3's native-style slide (parallax, veil, interactive edge swipe), now through `defaultTransitionSpec()` explicitly.
- Switching tabs is instant, like a `UITabBarController`.
- Sheets and native alerts opened as navigation dialogs no longer darken the background twice. The outer Compose `Dialog` stacked its 60% scrim on top of the sheet's own scrim, or under `UIAlertController`'s dim. Sheets now use 18%, matching the dim Android already applies through `DialogWindowDimEffect`, and native alerts use none. Android is untouched.
- The date picker's zoom-in is skipped when Reduce Motion is on, leaving only the fade.

The transitions live in `ui/utils/.../transition/`: a `NavigationTransitions` interface, a Material implementation and a Cupertino one, chosen by platform. Both the root and the tab `NavDisplay` use them, so neither platform overrides the other.

Checked on an Android emulator (API 37: push, back, predictive back held mid-gesture and cancelled, tab switches) and on the iOS simulator (push, edge-swipe back, tab switches, the Theme sheet's dim).

Out of scope, tracked in #481: keeping the tab bar visible on detail screens, as Apple's HIG asks, needs per-tab navigation stacks.

author: prakharsingh-74
body: closes - #2079 ## Description This PR resolves database CPU saturation, disk IOPS spikes, and connection pool starvation caused by `DatabaseManager.getMetadata()`. Previously, when the 60-second table count cache (`TABLE_COUNT_CACHE_TTL`) expired, `getMetadata()` constructed a single `UNION ALL` SQL statement executing exact `COUNT(*)` queries across every user table in the `public` schema. In PostgreSQL, `COUNT(*)` forces a full MVCC sequential scan over table pages on disk, causing heavy IOPS and CPU contention on large production databases. This fix replaces exact multi-table `COUNT(*)` sequential scans with $O(1)$ catalog statistics queries against `pg_class.reltuples` and `pg_namespace`. --- ## Key Changes - **`backend/src/infra/database/database.manager.ts`**: - Replaced the batch `COUNT(*) UNION ALL` query with a parameterized catalog query against `pg_class.reltuples`. - Used `GREATEST(0, COALESCE(reltuples::bigint, 0))` to safely handle un-analyzed tables (where `reltuples` may be `-1`). - Removed unused `pg-format` dependency import. - **`backend/tests/unit/database-manager-metadata.test.ts`**: - Added unit test asserting that `DatabaseManager.getMetadata()` queries catalog estimates (`reltuples`) and avoids issuing `COUNT(*)` / `UNION ALL` queries. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes database CPU saturation, disk IOPS spikes, and connection pool starvation caused by `getMetadata()` running exact `COUNT(*)` queries against every table. Replaces the batch `COUNT(*) UNION ALL` scan with an O(1) catalog query against `pg_class.reltuples` (closes #2079). - Clamps estimates to 0 when tables report `reltuples = -1` before being analyzed. - Adds a unit test confirming `getMetadata()` uses catalog estimates and never issues `COUNT(*)` or `UNION ALL`. Written for commit ce3c1d33345dda61c89add984a49f129f0c295be. Summary will update on new commits. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Performance** * Table metadata now uses PostgreSQL’s estimated row counts instead of exact counts, reducing the work required to retrieve metadata. Estimates are rounded to whole numbers and never fall below zero.

This PR adds a build system for generating printable A4 PDFs of entrance hymns with music notation space.

## Summary
Introduces a hymn book builder that converts structured song data into professionally formatted PDFs with blank notation bands above each lyric line. Two output variants are generated: one with 5-line music staff and one with plain writing lines for tonic sol-fa notation.

- **hymnbook/songs.js**: New module containing hymn data for 5 entrance hymns with ChordPro-style chord annotations inline with lyrics

  - Outputs `entrance-hymns-staff.pdf` and `entrance-hymns-lined.pdf`

## Implementation Details
- Chord parsing extracts `[CHORD]` markers and associates them with following lyric text
- CSS uses CSS custom properties for flexible band height and rule positioning
- Staff variant includes 5 ruled lines spaced 2mm apart; lined variant uses single line
- Each song starts on a new page with section header and song number
- Print-optimized styling with exact color adjustment and proper page breaks
- Supports both system Playwright and fallback to `/opt/node22` installation

body:
## TLDR

Rebased copy of #42871 by @clonylu (commit cherry-picked, authorship preserved) so it applies after #43199 moved the tests to `tests/unit/`. Supersedes #42871

Problem this solves:

- Streaming `/v1/responses` on Claude drops signature-only thinking: no reasoning item
- Default shape for Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Bedrock adaptive thinking

How it solves it:

- Open the reasoning item on a signed or redacted thinking block without text
- Keep signed blocks with empty text through stream assembly

## User Flow

Before: the stream never opens a reasoning item, so the client has nothing to replay on the next turn

1. A client sends a streaming POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses with `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` to a Claude deployment whose thinking block comes back signed but empty
2. `response.output_item.added` fires for `message` only and `response.completed` output is `[message]`, while `reasoning_tokens` is non-zero
3. On the next turn there is no reasoning item to send back, so the model continues without its earlier reasoning

After: the stream opens a reasoning item with replayable `encrypted_content`

1. Same request
2. `response.output_item.added` fires for `reasoning` then `message`, and `response.completed` output is `[reasoning, message]` with `encrypted_content` set
3. The client replays the reasoning item and the model keeps its earlier reasoning

## Relevant issues

Fixes #42869

Supersedes #42871

author: bsikar
body:
Seventh consequence of #768. The arena half is closed at four of five shims and all four private container sniffs are adopted; the fabric has a sniff, a geometry probe and a scratch carve. What it did not have is the thing the issue is actually about: a way for a consumer to treat a *set* of backends as one format matrix.

`ra8_imgdec_t` binds exactly one backend, which is the right shape for a backend and the wrong shape for a consumer. #768 is not about any one decoder, it is about four decode paths each reaching a different subset of the formats, so whether an app can show a WebP depends on which path it happened to pick.

`ra8_imgdec_mux_t` holds up to `k_ra8_imgdec_mux_max` (4, one per backend named in the issue) bound handles in the order they were added, reports the union of what they open, and routes a request to the first member advertising both the container and the destination layout it asks for. Adding WebP to a consumer that had only stb then becomes one more `ra8_imgdec_mux_add` call rather than a fifth special case, which is the shape #637 needs.

## Three design calls

**1. A mux is deliberately NOT itself an `ra8_imgdec_t`.** It would be tidy to bind one as a backend and let `ra8_imgdec_get_caps` report the union, and it would be wrong. `ra8_imgdec_caps_t` is a flat pair of sets and can only describe a matrix where every format is available in every layout. That holds for one backend and does not hold for a set of them: a mux of a WebP backend writing RGBA and a GIF backend writing grey8 would union to `{WebP,GIF} x {RGBA,grey8}` and answer yes to WebP-into-grey8, which no member can do. So the mux publishes its own queries, each evaluated per member as a *pair*, and `ra8_imgdec_mux_formats` takes the destination layout as an argument for exactly that reason. A test asserts both cross pairs are refused while the two real pairs are accepted.

**2. Order is priority, and overlap between members is expected rather than refused.** A consumer preferring the first-party JPEG over stb's adds it first. One internal helper holds the routing walk, so `_supports`, `_route` and `_decode` cannot drift apart about which member serves a request.

**3. The container is settled once, in the mux, before any member is chosen,** because the choice depends on the answer. The member is then handed a request with the format already named, so a decode sniffs once however many backends are in the set. Everything past the routing decision stays the single-backend fabric's job and is not repeated here: `ra8_imgdec_decode` re-validates the request, gates it against the chosen backend's own record, checks the arena against that backend's scratch budget and clears `*out` on failure. A test routes to a member publishing a scratch budget with no arena supplied and asserts the fabric refuses it (`k_ra8_err_invalid_state`) without dispatching.

An empty mux answers `k_ra8_err_not_initialized` rather than a quiet "nothing supported": a consumer that forgot to add its backends is asking a question the set cannot answer, which is a different thing from a set that genuinely does not open a format. A member's capability record is fetched and checked at `_add` time, not at the first decode, so an unbound handle or an unusable record is rejected while the caller is still assembling the set.

## Files

- **new** `libs/ra8_imgdec/inc/ra8_imgdec_mux.h` (289): the limits enum, `ra8_imgdec_mux_t`, and `_init` / `_add` / `_formats` / `_supports` / `_route` / `_decode`.
- **new** `libs/ra8_imgdec/src/ra8_imgdec_mux.c` (310): `internal_one_defined_bit`, `internal_usable`, `internal_caps_cover`, `internal_find`, `internal_pair_ok`, `internal_route_req_ok`, `internal_resolve`, `internal_clear_image`, all `RA8_INTERNAL static`, then the six entry points.
- **new** `tests/misc/src/test_ra8_imgdec_mux.c` (461, 10 cases): empty-mux refusals, add guards, the bounded set, the per-pair union, priority order, sniff-then-route with a decode-call counter proving the wrong member never ran, three unroutable shapes that reach no backend, query and decode argument guards, and the member gate still applying.

No backend is bound and no consumer is converted here.

## Wiring and verification

No cmake edit needed, each site checked: `tests/cmake/library_sources.cmake:34` globs `libs/ra8_imgdec/src/*.c` into `ra8_core_hal`, `tests/cmake/core_hal.cmake:132` carries `libs/ra8_imgdec/inc` on the PUBLIC include list, and `tests/misc/src` is auto-globbed. No world-tag scope edit: `libs/ra8_imgdec/` is already an unscoped root.

Compiled all four `libs/ra8_imgdec` TUs plus the test clean under `-std=c23 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -DRA8_OFF_TARGET=1 -DUNIT_TEST=1`, linked against the real fabric, sniff and arena, and ran it: **10/10 pass**. Gates run on the three touched files: `check_final_newline`, `check_comment_format`, `check_file_size`, `check_c23_patterns` all pass. No CI triggered, no CI polled.

author: atulpandey02
body:
## Summary

Test-only fix for a race in `tests/unit/test_pg_destination.py::test_capacity_exhaustion_fails_fast`, which failed twice consecutively in CI on PR #38. Production code is unchanged, and the `< 0.5 s` fail-fast requirement is unchanged.

### Reproduction

- **CI:** two consecutive failures, both `5.00 s` against the `0.5 s` bound. 5 s is the test's own `dns_timeout_s`, so the "fail fast" probe was **admitted** and waited out the DNS deadline.
- **Instrumented replica** using the module's own `_saturate`/`_blocking_resolver`: 7 slow probes in 300 runs. The recorded pool state was `2 live, 1 queued` after `_saturate`'s full 4 s wait, or a worker that was alive but not yet busy.
- A bounded local rerun of the unmodified test (40 iterations, 5-core contention, per-iteration timeout) did **not** reproduce it. The race is load-dependent, so the CI failures are the primary evidence.

### Race

`_saturate` started all callers at once and polled `live_worker_count()` / `qsize()`. A caller could find the bounded queue momentarily full before a live worker's first `get()`. It was then correctly rejected (production fail-fast behavior), leaving the pool one short of saturation for good. The poll could also see "2 live, 2 queued" while one worker had not yet dequeued. The test asserted only `<=` capacity, so the unsaturated pool went unnoticed and the probe fit into the queue.

### Fix

- **`_ResolverGate`:** the blocking resolver signals through a `Condition` each time a worker **enters** it, which proves the worker is occupied rather than merely alive.
- **Staged, event-driven saturation:** exactly `max_workers` callers start, and the test waits until every worker is occupied. At that point no `put_nowait` can overflow. Then exactly `max_queue` callers start, and the test waits on the queue's own `not_empty` condition until it is full. There are no sleeps; each wait is bounded and asserted.
- **Saturation asserted as equality** before the probe. The probe is asserted to have been rejected at admission (no extra worker entry; queue still exactly full).
- **Guaranteed cleanup** (`finally`): release the gate, join every caller, and wait on `all_tasks_done` until nothing is queued or in flight.
- `test_capacity_recovers_after_blocked_lookups_release` uses the same deterministic saturation and cleanup.

### Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Forced worker-lag interleaving (both tests) | 20 × 2 passed |
| Isolated runs under 5-core contention (bounded, per-iteration timeout) | 200 / 200 passed |
| Same replica harness, new helpers, full 10-core contention | 0 slow probes, 0 sync errors in 300 (was 7 / 300) |
| Full module | 4 × 57 passed |
| Unit suite (`-m "not integration"`) | 1,013 passed, 34 opt-in skips |
| Ruff format / check, mypy | clean |

Before: the trailer, the OP/ED jukebox and the tournament player only played after you pressed play, and kept playing after you scrolled past them.

After: each one starts by itself once at least half of it is on screen and pauses when you scroll away or switch tabs. If more than one is on screen, only the most visible one plays. It tries with sound first and falls back to muted when the browser blocks unmuted autoplay (the player's own controls unmute it). If you pause one yourself, it stays paused until it has fully left the screen; a video that played to the end isn't restarted.

How: a small `frontend/src/lib/autoplayOnView.js` helper built on `IntersectionObserver`. `<video>` players use `play()`/`pause()`. The YouTube trailer gets `enablejsapi=1` and is driven over `postMessage` (the IFrame API protocol, no extra script), with `autoplay` allowed on the iframe. Unit tests in `frontend/test/autoplayOnView.test.js`.

author: bsikar
body:
A beat comes back carrying NextBeatBy, which HolderLiveness documents as
"the only number a holder can act on: report before it or start reading as
overdue to anyone watching". KeepAlive owns the only wait that decides
whether it is met and never read it: the loop slept liveness.Interval and
nothing else.

Interval alone is not the same answer. The server measures silence from the
beat it recorded, so the stamp is already partly spent when the reply lands
and a full interval posts every beat one round trip late. That survives the
three-interval grace on its own; a blip does not. A refused beat kept the
interval and waited blind, unable to tell a stamp two seconds out from one
two minutes out, and the first beat of a loop starts from a one minute
default the server never said, so a holder on a two-second cadence whose
first beat blips sits out thirty beats before trying again.

Overdue never ends a lease, so nothing here loses a board. It loses the
truth about one: a healthy holder reporting late reads exactly like a
crashed one to the operator deciding whether a quiet board needs recovering.

nextBeatWait shortens the cadence to the time left before the due stamp,
floored at minHeartbeatInterval so a passed stamp cannot spin the loop
against the server, and left alone when the server named no stamp.
dueStamp carries the last due time across a refused beat so a blip waits
against what this holder was actually given.

Verified: gofmt, go build ./..., go vet ./internal/..., and the full
go test ./internal/... all clean. The Postgres integration tests need a
live database and were not run here.

author: jackspirou
body:
Starport accepted shared KV settings with replica-local SQL and file bytes. KV records and notifications lacked deployment isolation, and several connection and Badger settings had no effect.

Validate complete storage recipes and apply their settings through the owning adapters:

- Require PostgreSQL and shared object storage with durable Valkey. Reject unqualified cluster mode and insecure remote connections. Validate TLS identity, credentials, database selection, deadlines, and connection bounds.
- Scope durable KV keys and notification channels to the deployment identity. Restrict fresh initialization to an empty dedicated database and SQL schema.
- Apply Badger compression and collection settings at open and restore. Default persistent stores to synchronous writes. Keep development storage in memory.
- Supply separate local and candidate fleet Compose recipes with explicit storage roots. Test KV records, SQL audit records, file bytes, and catalog access through recreation and cold restore.
- Accept matching catalog candidates through the durable acceptance contract. Pin the published Starmap startup repair from agentstation/starmap#186. Remove the unused transaction interface. Its implementation did not provide the advertised atomic contract. Retain the tested atomic mutation operations.

The fleet recipe gives each replica a private local token volume through a separate Compose project. Shared application state remains external. A fixed container name prevents replicas within one project from sharing the private volume.

This change requires fresh shared storage. It does not migrate existing unprefixed records. CSP13 owns populated migration and controlled recovery. CSP15 owns complete fleet failure qualification. The candidate fleet recipe remains unsuitable for production upgrades until those gates pass. Merge after Starmap #186.

Validation on Go 1.27.1: all 15 CSP12 storage subcases and all 17 CSP12.1 cache subcases pass against the published Starmap module. Eight selected packages pass 1,225 named race results with real Valkey, PostgreSQL, and container fixtures. The initial container probe started before the image build completed. The full configuration package rerun passes all 345 results. The original failed invocation remains in the plan evidence.

The final architecture verifier passes all 12 conditions, including the full Go suite. Lint reports zero issues. Required independent review is clean. Authorization worker lifecycle tests use a catalog fixture and retain their original startup, catchup, and shutdown deadlines. Separate integration tests retain full embedded catalog startup, publication, recreation, and restore coverage.

author: tingyu123644
body:
When a caller explicitly asks `glob`/`grep` for files under a root whose **ancestor** matches an ignore pattern (e.g. a `build` or `node_modules` parent), the sandbox's `should_ignore_path(file_path)` check on the full absolute path hides every result — the caller asked for that directory, so its contents should be returned.

This mirrors the shell-side fix for #5666: the ignore check now applies only to the path **below** the requested root (`file_path[len(root_path):]`), while the root itself is always returned. Covers the five sandbox backends (aio_sandbox, boxlite, e2b_sandbox, opensandbox, tenki).

Verified: `python -m py_compile` on all touched modules; behavior for `root_path` (root match / below-root match / below-root ignore / unrelated ignore) checked against the `should_ignore_path` semantics.

author: anoth3rhellsing
body:
> **Fusionar después del #4.** La rama sale de la del #4 para tener el CI. Cuando el #4 esté en `main`, el diff mostrará solo este commit.
> Sustituye al #5, cerrado por decisión del equipo.

## Qué cambia y por qué
El equipo mantiene la presencia automática del PR #1:
- `online` al conectar;
- `offline` al desconectar;
- ausente por inactividad;
- "No molestar" en llamada.

Con una excepción: **quien elige "Desconectado" no cambia por ninguna actividad**. Pasa a ser un modo invisible.

| Pieza | Cambio |
|---|---|
| Base de datos | `users.invisible` (boolean, `false` por defecto). Migración 0010 **generada**: solo añade la columna. |
| `PATCH /users/me` manual | Elegir `offline` activa el modo invisible; cualquier otro estado lo desactiva. |
| `PATCH /users/me` con `auto: true` | Solo admite `status` `online`, `away` o `dnd`. En modo invisible se ignora y devuelve el estado real. Nunca activa ni desactiva ese modo. |
| WebSocket | Conectar no pasa a `online` a un usuario invisible. `presence:update`, que no escuchaba ningún cliente, se sustituye por `user:status`, que ya refresca las listas de miembros. Así los demás ven los cambios de conexión en vivo. |
| Login | No pasa a `online` a un usuario invisible. |
| Privacidad | `invisible` solo aparece en respuestas sobre uno mismo (login, `/auth/me`, `PATCH /users/me`). `/users/:id` no lo expone. |
| Cliente | La detección se desactiva en modo invisible y marca sus cambios con `auto: true`. Si otra pestaña tiene datos viejos, el servidor la frena igualmente. |
| Contrato | `invisible` en `User` y `auto` en `ProfileUpdate`. Código regenerado. |

## Evidencia (real, desde una copia limpia)
| Comprobación | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` | ok |
| `pnpm run typecheck` | ok |
| Builds de la API y del frontend | ok |
| `drizzle-kit generate` (segunda vez) | No schema changes |
| Codegen repetido | sin diferencias |
| `pnpm run test:regression` (no root) | 8/8, 376 comprobaciones (antes 361) |

**Prueba nueva** (`claims-realtime-isolated.mjs`): cuenta nueva no administradora, un observador distinto y `assert.notEqual` con el dueño y con el observador. La cuenta elige "Desconectado" y se comprueba que:
- conectar el WebSocket la deja en `offline`;
- `auto` con `away`, `dnd` u `online` se ignora;
- `auto` acompañado de otro campo da 400;
- el observador la ve `offline` y sin el campo `invisible`;
- volver a iniciar sesión la deja en `offline`;
- al elegir "Conectado", la presencia automática vuelve a funcionar.

**Mutaciones** (cada una hace fallar la prueba):
| Protección quitada | Falla con |
|---|---|
| Guardia al conectar | `connecting a WebSocket must not reveal an invisible user as online` |
| Guardia en `auto` | `'away' !== 'offline'` |
| Guardia en login | `logging in must not reveal an invisible user` |
| `/users/:id` expone `invisible` | `the invisible flag is never exposed to other users` |

## Honestidad
- **Sin verificar:** la interfaz en un navegador real, y el comportamiento con varias pestañas abiertas; eso último lo protege el servidor.
- **Se mantienen, por decisión del equipo, los otros comportamientos del PR #1:**
  - "Ausente" manual vuelve a "Conectado" al mover el ratón;
  - puede quedarse en "No molestar" tras colgar;
  - un F5 pasa a `online` a quien estaba en "No molestar" manual.

  El PR B del plan los resuelve si se quiere.

## Encontrado de paso (no tocado)
`ProfileUpdate` en el contrato limita `displayName` a 50 y `bio` a 200 caracteres, pero el servidor (PR #4) acepta 64 y 500. Hay que alinearlos en un PR aparte.

## Para que corra
Fusionar el #4 y después este PR, y llevar `main` a Replit. Al publicar se aplican las migraciones 0009 (categorías) y 0010 (`invisible`), las dos solo aditivas. Todos empiezan visibles: quien quiera ser invisible vuelve a elegir "Desconectado".

author: smarter-poker
body:
The authenticated pulse RPC failed when resolving `cron.job`, whose schema is deliberately unavailable to browser roles. Give its two existing operational counts a fixed, argument-free SQL aggregate boundary while keeping the pulse itself SECURITY INVOKER and preserving all product queries, outputs, caller RLS and permissions. The helper returns only two numbers; anonymous callers still cannot execute it or access cron.

The existing source guard mistook a single aggregate row declared with RETURNS TABLE for a roster. A separate authenticated-aggregate review pins its exact declaration/body and requires PUBLIC/anonymous denial; writer, anonymous-reader and clone rules remain enforced. The existing live telemetry review receives only a guarded metadata row, with no privilege changes. That name-based live table does not itself enforce future-definition hashes.

Installed once: pulse migration `20260927041025` (SHA256 `3cdf31dfd25f61cac9be7ae36f23be8308ef748df0bc4b72f55624d89c07b48e`) and metadata `20260927042050` (SHA256 `0d4664a759efd140219c43114420b1607c4fb26adfd000bddea797b919f40894`). Both source files record the installed bytes; never replay them. The existing outer RPC OID/ACL/settings remain unchanged. A read-only authenticated database-role invocation returned the complete object with 13 active jobs and 107 failures at 04:10 UTC. No maintained UI caller was found; this is RPC proof.

Validation includes actual PG17 cron ACL/RLS, three distinct users with unchanged non-cron payloads, anonymous and raw cron refusal, cross-owner/inactive/orphan/old-run count cases, empty counts, rollback/replay, metadata drift/conflict/duplicate behavior and a NOSUPERUSER BYPASSRLS owner. Existing discovery privacy, concurrent snapshot and refresh tests still run through their required native CI route. Final local and protected results are recorded separately.

_Requested by **Ritish** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01NBUJaACTtDHEA4ZJisjCTc?thread=cmsg_01NBUJaACTtDHEA4ZJisjCTcFiyGJFs6oWbScQs7n3pWoN)_

Before: sharing an AniNest link on WhatsApp, Discord, X or LinkedIn showed the title and description with an empty image.

After: the preview shows a 1200x630 AniNest card (logo, tagline, feature chips).

`index.html` pointed `og:image` / `twitter:image` at `/og-image.png`, but that file was never committed. Render's SPA catch-all rewrite (`/*` → `/index.html`) answered the request with HTML, so crawlers got a page where they expected an image.

How: adds `frontend/public/og-image.jpg` (JPEG, ~100 KB, under WhatsApp's ~300 KB cutoff), points both tags at it, adds `og:image:type`, `og:image:secure_url` and an accurate alt. The new filename also avoids crawler caches that stored the old HTML response. `frontend/test/linkPreview.test.js` checks that the referenced file exists and matches the declared type, width and height (it fails on master).

Note: apps cache previews per URL. After deploy, old shares may keep the blank image for a while; re-scrape with the [Facebook Sharing Debugger](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/debug/) (also refreshes WhatsApp) if needed.

## Implementato

- Gestita la forma corrente della sorgente `brefis.ch`: quando `addressLocality` contiene solo il codice cantonale `ZH`, il parser cerca una città soltanto dentro un contesto esplicito di luogo di lavoro, la accetta solo se corroborata dallo stesso cantone e non confonde l’HQ con l’Einsatzort.
- Conservata l’evidenza cantonale source-backed quando la descrizione non pubblica una città; non viene usato l’HQ del datore come sostituzione.
- Aggiunti test di regressione per il recupero di `Zürich`, la precedenza dell’Einsatzort, il fallback cantonale e il rifiuto senza segnale cantonale (`23/23` test mirati verdi).
- Probe live sulla pagina reale: `15` annunci estratti, `15` job pubblicati, tutti in `ZH`; `12` con località `Zürich` e `3` con evidenza cantonale `ZH`.

- Refs #9942

author: studiocactus
body:
## O que muda (0.1.16)

Correção dos três sintomas relatados na IA das Automações, sem mexer em nenhuma função existente:

1. **Endereço do provedor sem caminho duplicado** — `chat_url` em `src-tauri/src/ai.rs` monta o caminho conforme o provedor (`/api/chat` no Ollama, `/v1/chat/completions` na API compatível, `/v1/messages` no Anthropic), reaproveita um endereço que já traz caminho e converte um endereço de outro formato. `https://ollama.com/api/chat` com a API compatível selecionada vira `https://ollama.com/v1/chat/completions` em vez de `.../api/chat/chat/completions` (404).
2. **Erro diz qual é a ação** — 404 aponta o endereço exato usado na chamada, 401/403 a chave, 429 limite/quota, 5xx nova tentativa.
3. **Análise não vai para o chat** — quando o modelo devolve a leitura da mensagem (padrão que publicava `The user sent ...` em inglês), a ação falha com erro em português no Histórico e nada é publicado; o pedido ganhou `replyFormat` e as regras reforçam frase final em português. Conteúdo vazio por raciocínio ganhou aviso próprio.
4. **Mais espaço para o raciocínio** — orçamento de tokens 110/250/450 → 500/1000/1600; o texto publicado continua cortado em 120/300/450 caracteres.
5. **Gatilho Mensagem contém com lista por vírgula** — `comprei, comprar, gastei` dispara com uma das partes (antes a lista inteira precisava aparecer, e por isso a prévia passava mas a live não disparava); a prévia usa a primeira opção e o editor ganhou a dica.
6. **Marca `BotLive.` no topo esquerdo**.

Docs: capítulos 03, 04 e 08 do manual, `docs/VARIAVEIS.md`, entrada em `docs/VALIDACAO.md` e notas `updates/0.1.16.md`.

## Validação executada

- `node .tools/run.cjs cargo test --locked --lib --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml` → 77 aprovados (3 novos).
- `npm run check` → aprovado; `npm run test` → 24 aprovados.
- `npx playwright test` → 14 aprovados (asserções novas da marca e da dica de vírgula).
- `npm run test:updates` → 8 aprovados; `npm run build` → aprovado; `npm run update:check` → aprovado.
- Sonda HTTP real sem chave: `/api/chat/chat/completions` → 404 (caminho antigo) e `/v1/chat/completions` → 401 (caminho corrigido existe e pede chave).

## Limitações

- Sem chave de API nesta validação não houve geração real de um modelo pago: o caminho foi comprovado por sonda e por teste unitário, o que não equivale à homologação de uma resposta do provedor.
- Modelo com raciocínio muito extenso ainda pode estourar o orçamento e vira erro claro, sem resposta publicada; resposta que já vem como análise é descartada, sem nova tentativa automática.
- Conversão de endereço cobre os formatos conhecidos; caminho desconhecido é apenas completado com o sufixo do provedor e o 404 mostra o endereço final.
- A latência continua vindo do provedor, do modelo e da rede.

body:
KULLANICI ARTIK ŞUNU GÖRÜYOR: platform yöneticisi paneli için bir değişiklik yok (frontend bu ucu hiç çağırmıyor) — ancak backend artık `GET /api/system-logs` isteğinde ham `meta` (hata stack, userId, olası PII) döndürmüyor ve her erişim "kim, ne zaman, hangi filtreyle baktı" izi bırakıyor; ileride bu uca frontend bağlanırsa güvenlik açığı taşımadan bağlanacak.

## Özet
- **Kanıt:** `src/controllers/systemLogController.ts:20-34` (`listSystemLogs`) `select` yok + `auditPlatformAction` yok iken komşu uç `src/controllers/platformController.ts:180-206` (`getPlatformLogs`) ikisini de yapıyordu.
- `listSystemLogs` artık `getPlatformLogs` ile aynı korumaya sahip:
  - explicit `select` (`id, level, category, message, createdAt`) — `SystemLog.meta` (hata stack + userId/tenantId, PII taşıyabilir) response'a hiç girmiyor.
  - `auditPlatformAction('VIEW_SYSTEM_LOGS', req, { count, level, category })` — Y-02 (KVKK Md.12) deseniyle denetim izi.
  - `total` artık gerçek `count()` (önceden yanlışlıkla her zaman `logs.length`'e eşitti, limit'i yansıtmıyordu) — komşu uçla tutarlı.
- Rol/auth: uç zaten `requirePlatformAdmin` ile korunuyor (`systemLogRoutes.ts:9`) — `/api/platform/logs` ile aynı middleware, `auditPlatformAction` platform-admin sabit aktörüyle çalışıyor, ek değişiklik gerekmedi.
- **Frontend etkisi:** `/api/system-logs` frontend tarafından hiç çağrılmıyor (grep: `frontend/src` boş) — panel yalnızca `/api/platform/logs`'u kullanıyor (`frontend/src/lib/api/platform.ts:107`, `frontend/src/app/platform/dashboard/page.tsx`). Bu nedenle `meta`'nın kaldırılması kırıcı değil.

## Test planı
- [x] `tests/security.test.ts` (KRİTİK-2 komşusu, yeni `describe('AJ-02: ...')`):
  - `response içinde meta alanı hiç YOK` — meta içeren örnek log eklenip response'da hem alan hem ham içerik (sızıntı) olmadığı doğrulanıyor.
  - `VIEW_SYSTEM_LOGS denetim izi bırakır` — iz kaydı oluşuyor, PII içermiyor.
  - `NEGATİF: tenant ADMIN JWT ile → 403 ve VIEW_SYSTEM_LOGS izi yazılmaz`.
  - Mevcut `KRİTİK-2` testleri (401/403/200 + auth guard) değişmeden korunuyor.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — temiz
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json` — temiz
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 hata (3 ilgisiz mevcut uyarı, bu PR'dan önce de vardı)
- [ ] Entegrasyon testleri lokalde çalıştırılamadı — `DATABASE_URL`/`TEST_DATABASE_URL` yok, guard (`assertTestDatabase.ts`) devreye girip durdu (beklenen davranış). Asıl kanıt: backend CI (bu main-hedefli PR'da tetiklenecek).

## Kapsam dışı
- Migration/şema değişikliği yok, seed çalıştırılmadı.
- `server.ts` rate-limit/trust-proxy bölgesine dokunulmadı.
- Auth/KVKK/matching dosyalarına dokunulmadı (yalnız `systemLogController.ts` + testi).

author: panyam
body:
## What changes

The thambura's bar remembers that it was open again. Open it and reload, and it stays open; copy a link with the bar open, and it opens for whoever you send it to. Both had broken on master with #127/#129. The drawer now reads the bar's bit from the link the page was *opened* with, which `PageLink` keeps unchanged, instead of from the thambura's latest write. Closes #130.

## Prerequisite knowledge

- `CLAUDE.md`, the `pageLink.ts` and `thamburaDrawer.ts` notes: the page link is one part per instrument, and whether the bar is open is the drawer's business, carried as bit 2 of the thambura's part (#88).
- #130: the probe output that shows the bit being overwritten.

## Reviewer's guide

Think of a note left on a hotel room door saying "curtains open, please". Housekeeping comes in first and, as it always does, puts a fresh card on the door that says nothing about curtains, since curtains aren't its job. The guest arrives, reads the card now on the door, sees no request, and leaves the curtains shut. The fix is for the guest to read the note that was on the door when the room was booked, not whatever card is there now. Here the room is the page, the note is the link the page was opened with, housekeeping is the thambura presenter (since #127 it's made before its island and writes its part of the link straight away, with the bar's bit clear, because the bar isn't its business), and the guest is the drawer, which mounts afterwards.

Read in this order:
1. [web/src/player/pageLink.ts](https://github.com/panyam/thambura/pull/133/files#diff-c7574b51f1429c7ab945a51d37ee2aeef109773b6513773a4c169898b245de08): keeps the note from booking. `opened(id)` returns the part as the page was opened, which later writes don't change. `LinkPart.read`'s comment now says what it always did, the latest part.
2. [web/src/player/pageLink.test.ts](https://github.com/panyam/thambura/pull/133/files#diff-f00117a9c250febdb935ccd5097ab115860bad83b636f2dda4a2a25e3a3c381f): `opened` survives a write, and a scenario test of #130's exact order (the page is opened with the bit set, the presenter writes it clear, and the drawer still sees it set).
3. [web/src/player/thamburaIsland.tsx](https://github.com/panyam/thambura/pull/133/files#diff-6574d353adfd227c46dcd3f245d4ef3647f8b6be4eb2506f87a54c386a0e0dd4): the one-line change where the drawer reads `link.opened(presenter.id)`.

Skim: [CLAUDE.md](https://github.com/panyam/thambura/pull/133/files#diff-6ebdb617a8104a7756d0cf36578ab01103dc9f07e4dc6feb751296b9c402faf7).

## Decision log

- **A new `opened(id)` rather than reordering who writes first.** Building the drawer before the presenter would put a layout concern (the drawer) into the page context, which #88 split apart. Stopping the presenter writing on construction would change its contract (the address bar shows the setup from the start) to fix a layout bug, and would depend on mount order staying as it is. The opened link is the fact the drawer actually needs.
- **`read()` keeps returning the latest part.** Every other reader wants the current setup, and the presenter reads its part only in its constructor, before anything writes, so it sees the opened part either way.

## Tests

- `make test` passes (405 tests).
- Red before green: both new `pageLink` tests failed on master (`opened` didn't exist, and the scenario test read the overwritten bit).
- Assertions: 6 added, none removed.

## Before / after

The same browser script on master (:8031) and the branch (:8032), back to back:

| Step | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh page: bar open | no | no |
| After opening it: open, link bit | yes, set | yes, set |
| **After a reload: open, link bit** | **no, clear** | **yes, set** |
| Copied link's bit | set | set |
| **Second listener opens the copied link: bar open** | **no** | **yes** |
| After Hide: open, link bit | no, clear | no, clear |
| Hidden, then reload | closed | closed |
| `/labs/side-by-side`: docked, link bit set | yes | yes |
| `/embed/demo`: mounted, host URL untouched | yes | yes |
| Page errors | none | none |

On master the copied link does carry the bit. The second listener's bar still opens closed, because the same overwrite happens on their page.

## Risk / blast radius

- Affects: the drawer's starting state on `/`. Docked thamburas (labs, embed) don't use the drawer.
- Be paranoid about: a page opened with a link whose thambura part is unreadable. `decodePage` skips it, so `opened` is null and the drawer falls back to its saved state, as it did before #127.
- Related: #127 and #129 (where it broke), #88 (the drawer), #100 (instance ids in links).

author: ibnutoriq
body:
Before 0.2.0 is published: `renderMathText` is meant for visitor text (comments), and `\rule{5000em}{5000em}` rendered a box that covers the page. It now passes KaTeX `maxSize` (default 10em, option `maxSize`). Math blocks written in the editor are unchanged.

Found by probing the comment renderer. Recursive macros (`\def\a{\a\a}\a`) are already stopped by KaTeX's `maxExpand` (2 ms). A 5000-character formula renders in about 85 ms.

Tests 52/52 (2 new), typecheck and build OK.

## Summary

Closes #111 · Wave 9 Issue #106 · Category: Data Integrity · Priority: P1

The `append_custody_entry` call already exists inside `finalize_transfer`, `complete_adoption`, `waive_waiting_period`, and `batch_transfer` in the `pet-transfer-adoption` contract. However, **no test exercised `get_custody_chain` after any of these paths**, leaving the entire provenance logging trail completely unverified. This PR closes that gap with comprehensive unit and integration tests.

---

## What was missing

| Function | `append_custody_entry` present? | Test verifying `get_custody_chain`? |
|---|---|---|
| `finalize_transfer` | ✅ line 1191 | ❌ none |
| `complete_adoption` | ✅ line 960 | ❌ none |
| `waive_waiting_period` | ✅ line 1041 | ❌ none |
| `batch_transfer` | ✅ line 1503 | ❌ none |

---

## Changes

### `stellar-contracts/contracts/pet-transfer-adoption/src/test.rs`

Six new unit tests:

| Test | What it verifies |
|------|-----------------|
| `finalize_transfer_appends_direct_custody_entry` | Correct `from`/`to`/`TransferType::Direct` after `finalize_transfer` |
| `finalize_transfer_custody_entry_records_correct_timestamp` | Entry timestamp equals ledger time at finalization |
| `complete_adoption_appends_adoption_custody_entry` | Correct addresses + `TransferType::Adoption` after `complete_adoption` |
| `waive_waiting_period_appends_adoption_custody_entry` | Waived adoption also logged with `TransferType::Adoption` |
| `multiple_transfers_produce_sequential_custody_chain` | Two sequential finalizations → two chronologically ordered entries with correct from/to chain |
| `custody_chain_empty_before_any_transfer` | `get_custody_chain` returns empty vec before any finalization (append-only invariant) |

### `stellar-contracts/contracts/pet-transfer-adoption/tests/integration_adoption.rs`

Two new end-to-end integration tests (in addition to the existing ownership test):

| Test | What it verifies |
|------|-----------------|
| `adoption_flow_records_custody_chain_entry` | Full adoption flow → exactly one `CustodyEntry` with `TransferType::Adoption` |
| `finalize_transfer_records_custody_chain_entry` | Full escrow+finalize flow → exactly one `CustodyEntry` with `TransferType::Direct` |

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Finalizing a transfer records a custody chain entry (`finalize_transfer_appends_direct_custody_entry`)
- [x] Provenance history reflects the adoption transfer (`complete_adoption_appends_adoption_custody_entry`, `adoption_flow_records_custody_chain_entry`)
- [x] Waived adoptions also appear in the custody trail (`waive_waiting_period_appends_adoption_custody_entry`)
- [x] Multiple sequential transfers produce a consistent, chronologically ordered chain (`multiple_transfers_produce_sequential_custody_chain`)

---

## Testing

CI runs `cargo test` across the full `stellar-contracts` suite and the `pet-transfer-adoption` integration tests. No production logic was changed; all existing tests remain unaffected.

author: davekim917
body:
The Codex round cap (`REVIEW_ROUND_CAP`, default 3) was meant as a point where the agent steps back and judges whether review rounds are hardening the PR or chasing their own fixes. The skill and the script's cap message instead told agents to stop and "escalate to the operator", so PRs across the fleet parked at round 3 waiting for Dave to read them and make calls an agent can make.

This rewrites the cap as an agent checkpoint:

- **Assess:** classify the rounds by file and class, optionally with a fresh-context subagent's opinion.
- **Converging:** fix the open findings, then a fresh-context substitute review of the new head, posted with `receipt`; merge on approve. That path already exists and the gate already honours it.
- **Churning:** rebuild instead of patching: fix the shared seam once, split the PR, or redo it in a fresh session. More than six review rounds in total means the PR is wrong, not unlucky.
- **Operator:** only for a decision that is genuinely theirs (scope, product behaviour, an authority gate), with a recommendation.

No gate behaviour changes: `request` still refuses past the cap (exit 23), and merge still needs a clean review or an approving receipt on the exact head. Only the instruction for what to do at exit 23 changes, in `SKILL.md` and in the message `codex-review.sh` prints.

Replaces: the "stop, summarize, escalate to the operator" instruction at the round cap.

Checks: `bash -n` on `codex-review.sh`; no test pins the old message text (grep over `scripts/`, `src/` and `container/`).

author: stijn-dejongh
body:
## Issue

closes #5138
closes #5139
closes #5168

Ad-hoc governed Op `01M3FMD8YW5N7K04D1Y6FDQ7NA`. This follows #5141, which has merged. It replaces #5144, which was stacked on #5141's branch and auto-closed when that branch was deleted on merge. It is rebased onto current `main`.

#5168 was found on this PR and folded in while the PR was still a draft. CI had skipped the architectural battery, so the gates this PR changes never ran in CI.

Refs #5015: this removes one of the drift-prone lifted-test ledger copies. Evidence for the other five is posted on that issue.

## Change

Six signed commits, in linear history:

1. **`test(arch)`: shared fail-closed parse helpers.** New `tests/architectural/_ast_scan.py`.
   - `read_source`, `parse_source`, `read_and_parse` and `parse_file` raise `UnparseableSourceError`, an `AssertionError` that names the file. They raise on `OSError`, `UnicodeDecodeError`, `SyntaxError`, and the `ValueError` a NUL byte produces.
   - It also provides `qualname_by_line`. This deliberately does not reuse `anchoring`, because census ledgers are keyed on this exact line-span walk.
   - The home-pin gate keeps its own self-contained SC-013 `parse_module`.
2. **`test(census)`: one home for the `load_meta` census (#5138).**
   - The scanner and the `ACCOUNTED_SITES` ledger were hand-copied into the out-of-matrix contract module and into its always-on lift. The two copies drifted, which caused #5135.
   - Both now live in `tests/architectural/_load_meta_census.py`.
   - The always-on gate owns the full three-way ledger check. It also owns the scanner's non-vacuity proofs, which moved out of the out-of-matrix module and now run on every PR.
   - `test_census_has_exactly_one_home` is an AST check. It fails if a second definition appears anywhere under `tests/`.
3. **`test(arch)`: every `tests/` scanner fails closed (#5139).**
   - 44 handlers across 34 test modules could swallow a parse failure. All now route through `_ast_scan`, and none needed an allowlist row.
   - The new always-on gate `test_scanner_parse_fail_closed.py` scans all of `tests/`. It flags any construct that can swallow a parse failure:
     - an `except` catching `SyntaxError` or one of its subclasses;
     - a bare, `Exception`, `BaseException`, `AssertionError` or aliased handler around a parse call, including a same-module parser helper one hop away;
     - `contextlib.suppress`, including `*args`;
     - `finally: return`;
     - a handler that only re-raises conditionally.
   - `re.compile` and `json.loads` are not treated as parse calls.
   - The allowlist is checked for exact equality, and every row needs a rationale. It is empty today.
   - Non-vacuity: the gate must scan at least 2500 files (3364 live). 20 planted evasion cases must be flagged and 8 negative controls must not.
   - Also in this commit: four read-side swallows now use `read_source`. Three tests that asserted the old swallowing behaviour are re-pinned to expect the fail-closed contract. Dead `tree is None` branches are removed.
4. **`chore(ops)`:** Op trail.
5. **`docs(dev)`:** a `ci-gate-mechanics.md` entry for the new gate, with the docs index regenerated.
6. **`ci(router)`: run the architectural battery when `tests/architectural` changes (#5168).**
   - **Problem:** `tests/architectural` has no module-registry row, so its only per-PR home is `architectural battery (heavy, code-scoped)`. That job's `if:` was exactly the src-backed filter groups. A PR touching only `tests/architectural/**` matched none of them, so the battery was skipped.
   - **Fix:** adds a non-src `architectural` routing group (`tests/architectural/**`, as a filter plus a `changes.outputs` entry) and ORs it into the battery's `if:`.
   - The completeness oracle's exact-equality invariant becomes `src_backed_groups | HEAVY_BATTERY_NON_SRC_GROUPS`, an enumerated set rather than a `>=` comparison.
   - A self-mutation test fails if the group is dropped. There are also red-first `select_gates` acceptance tests and a golden `if:` case.
   - **Not in scope:** the `ci` group still gates no router job. That was a deliberate #4386 decision, pinned by `tests/ci/test_ci_module_wiring.py`. The remaining CI-config-only gap is recorded in `test_module_length_agreement.py`'s shard note.

**Formatting:** converted files that are on the shrink-only `[tool.ruff.format].exclude` list were edited without being reformatted, so the ratchet is unchanged.

**CHANGELOG:** not updated. The diff is test and CI infrastructure only, and review-gates.md §Changelog applies to user-facing changes.

## Tests run

Red-first:
- **#5139:**
  - The meta-gate is red on all 41 `tests/architectural` handlers before conversion.
  - The detector finds 47 sites on pre-#5141 `origin/main`, 44 across 34 modules on the #5141 tree, and 0 on HEAD.
  - Each of the 15 hardening fixtures was red against the earlier detector.
  - Three converted gates each raise `UnparseableSourceError` on a planted `def broken(:`.
- **#5138:** the single-home guard finds the two duplicate homes in the pre-#5138 layout.
- **#5168:** five new `select_gates` acceptance cases were red before the router change. One example: `tests/architectural/test_scanner_parse_fail_closed.py` did not select `architectural-heavy`.

Local runs:
- Every test touching the router or topology, plus `tests/ci` (73 files, found with `grep -rlE "ci-router|gate_selection|_ci_integrity_oracle|ci-module-registry|_gate_coverage" tests`), on the router fold: **970 passed, 4 failed**.
  - Two failures (`test_ci_module_wiring` golden context) were real and are fixed by modelling `changes.architectural`.
  - The other two fail identically on clean `main`: `tests/release/test_release_ci_ownership.py::test_release_checklist_marks_deferred_publish_workflows_as_p3_4b_prerequisite` and `tests/architectural/test_archive_root_byte_identical.py`. The latter is because this container is a shallow clone.
- The CI architectural battery command, run locally on the pre-fold tip: `pytest tests/architectural -q -m "not performance and not stress and not timing" -n 6 --dist loadfile` with the four always-on `--deselect`s. Result: **2594 passed, 9 skipped, 2 xfailed**. The remainder is environmental:
  - 154 errors and 2 failures come from the shallow clone (`git archive`/`git show` of historical SHAs exit 128) and also occur on `main`.
  - `test_remediation_effectiveness` (#3978) and `test_status_module_boundary` hit timing budgets under load. Both pass alone on HEAD and on `main`: 24 passed each.
- On the final tip after the rebase: `PWHEADLESS=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/architectural/test_scanner_parse_fail_closed.py tests/architectural/test_lifted_root_meta_fail_closed_census.py tests/specify_cli/test_meta_fail_closed_full_census_contract.py tests/architectural/test_destructive_op_routing.py tests/architectural/test_gate_selection_authority.py tests/architectural/test_ci_integrity_oracle_nonvacuous.py tests/ci/test_ci_module_wiring.py tests/architectural/test_ruff_format_exclude_ratchet.py tests/architectural/test_inline_meta_read_gate.py -n 5 --dist loadfile` → **174 passed, 1 skipped**.
- Full blast radius for #5138/#5139 (55 files), on the pre-merge tip with patch-identical content: **964 passed, 1 skipped, 2 xfailed**. The same set ran clean in 3 of 3 loops at `-n 8`.
- `make test-fast` → **2044 passed, 1 failed, 8 skipped**. The failure is `tests/specify_cli/runtime/test_agent_commands.py::TestFreshnessShortCircuitOSErrorFallthrough::test_destination_health_check_oserror_falls_through_to_render`, also red on the base: the container runs as root, so chmod does not take effect.
- `ruff check .` is clean. `ruff format --check .` reports 2383 files already formatted.
- `PYTHONPATH=. uv run python -m scripts.docs.check_docs_freshness --ci` → 0 errors.

**Expected on this PR's CI:** with #5168 in, `architectural battery (heavy, code-scoped)` should run, where before it was skipped. That confirms the fold end to end.

Self-review:

## Problem
docs/01 §6.1 / §12.6 describe one active Relay Key, with the previous key kept for 10 minutes of grace; revoke or expiry rejects it. The doc does not define an extra-keys list.

`SetActiveRelayKeys` puts the first `RELAY_KEYS` entry in `relayActive` and every later entry in `relayAlso`. If the first key appears again later in the list (e.g. `RELAY_KEYS=rk_a,rk_b,rk_a`), its digest ends up in both places. After `RotateRelayKey`, `rk_a` moves to grace but stays in `relayAlso`, so `ValidRelayKey(rk_a)` still returns true after `RevokeGrace` or after grace expires.

## Fix
`RotateRelayKey` removes the outgoing active digest from `relayAlso` when it moves that digest into grace, using the existing fields. Other entries in `relayAlso` behave as before (`TestRelayAlsoKeysSurviveRotate` still passes). Header collection and the grace duration are unchanged.

## Test

author: lex00
body:
`chant operator --steward` registered its SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers with `process.once`. A `.once` listener tears itself down the instant it fires, before the handler body even runs, so a second SIGTERM arriving while shutdown is still in flight finds nothing listening and takes Node's default disposition, ending the process before the `finally` block that releases the steward's lease. The next `chant operator --steward` then refuses with "already running" until the stale lease expires (5 minutes by default). This is the shape a supervisor produces when it signals both a process group and a child (seen through arugula-salad/studio's box smoke; the kit worked around it by signalling once, arugula-salad/studio#147).

Both `chant operator` and `chant operator --steward` now register with `process.on` instead, kept for the whole shutdown, with a `stopping` flag so a repeat signal is a no-op (no second abort, no repeated log line) rather than a second attempt to tear anything down.

That alone did not close the whole hole. The steward path's `finally` block removed the listeners as its first two statements, before awaiting the lease release (two more git plumbing calls). A repeat signal landing in that window reopened the same problem one step later. `process.on` kept the listener around through the `try`, but the `finally` itself then handed control straight back to Node's default disposition mid-release. The listener removal now happens last, after the lease read/release attempt, so a second, third or later signal is absorbed for the whole shutdown, not just the abort.

This branch is rebased onto main after #2861/#2881 landed (a steward runs an Op beside its turns, in its own `chant run <op>` process, stopped with SIGINT and up to 10s grace when the operator stops). The operator side of that new stop path is already covered here: `stopBesideRuns`'s wait is a plain `Promise.race` the steward operator's own signal handling never touches, repeat signal or not. `run.ts`'s `runOpOnRuntime` had a separate, matching problem though: the process a beside run actually is used `process.once`, SIGINT only, and removed its listener before the async release of the beside run's own Op lease (`stewardGate.release`). Fixed the same way, so a beside run's own lease is released whether the repeat signal lands on the steward operator or on the run it started.

I checked the bug by hand before writing the automated test: reverting to the original `process.once` code and sending three real SIGTERMs (30ms apart) at a spawned `chant operator --steward` reliably reproduces it, exiting via signal with the lease ref left behind. The fix reliably exits 0 with the lease released, across repeated runs.

## Acceptance
- `chant operator --steward` releases the steward's lease on a second (or third) SIGTERM: done.
- Test that spawns the operator, sends SIGTERM twice quickly, and reads the lease after exit: done (`packages/core/src/cli/handlers/operator-steward-signal.e2e.test.ts`; spawns the real CLI so a regression kills only the child, not the test runner).
- Same handling for the plain `chant operator` path: done (no lease there, but the same `process.once` hole existed).
- The beside-run stop path added by #2861/#2881 also releases its leases under a repeat signal: done for the operator side (mechanically unaffected, explained above); the child's own `run.ts` handling fixed the same way. Not covered by a new automated test. Building a full steward+beside+cron fixture across two real processes was judged not worth it against the existing steward-beside.test.ts and op/operator.test.ts coverage of the beside mechanism itself, which stays green. Flag it if you want that test added too.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run --project e2e packages/core/src/cli/handlers/operator-steward-signal.e2e.test.ts`: 1 passed. Also confirmed it fails against the pre-fix code (checked out from before this branch): the child is killed by signal and the lease is left behind.
- `npx vitest run --project unit`, targeted at everything importing the two changed files (`run.test.ts`, `operator.test.ts`, `main.test.ts`, `steward-beside.test.ts`, `op/operator.test.ts`): 272 passed.
- `npx tsx scripts/typecheck.ts`: 31 known failures, no regressions (baselined).
- `node scripts/lint-docs-sentences.mjs`: 4170 gated findings, no regressions (below the 4198 baseline).
- Full unit suite deferred to wave 4, per the orchestrator's standing rule that full suites wait for the end of the goal. The targeted tests above cover every caller of the two changed files.

Closes INTENTIUS/chant#2872.

author: rcbevans
body:
## What

Revives 1,257 lines of stranded test pins from `772d8b5f` (Sep 23), rebased onto main:

- `tests/_redis_time_skew_proxy.py` — a wire-level TIME-skew proxy (RESP2/RESP3, pipelining-aware, out-of-band pushes excluded) that shifts the client-visible `TIME` reply by a fixed offset while forwarding everything else byte-for-byte.
- `tests/test_ratelimit_fallback_clock_crossing.py` — 18 pins across the four clock-crossing contracts the Redis↔PG fallback owns.

## The four contracts pinned

1. **Fresh-domain stamps (the PG outage fallback).** When a Redis acquire fails over to PG, the PG recovery stamps its own row with the PG clock: a Redis-domain ts/TAT/score poisoned ±2 min (the hypothesized outage residue) can neither wedge the fallback, mint it a phantom refill, nor move the PG row's state one microsecond. Token bucket, GCRA, and log-style, both poison directions where they discriminate.
2. **Ignore-on-failover-back.** Symmetric: with Redis healthy again, the Redis acquire runs on the Redis domain alone — a poisoned PG row (either direction) changes nothing, and the Redis path leaves the PG row byte-identical (it never reads or writes PG).
3. **Epoch-scale persistence.** After exercising every persisted write (PG token-bucket acquire + refund, PG GCRA, Redis token bucket / GCRA / log), every stored stamp sits within an hour of its store's clock — no `time.monotonic()` value (uptime-scale, meaningless to the other backend and to a restarted process) ever reaches either store.
4. **Client-skew immunity.** Through the ±2 min proxy: the acquire scripts ignore a client-visible `TIME` skew (server-side `redis.call('TIME')` cannot be reached on the wire — a client-supplied-now acquire, the shape the C8 doctrine removed, would mint 1.2 phantom tokens from +2 min of elapsed); the peek paths measure against the store clock the client sees.

Plus the boundary pins that make the harness honest: the proxy skews `TIME` and nothing else (an HMGET reply structurally identical to a TIME reply passes through untouched), and the progress flush crosses no clock (no timestamp function in the SQL, no time-ish parameter in the binding contract).

## Why the gap is real

Main's own source comments promise exactly these semantics — `_sliding_window_pg.py:7`, `_redis_utils.py:37`, `_scripts.py:135` describe fresh-domain stamps and same-domain measurement — and before this branch nothing enforced them. The pins enforce what the comments promise: every docstring names the regression it hunts (the client-supplied-now acquire, the poisoned cross-domain stamp, the monotonic leak).

## Reconciliation notes (rebase onto main was clean; two seams had moved)

1. **The log peek's behind direction → the fail-closed verdict (a837931e).** The lying-store hardening (#500, Sep 24 — postdates the pins' original base) added an oldest-score trust boundary to the log peek: every selected score is bounded to `(cutoff, now]`, because a future-dated score was the crash direction. The behind-skew scenario puts the stored entry's score 120 s in the FUTURE of the behind peek's own clock read, so that direction now raises `RateLimitStoreCorrupt` instead of measuring a stretched window. The pin is reconciled: the behind direction asserts the fail-closed raise (a Python-clock peek in the same scenario sees the entry in-window and does not raise, so the raise still discriminates the store-clock read); the ahead direction keeps its original measurement assert. The GCRA and token-bucket peeks clamp (`tat = max(tat, now)`, `max(0, elapsed)`) and their behind directions still measure — unchanged.
2. **The transient-retry machinery (cc611f09) prices the outage harness.** `with_pg_fallback` now weathers the connection family with a bounded retry (3 attempts, 0.25/0.75 s backoffs) before the fail-closed decision. The pins' `_OutageRedis` raises on every call, so every outage acquire spends the ~1 s weathering budget and THEN lands on the PG fallback. The contract is unchanged — a persistent outage still ends in the fallback — so only the harness/module docstrings note the budget; no assertion moved.

Everything else survived the rebase untouched: the proxy's fake-TIME surface still matches redis-py 8.x's call shapes (RESP2 default, the maintenance-notification push handling still needed), and the key spacing, constructor signatures, fixtures, and the flush binding contract are identical.

The admitted, bounded divergence a stateless failover cannot avoid (admission capacity during an outage is bounded by outage duration + window) is documented on the acquire docstrings and deliberately NOT pinned as a bug: it is the fallback's contract, not a skew defect.

## Gates

- `ruff check .` — 0 errors; `ruff format --check .` — clean (1,330 files)
- `pyright` — 0 errors, 0 warnings
- ratelimit family (full `-k` selection, all backends): **953 passed**
- revived suite: **18 passed, 3× stable** (14.2 s / 14.2 s / 14.3 s)

- **Extraction (`src/lib/share-intake.ts`, on-device only):**
  - Strict patterns: UPS `1Z…`, Amazon `TBA/TBC/TBM` + 12 digits, USPS 20 to 22 digits starting with 9 (a `420`+ZIP prefix is stripped), USPS `..#########US`, OnTrac `C/D` + 14 digits and zero-padded 20-digit, DHL `JD/JJD`, HDX, FedEx `DT`.
  - Carrier links: `tLabels`, `tracknum`, `trknbr`, `tracknumbers`, `tracking-id`, `tracking_number` and `track.amazon.com/tracking/…`.
  - Bare 10/12/15-digit runs (DHL/FedEx) count only when the carrier is named or a "Tracking number:" label is right before them. They never count after order/phone/account/ref labels, as toll-free or phone-shaped numbers, or as ZIPs.
  - A share that is only one number is always taken.
  - Carrier naming reuses `guessCarrier`.
- **UX:**
  - One number: the form is filled with the carrier set, and the nickname comes from the title when it reads like one (an email subject with `Fwd:`/`Re:` stripped; carrier tracking-page titles are skipped).
  - Several numbers: a small list, each with Pin (or tap the number to load it into the form).
  - No number: the shared text goes in the tracking field with "Couldn't find a tracking number in what you shared."
- **Privacy:**
  - `/share` returns a fixed page (`Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, no SSR, no head injection) whose only script moves the query into `/#share=…`.
  - An inline script at the top of `<head>` keeps that in memory and drops it from the address bar before any other script loads, so a refresh doesn't re-trigger.
  - `public/share-sw.js` (scope `/share` only) makes the same redirect on the phone once the app has been opened, so later shares never reach the network.
  - Nothing goes to `/api/og`, the tracker lookup, or Firebase until a slip is pinned.
  - The privacy panel adds: "Sharing to Waybill Wall from another app only fills in the form on your phone; nothing is saved until you pin it."

## Checks
- Typecheck, lint, tests (Node 22: 196 + 128 passing, including new `share-intake.test.ts` and `scripts/share-target.test.mjs`) and build all pass.
- Tested at 412×915 with a Pixel user agent against the built output. Each case:
  - UPS (with title): filled, UPS, nickname "Camera lens".
  - Amazon TBA: filled.
  - USPS 9400…: filled.
  - Amazon track URL: TBA334894092403, Amazon.
  - Email with an order number and phone numbers: only the UPS number, nickname from the subject.
  - Three numbers: list of 3.
  - No number: text in the form plus the notice.
- In every case the URL ends as `/`, nothing is pinned, the shared numbers and text appear in no request URL, body or Referer, and a refresh doesn't re-trigger. With the worker registered, `/share` never reached the server.

author: antimora
body:
`V3::equals_f32` and `V3::equals_f64` use `_CMP_EQ_UQ`. The `U` means unordered: the predicate is true when either operand is NaN. So on AVX2 CPUs:

| | V3 (before) | V2, V4, NEON, wasm, scalar |
|---|---|---|
| `NaN == NaN` | true | false |
| `NaN == 1.0` | true | false |
| `NaN != NaN` | false | true |

This PR switches both to `_CMP_EQ_OQ`, which is what V4 already uses. The ordering predicates (`LT_OQ`, `LE_OQ`, ...) were already ordered.

This affects downstream code today. burn-ndarray's `equal` goes through `VEq` for f32/f64, so on AVX2 machines a NaN compares equal to every value in large tensors.

### Tests

The comparison tests only generated random values in `0..127`, so NaN never reached them. This PR:

- adds an `@inputs` arm to `testgen_cmp!`, with the random-operand arm delegating to it (`testgen_min_max!` reuses the same helper);
- runs `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `gt` and `ge` for f32/f64 on every pairing of NaN (both signs), signed zero, signed infinity and ordinary values;
- adds the missing `ne` test for all types.

Verified:

- `cargo test` on aarch64 (NEON and NeonFP16);
- Miri with the V3 feature set from `miri.yml` (`--features miri-x86_v3`, covers V3, V2 and scalar): the new `eq`/`ne` NaN tests fail before the fix and pass after;
- Miri on aarch64.

f16 isn't in the NaN tests yet because f16 `ne` is broken on several backends for a different reason; that fix and its tests are in a follow-up PR. Float `min`/`max` also treat NaN differently per backend, but that needs a decision on the intended semantics, so it's out of scope here.

## Summary

- PG guard unification (owner directive NEXT after #3481): `test_rq29_end_to_end_path_pg.py` (PR #3474) carried its own private local-only admin-DSN guard alongside the shared `tests/_pg_admin_guard.is_local_admin_dsn` (#3468, consumed by 18 fixture modules). Read-only investigation first: a shape-by-shape probe (23 DSN/env cases, `scripts/probe_guard_divergence.py`) proved the two guards diverge on 11 of 23 — and that the SHARED validator, not the harness one, holds the gaps.
- Headline finding (P1, RED-first): `?HOSTADDR=10.9.8.7` (uppercase key) — libpq matches conninfo parameter names case-insensitively, so this spelling dials 10.9.8.7 exactly like `?hostaddr=`, but the shared validator only read the lowercase key and ACCEPTED the DSN on a loopback netloc: a remote dial through a case variant. The RQ29 private guard rejected it (case-insensitive normalization).
- Shared-validator P2 gaps proven by the same probe: `?service=` accepted (a service file may inject any unspelled parameter — `hostaddr` included — at connect time); `PGHOSTADDR`/`PGSERVICE` environment re-dial not checked (with either set, libpq re-dials every candidate); repeated `?host=a&host=b` keys CRASHED the validator (`AttributeError` on the folded list value) instead of returning a verdict; a non-postgresql URL with a syntactically local `?host=` (`sqlite:///f.db?host=localhost`) was admitted.
- Unification (tests-only, minimal): the shared validator adopts the RQ29-grade contract — case-insensitive query-key normalization, duplicate-safe sequence handling, `?service=` rejection, `PGHOSTADDR`/`PGSERVICE` env re-dial rejection, postgresql-only drivername — so all 19 wired modules run ONE rule set; the harness deletes its private `_is_local` (~50 lines) and wires `_candidate_admin_urls` onto the shared guard. Deliberate deltas documented in both docstrings: bare hostless DSNs stay fail-closed REJECTED (the RQ29 guard used to auto-accept them — the module now SKIPS such candidates instead of provisioning through the environment-dependent default socket directory); loopback `?hostaddr=` stays admitted element-wise (the audited #3468 rule — the RQ29 guard used to reject it outright).
- Unchanged harness surfaces: the explicit `RQ29_PG_ADMIN_URL` remote escape hatch and the `LOCAL_PG_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD` loopback candidate (with its env re-dial guard) behave exactly as before; scratch-DB lifecycle (run-unique `rq29_check_<hex>`, alembic upgrade head, try/finally teardown with `pg_terminate_backend` + DROP) untouched.

After the fix: 192/192.

The "contract" here is the internal test-suite admin-DSN admission rule set, which is unified (one shared validator) rather than changed for consumers: every admission verdict the 18 legacy modules relied on is preserved (positive pins included), and the only behavior changes are the fail-closed directions the new pins require.
