## Owner-requested scope

Establish one reusable Mac landing point, a portable SKILL.md and a bounded RDC/GitHub runner, without adding a second product roadmap or changing clinical/patient-facing behaviour. Application basis: `6bc4d77f9ee9bbe95ef181d50fbaf94cf2388f84`.

Start at `.agents/skills/physioassist-hybrid/SKILL.md`. Its evidence directory contains qualification records and the inspected native onboarding screenshot. Root `AGENTS.md` supplies pickup instructions. This is guidance/tooling, not a permanent agent or an expansion of permissions.

## Changes

- Exact-revision/origin checks, single-job advisory lock, bounded commands/time/logs, reduced priority, two test/compiler workers and preflight disk/cache budgets.
- Dry-run-first cleanup limited to named generated cache paths; no automatic source/evidence/credential deletion.
- Reconciled native lock; repeated `NO_FLIPPER=1 pod install --deployment` passes without lock drift.
- Removed tracked machine-specific `.xcode.env.local`; each host provides its ignored local Node location.
- Normalized generated native project/plist state and removed obsolete Firebase build integration.
- Excluded generated Pods/build directories from lint without excluding more authored application components.
- CI now uses `pod install --deployment` plus `pipefail`, so dependency failures cannot be hidden by `tee`.

## Validation actually performed

- Typecheck passed; lint: 0 errors / 450 warnings, approximately 16 seconds after generated-tree exclusions.
- Claude's shutdown fix independently retested at 6bc4d77: each of parallel and --detectOpenHandles runs had 1,593 passing tests / four skipped, exit 0, no forced-worker or detected-open-handle warning, no --forceExit.
- Runner: 22 synthetic tests passed in cloud Linux and on the Mac.
- Frozen Pods passed repeatedly, including from clean published commit 5cc5d5a; the worktree remained clean.
- Fresh Xcode 16.2 Release simulator build at the new landing root passed in 352.71 seconds. Native app installed/launched, running at 10 seconds; screenshot actually opened/inspected; owned simulator shut down.
- Main patch and subsequent documentation used ordinary commit/push hooks; 21 Integration tests actually ran.
- CI shell syntax checked; a controlled failing-Pod probe returns exit 7 with pipefail versus exit 0 in the control without it. This is failure-propagation testing, not a completed hosted native run.

## Publication route, transparently recorded

The Mac OAuth credential initially refused workflow edits for lack of workflow scope. The already-connected GitHub app had separately authorised workflow permission and published the exact two-line CI change in `343a400c115f347f7fcd46a97ac3a8953883cea5`. No account/credential scope was changed. This API commit did not run local hooks at publication; it was read back, compared and locally syntax/failure tested. The earlier refusal and subsequent resolution remain recorded separately. Current head includes the CI change; the former inactive patch file was retired to avoid stale instructions.

## Resource/privacy boundaries

Moved existing checkout/toolchain/evidence instead of duplicating them. Removed four obsolete dependency copies and an obsolete pre-move cache after inventory (~5.30 GiB allocated blocks, not an equal physical APFS free-space claim). One useful current native cache is retained. Temporary handover clone was verified clean/published and retired; future documentation uses temporary worktrees. Historical source/evidence, private protocols and existing agent metadata remain preserved.

No private sources, identifying media, machine paths, credentials, signing material, permanent daemon or self-hosted runner were uploaded/installed. No global macOS/Xcode upgrade.

Independent review and hosted CI qualification remain required. Full native rehab UI journeys, physical-device performance/camera accuracy, clinical validation and current App Store submission qualification are not established by this patch. No PR is merged by this setup.

author: yehzu
body:
## Root cause

**1. The channel lag grew past what the alignment would accept.** The system channel of recent recordings is **~5.45 s late** relative to the mic. That is a GCC-PHAT cross-correlation of the two channels in 20 s windows. On a 63-min meeting (09-16), 174 of 188 windows gave a confident peak, with a median of 5.45 s (p10–p90: 5.34–5.55 s). The lag is steady across the meeting (quarterly medians: 5.49 / 5.47 / 5.45 / 5.41 s), and an 08-06 standup shows the same 5.45 s. When the alignment was written in 0.8.7, the lag was ~1.5 s, and a 05-26 recording has 2.5 s, so it varies between recordings.

`post-meet.sh` did find it. On 09-16, 650 bleed matches gave a median of **5440 ms**. But the gate `200 <= cand <= 4000` (main, `post-meet.sh:219`) rejected that value, so nothing was shifted. With the channels unaligned, bleed suppression uses a ±4 s window (`:232`). That window never reaches the far-end copy that is 5.4 s away, so it dropped only 99 of 1220 mic segments. The rest came through as `Me:` lines that repeat an `[Other]`/`SPKn` line about 5 s later. The vote window itself (`SEARCH_MS = 6000`, `:195`) would also have clipped any lag past ~6 s.

**2. Diarization looked speakers up on the wrong clock whenever the alignment did apply.** The merge moves `[Other]` times earlier by the offset (onto the mic clock). `diarize.py` then ran the model on the **unshifted** system WAV and called `label_at(t)` with the shifted line time (main `diarize.py:222`, `:256`), so every lookup landed `offset` seconds early. This happens on real recordings. A 37-min meeting from 05-26 has a 2.5 s lag, and main aligns it (−2500 ms, 324 matches). Moving the lookup onto the right clock changes the speaker on **131 of 333** non-Me lines (39%). A 10-min excerpt of 09-16, re-cut so its lag was 2.76 s, gives 12 of 32.

**3. It also exposed a third issue.** Consecutive `[Other]` segments are merged into one line *before* diarization, and the whole line takes the speaker at its first second. The duplicate `Me:` lines used to break those runs every few seconds. Once they are suppressed, a run can span several people: on 09-16, 44% of the diarized speech inside SPK lines sat under another speaker's label.

## Changes

- **`tools/recording/post-meet.sh`** (merge step)
  - **Offset estimate.** Each mic segment votes with the lag of its best text match (ratio ≥ 0.7) in a −2…+10 s window. The estimate is the median of the densest 1 s group of votes.
  - **Confidence gate.** The shift is applied only if the group has **≥ 8 votes**, holds **≥ 50% of all votes**, and lies in **0.2–9 s**. Otherwise timing is left as it is, which was already the behavior for recordings without bleed.
  - **Logging.** Both outcomes are logged with the vote counts.
  - **Temp files for diarization.** The merge writes the applied offset and the unmerged segments (JSONL) to temp files, which the EXIT trap removes.
- **`tools/recording/diarize.py`**
  - `--sys-offset-ms` moves the model's turns by the same offset, clamped at 0 the same way the merge clamps.
  - `--segments` labels each whisper segment on its own, then joins same-label runs into the unchanged `[MM:SS] Label: text` format.
  - Both flags are optional. With neither, the output is byte-identical to main; I checked this on the excerpt.

Two commits: the first is the alignment and the clock fix, the second is the per-segment labelling. The second can be dropped on its own, but without it the first commit makes speaker attribution worse (see the table).

## Results

Whisper output was cached once per recording, so "main" and "PR" below differ only in `post-meet.sh`/`diarize.py`. On 09-16, the main re-run from cache is byte-identical to an earlier run made without the cache.

**Duplicate** = a `Me:` line (≥ 4 normalized chars) whose text is ≥ 60% covered, in ≥ 3-char blocks, by a non-Me line that starts 2–10 s later. As a control, the same test looking 2–10 s *earlier* matches 4 lines on main. **Misattributed speech** = diarized speech inside an SPK line's span that belongs to a different speaker.

The meetings with the bug:

| | 09-16 main | 09-16 commit 1 only | 09-16 PR | 08-06 main | 08-06 PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lag (cross-correlation) | 5.45 s | | | 5.45 s | |
| offset applied | none | −5460 ms | −5460 ms | none | −5420 ms |
| mic segments suppressed | 99 / 1220 | 877 / 1220 | 877 / 1220 | 48 / 490 | 278 / 490 |
| `Me:` lines | 769 | 221 | 221 | 286 | 110 |
| duplicate `Me:` lines | **472** | 12 | **12** | **152** | **5** |
| `[Other]` lines | 16 | 12 | 17 | 19 | 14 |
| SPK lines | 752 | 208 | 405 | 267 | 114 |
| per speaker | 209/171/175/77/120 | 58/41/44/18/47 | 125/79/78/41/82 | 15/39/86/39/18/26/41/3 | 8/15/32/19/8/10/19/3 |
| misattributed speech in SPK lines | 17% | 44% | **11%** | 2% | 2% |

Controls. On 05-26 main already aligned correctly; 05-27 was recorded on headphones:

| | 05-26 main | 05-26 PR | 05-27 main | 05-27 PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| lag | 2.49 s (cross-corr., 3 windows), 2.5 s (votes) | | no bleed | |
| offset applied | −2500 ms | −2500 ms | none (0 votes) | none (0 votes) |
| `Me:` lines | 334 | 334 (identical) | 236 | 236 (identical) |
| duplicate `Me:` lines | 2 | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| `[Other]` lines | 9 | 5 | 2 | 3 |
| SPK lines | 324 | 576 | 234 | 348 |
| per speaker | 122/18/70/53/61 | 232/47/112/107/78 | 34/33/21/77/27/34/8 | 61/60/26/95/42/47/17 |
| misattributed speech in SPK lines | **51%** | **18%** | 33% | **13%** |

On both controls the words are unchanged (identical once labels and line breaks are stripped). Only runs that span several speakers are split. A 06-04 standup (0 votes, no speech found on the system channel) produces identical output.

Three spot checks:
1. **09-16, 01:40–02:10.** Main has five `Me:` lines in 12 s, each a copy of the SPK line ~5 s later. With the PR, that speaker's line starts at 01:44, where the mic heard it. Two `Me:` lines remain: a short interjection with no system-channel counterpart, and one residual echo (see Risks).
2. **09-16, 15:28–15:58.** Commit 1 alone gives one 30 s SPK line, although the model has two people alternating (13.6 s and 9.4 s). The PR splits it into five lines that follow the turns.
3. **05-27 (headphones).** No offset is applied, and the `Me:` lines and all text are unchanged. SPK lines go from 234 to 348 because merged runs are now split where the speaker changes, and misattributed speech falls from 33% to 13%.

On the 10-min excerpt, main's lookup matched the speaker from the full-meeting run (which had no offset, so its clock was right) on 8 of 17 matched lines. With the clock fix it matched on 15 of 17.

## Risks

- **A false shift on a meeting without bleed.** Chance text matches at ratio ≥ 0.7 barely occur. Five cross-meeting pairings of mic and system channels produced 0 votes each. On top of that, the 8-vote and 50% gate has to pass. The headphone recordings (05-27, 06-04) get 0 votes and are untouched. Where bleed exists, the densest group held 79–90% of the votes (09-16, 08-06, 05-26, excerpt).
- **A small real offset with little bleed.** Main aligned on ≥ 4 matches. The PR needs 8 votes in the densest 1 s group, so a recording with 4–7 bleed matches is now left unaligned, which keeps the ±4 s dedup window.
- **Residual echo.** Dedup still compares segment *starts* within ±2 s using a whole-string ratio. When the mic copy is the tail of a long system segment, it survives. On 09-16, 50 of the remaining 221 `Me:` lines match a non-Me line within ±10 s (main: 500). This is not a regression; it is a follow-up.
- **Line structure changes on reprocess.** Transcripts made with this PR have more, shorter SPK lines. Existing transcripts change only if they are reprocessed.
- **Not addressed here.** Why the tap's lag varies: ~1.5 s at 0.8.7, 2.5 s on 05-26, and 5.45 s on 08-06 and 09-16 (`coreaudio-tap` / `record-meet.sh`).

## Rollback
Revert the PR (or just the second commit) and ship. The scripts re-sync to `~/.ycal` on the next launch.

author: williamchiii
body:
A saved clip can get stuck in "Recording" when its camera stops sending video, because the footage after the press never arrives. There was no way to get rid of it from the Library.

## What changed
- **Library card:** a clip still recording shows a **Cancel** button in the same spot and width as Download and Delete.
- **Confirmation:** "Cancel this recording?", with **Cancel recording** and **Keep recording** buttons. Confirming deletes the incident, which stops the recording and releases the footage it held, and shows a "Recording cancelled" toast. `ConfirmDialog` gets an optional `cancelLabel` for the back-out button.
- **409 handling:** if the recording finishes and the clip is being assembled at that moment, the server returns 409 and the box says to try again in a few seconds.
- **Server:** no change. `DELETE /incidents/{id}` already allowed recording incidents and refuses only while assembling. The contract now says so, and a new test covers it.

## Testing
- Server: all 82 unit tests pass, and ruff passes.
- Client: lint and build pass.
- Headless Chrome with the mock API, all 7 checks passed:
  - two recording clips show only Cancel;
  - the box wording is right, and Keep recording leaves both clips;
  - confirming removes one clip and shows the toast;
  - the other clip finishes and switches to Download and Delete;
  - all three buttons measure 144 px.

author: siradoni
body:
## Linked issue

Closes #6708

## Why this change

Memory rebuilding currently sends the entire chat's chunks in one embedding request. Long chats can exceed a provider's aggregate request limit even when each chunk fits individually. The existing rebuild also deletes the native index before obtaining replacement vectors, so a failed request can leave the chat without its previous index.

## What changed

- Batch the existing embedding helper sequentially at 64 texts or 100,000 JavaScript string code units, preserving input/vector order. This is a conservative character budget, not a tokenizer-derived guarantee for every provider. An oversized individual input stays intact; existing memory chunk splitting remains in place.
- Validate returned counts, finite nonempty vectors, and consistent dimensions across batches. Reject cancellation before and after each awaited batch, including a provider that returns a final response after cancellation.
- Build and validate replacement rows before changing the native index, then replace it transactionally. Failed embeddings, cancellation, and insertion failures preserve the previous native index. Imported memory rows are excluded from native replacement.
- Retain the existing per-chat mutation serialization and embedding-space checks. Failed explicit rebuilds now report failure instead of appearing successful with an empty replacement.
- Add regression coverage and an Unreleased changelog entry. No new dependency, schema migration, UI, or provider-specific implementation.

Resumable partial progress, configurable batch limits, and provider-error-driven adaptive sizing are not implemented. A failed rebuild keeps the old index; retry starts the embedding work again.

## Validation

Maintainer integration validation on `9742b28f5c95dd008a08c05dee95136cf3a90b02` (merged with staging `4be7698e7`):

- `pnpm check` passed in one complete run.
- `node scripts/run-regressions.mjs --filter memory-recall`: 2/2 files passed, including batching, order, failed/canceled rebuild preservation, transaction rollback, imported rows, and unavailable-embedder warning coverage.
- Local CodeRabbit reviewed all three changed files; zero findings.
- Resolved the changelog conflict and fixed the review finding so an unavailable embedder warns once; malformed non-null results still report a count mismatch.
- GitHub checks and CodeRabbit on this head are merge gates; their status is recorded by GitHub.

Human verification checklist:

- [ ] `pnpm check` passes locally
- [ ] Container (Docker / Podman) built and ran without issue
- [ ] Ran the app, clicked through the changes manually
- [ ] Checked edge cases (light + dark mode, mobile viewport, empty states, error paths)
- [ ] Above manual verification completed (describe below)
- [x] Read and followed `CONTRIBUTING.md`

### Manual verification notes

Manually rebuild a long chat using the intended embedding provider and confirm multiple bounded requests complete. Verify retrieval afterward. Cancel or interrupt a rebuild and confirm the previous native index remains usable; then retry. No human or real-provider verification is claimed by the automated results above.

## Docs and release impact

Unreleased changelog updated. No version bump or changes under `docs/`.

- [ ] No docs changes needed
- [ ] Updated docs (README / CONTRIBUTING / android/README / CHANGELOG) as needed
- [ ] Translated docs updated or follow-up issue opened, if applicable
- [ ] Version/release files updated, if applicable

## UI evidence (if applicable)

No UI changes.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Existing long-chat memory remains available if a rebuild fails or is canceled.
  * Incomplete, invalid, or inconsistent embedding results no longer replace stored memory.
  * Memory rebuilds split large sets of messages into batches of up to 64 texts and 100,000 characters, while preserving result order.
  * Canceled embedding requests and failed replacement writes leave the previous memory index intact.
  * Rebuilding an empty native index skips embedding and retains imported memory.

body:
## 요약

현재 서버 응답 스키마(2026-09-27 `/v3/api-docs`)에 없는 응답 필드 4개를 앱에서 제거합니다.
서버가 보내지 않으니 이 값들은 늘 기본값(`false`·빈 맵·`null`)으로 채워졌습니다.
지금은 읽는 화면이 없어 사용자에게 보이는 증상은 없습니다. 다만 나중에 누가 이 값으로
화면을 만들면 항상 틀린 값이 나오므로, 서버 계약이 없는 필드를 정상값처럼 남겨두지 않습니다.

| 필드 | 서버 근거 | 앱에서 읽는 곳 |
|---|---|---|
| `PracticeItemResponse.isVerified` (`GET /members/me/practices`) | `PracticeItem`에 없음 | 없음(미리보기에서 `true`만 넣음) |
| `PracticeVisitResponse.isVerified` (`POST /practices/{id}/visits`) | 없음. 서버에는 `isCertifiedNow`("이번 방문으로 인증되었는지")만 있음 | 없음 |
| `ReviewSummaryResponse.congestionCounts` | 없음. 후기 목록 설명에 "혼잡도는 저장만 하며 어느 API로도 내려주지 않는다" | 없음 |
| `RecentSearchResponse.regionKey` | 없음 | 검색 화면. 항상 null이라 이미 키워드로 지역을 찾고 있었음 |

`isVerified`와 `isCertifiedNow`는 #75에서 함께 추가됐습니다. 한쪽이 다른 쪽의 옛 이름이 아니므로
합치지 않았습니다. `isCertifiedNow`는 서버 필드라 그대로 둡니다.

## 변경

- 응답 DTO, mapper, 도메인 모델(`PracticeRecordItem`·`PracticeVisitResult`·`ReviewSummary`·`RecentSearch`), 미리보기, 테스트 fixture에서 위 필드를 끝까지 제거
- `SearchViewModel`은 최근 검색어의 지역을 키워드로만 찾음(기존 동작과 같음)
- `ResponseContractTest`에 "응답 모델은 서버가 보내는 필드만 선언한다" 테스트 추가

## 테스트

- 새 테스트는 수정 전 코드에서 `isVerified`(2건), `congestionCounts`에 대해 FAIL, 수정 후 PASS
- `regionKey`는 DTO에 필드를 되돌리면 같은 테스트가 FAIL하는 것 확인
- `./gradlew test assembleDebug :core:data:lintDebug :feature:mypage:lintDebug :feature:home:lintDebug --rerun-tasks` 통과
- `check-conventions.sh` BLOCK 0 / WARN 2(변경 전과 같음), `git diff --check` 통과

## 이 PR에서 다루지 않은 것

같은 조사에서 서버 계약이 바뀐 것을 더 찾았지만, UX나 인증 흐름을 정해야 해서 코드에 넣지 않았습니다.
- 로그인·복구 응답의 `isOnboarded`: 서버는 온보딩 분기를 이 값으로 하라고 명시하지만, 앱은 `isNewMember`로 분기
- 로그인·복구 응답의 `WITHDRAWAL_LOCKED` + `reRegisterableAt`: 앱이 처리하지 않아 알 수 없는 상태 오류가 남
- 저장·연습 목록의 `isDeleted`: 삭제된 코스를 눌렀을 때 어떻게 보여줄지 정해지지 않음

author: novalux12
body:
Closes #655 — the third acceptance criterion, the one that was easy to believe was already met: **`server.json` validates against the MCP registry schema in CI.**

## What was actually there

`server.json` carries `"$schema": "https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json"`. Nothing was loading it. A `$schema` key is an annotation — it tells an editor what to load and a reader where the contract lives. The only party that actually validated the manifest was `mcp-publisher`, at publish time, answering with a 400 that names a property — *after* `npm publish` had already made the release public.

`tests/registry-meta.test.ts` looked like it closed the gap, and did not. Its ajv check `return`ed without asserting whenever the schema fetch or the ajv import failed, so the single claim the suite made was the one thing it could not promise. The criterion stayed open correctly; this closes it.

**I re-checked the other two criteria rather than assuming. Both still hold** — `CANONICAL_DESCRIPTION` is byte-identical across `package.json`, `server.json`, the README one-liner and both `docs/distribution.md` blurbs, it ends with `NON_AFFILIATION_NOTICE` verbatim, and editing one mirror without the others fails `npm test`.

## What this adds

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `scripts/registry-schema.mjs` | The checker. Three verdicts, not two. |
| `scripts/check-server-schema.mjs` | The CLI — same shape as the repo's other `scripts/check-*.mjs` gates, so it needs **no `package.json` entry**. |
| `tests/server-schema.test.ts` | 19 cases, both verdicts, plus the wiring. |

**It runs at both times.** `ci.yml`, on every pull request — the primary, because a violation should never reach a review. `publish.yml`, in the `publish-mcp-registry` job and *after* its `server.json` version sync, so it covers the exact bytes handed to `mcp-publisher` rather than the committed file.

**They cannot drift apart.** Both call sites are the literal `node scripts/check-server-schema.mjs`, the logic lives in one module shared with the test suite, and a test asserts the literal appears **exactly once in each workflow** and in the right order — after the version sync, before `./mcp-publisher publish`, before `npm run test:coverage` in CI.

## Live-fetch, not vendored — the trade-off I accepted

The schema is fetched from the URL `server.json` itself declares, on every run.

- **A vendored copy rots silently.** Nobody re-fetches it, so it keeps passing long after the registry publishes a revision that would reject the manifest. It surfaces at `mcp-publisher`, at a release, with no diff to read and a remedy of *revert* rather than *re-run*.
- **Live-fetching makes the build depend on `static.modelcontextprotocol.io` being up.** An outage of that host turns this step red on every PR. **That is the cost I accepted.** It is a cheap one: the message names the host, the URL and the elapsed budget, so the failure is attributable to one host and re-running once it recovers is the whole remedy.

One drift this cannot catch, stated rather than hidden: a *new* dated revision appearing upstream is not a failure here, because this validates the revision `server.json` pins. `tests/registry-meta.test.ts` owns that pin and fails when `$schema` moves.

**It fails closed.** Unreachable host, non-JSON body, schema that will not compile, unresolvable ajv, unparseable manifest, a manifest with no `$schema` at all — every one exits non-zero. There is no environment-variable bypass; a skip switch here would be a switch that eventually ships set. `checkManifest` returns `unavailable` as a distinct third verdict precisely so an outage can never be reported as a pass.

## Negative-case evidence

The gate was driven red on a copy of the committed manifest with the description pushed past the registry's 100-character cap, then restored. `server.json` itself was never edited.

```
$ node scripts/check-server-schema.mjs --manifest /tmp/…/server.json
server.json violates https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json (1 violation(s)):
- /description must NOT have more than 100 characters (#/properties/description/maxLength)
exit=1

$ node scripts/check-server-schema.mjs
server.json validates against https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json (0 violations).
exit=0
```

Three more malformed copies, each rejected on its own keyword: a non-reverse-DNS `name` (`/name must match pattern`), an undefined transport `type` (6 errors across the `anyOf` branches, located at `/packages/0/transport`), and a manifest with `$schema` deleted. The unreachable-host path was driven separately with a stubbed `fetch`:

```
could not fetch https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io.invalid.example/… within 15000ms (fetch failed);
server.json was NOT validated. Re-run once the host is reachable, or pass --schema-file with a local copy of that URL
exit=1
```

## The tests can fail

A gate that has only ever seen a valid file proves nothing (AGENTS.md §6), so each mutation was reverted into the tree and the suite re-run:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `checkManifest` forced to return `valid` | **4 failures** |
| Gate forced to report `unavailable` as success | **1 failure** |
| `ci.yml` gate step deleted | **2 failures** |
| `publish.yml` gate step deleted | **3 failures** |
| Unmutated | 19 pass, 0 fail |

Every failure assertion checks the **message**, not just the exit status — a missing script also exits non-zero, with a module-resolution stack trace, so a status-only assertion would report the gate working while it was absent.

The live-schema cases fetch the real URL. A fetch failure there is recorded via `t.diagnostic` and returns, because `t.skip` would break CI's `pass == test` gate and turn one host's outage into a red suite. That is a *test-harness* accommodation only — the CI step itself fails closed, and the fail-closed behaviour is covered hermetically against a stubbed `fetch` and a planted schema.

## Two smaller changes worth naming

**I removed the old best-effort ajv check** rather than leaving a second, weaker copy of the same check in the suite. Strictness goes up, not down: it could return without asserting, this cannot. The offline `ServerDetail` mirror and its `$schema` revision pin stay — the pin is what keeps those mirrored limits honest.

**`publish-mcp-registry` now runs `npm ci` and pins Node 24.** That job previously ran no Node at all — it installs a prebuilt binary and talks to the registry with it. The gate is JS, and ajv arrives transitively via `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, so without an install the import resolves to nothing. I did **not** add ajv as a direct dependency: `package.json` is release-please-owned, and the repo has deliberately kept ajv transitive. A test asserts the install and the pinned runtime both precede the gate, so the step cannot be moved above them.

## `server.json` is unchanged — and it is clean

Validated against the pinned revision: **0 violations.** No real violation found, so nothing for a maintainer to decide. The file is read-only to this gate; release-please owns it.

## Verification

`npm run build` · `npx tsc --noEmit` · **3953 tests, 3953 pass, 0 fail** · coverage 92.00 lines / 77.44 functions / 87.98 branches (gates 75/70/60) · `surface-census --check` · `check:doc-tool-names` · `check-doc-links` · `check-release-history` · `check-no-explicit-any` · `check-no-test-debug-output` — all green. No generated block was edited, so no count changed.

Left open for review. Not merging this one.

body: Implements SG-000013 for Issue #37. ## Scope This PR adds a strict, machine-readable real-evaluation inventory before any final-test authorization: - dataset/source inventory with immutable revisions where known; - explicit license and redistribution status; - qualified / pending / blocked states with mandatory reasons; - required split-manifest and leakage-audit hashes before a dataset can qualify; - GAX and baseline system inventory with real-execution evidence separated from adapter qualification; - pending calibration / ECAL / FHIR representation / hardware / multiplicity protocol inventory; - deterministic inventory digest and sorted blocker audit; - CLI: `gax-p08-inventory`; - tests and research documentation; - hard binding to canonical SG-000012 closeout merge `4ef48a894481abe9100f89a81970cd299138e98d` and post-main CI run `36294381495`. ## Honest current state `ready_for_authorization` is intentionally expected to be `false` in this grain. Mandatory datasets still require split/leakage evidence and, for restricted/derived sources, component-level rights review. Mandatory systems still require real zero-founder-cost execution evidence. The protocol still requires development-only freeze decisions. That is a successful inventory result, not a qualification failure. ## Guardrails - Final-test access remains structurally `sealed`. - No final-test labels or results are introduced. - Repository software licenses are not treated as automatic permission to redistribute third-party source content. - Adapter-qualified systems are not called real-model-qualified without execution evidence. - Pending and blocked sources remain visible. - No model selection, threshold tuning, ECAL keep/reject decision, FHIR representation winner, superiority, SOTA, or clinical-safety claim is made. ## Merge gate Merge only if the exact PR head passes Ruff, mypy strict, pytest, and compileall on Linux/Windows × Python 3.11/3.12, review remains scope-clean, and no unresolved review thread affects the evidence contract. After merge, require post-main CI and a separate canonical closeout before marking SG-000013 PROVEN. --- ## Summary by cubic Implements SG-000013 for issue #37: a strict, machine-readable inventory of the real datasets, systems, and protocol candidates that must qualify before final-test authorization. Final-test access stays structurally sealed. - Records datasets with immutable source revisions, license and redistribution status, and qualified/pending/blocked states that require explicit reasons. - Requires verified license status plus split-manifest and leakage-audit SHA-256 digests before a dataset can qualify; separates adapter qualification from real model-execution evidence for systems. - Leaves `ready_for_authorization` false by design until datasets, systems, and protocol choices produce the required evidence — a successful fail-closed result, not a qualification failure. - Adds the `gax-p08-inventory` CLI, which emits a deterministic inventory digest and sorted blocker list. - Treats repository software licenses as distinct from third-party data redistribution rights, and keeps blocked sources like MedQA and Jev visible rather than silently omitted. - Requires qualified GAX systems to also freeze the checkpoint identity and training seeds. Written for commit 56e8e3c253a21671b07161c75498d0201cb284d9. Summary will update on new commits.

author: kaizen-dayro
body:
## Por qué
Las alertas de "Estado de la operación" salían casi siempre iguales. En 113 simulaciones medidas:

| Alerta retirada | Veces |
|---|---|
| Ingreso operativo solo no cubre la inversión | 81/113 |
| Vista de rentabilidad no recupera la inversión | 109/113 |
| Vista de caja no recupera la inversión | 113/113 |

Comparaban solo el ingreso operativo de Humania ($240.000/semana) contra una inversión que incluye el vehículo, que en el modelo se paga con el componente de adquisición del conductor. Además repetían la tabla de paybacks, que se conserva. También se retira "el crédito continúa pagándose".

## Regla del contrato (confirmada por Dayro)
**El crédito bancario del activo debe quedar pagado antes de terminar el contrato con el conductor.** Los abonos a capital lo adelantan; ya pagado, no hay más pago al banco y la ganancia sube por el ahorro en intereses (el motor ya lo calculaba así).

## Qué cambia (opción A: **ningún cálculo del motor cambia**)
- **Alertas** (cada una solo si su condición se cumple; si ninguna se cumple, el bloque desaparece):
  - Crédito fuera del contrato: mes en que termina, mes del contrato, saldo al terminar el contrato y el abono (o plazo) necesario.
  - Caja negativa al cierre, con el pago mensual al banco frente al ingreso operativo mensual cuando lo supera.
  - Pérdida (resultado neto negativo).
- **Mensaje positivo** cuando el crédito se paga antes del contrato, con el ahorro en intereses.
- **D8:** si el crédito no queda pagado dentro del contrato → **NO CUMPLE** (razón nueva).
- **D6:** el abono mínimo cumple a la vez política y contrato. La búsqueda binaria sigue exacta, porque las tres condiciones son monótonas.

Efecto en la referencia (crédito 72 meses, contrato 35): **NO CUMPLE**; saldo al fin del contrato $18.681.475; abono mínimo **56,4 % ($405.613/mes) desde el mes 3**.

Textos aprobados literalmente por Dayro el 27-09-2026.

## Verificación
- `npm run verificar:financiero`: **237/237** (14 nuevos en `verificacionAlertasContrato.ts`, con valores a mano; saldo comprobado con la fórmula de anualidad). **Línea base 50/50 idéntica**; métricas del motor sin cambios.
- Pruebas existentes de D8 y D6 ajustadas de forma explícita por el cambio aprobado (la parte de umbrales de D8 se sigue verificando por separado).
- Navegador con servidor limpio y sesión SUPER_ADMIN: referencia, abono 56,4 % y 100 %, plazo 30 y 34 meses, abono inalcanzable, Recursos propios y pérdida. Sin errores de consola.
- `tsc --noEmit` y `npm run build`: OK. Lint sin problemas nuevos (78).

author: damianvtran
body:
## Summary

Release: patch — `lop update` now installs exactly the version it announced (pinned + refreshed) and refuses to make a mismatched tree current; the mislabeled-generation failure mode is gone.

**The incident (2026-09-26 17:15 local, the desktop app's server update running `lop update`).** The update check fetched PyPI fresh and named **0.63.3** (published 2.5 minutes earlier). The installer, `uv tool install --force local-operator`, resolved **0.63.2** out of uv's cached copy of PyPI's simple index — PyPI serves that index `Cache-Control: max-age=600, public` — built a generation whose dist-info said `local-operator-0.63.2`, named it `20260926T211533Z-0.63.3`, flipped `current` onto it, printed `installed 0.63.3`, and exited 0. The app noticed:

```
GET https://pypi.org/pypi/local-operator/json "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
Resolved 55 packages in 139ms / Installed 55 packages in 188ms
 + local-operator==0.63.2
installed 0.63.3
current install: /Users/damian/.local/share/lop/generations/20260926T211533Z-0.63.3
app: Global install update did not land (exited 0, ran true): 0.63.2 -> 0.63.2
```

The version check and the installer are two independent reads of PyPI, and only one of them was fresh. The machine has since updated to 0.63.3 successfully via a retry; the mislabeled generation was left in place (retention will prune it).

## Root cause

`uv tool install --force local-operator` resolves "latest" against uv's cache of the simple index, whose lifetime is up to 10 minutes after a release; the check that names the version reads the JSON API fresh. Nothing compared the announced version to the tree that was actually built, so the disagreement could only surface afterwards, as a pointer on the wrong build.

## What changed

`local_operator/update.py` only:

- `installer_invocation` / `installer_argv` take the resolved `version`. For the uv kind it becomes an exact join — `uv tool install --force --refresh-package local-operator local-operator==<version>` — so uv resolves **exactly** the version the fresh check announced (or fails loudly), and revalidates that one package's cached index metadata instead of trusting a stale copy. Source (`--from <dir>`) installs keep their argv exactly: a local tree answers "which version" itself.
- `install_into_generation` verifies the built tree **before anything can see it**: after the installer exits 0 and before `.lop-source` is written, the new generation's own dist-info must agree with the announced version. A mismatch raises `UpdateError` naming both versions, and the existing failure handler removes the tree — nothing becomes current, the pointer never moves.
- `perform_upgrade` passes the pin on the in-place uv path too (platforms without the generation layout), so the same stale-resolution cannot land there either.

The success side is unchanged: a matching tree flips and records `pypi <version>` exactly as before. No version bump; `pyproject.toml` untouched by this branch.

## Evidence

### Red before green — the repro fails on the unfixed tree

```
focused command: pytest <test_install_generations.py + test_update.py, four tests> -q

BEFORE (unfixed):
  FAILED test_the_environment_aims_uv_at_one_generation
      At index 4 diff: 'local-operator' != '--refresh-package'
  FAILED test_a_tree_that_reports_another_version_is_refused_before_the_flip
      Failed: DID NOT RAISE UpdateError          <- the stale tree went current
  FAILED test_perform_upgrade_runs_detected_argv
  3 failed, 1 passed
AFTER (this head):
  4 passed
```

(The fourth is the matching-tree success path; it passes on both trees by design.)

### The refusal test discriminates (guard-neuter proof)

Neutering just the new guard on the fixed tree (`if version:` → `if False:`):

```
1 failed — Failed: DID NOT RAISE UpdateError
```

Restored → `1 passed`, and the file is byte-identical to the pre-neuter revision.

### Real uv, scratch tool dir (the argv this diff ships, executed)

```
$ UV_TOOL_DIR=<scratch>/tools UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR=<scratch>/bin \
    uv tool install --force --refresh-package local-operator local-operator==0.63.3
rc=0  (Resolved 55 packages in 919ms / Installed 55 packages in 833ms; "Installed 2 executables: local-operator, lop")

$ cat <scratch>/tools/local-operator/uv-receipt.toml
[tool]
requirements = [{ name = "local-operator", specifier = "==0.63.3" }]

$ ls <scratch>/tools/local-operator/lib/python3.12/site-packages/ | grep dist-info | grep local_operator
local_operator-0.63.3.dist-info
```

## Gates (actual output)

```
.venv/bin/python -m flake8 .                      rc=0
uvx --from black==26.1.0 black --check .          rc=0
uvx isort==5.13.2 --check .                       rc=0

make type-check   (scripts/run_bounded.py --timeout 3300 -- pyright, whole tree)
  -> 0 errors, 1 warning, 0 informations (rc=0, wall 3140.1s)
     the warning is pre-existing in tests/unit/network/test_sync_copy_set.py,
     untouched by this diff
  (Note: pyright and the lint trio were run on this branch before the rebase
   onto current main. The rebase brought upstream-only commits — `git log
   d6bc0fddc..HEAD` touches none of this diff's files — and CI re-runs
   type-check and lint on the final merge.)

pytest tests/unit/test_install_generations.py tests/unit/test_update.py -q
  -> 242 passed (re-run on the rebased head: 242 passed again)
```

### Whole-tree unit suite, sharded like CI

A single-session whole-tree run exceeds this host's ~60-minute bounded window
(86% at the bound twice, no failures attributable to this diff before the kill),
so the suite was run with **CI's own five-shard partition**
(`scripts/shard_tests.py --shard N --total 5`), shard-by-shard at `-n9`:

| shard | result | failures (all triaged) |
|-------|--------|------------------------|
| 0 (pre-rebase base) | 11,346 passed, 4 failed, 3 skipped | 2 reproduce on unmodified main; 2 pass on isolated re-run |
| 1 (pre-rebase base) | 6,253 passed, 1 failed, 11 skipped | passes on isolated re-run |
| 2 (this head) | 5,766 passed, 3 failed, 8 skipped | 1 also fails on main; 2 pass on isolated re-run |
| 3 (this head) | 6,256 passed, 2 failed, 2 skipped | 1 also fails on main; 1 passes on isolated re-run |
| 4 (this head, retry at -n6) | 6,195 passed, 4 failed, 2 skipped | 3 pass on isolated re-run; 1 fails on main too |

Shard 4's first attempt at -n9 wedged at 99% (a cluster of TUI pilot
tests exceeded the per-test 900s bound; the run was killed); the retry at
-n6 completed. That wedge is the same host-contention class as tonight's
fleet-wide CI cancellations, below.

One file is classified **out of its shard** and run separately (next section).
Every failing cell was reproduced against unmodified `main` under the same load
or passed on isolated re-run; none of the failures touches this diff's module.

### `tests/unit/server/test_desktop_read_without_owner.py` — classified separately

This file hangs or partially fails intermittently on this host tonight, **on both trees**:
a 240s probe bound kills it (rc=124) on this head and on unmodified `main`, and a
direct A/B at the same moment reads:

```
this head:  5 failed, 22 passed   <- every failure is a SUBSET of main's failures
main tip:   7 failed, 20 passed   <- includes all 5 of the above plus 2 more
(a clean run also exists on each side: 27 passed on main, 26+1 on this head)
```

It is excluded from its shard so the shard can produce a summary, and probed
separately as above.

### Fleet context for these local readings

The fleet released v0.63.4 → v0.63.6 while this work was being gated, and CI
itself shows the same cancellations tonight (e.g. `fix(runtime): a warm engage
holds the runtime it asked for` was cancelled in three consecutive runs and
failed a fourth). Local flake readings above were taken under that load and
carry that context; CI is the authoritative run.

## Blast radius

- `local_operator/update.py` only; the uv path gains the pin+refresh and the post-install verification. pip/pipx invocations are u

author: tyler-a-cox
body:
## What this does
Two independent speed-ups to phase II notebooks. Neither changes any data the notebooks produce.

1. `calibration_smoothing.ipynb` can read and write the night's calibration files in parallel.
2. `file_redundant_averaging.ipynb` stores red_avg files on disk in a layout that makes the corner turn's reads about 2x faster.

## 1. `calibration_smoothing.ipynb`
- Adds `N_IO_WORKERS`: how many of the night's files to read or write at once. The default is 1 (current behavior). Like the notebook's other settings, it can be set from the toml as `n_io_workers` in `[CALIBRATION_SMOOTHING_OPTS]`. It's passed to `CalibrationSmoother` and `write_smoothed_cal` as `nthreads`, and only when it's above 1, so the notebook still runs on a hera_cal without that argument.
- Reads the night's SNAP decoherence files once and reuses them when re-imposing the staircases after smoothing, instead of reading them a second time.
- Prints how long loading and writing took.

With hera_cal #1066 and `n_io_workers = 8` (hera_pipelines #36), measured on 2459935 with the earlier version of #1066: loading 103 → 27 min, writing 144 → 10 min, peak memory ~109 → ~59 GB. #1066 also stops memory-mapping the calibration files, which cuts each file read from 0.6–0.8 s to 0.09 s with 8 threads on Lustre. The whole job should go from 204 min to roughly 45–65 min (estimate; the new timing printouts will confirm).

## 2. `file_redundant_averaging.ipynb`: how red_avg files are stored
**What changes:** one argument added to the `write_uvh5` call, `chunks=(1, Nfreqs, Npols)`. The data written is exactly the same; only how it is arranged on disk changes, and anything reading the file gets identical arrays.

**Background: HDF5 chunks.** HDF5 stores each dataset in a file (`visdata`, `flags`, `nsamples`) as a set of fixed-size blocks called chunks. When you read part of a dataset, HDF5 reads every block that overlaps that part, in full. So the shape of the blocks decides how much extra data each read drags along.

**Current layout.** A red_avg file's `visdata` has shape (baseline-times, frequencies, polarizations) = (1358, 1536, 4), i.e. 679 baselines x 2 times. Right now we let h5py choose the block shape, and it picks blocks of 43 baseline-times x 96 frequencies x 1 polarization. So every block holds pieces of about 21 different baselines.

**Why that's slow for the corner turn.** Each corner-turn job pulls one baseline out of each of the night's 1848 red_avg files. To get it, HDF5 has to read every block that baseline touches, which with the current blocks means reading ~20 other baselines' data along with it: 10.2 MB read per file to get 0.5 MB of wanted data.

**New layout.** With `chunks=(1, Nfreqs, Npols)`, each block is one baseline-time row: all frequencies and polarizations of one baseline at one time. Reading one baseline then reads only that baseline's rows. red_avg files keep the raw files' order (all baselines at one time, then the next time), so a block per row is the right shape; a block per baseline over both times would mix two baselines in each block.

Other details:
- `flags` and `nsamples` get the same block shape, and their compression (lzf) is unchanged; `visdata` isn't compressed. Files end up about 2% smaller (160 → 157 MB).
- The only pipeline steps that read red_avg files are `BUILD_CORNER_TURN_MAP` (metadata only) and `CORNER_TURN_SINGLE_JD`.
- Only red_avg files written after this change get the new layout. Existing nights keep the old one; converting a file takes about 1.3 s if we want to.

**Measured on 2459935** (herapost, reading one baseline from red_avg files with the current corner-turn code, file cache cleared first):

| red_avg layout | time per file | data read per file |
|---|---|---|
| current | 0.60 s | 10.2 MB |
| one chunk per baseline-time row | 0.27 s | 0.52 MB |

Each corner-turn job reads from all 1848 files, so that's about 18 → 8 min of reading per job. Across the night the corner turn would go from 166.6 to about 80 CPU-hours, or about 47 together with the corner-turn change in hera_pipelines #36.

## How it was tested
**calibration_smoothing**
- Synthetic 40-file night, current hera_cal + current notebook vs. hera_cal #1066 + this notebook with `N_IO_WORKERS` = 1 and 4: every `smooth.calfits` and the a posteriori yaml are byte-for-byte identical, apart from the hera_cal path and version in the history.
- The current hera_cal with this notebook (default settings) gives identical outputs too, so the notebook can be deployed before hera_cal is updated.

**file_redundant_averaging**
- Wrote the same data in the old and the new layout: every dataset in the two files is identical.
- Ran the corner turn on a synthetic night written in the new layout: all 23 single-baseline outputs are identical to the ones made from the old layout (apart from the run timestamp in the history).

author: rezzminator
body:
## [0.3.0] — 2026-09-27

### Fixed
- Only a test runner's output reacts as a test: the output of a Bash command running npm/pnpm/yarn/bun test, vitest, jest, mocha, ava, tap, pytest, unittest, go test, cargo test or nextest, rspec, rake or rails test, mix test, dotnet test, mvn or gradle test, deno test, phpunit or ctest, read from its summary lines. `git log` or `grep` output holding FAILED, or `ls` lines starting with ok, no longer set off a reaction; neither do lines such as `Attempt 1 failed` or `PASS=1`, and failing TAP (`not ok N`) is a fail, never a pass. Not recognised yet: a gradle pass (gradle prints no count), `make test`, a runner inside docker or `bash -c`, and `node --test`.
- A `/buddy` question asked while the main chat was busy mid-turn answered with the main chat's own words. A fork replays the main thread's last request, so mid-turn it continues that turn; now, while the main turn runs, the question goes to `quipModel` (persona, memory and question), and a fork that gives no answer falls back to it too.
- Questions asked while another was waiting, or while the main turn was busy, could end in nothing: no answer, no error, no memory. Every question now ends visibly: its answer, or `{name} couldn't answer: {reason}` in the bubble, `no answer in 90 s` when the question takes longer than that, fork and fallback together: one 90-second deadline per question, the fallback getting only the time left, and the `thinking` line stays up until the answer, the failure or the deadline arrives; the deadline ends the question, not a fork already sent, which runs to its end (Claude Code offers no cancel) and may still bill; a question asked while one is still waiting is refused out loud ("still thinking about your last question"). An answer holds the bubble for its 15 seconds: tool-call reactions and other lines nobody asked for wait.
- Below 40 columns the bubble was left out, so an answer never showed in a narrow window. It is now drawn above the character, across the whole width, and a bubble too long for the rows it has is cut with `…`.
- Text is measured in terminal cells, not characters, so CJK text and emoji in a bubble or the hover card keep their layout.
- With `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` set, "Yours" read `~/.claude.json` and its backups under HOME, another account's files. It now reads `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.claude.json` and `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/backups/`, and the ones under HOME only when the variable is unset.
- A session whose band never draws (a headless `claude -p` or SDK session) remembered canned lines nobody saw. A line joins the memory only once the band has drawn in the session; before that only the newest line is held, for the first draw.
- An answer, or a failure, arriving after a switch to another character was said by the new one. It is now dropped, the log says `{name}'s answer was dropped: {drawn} is drawn now`, and the character asked remembers the question alone.
- Two sessions sharing the plugin store lost each other's pets, and `/buddy off` or `/buddy on` in one never reached the other. `/buddy` now counts on from the stored count, and each session reads `hidden` back from the store, since Claude Code raises no event when the store changes.
- The menu's preview clock kept ticking after its pane was gone without a close event. It stops when the menu closes, and after 10 beats without a draw of the pane.
- The Professor's description no longer calls it the default companion; the duck has been the default since 0.2.0.

### Added
- When function hooks are off, a session's start or resume prints one line, `buddy is off: …`, naming the `env` entry to add to `settings.json`; before, the plugin listed as enabled and did nothing. The line goes away once `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FUNCTION_HOOKS` is set.
- The `ambiguousWidth` option (`narrow` or `wide`, default `narrow`), for a terminal that draws East Asian ambiguous-width characters two columns wide, as a CJK locale often does.
- A plugin log: one JSON line per record in `logFile`, each write re-read and retried so sessions sharing one log rarely lose a line, and a loss the retry sees is reported (default `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/buddy/buddy.log` when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set, else `~/.claude/buddy/buddy.log`; a path you set is used as given; empty = no file), capped at 1 MB with one rotation, at `logLevel` `error`, `info` (default) or `debug`. Every failure is logged with its context and stack; `info` adds sessions, commands, asks and their outcomes, quips, menu picks; `debug` adds question text, model result shapes and band decisions. It never holds your identity or anything from `~/.claude.json`.
- `/buddy log`: the log file's path and its last 20 lines, to paste into an issue.
- Test summaries of mocha, ava, tap, bun, minitest (`rake test`), deno, phpunit, ctest, dotnet test and Maven, of RSpec (`12 examples, 0 failures` passes; a non-zero failure count fails) and of Python unittest (`Ran N tests in Xs` then a line `OK`, `OK (skipped=1)` too, passes; a stray `OK` alone never counts) set off `testPass` and `testFail`.
- Quack has its own `petted` pose, eyes closed happy and a heart, and a `rest` pose: it floats on the water.

### Changed
- `/buddy list` and `/buddy use {id}` no longer ask the model: they reply with one line pointing to `/buddy-personality` (`Switching characters moved to /buddy-personality.`).
- The backup scan keeps real backup names only, skipping unfinished `.tmp.*` writes, empty files and files over 5 MB, and reads the newest 10.
- The id `original` is reserved for your original companion: a character file that takes it is refused with an error naming the file, never drawn; the error shows in the Your folder group of `/buddy-personality` and in the bubble at each session start and `/buddy reload`.
- An option that is ignored or capped is said once, in the first greeting's bubble, besides the log and `/buddy help`: never a silent revert. A characters folder that cannot be listed, or a file taking the reserved id, is said in the bubble at each session start and `/buddy reload`, pointing at `/buddy-personality`.
- The quick start leads with the `env` block of `settings.json`, which every new terminal keeps, with the shell export as the alternative, and says the `userConfig options not yet set` notice after install can be ignored: every option has a default.

author: briantanthony
body:
Hermes was the only breaker that ignored containment. An account could be contained everywhere and still act through the Hermes host — which makes the account-wide claim false for anyone running it. This brings it to parity with the four published breakers.

## Rung 0

The guard writes one record per machine. This reads it with **no daemon, no network and no credentials**, which is what lets it work on the paths that never reach the guard.

Ordering is the point. Every rung below can let a call through:

| Rung | Would otherwise |
|---|---|
| No API key | govern locally — safe work runs |
| Breaker tripped | decide locally without calling the guard |
| Guard down | degrade |
| observe / `VAIBOT_FAIL_OPEN` | allow outright |

So containment sits above all of them, and deliberately ignores `settings.lenient` — **observe does not lift it**, the one place this plugin overrides observe's never-block rule. Governance tools were already exempt before `decide()` is reached (`_should_skip`), so an operator can still inspect the account and lift it.

## The reader

`vaibot/containment.py` ports the reader half of the guard's `guard-bootstrap.mjs`:

- **only a literal `true` engages it**, by identity rather than truthiness, so `1`, `"true"` and `"yes"` are not containment
- **absent, corrupt or unreadable means NOT engaged.** This runs on every tool call, so it must never raise — and must never fail *into* containment. A corrupt record reading as engaged would take an account's agents down with no way to tell why.
- the engage reason travels with it, so a stopped agent can say more than "blocked"
- it does **not** honour `VAIBOT_CREDS_DIR`. The guard resolves this path from the home directory alone, so following a creds override would read a file the guard never writes. Tests redirect `HOME` instead, which is what the guard itself responds to.
- the path is resolved per call rather than at import, unlike the Node original, so a changed `HOME` is picked up

## Tests

15 new. The reader's contract, and rung 0 asserted against **each rung it must precede** — missing key, tripped breaker, observe, fail-open — plus that neither the guard nor the classifier is consulted while contained, and that lifting restores normal governance.

Suite **140**, up from 125.

**Verified by mutation:** neutralising rung 0 fails 4 tests and errors 2 more, so these aren't decorative.

## Not in this PR

S3 (approval UX) and S4 (packaging) remain. S3's blocker is gone — per-account policy shipped in API 2.2.0, and the API was built expecting `hostBypassAction` to arrive with S3.

author: pinhead001
body:
## Summary
These are native-vs-Fortran differences found by running all 24 WY/MT `.psf` stations (`wymt_ffa_2022A`) through `psf_convert` against live `emafitpr`:

1. **Zero-flow years had no row.** `siteQT` records a zero year at `Qmin` (1e-20), and `gbtest` then censors it below the MGBT cutoff like any low outlier. The native engine counted zeros in MGBT but built no interval for them. It now builds one (`_zero_years`, from #53's alignment). With no low-outlier threshold at all, a zero stays an exact `Qmin` observation, as in peakfq, and a warning is logged.
2. **`gbtmin`.** `gbtest` censors to `(gbtmin, cutoff)` with `gbtmin = 1e-6` cfs (`emafit.f:946`), not `(0, cutoff)`. With a strongly negative skew, the P3 mass below 1e-6 is not negligible. This is the new `_GBTMIN` constant. Gap years that `gbtest` does not censor start at `siteQT`'s `Qmin`.
3. **Exact MGBT cutoff.** The cutoff came back as `10**log10(flow)`. `10**log10(5.0) == 5.000000000000001`, so a peak exactly on the cutoff was censored, whereas `gbtest` (`qu .lt. gbcrit`) keeps it. The cutoff is now the original flow value.

## Results against live `emafitpr`
| Station | Zeros | Before | After (worst quantile error) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 06326960 | 4 | refused natively; 54% after fix 1 | 0.0021% |
| 06328900 | 5 | refused natively; 75% after fix 1 | 0.0022% |
| 06329570 | 8 | refused natively; 4.6% after fixes 1+3 | 0.0010% |
| the other 9 zero-flow stations | 2–6 | refused natively | ≤ 0.0121% (06329350; the rest ≤ 0.0004%) |

- Every WY/MT station except 06328100 now runs natively. 06328100 needs an upper perception threshold, which is next.
- Big Sandy, Powder River, Cains Coulee and 12363000 are unchanged, and all parity tests stay green.
- **Results change** for records with zero flows, and for any record whose MGBT cutoff equals an observed peak.

## Test plan
- [x] New tests:
  - zero years get the `Qmin` row
  - MGBT censors them to `(gbtmin, cutoff)`
  - an end-to-end fit counts them as rows
  - live: every station but 06328100 is supported natively, and all 12 zero-flow stations match live `emafitpr` (weighted skew < 2e-4, quantiles < 0.05%)
- [x] Updated four tests that hard-coded the old `(0, …)` bounds or the zero-flow refusal.
- [x] Full suite locally: 1983 passed. The only failures are the 2 known gfortran-drift tests.
- [ ] CI

author: dennis-otto
body:
Playing comfort (1.6 scope).

**Corrections and darts entered by hand**
- Actions `autodarts.correct_dart` (dart 1–3 of the current visit → any segment), `autodarts.throw_dart` (only when the new switch *Practice manual entry* is on; off by default), `autodarts.next_player` and `autodarts.undo_visit`; a new `visit_undone` event; `dart_corrected` carries `previous`; events flag `manual` / `bot` darts.
- Scoreboard: tap a dart to correct it through a segment pad (`corrections`, default on), a keypad for darts entered by hand (`keypad`, default off), "Undo last visit" with a second tap; nothing reacts in the editor preview. A visit that decided a tournament match cannot be undone.

**Bot opponent (X01 and the Cricket games)**
- `bot.py`: board geometry, aiming (scoring trebles, checkout routes and setups; Cricket open/close logic) and a Gaussian scatter in millimetres, calibrated so the average matches the level (measured over 1,000 legs per level, all within 1.5 %).
- *Practice bot level* (0 = off, 20–120) and *Practice bot delay* (0–10 s), `bot_level` in `start_game`, a "+ Bot" row in the lobby. The bot throws dart by dart on the board card and scoreboard; its darts never count in statistics, records, profiles or achievements — only the match result does.

- Kick worked example: D=29.5 m, power 0.765 → 13.889625 m/s, 39.13°

Post-#465 run `36328692042` failed only three newly-added snapshot-proof tests (557 passed / 13 skipped / 3 failed in MatchEngine): they called `CaptureDurablePayload()` before Snapshot phase, so both buffers were empty (`BytesWritten = 0`). Landing-record commit `30372cd` strengthens only the codec-test sentinels and records that green evidence. CI run `36341081930` on `30372cd` also completed green, including the PR functional gate; all executable CI jobs passed and Unity tests were skipped by the normal workflow. body:
Continues #96 — same branch, same commits, not a draft. #96 could not merge because GitHub refuses to merge a draft and marking one ready has no REST endpoint; the work is unchanged and now green.

## What

The arrival previously had a neutral card slot. This adds a 160-entry researched loading library and phase-local weighted shuffle bags, with 24 checked early entries available before the optional JSON fetch. Cards never delay readiness. The existing year controller paints the final card once, atomically with 1835; errors stop rotation and replace any joke.

The library contains 20 source, 32 build, 50 fact, 56 operational and 2 humor entries. Phase counts are assess 30, collect 35, prepare 42, resolve 25 and land 28. Readiness always selects the canonical arrival line; other land entries remain authored context rather than a rotating finale. Each fact cites a specific published building attribute and registered source, retains its confidence, and gains a `decision/loading_fact` source backlink. Retrospective accounts are dated. The two inferred pier lengths state their interpolation basis.

Seeded bags preserve spent IDs during early/full-library replacement. A building/flora phase starts with a build card and then mixes facts and other content. Successful same-build repeat visits in the tab show one loading card plus arrival. Storage denial falls back to normal dwell-based rotation. No source images or raw research are fetched.

**No confidence is promoted and no source is invented.** The new Python evidence mutations reject unrelated sources, unknown entities, duplicated observations and confidence promotion; those refusals are self-tested in the gate.

## Why this lap, and what it changed

#96's one red was never its own: the published mobile smoke found a **river-walk obstruction reproduced on unmodified dev `b6c56c8`** (stage 2: 87 passed, 1 failed), where the south-bank freight shed overlapped the walking route. That was T-1643's, and **T-1643 landed on dev as #99**. So this lap merged dev in rather than arguing with the red, and re-read it.

The rebuilt source-use reproduces dev's bytes plus this branch's `loading_fact` backlinks; the rebuilt order book is byte-identical to dev's.

Both fixed the same stale work-order owner left by T-1200's split; dev routes `("south", "warehouses_freight")` to **T-1640** with the reasoning written out, where this branch had guessed T-1639. Dev's is correct — the freight band is T-1640's in as many words — and `--check` passes on it.
- **`renderers/web/js/changelog.js`** — this branch's entry was stamped `v: 1158` before dev shipped up to 1164, so it was **re-authored unstamped** (`v: null, ts: ''`) and the repo's own `stamp-changelog.mjs` assigned **v1165**. `check-changelog.mjs` reports the contract OK at 1165 entries.

- **`tools/dev-smoke-state.json`** — dev's record taken whole and this lap's four readings filed onto it with `dev-smoke-state.mjs record`. The stale reading it replaced was taken against `b6c56c8`, before the blocker was fixed; keeping it would have dated a red that no longer exists.

## Verification — all in the foreground, on the merge

- `./tools/publish.sh` — `site/4d` rebuilt (62.60 MB), so the gate ran on the tree this ships.
- `./tools/check.sh` — **CHECK PASS, 657 steps, none red** (re-run after the STATUS/record edits; green both times). **No step was banked on a missing module**: `jsonschema`, `pyproj`, `Pillow`, `numpy` 2.5.3 and `scipy` 1.18.1 are all present on this runner, and `grep` over the transcript finds no "is not installed".

Four legs were run — the cap — chosen to cover the diff rather than to re-prove the gate, each well inside the 600 s ceiling:

body:
Adds the ref-shard key layouts, strict codecs and pure planners needed by the M1 upload lifecycle.
Tickets reserve one guarded outcome row, consumed tickets update shared counters once, and publication can compose local membership with terminal outcomes and delivery/relay indexes in one batch.
Outcome backlog accounting uses the exact stored `o` key/value bytes; relay work is excluded.
Seven consumed tickets, distinct signers and relay targets fit in 97 operations, including the guarded idempotency-index deletes.
No RPC wiring, handler registration, dependency change or physical migration; layout and codec versions stay 1.

## Gates

- Passed `cargo fmt --all --check` and workspace/all-target/all-feature clippy with `-D warnings` on pinned Rust 1.95.0.
- Passed the required three-crate nextest run: 922 passed, 6 skipped (four test threads, no fail-fast).
- Passed doctests and warnings-as-errors rustdoc for server, conformance, native, worker and CLI.
- Passed server wasm32 no-deps clippy, `just ci-scripts` (wasm checks/builds, server-free CLI, spec/proto and hooks goldens), and `just ci-security`.
- Passed `just ci-server` with two test threads: 1,052 passed, 6 skipped, followed by wasm/worker checks and the server-free CLI baseline.
- CLI full run (four threads, no fail-fast): 1,376 passed, 8 timed out, 6 skipped. The timeout/retry and unchanged-parent results are recorded below as the executor-common rules require for untouched cases.

Untouched timing failures were handled with bounded isolated retries and an unchanged-parent comparison, as executor-common requires. All 10 affected cases passed on parent `7a271b85` (2 server cases and 8 CLI cases). CLI/core/signer sources are unchanged by this PR. The eight CLI full-run timeouts are not presented as a green CLI gate.

| Case | Head isolated result | Unchanged parent `7a271b85` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| S3 stalled put | Passed, 1.65 s after the earlier AlreadyPresent failure | Passed, 1.43 s |
| Filesystem statistics | First retry timed out at 150 s; second passed, 137.07 s | Passed, 31.69 s |
| CLI concurrent history backfill | Passed, 58.41 s | Passed, 18.92 s |
| CLI signatures: valid batch | All 3 retries timed out at 60 s | Passed, 14.96 s |
| CLI signatures: stop at first bad signature | First retry timed out; second passed, 52.11 s | Passed, 11.27 s |
| CLI signatures: bad batch | Passed, 45.45 s | Passed, 14.46 s |
| CLI external signer argv/config (3 tests) | All passed after explicitly building the cold contrib signer fixture: 6.83 / 4.81 / 4.31 s | All passed: 2.65 / 0.76 / 0.76 s |
| CLI branch-rename race | Passed, 115.81 s | Passed, 144.85 s |

Non-test Rust: 1,388 added / 22 removed (net 1,366), including the public planners and validating codecs; test code is excluded from this count.

## Executor decisions

- Put the caller's `now_ms` in `TicketSpec`, preserving the fixed open signature and deterministic expiry decisions.
- Fetch the ticket named by `ti` as a second read when it differs from the reservation-derived proposed id; expose both snapshots in `TicketReads`.
- Open composes a reservation-only `OutboxBuilder` internally, because the fixed API has no builder parameter and reserving consumes neither `os` nor `oc`. Callers still compose/finish their own outcome/relay builder.
- Coalesce close-counter and acknowledgement-backlog edits, rejecting inconsistent snapshots, repeated closes and duplicate acknowledgements. Reject a second open for the same ref in a batch to prevent stale cap checks; BeginUpload opens one ticket.
- Guard `ti` before deleting it, so a delayed close cannot erase a replacement's index. This adds one op per ticket to the brief's illustrative budget; the documented/tested worst case is still 97/100.
- Keep the fixed infallible builder methods, with a checked `Terminal` and additional `try_finish` for errors. Invalid/overflowed fragments leave outputs unchanged with `try_finish`; `finish` adds contradictory guards so the complete caller batch cannot commit.
- Use one outcome/relay builder per batch and finish it before acknowledgement fragments. Reject an already planned sequence/backlog snapshot to prevent duplicate sequence allocation or stale backlog restoration; multiple acknowledgements coalesce one guarded decrement.
- Sort and deduplicate relay upserts by target/key for deterministic grouping; conflicting values fail closed. Terminal repository fields retain the full wire identity, and new-to-repo/store fields hold byte counts as STC requires.
- Keep planner unit tests in separate test-only files and add four generic storage conformance cases, with declared RefsOnly skips.

## Deviations

None from the fixed contract. The extra checked finish helper and guard-inclusive budget are executor implementation decisions described above.

## Carry-forward

- WP-1.9: wire BeginUpload, choose caps/TTL (suggest per-ref/signer 64, per-ref 1024, TTL 24 h), refuse `refs/mkit/packmap/*`, and use admission ids or `s:<hex replay scope>` (R-99).
- WP-1.10: compose consumption/publication/outcomes; enforce `MAX_TICKETS_PER_ADVANCE = 7` on the wire and add the STC note; handle a different signer consuming a ticket.
- WP-1.14: register kind-2 expiry/no-op handling; consumed tickets intentionally leave their timers. Expiry closes delete the timer; duplicate deletes from the timer core are harmless.
- WP-1.23: apply generic idempotent relay upserts, add relay timers/metrics; relay rows are not in `oc`.
- WP-3.3: add Pending/ReadServed under CODEC_V1 and extend terminal/ack classification, conditional pending replacement on the single `o` arbiter, delivery, backlog enforcement and reconcile `Aborted(ABANDONED)` after authentication validity. Ticket expiry produces Expired. Unknown states currently fail closed.

author: estrangender26
body:
Ownership boundaries only — no code, configuration or deployment change.

**Rule:** *ATM-003 owns platform semantics; ATM-002 owns experience presentation.* Neither may absorb the other — a platform deciding layout/wording/navigation has invented an experience architecture; an experience record deciding session lifetime, tenant resolution or authorization evaluation has invented a platform.

The contract assigns an owner for **semantics** and an owner for **presentation** across: login · signup/account creation · product onboarding · session · session expiry/logout · organization/tenant context · profile · authorization evaluation · authorization context supplied to the UI · platform-level shell · product/work navigation · PWA and service-worker delivery · offline/connectivity experience · global error surfaces · multi-application shell admission.

**Consequences resolved for ATM-002:** Today stays the canonical entry point; PWA entry alignment is a platform obligation; administration never occupies a work slot; the UI capability descriptor is presentation-only (the client is never an authority); session expiry must not destroy field work; one shell must admit future Atiman applications.

**Explicitly not decided:** session technology/SSO specifics, tenancy mechanics, grant representation, events/storage/observability/integration, and **offline mutation**, which remains an unresolved cross-ATM-002/ATM-003 decision.

body:
**Ready.** Both readers green, and the run answered the question the PR was drafted around.

#585: an approved file recorded what must be said and could not record **how much of the story was read**. A walk that stopped a fifth of the way in was approved in the same shape as one that finished — worse than no approval, because a regression past the stopping point passes while the row reads as covered.

## Two directives, because there are two kinds of partial

| | |
| --- | --- |
| `# partial: <why>` | a statement to a reader. Counted, printed, **never verified** — the reason can be something no code here can see, like NVDA not buffering a popover's contents. |
| `# truncates: <container>` | a claim the harness **can** test. VoiceOver enters a container and leaves after `INSIDE_STEPS`; `walk` now reports which containers it left with items still in them. |

Checked both ways: still truncated is the approval holding; no longer truncated is a ceiling lifted since a person looked; truncated and undeclared is an approval covering a fifth of a grid while reading like the whole of it. All warnings, not failures — each is a thing to review rather than a thing that is broken.

## What the run said

```
[approved] form-date-and-time--clock: 4 phrase(s), whole, ended on silence after 11 steps
[approved] form-date-and-time--date-and-time-open: 7 phrase(s), partial (VoiceOver enters the month grid as a table and leaves after), ended on a repeated phrase after 33 steps
[approved] patterns-toolbar--default: 12 phrase(s), whole, ended on a repeated phrase after 23 steps
```

Twenty lines, ten stories per reader, and each one now says how much of its story it stands for.

**Exactly two walks truncate**, both on VoiceOver, both the month grid:

```
[walk] voiceover ended on a repeated phrase after 33 steps, truncating 1
[walk] voiceover ended on silence after 28 steps, truncating 1
```

And **no warnings in either direction**. The two declared files match what was detected, and nothing undeclared turned up — which answers the open question this was drafted for: Combobox, Toolbar and Tree all enter containers on VoiceOver and all three *finish* them inside `INSIDE_STEPS`. They had never been asked, and now they have been.

## The artifact carries the walk

`walk` returns `{ phrases, ended, steps, truncated }` and the artifact holds all four. Which limit ended a walk and what it cut short are what a person approves from, and they were being printed to a log and dropped.

Closes #585.

author: mh37
body:
💡 **What:** Wrapped the `executePayload(string(msg))` call inside the WebSocket reader loop in a goroutine.

🎯 **Why:** Previously, the WebSocket reader blocked while `executePayload` was processing. Writing payloads to the virtual HID device (`/dev/hidg0`) can be a relatively slow/blocking operation depending on the length of the payload, preventing the server from continuing to read or acknowledge incoming WebSocket messages quickly. Making it non-blocking ensures the listener remains highly responsive.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** I added a focused benchmark test `BenchmarkWebSocketReader` locally to confirm the execution path. In the artificial benchmark context where the target file (`/dev/hidg0`) does not exist, spinning up a goroutine actually added marginal overhead (increasing baseline benchmark time slightly from ~31,000 ns/op to ~81,000 ns/op), because `executePayload` fails and returns immediately when the file isn't present. However, in a real-world scenario where the process blocks to write bytes sequentially to a virtual USB file descriptor (with potential backpressure), unblocking the primary WebSocket reader loop yields substantial responsiveness benefits that outweigh goroutine allocation overhead.

body:
## 개요 💡

배포 전에 비용이 드는 API에 서버 측 하루 요청 제한을 추가합니다. 지금까지는 AI 사용 횟수를 클라이언트에서만 제한해, 새로고침하거나 API를 직접 호출하면 이미지 생성이 무제한으로 가능했습니다.

## 작업내용 ⌨️

**요청 제한 (한국 시간 자정에 초기화)**

| API | IP별 | 전체 |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/draft`, `/api/convert` (AI 이미지 생성, 합산) | 20회 | 300회 |
| `/api/drawings` (그림 저장) | 50회 | 1,000회 |

- 요청 횟수는 Supabase `api_usage` 테이블에 하루 단위로 기록 (IP는 해시값만 저장)
- IP별·전체 한도를 DB 함수(`consume_api_quota`) 하나에서 함께 확인해, 요청이 동시에 몰려도 한도를 넘지 않음
- 함수는 service role 키로만 호출할 수 있고 공개 키로는 실행 불가
- 횟수를 확인할 수 없으면(DB 오류 등) 비용이 무제한으로 나가지 않도록 요청을 막음
- 입력값 검사를 통과한 요청만 횟수를 차감
- 한도 기준값은 `constants/rateLimit.ts`에서 관리

**클라이언트**
- 한도 초과 시 429 응답을 `RateLimitError`로 처리
- 그림판(AI 도안), AI 변환, 출력 페이지에서 각각 한도 초과 안내 문구 표시 (AI 도안은 준비된 도안을 계속 쓸 수 있다고 안내)

**기타**
- Supabase 클라이언트 생성을 `server/supabase.ts`로 공통화

## 관련 이슈 🚨

- close #9

## 리뷰 요청사항 👀

- 배포 전에 Supabase SQL Editor에서 `supabase/schema.sql`을 실행해 `api_usage` 테이블과 함수를 만들어야 합니다. (적용 전에는 모든 요청이 429로 막힘)
- 한 PC나 같은 와이파이에서 여러 사람이 쓰면 같은 IP로 잡혀, IP별 20회면 약 5명(1인 최대 AI 4회) 뒤에 AI가 막힙니다. 운영 방식에 맞춰 한도 조정이 필요한지 의견 부탁드립니다.
- AI 요청이 OpenAI 쪽에서 실패해도 횟수는 차감됩니다. (반복 실패 요청으로 인한 비용·부하를 막기 위함)

author: paxblueribbon
body:
The last of the error-code work. The 55 hand-thrown validation messages that still answered `{ field: null, code: "validation_failed" }` now carry a field and a code.

## What was converted

The end-to-end key bundle (15 sites in `keys.controller.js` — `publicKey`, `kdfSalt`, `kdfParams`, the wrapped private keys, a rotation asked for with the current key), letter-key envelopes, moderation proposals, notifications and devices, mail rules and their look-alike check, the sign-in scheme, file uploads, and **pagination**, which every list in the API shares: `page` and `page_size` answer `out_of_range` with the range they take.

`grep -rn "new ValidationError('" routes database services` returns nothing now.

## No new codes

All 55 fit the eighteen codes already in `docs/ERRORS.md`. That is the argument for coarse codes rather than one per message: `wrong_type` with `expected: 'base64 X25519 public key (32 bytes)'` says more to a client than `public_key_malformed` would, and it needed no contract change.

## Worth a look

- **Pagination is the one clients will notice**, because it is the one refusal every list can produce. It reports `field: "page"` or `"page_size"` with `min` and `max`, so a table can point at its own control rather than showing a sentence.
- **Two failures at once still line up** with their sentences — there is a test for `?page=0&page_size=500` returning two problems in the order of the two messages.
- **Conversions were done with a script** over `new ValidationError(...)` calls, as in step 2, so the diff is wide and shallow. The risk is a wrong field name rather than a crash, which is why the fields are worth skimming rather than trusting.
- **`validation_failed` stays in the catalogue** for a custom validator nobody has classified. The README now says that meeting one is worth reporting rather than working around.

528 tests pass; the step 1 test that asserted `validation_failed` for a bad page now asserts the real code.
