author: jhtonel
body:
## Empilhada sobre a PR #742

Esta branch parte de `origin/725-action-bar-click-fire-aim` (a branch da PR #742, "make the
action bar click-to-fire with aim") e a base deste PR é `725-action-bar-click-fire-aim` — **não**
`tibia-parity`. Ela reaproveita `use-slot.target`/`UseSlotTarget`/`#resolveManualTarget`/
`#resolveUseSlotTarget` que a #742 introduziu, ainda não mesclados em `tibia-parity`. Mesclar
nesta ordem: #742 primeiro, depois este.

## O que mudou

Implementa a issue #726 (ADR 0049 — branch `docs/adr-0048-0051-playable`, ainda não mesclada,
usada aqui só como especificação a seguir):

- **`use-item`/`use-item-on`** (C2S 25/26; `use-result` **S2C 37** — o 36 é `corpse-contents` da
  #722/PR #749, conferido antes de escolher o número): usar um item da mochila/bolsa
  (`ref: { instanceId }`) ou uma unidade do estoque de suprimento (`ref: { supplyId }`) **sem
  passar pela barra de ações**. `ref.supplyId` reaproveita `#useSupply`/`useSupply` (`casting.ts`)
  por inteiro — o MESMO caminho que `use-slot` já usa. `target` é a mesma mira opcional de
  `use-slot` (obrigatória em `use-item-on`).
- **Comida executável** (`packages/sim/src/food.ts`): `feed`/`drainFedMs` implementam o mecanismo
  do `foods.lua` do Canary — `durationMs = value × 12s`, contador `fedMs` capado em 1.200.000 ms
  ("You are full", sem consumir o item no teto). `cheese`/`meat`/`ham`/`dragon-ham`/
  `green-mushroom` viraram `kind: 'consumable'` com os números reais do Canary.
- **`progression.regeneration.requiresFood`** (default `false`, preserva o Huntera): quando
  ligada, `HuntRuleset#onRegen` só aplica o pulso de regeneração com `fedMs > 0`.
- **Executor da `blessing-charge`**: consumir soma `CharacterRuntime.blessings` (capado em 5).
  Ligar isso à redução de perda de item na morte é o ADR 0042/TP-03 — fora do escopo aqui.
- **Exaustão de ação adiada, não recusada** (`exhaust:action`, #690): um `use-item`/
  `use-item-on` que chega com o livro trancado vira `pendingManualAction` (evento
  `pending-manual-action` na fila, nunca contador por tick), reagendado para o vencimento; um
  segundo clique antes disso SUBSTITUI o primeiro. Cooldown de GRUPO/individual da runa/poção
  continua recusa imediata, como sempre.
- **Estoque visível**: `inventory.supplies`/`ammunition` (`[{ id, quantity }]`) expõem
  `supplyStock`/`ammunitionStock` — o jogador vê o que o loot já deu antes de gastar gold.
- **`fed_ms` persiste** como a stamina: migração `0013_726-fed-ms.sql` (aditiva, `bigint default
  0`), levada pelo ticket e pelo extrato (mesmo caminho de `supplyStock`).
- **Cliente**: o menu de contexto da mochila (`ContainerWindow.tsx`) abre no clique direito de um
  item `kind: 'consumable'` — "Usar" manda `use-item` na hora; "Usar com…" arma a mira
  (`state/aim.ts`, generalizado de "mira de slot" para uma união `SlotAim | ItemAim`) e o
  PRÓXIMO clique no mundo/Batalha resolve com `use-item-on`. O `ContextMenu`
  (`shell/ui/ContextMenu.tsx`) foi trazido **idêntico** de `origin/724-sell-and-discard-items`
  (a PR #741 já o criou para "Vender/Descartar") em vez de escrever outro, para a tela nunca ter
  dois menus de contexto. A seção **Suprimentos**, sob a mochila, lista `inventory.supplies` por
  nome (resolvido em `catalogue.bot.supplies`) e contagem — clicar usa direto, clique direito
  abre o mesmo menu; sem sprite, porque o catálogo de suprimento abstrato não carrega
  `appearanceId` hoje (só item de verdade tem essa coluna, FUN-94).

## Verificação

```
pnpm lint                                    # ESLint: No issues found
pnpm typecheck                                # limpo (tsc -b --force + tooling + client + tests)
pnpm vitest run --project unit                # 4353/4377 passaram; 12 suítes falham só por
                                               # TEST_REDIS_URL ausente (infra compartilhada, não
                                               # rodada por instrução — pré-existente, não desta PR)
pnpm docs-check                                # passou
```

23 testes novos: `packages/sim/src/food.test.ts` (6), `packages/sim/src/rulesets/hunt.test.ts`
(9), `packages/client/src/state/aim.test.ts` (+3, mira de item), `packages/client/src/shell/
use-item-intent.test.ts` (2), `packages/client/src/shell/ContainerWindow.test.ts` (+3, seção
Suprimentos).

## Desvios da spec (documentados na issue, seção 11)

- **Sprite na seção Suprimentos** — sem `appearanceId` no catálogo de suprimento abstrato hoje;
  a linha é texto (nome + contagem).
- **Ferramenta (`machete`/`rope`/`shovel`/`pick`/`key`) sobre tile** é o ADR 0050 (issue própria,
  ainda não implementada): `use-item`/`use-item-on` sobre item não-`consumable` recusa
  `not-usable`.
- **Emenda formal do texto do ADR 0032 d.9 e do ADR 0043** fica para o pouso do próprio ADR 0049
  (branch separada) — esta PR já implementa o COMPORTAMENTO que a emenda descreveria, sem
  duplicar/discordar do texto que chegará com aquele merge.
- **Mensagem "Munch." e exibição de `fedMs` no HUD**: sem campo de protocolo hoje; a confirmação
  visível é o `inventory` reenviado.
- **Opcodes 21-24, 36** (`sell-items`/`discard-item` da #741/#724, `corpse-contents` da #722/#749)
  foram conferidos e não colidem com 25/26/37 — nenhum código dessas issues foi duplicado aqui.

Closes #726

body:
## 요약

quality-gates **9.2.0**. PR4c(#178)는 같은 키 토픽에서 이미 머지된 앞 브랜치를 어떻게 다룰지(I1)를 알려진 한계로 남겼다. 이 PR 은 그 규칙을 설계 층위에서 다시 정했다. 같은 `Spec:` 키의 선언 커밋 가운데 이미 `base_ref` 에 든 것은 **판정 대상이 아니라 기준선**이다. 그 조각은 자기 PR 에서 이미 판정됐다. 기준선에 든 선언 커밋 수는 `in_base` 로 스코프 튜플, `scope:` 블록, SKILL ① 공지에 싣는다.

- `resolve-topic.sh`
  - 구성원 근거를 `C_live`(아직 base 에 없는 선언)로 좁힌다.
  - 머지된 구성원 단계(`merged:` · `MERGED_MAINLINE` · `--ancestry-path`)와 그 분기점 보정을 지운다.
  - 출력은 11키다.
- `topic-head.sh` · `scope_tuple.py`
  - 둘 다 13키다. `in_base` 는 `-` 또는 수이고, `status: ok` 면 반드시 수다.
  - `scope:` 블록에서 `branches` 바로 다음 줄에 렌더한다.
- 키의 선언이 전부 base 에 있으면:
  - `resolve` 는 `no-declaration` 을 내고 사유는 `all declared commits are already in base_ref` 다.
  - 그 키를 `--topic` 으로 주면 `topic-head` 는 `declaration-invalid` 를 내고 같은 사유를 싣는다.

## 사용자가 뒤집을 수 있는 자리

- **AC4 재정의.** 2026-09-27 선택지 셋(조각 입도 강제 · 머지된 조각은 기준선 · AC4 글자대로 유지) 가운데 「머지된 조각은 기준선」을 골랐다. 이제 머지된 앞 조각의 변경은 이번 판정에 다시 들어오지 않는다.
- **squash · rebase-merge · cherry-pick 한계(설계 §15-12).**
  - 앞 조각의 ref(로컬이든 `origin/<b>` 원격-추적이든)가 남아 있으면, 그 조각은 여전히 구성원이다.
  - 그러면 경계가 그 조각의 옛 분기점으로 내려가고, 그 뒤 base 이력까지 리뷰 대상에 든다. 최종 리뷰가 /tmp 에서 재현했다.
  - README 알려진 한계에 영향과 처방을 적었다(로컬 · 원격 브랜치 모두 삭제, 또는 조각마다 다른 키).
  - 코드로 막는 장치(구성원 fork 가 서로 다르면 경고)는 후속 과제다.
- **로컬 전용 머지.** 앞 조각을 로컬 `main` 에만 머지했거나(push 전), 원격에서 머지했지만 아직 fetch 하지 않았으면 그 조각은 아직 기준선이 아니다. README 에 공시했다.

## PR5 로 넘기는 것(범위 불변식 때문 — 이 PR 은 스펙 · references 를 더 고치지 않는다)

- 설계 §15-12 · §16 의 「옛 분기점이 경계가 될 자리가 없다」는 squash 경로에서 틀리다. README 처럼 실제 영향을 적도록 정정한다.
- 설계 L212 「세 갈래 전부에 답이 있다」 문면(2단계를 지운 뒤라 맞지 않는다).
- SKILL 공지와 README 의 「기준선에 포함됐다」는 형제 토폴로지에서 부정확하다(B 가 A 머지 전에 갈라졌고 main 을 아직 들이지 않은 경우). 「판정 대상에서 빠졌다」로 고치되, 이 문구를 잠근 공지 락과 변이 행을 함께 고친다.
- `qg-worktree.sh` 의 `create-head --topic` die 메시지가 `status` 만 싣고 사유는 버린다(드문 레이스).
- README squash 항목의 「그 뒤 base 이력까지 리뷰 대상에 든다」는 조건이 붙어야 맞다.
  - 사이에 낀 base 커밋에 다른 `Spec:` 키가 있으면 이력이 흡수되지 않는다. 대신 `declaration-invalid (2 distinct Spec keys)` 로 막힌다.
  - 경계는 구성원 fork 들의 merge-base 다.
  - 재리뷰가 실측했다. 결과가 막는 쪽이고 처방은 같다.
- README 로컬 전용 머지 항목의 「원격에서 머지했지만 fetch 전」 갈래는 결과 서술이 틀렸다.
  - 실측으로는 로컬 `main` 이 구성원이 되는 것이 아니다. 남은 `origin/<b>` ref 때문에 앞 조각을 다시 보는 것이다.
  - 처방은 맞다.

## 이 PR 이 지는 것

| 항목 | 내용 | 집행 자리 |
|---|---|---|
| AC4 재정의 | 이미 `base_ref` 에 든 선언은 기준선이 되고 `in_base` 로 공시된다 | `resolve-topic.sh` · `topic-head.sh` · `scope_tuple.py` · SKILL ① 1a |
| §6.2.2 1단계 | 구성원 근거 = `C_live` | `resolve-topic.sh` |
| §6.2.2 2단계 삭제 · §6.2.3 보정 삭제 | `merged:` · `MERGED_MAINLINE` · `--ancestry-path` 제거 | `resolve-topic.sh` + 부재 락(양의 짝) |
| §6.2.2 3단계 | `C_live` 에 고아가 있으면 `declaration-invalid`, `C_live` 가 비면 `no-declaration` | `resolve-topic.sh` |
| §6.2.6 | 튜플에 `in_base` | `topic-head.sh` · `scope_tuple.py` |
| 옛 고침의 반례 N1 · N2 · N3 | 회귀 락 | `test_topic_boundary.sh` |

## 끝에서 끝 흐름

| # | 자리 | 산출 | 소비자 | 최종 리뷰 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `resolve-topic.sh resolve` | `C_live` · `in_base:` · 구성원 · 경계 | `topic-head.sh`(키 이름으로 읽음) | OK |
| 2 | `topic-head.sh` | 13키, `in_base` 는 `branches` 다음 | SKILL ① 1a 스코프 파일 | OK |
| 3 | SKILL ① 1a | `in_base` > 0 이면 공지 한 줄 | 사용자 | OK(기본 경로에서 도달 확인) |
| 4 | `scope_tuple.parse` | `in_base` 검증(fail4 원자) | 합성기 `--scope` | OK |
| 5 | `scope_tuple.render` | `  in_base: N` | Step 4.5 · Final Summary | OK |
| 6 | 레퍼런스 R-init | `boundary:` | R4 | OK(코드 변경 없음, `differential-test.md` 한 줄만 정정) |

## 선재 RED

`~/Downloads` 밖 clone 에서 잰 값이다. 착수(db5b1aca), 종료(70c979fd), 최종(b51cc1f2) 모두 217 파일이고, 0 이 아닌 파일은 같은 넷이다.

- qg `test_codex_backward_compat.sh`(1)
- qg `test_runner_adapters.sh`(1)
- qg `harness/test_skill_orchestration_behavior.sh`(2)
- spec-distill `test_no_write_matcher_hooks_repo.sh`(1)

그 밖의 결과:

- 착수 대 종료 join 은 빈 출력이다.
- unittest `Ran 197` OK.
- 하네스 실패 이름은 기준선과 같은 둘이다.

> 이 세션의 워크트리에서는 macOS 가 `~/Downloads` 아래 `access()` 를 기준선 실행 도중부터 거부했다(`cat` 은 된다). 그래서 워크트리에서 돈 스위트는 `[ -r ]` 가드가 있는 락 14개가 RED 로 오염됐다. 회귀 판정의 정본은 위 clone 비교다.

## 변이 표(락 이빨)

20행이다. 계획의 17행에, 앞 Task 리뷰가 사본에서 찾아낸 생존 변이 셋을 더했다. 변이마다 새 사본(`git archive HEAD` → `mktemp -d`)에서 돌렸다.

- 닫기 전: KILLED 17 / SURVIVED 3.
- 살아남은 셋(`resolve` 의 `in_base: -` 분기, 공지 창 끝 마커, 공지 줄 끝 앵커)은 락 한 라운드로 닫았다.
- 닫은 뒤: **20/20 KILLED**. 양성 대조는 락 다섯 모두 `Fail: 0` 이다.

## 검증 과정

SDD 로 진행했다. 구현은 sonnet, Task 리뷰와 최종 리뷰는 opus 가 맡았다. Task 리뷰 다섯 개가 모두 승인했고, Task 5 는 수정 라운드 하나를 거쳤다. 최종 리뷰는 「With fixes」(Important 1)였고, 수정 한 번과 재리뷰를 거쳤다. 원장의 판정은 다음과 같다.

- **R1** — T1 커밋과 T2 커밋 사이에 `test_topic_head.sh::case_merged_member_combined` 가 RED 인 것을 허용했다(T2 가 고쳐 쓴다).
- **R2** — T5 구현자는 커밋까지만 한다. push · PR 은 최종 리뷰 뒤 컨트롤러가 한다.
- **R3** — push 직전 `origin/main` 을 다시 확인한다. 움직였으면 merge 하고 버전을 다시 올린다.
- **R4** — 변이는 사본에서만 한다.
- **R5** — 워크트리 기준선의 spec-distill 환경 RED 셋을 기준선의 일부로 받았다(clone 비교로 환경 탓임을 확정).
- **R6** — 앞 Task 리뷰가 찾은 생존 변이 셋을 Task 4 변이 표 18–20행으로 넣었다.
- **R7** — CHANGELOG 둘째 불릿을 고쳤다. 출시되지 않은 옛 고침의 반례 N1 · N3 를 9.1.0 결함으로 적고 있었고, N2 의 원인도 잘못 짚었다.
- **R8** — 회귀 판정의 정본을 `~/Downloads` 밖 clone 비교로 둔다.
- **R9** — 최종 fix 는 문서 층에서 했다. squash 한계의 영향과 처방, 로컬 전용 머지 조건 분리, 주석 한 곳이다. 코드는 설계가 받아들인 한계 그대로다.
- **R10** — 스펙 정정과 형제 토폴로지 문면은 PR5 로 넘긴다.
- **parked ×2** — 최종 fix 재리뷰의 README Minor 둘(squash 흡수 서술이 조건부로만 맞음 · fetch 전 원격 머지 갈래의 결과 서술). 두 번째 fix wave 는 두지 않는 규칙이라 PR5 로 넘긴다.

author: shiinayane
body:
## 变化

- **主区固定、不滚动。**
  - 视频取剩余空间里最大的 16:9，下方固定放相关推荐横排。工具栏到视频、推荐卡片到窗口底边，各留 24pt。
  - 真实页面与加载骨架共用 `PlaybackDetailLayout`。
  - 推荐的加载、失败、空状态与已加载状态同高。
- **标题与数据交给系统工具栏。**
  - 主标题是视频标题。
  - 副标题是播放 · 弹幕 · 发布时间，有充电专属或试看限制时接上访问提示。
- **弹幕移到工具栏。** 工具栏按钮显示"弹幕"文字加图标，图标随开关变化。弹出面板顶部是开关，关闭时其余设置不可调。
- **推荐横排的几何常量合并。** 卡宽、间距、边距、可视区高度统一到 BiliUI `VideoCardShelfGeometry`，App 原生横排与 Feature 骨架共用。
- **播放页自铺不透明窗口背景。**
- **删除（约 1,000 行）：**
  - 外层 AppKit 纵向滚动包装 `NativePlaybackDetailView`；
  - 播放器滚轮路由、窗口滚轮 shield、独立的键盘锚点视图，以及对应测试。

  播放器上的滚轮交给 AVKit 原生处理。键盘快捷键改以 content overlay 中的弹幕层为窗口锚点，随 AVKit detached 全屏移动。
- **删除"正在准备播放"遮罩**，准备阶段交给 AVKit 原生表现。
- **修复：打开视频时，视频区不再从旁边飞入。**
- **播放态侧栏 520–720**，最小窗口不变。
- **文档：** ARCHITECTURE 新增"播放页布局"；ROADMAP 中详情页重构完成，下一项是 UP 主空间。

## 原因

- **滚动和截断：** 视频随页面滚动时，需要一整套滚轮截断与安全区投影。这几轮的多个 bug 都出在这里，包括滚轮、提示浮层安全区，以及透出来源页。
- **主区腾空间：** 标题、数据、弹幕设置占着主区空间，而系统工具栏与弹出面板可以原生承载它们。
- **不透明背景：** 播放页压在 NavigationStack 根（来源页）之上，根页面为保留状态仍在渲染。macOS 不为压栈页面绘制底色，原来靠外层 NSScrollView 的背景顺带提供。删掉包装后一度复发，现在由播放页自己负责，ARCHITECTURE 写明了原因。
- **飞入：** 纯 SwiftUI 布局下，加载阶段切换的动画会带动新建的 AVPlayerView frame；视频区现在不参与布局动画。
- **侧栏宽度：** 侧栏在 480 宽时读评论偏窄。两种状态共用一列，`ideal` 只在首次布局生效，所以进入播放时宽度等于最小值。

## 用户影响

- 读简介、评论或看推荐时，视频始终可见；标题和数据一直留在工具栏。
- 弹幕开关和设置集中在工具栏按钮里；D 键照旧可用。
- 打开视频时画面原地加载，不再有视频框飞入。
- 侧栏默认更宽，评论更好读。

## 验证

- [x] 唯一最高适用 Gate（`app`；实际命令：`sh Scripts/run-quality-gates.sh app`）
- [x] 真机（维护者），各项结构都在 spike 与本分支上逐项确认：
  - 固定布局的比例与缩放；
  - 骨架到内容无跳动；
  - 推荐延伸到侧栏下、首卡对齐；
  - 焦点环未被裁切；
  - 工具栏标题与副标题；
  - 弹幕按钮与面板；
  - 播放器上滚轮无异常；
  - 全屏快捷键；
  - 切换侧栏不透底；
  - 视频不再飞入；
  - AVKit 原生的准备阶段表现；
  - 侧栏 520–720。

## 未覆盖边界

- "播放页必须自带不透明背景"是 SwiftUI `.background` 修饰，没有单元测试能固定。原先检查外层 NSScrollView 背景的测试已随包装一起删除，这条约束由 ARCHITECTURE 记录，并依赖真机检查。
- 删除准备遮罩后，准备阶段播放器对 VoiceOver 隐藏，没有"正在准备播放"的朗读；宿主在这一阶段仍会禁止交互。
- README 的截图与"接下来"一节，等下个版本发布时再更新。

body:
The attribution half of issue 559 (refs #559). The commercial-use half is left open for the owner, so this PR only refers to the issue and does not close it.

**What changed**
- **NOTICE**: a new "Data fetched at runtime" section beside "Embedded data". It names Open-Meteo, the CC BY 4.0 licence and which paths use the data, and points to the issue for the non-commercial terms.
- **`ExtendedForecast.IncludesOpenMeteo` / `.Credit`**: whether any of the hours are Open-Meteo's. The driver that fetched sets it, never a display name, which the user can rename. It is true for an Open-Meteo profile, and for an OpenWeatherMap profile once Open-Meteo has extended it past 48 hours or filled in its upper-air winds (the seeing row). `Credit` returns `Weather data by Open-Meteo.com (CC BY 4.0)`, or null.
- **Planner weather band** (`AltitudeChartRenderer`, so GUI, TUI and web alike): the credit is drawn right-aligned in the legend row, under the plot's right edge. The legend's target entries make room for it. It is drawn only when a band is drawn and its data includes Open-Meteo's.
- **Night calendar** (`NightCalendarPopover`, one widget on all three hosts): a footer line under the detail strip when the calendar's forecast includes Open-Meteo's data. The TUI's calendar design height goes from 480 to 500 so the extra row fits.
- **Past-night request**: `NightCalendarActions` uses the new `GetAttributedHourlyForecastWithUpperAirAsync`. That request used to rebuild its provenance from `driver.Name` and would have lost the flag.

**A choice worth checking**
An OpenWeatherMap profile is still credited whenever Open-Meteo actually supplied data: the days after OpenWeatherMap's 48 hours, or the seeing row's jet wind. Under CC BY that data needs the credit even with another provider selected. A forecast from OpenWeatherMap alone, with the supplement failed or absent, shows no credit. So does the Moon-only calendar.

**Tests**
A filtered `TianWen.Lib.Tests` run (Release) over WeatherUpperAirSupplement, NightCalendar, WeatherForecastMerge, AltitudeChart and ObservationScheduleVisualization: 55 passed, 0 failed. New assertions:
- the credit for OpenWeatherMap with upper-air, for Open-Meteo, for the OpenWeatherMap calendar supplement and for the Open-Meteo calendar;
- no credit for OpenWeatherMap alone, and none for a name-only "Open-Meteo";
- `AltitudeChartRenderer.WeatherCredit` over the planner band, including the past-night path and no weather device at all.

No screenshot was taken of the drawn credit.

author: cyohn55
body:
First of the three remaining Phase 2 items in ENGINE_ROADMAP.md.

## What's new for carts
- `cartbox.sweep(slot, shape, x, y, z, dx, dy, dz, max, ignore)` sweeps a solid shape instead of a thin ray. It shares the 16 ray slots and is read the same way, a tick later, with `cartbox.hit(slot)`.
  - `shape` is one of:
    - a number: a sphere's radius
    - `{hx, hy, hz}`: a box's half-extents
    - `{radius, halfheight}`: an upright capsule
  - The hit reports the surface point touched, that surface's normal, and how far the shape's centre travelled first.
  - Useful for thick bullets, landing and ledge checks, or checking whether a body fits somewhere.
- `cartbox.ray(…, max, ignore)` and `cartbox.sweep(…, ignore)` accept an object to pass through, so a character can cast from inside itself. Before this, a ray from a character's centre hit the character.
- Trigger zones stay see-through for both.

## How it works
- There's one new block command: `PHYS_OP_CAST` (op 8). It carries the shape kind, its size and the object to ignore, and is sent just before the slot's ray command. A ray with neither a shape nor an ignore object sends only the ray command, as before.
- `PhysicsBackend` gains an optional `shapecast` method, and `raycast` takes an optional `ignore`. The Rapier backend implements `shapecast` with `world.castShape` using a unit velocity, so the time of impact is the distance travelled. It skips the ignored object's rigid body.
- The SDK defaults (`cartbox.lua` and `sdk.ts`) and the editor's SDK reference document `sweep`. The player dist is rebuilt.

## Tests
- A new real-engine test (Xbox 360 core with Rapier) covers:
  - a ball swept past a trigger stopping 0.5 m short of a wall
  - a box dropped onto the floor
  - a capsule dropped onto a character
  - a ray from inside the hero hitting the hero, and missing it when told to ignore it
  - a sweep too short to reach the wall missing
- Full suite: 2326 passed, 32 skipped.
- Typecheck is clean. Lint has 0 errors. `check:dist` is up to date.

## Summary

- Adds the third Design Studio vertical slice: an open-front base cabinet (`KIT_BASE_OPEN`) with configurable loose shelves, alongside the shutter (Slice 1) and drawer-bank (Slice 2) cabinets.
- New `KITCHEN_BASE_OPEN_V1` construction recipe reuses `KITCHEN_BASE_STANDARD_V1`'s exact carcass and shelf mechanism (sides, bottom, back, top rails, evenly spaced `SHELF` components), dropping the shutter front entirely: no door, no hinge, no front board or finish.
- `hardwareRuleSetId` names a rule set with **zero rules** (`OPEN_STANDARD`) and `edgeRuleSetId` a rule set with no front-facing component types (`OPEN_CARCASS_STANDARD`, each recipe's edge rule set must be fully self-contained, per the Slice 2 precedent).
- **No new construction-variable codes and no database migration** — every variable `KITCHEN_BASE_OPEN_V1` needs was already registered for the shutter recipe, and a `hardware_rule_set` has never required at least one `hardware_rule` at the database level.
- `@lintel/cabinet-engine`: `Shelf` (D4, previously reserved for this slice) is now compiled/decoded end to end for `BASE_OPEN`. Deliberately *not* also wired for `BASE_SHUTTER` (which already produces `SHELF` components today via its own `shelfCount` parameter, never exposed as a Properties control): `decode.ts` gates shelf decoding on `productCode === "KIT_BASE_OPEN"`, not on `SHELF`-component presence, so a shutter cabinet's own save is unaffected.
- Design Studio UI: open-cabinet library entry, a "Shelf count" property control replacing "Front"/"Drawer count", and no "Overlay" control at all (there is no door).
- `apps/db-tools`: intake validation and rehearsal dataset updated for the new product/recipe/hardware rule set. `OPEN_STANDARD`'s empty `rules` array is a correct, complete value (an open cabinet genuinely has no hardware) — it intakes as `WORKING_DRAFT` since the generic completeness heuristic can't otherwise distinguish "zero rules is complete" from "not yet filled in"; nothing in the database's own approval preconditions requires a hardware rule set to carry at least one rule.

A resolved `BASE_OPEN` object shows 10 non-blocking `ERROR`-level `STANDARD_UNKNOWN_VARIABLE` findings (`canApprove: true`, 0 `BLOCKER`) — the same characteristic Slice 2's drawer cabinet already showed at a smaller scale (2), since the rehearsal construction standard is one shared bag covering the union of every recipe's variables and `validateStandard()` requires an exact declared-set match per recipe. Documented in `docs/architecture/DESIGN-STUDIO-D1-D6.md` §7, not a regression.

No changes to manufacturing/CNC/nesting/drilling workflow, client portal, or `lintel-os-ops`. No Hettich technical specifications or Lintel production values were invented.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` — 731/731 tests passing across 56 files
- [x] `pnpm test:db` — 367/367 DB-integration tests passing (no migration needed this slice)
- [x] Full typecheck clean (root, `apps/api`, `apps/db-tools`, `apps/web`)
- [x] Full `eslint .` clean
- [x] `pilot:demo --reset` — full rehearsal dataset (25 reference versions, including the new product/recipe/hardware rule set) imports and approves without error
- [x] Live browser verification (Playwright against the running rehearsal stack): added an open-front cabinet, confirmed the "Shelf count" control (not "Front"/"Drawer count", no "Overlay"), widened to 900mm and changed to 3 shelves, saved, confirmed the Elevation view shows an open carcass with shelf lines and no door, generated a BOM and confirmed the payload includes `SHELF` panels — 0 console errors

author: antonlvovych
body:
## What

Carries #5971 by @samcharles93 (squashed onto current `main`, authorship kept) and fixes its review findings, so `bd github sync` / `bd github push` link beads relationships on GitHub: `parent-child` dependencies become sub-issues and `blocks` dependencies become "blocked by" relationships.

## Why

Closes #5970. #5971 had three blocking review findings from @bee-ghosttrack plus several nits. This PR keeps Sam's commit as the base and adds one commit per finding on top, so each fix can be reviewed on its own.

| Review finding | Status | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (blocking) `ListSubIssues` / `ListBlockedBy` unpaginated | fixed: `per_page=100` and `Link` following; a test with 150 links proves the second push makes 0 POSTs | 6b6b1fb38 |
| 2 (blocking) `last_sync` bumped after the relationship pass | fixed: only the engine writes `github.last_sync`; Dolt-backed tests count the writes for `push` and `sync --push-only` | 89e4c24f5 |
| 3 (blocking) `IssueNumberFromRef` accepts refs from any host/repo | fixed: only the configured host and exact owner/repo (HTML, REST and GHES `/api/v3` forms) or `github:N`; other refs are skipped with a warning | 1617f135f |
| 5 parent-child only for epic parents | fixed: any parent-child link becomes a sub-issue | 2caf8ab05 |
| 8 a warning per issue on GHES / feature off | fixed: the first 404 turns off that link type for the pass, with one warning per type | 3dc9b41d2 |
| 9 `Tracker.GitHubClient()` widens the tracker | fixed: `PushLinks` is a method on `*github.Tracker`; the accessor and `LinkResolver` are gone | d244504a9 |
| 4, 6, 7 | not changed here; each changes behavior beyond this fix | - |

Two more fixes from a follow-up review of this branch:
- A 404 from one deleted or transferred source issue no longer turns off the whole link type: bd checks whether the issue exists; a missing issue is skipped with a warning naming it (0c8c3d93c).
- With `--dry-run`, the relationship pass prints "Would sync N relationship links" and makes no POSTs (7b2777e67).

Out of scope, not changed: the engine itself writes `<prefix>.last_sync` after every non-dry-run push-only sync for all trackers; this predates #5971.

## Verification

```sh
export GOFLAGS=-tags=gms_pure_go
go test ./internal/github/... ./internal/tracker/...
go test -count=1 ./cmd/bd/ -run 'GitHub|Github|RelationshipPass'   # the Dolt-backed tests need Docker
GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.7 golangci-lint run --build-tags gms_pure_go ./internal/github/... ./cmd/bd/...
```

All pass locally; the four Dolt-backed tests ran against `dolthub/dolt-sql-server:2.2.0` (none skipped), lint reports 0 issues, gofmt is clean. Each fix was also checked by reverting it and confirming its test fails. A build of this branch also ran a real two-way sync against a private repo whose 163 relationships already existed on GitHub; it added no duplicates.

@samcharles93 - happy to fold these commits into your branch instead if you prefer to keep #5971.

author: ahmedelbanna80
body:
## Root cause

The first real docs deploy through the platform (run 36300738817, job 108567783572, right after #1490 merged) failed closed in the action's "Credential preflight" step:

```
underlying error: Command failed: kubectl auth can-i --list -n knext-docs -o json
error: unknown shorthand flag: 'o' in -o
```

`-o`/`--output` has **never** been a flag `kubectl auth can-i` accepts, on any kubectl release — this was not a version-skew bug (the issue's original framing), it could not have worked anywhere.

**kubectl versions checked:**
- Local client: **v1.33.3** — reproduces the identical error against the live cluster.
- Live OKE cluster (`knext-oke-sa` read-only context): confirms `kubectl auth can-i --list -n default -o json` fails the same way, and confirms the fix's replacement command works (see below).
- Runner (`ubuntu-latest` → Ubuntu 24.04, image `20260920.314.1`, per `actions/runner-images`): ships **kubectl 1.37.0**; its `auth can-i --help` has never listed `-o` either.

## Fix

Stop depending on `auth can-i --list`'s output format at all. Submit the `SelfSubjectRulesReview` directly:

```
kubectl create -o json -f -
```

feeding the review object on stdin. `create` has always accepted `-o json` — verified live against the real cluster:

```
echo '{"apiVersion":"authorization.k8s.io/v1","kind":"SelfSubjectRulesReview","spec":{"namespace":"default"}}' \
  | kubectl --context knext-oke-sa create -o json -f -
```

returns a populated `.status.resourceRules`, the same shape the classifier already consumed. `kubectl get --raw` doesn't apply — a review is created (POST), not read (GET).

Stays fail-closed in shape as well as verdict: a response with no `.status` is refused rather than defaulted to an empty (and therefore vacuously-passing) rule set.

## Tests

`tests/kn-next-action-preflight.test.ts`, stubbed `kubectl` on PATH (existing convention, e.g. `tests/e2e-deploy.port-ownership.test.ts`):
- (a) kubectl rejects `-o` for `auth can-i` but answers `create -o json -f -` with scoped rules → **passes**
- (b) that review reports a wildcard rule → **refused**, same refusal message as before
- (c) `kubectl create` itself fails → **refused** (fail closed)
- (d) kubectl has neither working form → **refused**, message names the cause
- a review with no `.status` at all → **refused**, never silently treated as zero rules
- regression guard: the fix never depends on `kubectl auth can-i` succeeding at all

The existing B2 step-shape guard from #1490 (asserts the preflight step can't be silently disabled) is untouched and still green — 12/12 in the file.

## Mutation proof (sha256-anchored restore, clean tree verified after each)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Fall back to `auth can-i --list -o json` | **RED** — test (a) and others fail |
| Swallow the `kubectl create` error | **RED** — tests (c)/(d) fail |
| Default a missing `.status` to `[]` instead of refusing | **RED** — dedicated guard fails |

Each mutation was applied via an anchor-uniqueness-checked script, the test file run under bun, then `git checkout --` restored the file and its sha256 was verified to match the pre-mutation hash before the next mutation.

## Docs

`packages/kn-next-action/README.md` gets one clarifying sentence: the check no longer depends on the runner's kubectl version. No numbers, no internal references. The docs-site page (`apps/docs/content/docs/github-action.mdx`) doesn't mention a kubectl version requirement, so nothing there needed correcting.

Also fixed a stale comment in `ci-credential-scope.test.ts` that cited the exact broken `can-i -o json` command as the provenance of its fixture data.

## Changeset

None. The fix ships entirely in `@getknext/action` (`packages/kn-next-action`), which is `private: true` and consumed from the repository tree (`uses: ./packages/kn-next-action` in `docs-deploy-oke.yml`), never published to npm — matching the precedent set by #1481 (the immediately preceding fix to this same file, also unaccompanied by a changeset). `@getknext/core`'s shipped code is unchanged; only its test suite's comment was corrected.

**user-visible:** the action now works on stock runners; no CLI flag, config schema, or documented behavior changed for consumers beyond "it no longer fails."

## After merge

`workflow_dispatch` the docs deploy on `main` to complete the first-run verification (NextApp adopts the ksvc, revision Ready, `/api/health` 200 through the LB) — tracked as the remaining step from #1493's own description, not part of this PR's diff.

## Round 2 (review fixes)

- **Namespace not actually tested** — the stub `kubectl` for #1493's tests drained stdin without inspecting it, so hardcoding `spec.namespace` in `preflight.mjs` stayed green. The stub now captures the piped review body to a file and a new test asserts it carries the `--namespace` argument, not a literal — mutation-proved RED.
- **`-o json` drop was invisible in tests** — the stub ignored kubectl's argv entirely, so dropping `-o json` from the shipped command stayed green in tests while it fails closed (on non-JSON output) live. The stub now rejects a `create` invocation that doesn't carry exactly `-o json -f -` — mutation-proved RED.
- **`status.incomplete` now warns instead of being silently ignored.** On webhook-authorized clusters (OKE/GKE IAM), the SelfSubjectRulesReview answers but marks itself incomplete; the preflight now emits `::warning::`, quoting `status.evaluationError`, and evaluates whatever rules came back rather than failing closed — refusing there would refuse every credential on such a cluster, not just an over-broad one. The real fix (a `SelfSubjectAccessReview` spot-check of hazardous verbs) is filed separately as security tech-debt (#1495) and referenced in the warning's rationale; not attempted here.
- **README:45 corrected** — it claimed the action fails whenever "your cluster's authorizer cannot answer that question." That's no longer true for an *incomplete* answer (see above); the section now states both actual behaviors: fails closed only when the cluster can't answer at all, warns-and-proceeds when it answers incompletely.
- Re-ran the full suite (`kn-next-action-preflight`, `docs-deploy-oke-workflow`, `github-action-docs-parity`) green, Biome clean at `--diagnostic-level=error`, and mutation-proved (sha256-anchored restore, clean tree verified after each): namespace hardcoded → RED, `-o json` dropped → RED, `status.incomplete` warning removed → RED, plus the three round-1 mutations (fall back to `auth can-i --list -o json`, swallow the `kubectl create` error, default a missing `.status` to `[]`) re-verified still RED against the current tree.

Closes #1487 — its premise (kubectl version skew: "kubectl v1.33 rejects `-o` there... on an older client") is disproven by this PR's own root-cause finding: `-o`/`--output` has never been a flag `kubectl auth can-i` accepts, on any release, so no client version ever made it work.

**Correction to #1490:** that PR's "Action credential preflight, live rules" verification used a local kubectl 1.33 shim that POSTs the `SelfSubjectRulesReview` directly (because 1.33 already lacked `can-i --list -o json`) — it exercised the classifier and the review shape, not the command the action actually shipped (`auth can-i --list -o json`), which is the command #1493 shows failing on every runner. "Verified live" there proved the classifier, not the shipped preflight.

Fixes #1493

author: bdraco
body:
# What does this implement/fix?

The protocol mirror for the web.esphome.io flash hand-off gains the two optional fields the frontend adds for RTL8720C support: `flasher` on the firmware frame (absent means esptool, so an older dashboard's frame is unchanged and an older receiver ignores it) and `flashers` on the ready frame (absent means esptool only, so a newer dashboard declines a hand-off an older receiver cannot take). The state frame also gains an optional `note` for what the user has to do by hand, on any state: strapping the board before the write, resetting it after. The reference flasher page now lists `flashers: ["esp"]` on its ready frame and answers a firmware frame naming any other flasher with an error instead of trying it as an ESP image; its handshake test covers both. The ids name the flasher rather than the platform, since rtl87xx also covers the RTL8710B, whose ROM speaks another protocol.

author: muflub
body:
vbsp barely uses more than one core. On ss_sandbox on a 32-thread Ryzen it takes 0.65 s at 1 thread and 0.60 s at 32, and about 61% of its CPU is collision cooking.

`PhysCollisionEmitter.EmitAsync` already cooks one task per model, but model 0 (the world) holds nearly every brush. Its `PlaneList.AddBrushes` loop builds every brush's convex (qhull) one after another.

## What is pure and what isn't
- **Pure per brush:** `BuildConvexForBrush` reads only the finished BSP and its options.
  - The builder scratch is per thread (`ManagedCollisionCooker._contexts`).
  - The qhull pool hands objects out as if new and seeds its random numbers per build, so earlier builds don't change the output.
  - The shrink test and the water-cut test are also pure within one session: their test collides are built from that brush's own ledge and destroyed straight away.
- **Stateful:** the session's handle tables, `SetConvexGameData`, the `TotalVolume +=` float sum and the order of `Convexes`. The native vphysics session isn't thread-safe.

## Design
- **Two phases in `AddBrushes`:**
  - `BuildBrush(session, brush, clipAtSurface)` builds one brush, including the shrink test or water cut.
  - `Register(convex, brush)` then runs on the cook's thread in brush order, exactly as before, so the float sum and convex order are unchanged.
  - The `WaterBrushNotClippedAtSurface` quirk check stays in `AddBrushes`, so its catalogue entry is unchanged.
- **New optional `Phys/IConcurrentConvexSession.BuildConvexes`,** implemented only by `ManagedCollisionSession`:
  - each participating thread gets its own worker session over its own thread's IVP scratch;
  - ledges are adopted into the cook's session in index order, and only after every item has succeeded;
  - a convex that doesn't belong to the worker session is refused.
- **New `Parallel/CallerParallelFor`:**
  - The calling thread works items itself, and helpers are queued on the cooker's scheduler: the compile pool under `ssmap all`, the .NET pool under `ssmap vbsp`.
  - The caller never waits for a helper that hasn't started. That avoids deadlocking a pool whose threads are all cooking, and it passes the sync-over-async IL scan.
  - When several items fail, it rethrows the lowest failing index, the one the serial loop would have stopped at. The token is checked before every brush.
- **What stays serial:** lists under 8 brushes, `MaxDegree` 1, and any session without the interface, including native vphysics.
- **Leaks:** worker sessions hold only managed objects, a failure adopts nothing, and there are no new statics.

## Tests
- **`CallerParallelForTests`:**
  - every index runs exactly once, with per-participant scratch made on its own thread, and items really run at once;
  - unstarted helpers are never waited for, and running ones are;
  - a failure rethrows the lowest index and stops new claims, and a failing scratch factory counts as the item's failure;
  - cancellation, both before and mid-run;
  - a disposed pool, and a one-thread pool that must not deadlock.
- **`ManagedConcurrentConvexTests`:**
  - bytes and volumes match serial in index order, at correct and stock precision;
  - builds run concurrently on worker sessions;
  - a failure or cancellation adopts nothing;
  - a foreign convex, a null build and a session with no cooker are handled;
  - helpers queue on the cooker's scheduler.
- **`PhysCollisionConcurrentBrushTests`:**
  - the lump, key text, world materials and leaf water ids match degree 1 at degrees 2, 3 and 8, under correct and stock. The fixture has 40 world solids, clip and water brushes (some cut at the surface), and shrunk brushes with thin and hidden sides.
  - the same holds on 3-thread and 1-thread compile pools;
  - the world's convexes keep brush order;
  - the 8-brush threshold, and degree 1 never going concurrent;
  - a session without the interface sees identical calls at degrees 1 and 8;
  - cancelling mid-cook, and a brush that fails to build, both leave the cooker and pool fit for the next compile.
- **Mutation check:** registering in reverse order fails 10 facts.
- **Full suite:** 4,915 passed. The only failures are the 6 `VulkanRayTracerFacts` that also fail on main in the dev container.

## Measured
**Byte checks:** `ssmap vbsp` `.bsp` sha256 equals main at `-threads` 1 and 4.

| map | default | `-compliance stock` |
|---|---|---|
| ss_sandbox | `d53fd7a8…` | `d7534649…` |
| sdk_ctf_2fort | `44dbca87…` | `3e4086ab…` |

**Timing:** the 4 shared cores were saturated (load 10–17), so wall times are inconclusive.
- Collision emit alone on 2fort at 4 threads, best of 30: main 237–241 ms, this PR 185–209 ms. At 1 thread both were about 310–340 ms. The medians overlapped.
- On 2fort, helper threads built 2,452 of the world's 4,103 solid brushes.
- **Ceiling:** on 2fort the world's `AddBrushes` is about 127 of about 375 ms of emit. World `ConvertConvexToCollide` (about 56 ms) and the displacement polysoup (about 40 ms) stay serial, so the gain is smaller than the 61% profile share suggests.
- Please measure on idle cores, e.g. `tools/compile-perf.sh --quick --stages vbsp` on 2fort.

body:
## Type

Bug fix

## Linked issue

Closes #545

## Summary

- Parse `set_config`'s `is_local` argument as a boolean before mutating the session.
- Reject true forms as unsupported transaction-local scope and reject invalid types/text.
- Document the settings behavior and cover literals plus bound text parameters.

## User/operator impact

A request for transaction-local scope can no longer silently become a permanent session setting. Invalid values also fail before the setting is changed.

## Current and expected behavior

Previously, only a typed boolean `true` was rejected. Text values such as `'true'` and `'on'`, and numeric values such as `1`, fell through to session-scoped mutation. Now supported boolean text is parsed, true is rejected as unsupported, false retains session scope, and invalid input returns an error without changing the setting.

## Scope

Runtime behavior, scalar-function integration coverage, and PostgreSQL compatibility documentation.

## Evidence and support status

- Red on main `6a0b0c484454b25afc2508245d198737b5a2caf4`: `should_reject_text_true_for_transaction_local_set_config` failed because text `'true'` updated the setting.
- Green after the fix: literal `'true'`, literal `'on'`, and bound text `'true'` return the transaction-local unsupported error; numeric `1` returns the boolean argument error; `'false'` remains session-scoped; the prior setting remains unchanged after the errors.

## Validation

Passed in the prescribed order:

1. `cargo build --locked`
2. `cargo test --locked`
3. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings -D clippy::pedantic`
4. `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
5. `cntryl-tools validate-tests -f tests/sql_queries.rs` (207/207 compliant)

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] A failing `should_*` regression reproduced the bug on current main.
- [x] The regression lives with SQL scalar-function integration tests and uses Arrange/Act/Assert sections.
- [x] True boolean spellings cannot be applied as session-wide settings, and invalid values fail before mutation.
- [x] Required local validation passes without lint suppressions.

## Status

Ready for hosted exact-head checks and review.

author: paul-hammant
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"paul-hammant"} -->
_Requested by **Paul** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01MPLwWk2T8wRsisgCk9wYcx?thread=cmsg_01MPLwWk2T8wRsisgCk9wYcxErM8N74L6JLtxEpsFx4NMG)_

Closes aether-lang-dev/aether#2209

Before: two modules whose paths end in the same segment (`mine.vk` and `contrib.vulkan.vk`) shared the namespace `vk` for the whole program. Whichever was imported first answered for both, so the issue's `c.ae` failed with `'mine' is not exported from module 'vk'`, and with the imports swapped it failed inside `pb` instead. `import contrib.vulkan.vk as vkapi` written inside a library module was ignored (`Undefined variable 'vkapi'`), and at program level an alias on a local package merged nothing, so `vkapi.ok()` was `Undefined function`.

After: all four shapes from the issue compile and run. Each library's `vk.` means the module that library imported, `import X as Y` works in a library module the way it does in a program, and a program-level alias reaches a local package's functions and consts.

A module's imports now resolve in that module, by their full path or alias, rather than program-wide by last segment (the first of the two fixes the issue proposes; it gets the second for free).

How: once every import is loaded, each registered module is assigned a namespace: its last segment, or its full path with dots as underscores (`mine_vk`, `contrib_vulkan_vk`) when another loaded module ends the same way, so merged symbols never collide. Before typechecking, the merger rewrites every qualified prefix a scope wrote (the leaf, or an `as` alias) to that namespace, in the program's own code and in each cloned library body, skipping functions and closures that bind the prefix as a local so `vkapi.count` on a local struct stays a field read. The typechecker's namespace registration and its module-by-prefix lookups use the same rule. Unaliased imports whose last segment is unique keep exactly the namespace they had, so existing programs' generated C is unchanged. Separately, an alias-only import (`import m as x`) was being read as a selective import of `x`; the selection check now ignores the alias child.

Tests: 7 unit tests in `tests/compiler/test_module_orchestrator.c` (namespace assignment, lookup by namespace, and the merge rewrite for a program alias, a shared leaf, and a library's own import), and `tests/integration/module_leaf_collision/` with the issue's library layout, run in both import orders, plus alias-in-library, program-level alias, and alias-shadowed-by-a-local cases. `make test HARDEN=1` passes (481), `test_runner` is valgrind clean, and `make test-ae` shows only the two failures already present on `main` in this environment (`ae_help` Levenshtein hint, forward-proxy SSRF).

author: 01shane89-jpg
body:
Before: the report list's Refresh button only reloaded the page. On a slow connection, or with the browser's cache, that could bring back the same data, and nothing said which feeds were live and which were saved copies.

After: "Refresh now" fetches every feed file fresh, bypassing the browser cache and the offline copy, then reloads. USGS earthquakes, Open-Meteo air quality and now GDACS disaster alerts are read live by the browser. Every other feed comes from the refresh job's newest snapshot. The "Data ..." time beside the button opens a list of every feed, each marked LIVE or SNAPSHOT with its time, and says why when a live request failed. The list opens by itself after Refresh now.

How: the service worker waits for the network on `?fresh=` requests and saves the result as the copy for the plain address, so the reload uses it. GDACS is read from its event-list API. If that request fails, the snapshot stays, and cyclone tracks always come from the snapshot. The Data time now counts only snapshot feeds, so a live feed can't make old snapshots look new. The page cannot start the GitHub refresh job itself: that would need a GitHub key inside a public page. With #35, the job runs every 15 minutes instead.

Tested: Playwright on desktop and iPhone 13 with USGS and GDACS answering and air quality blocked. Earthquakes and GDACS showed LIVE, air quality showed SNAPSHOT with the reason, Refresh now sent 26 fresh feed requests and reloaded, the list reopened, and there were no page errors. The run with GDACS blocked kept the snapshot. Whether GDACS lets real browsers read its API (CORS) has not been checked from a browser. If it does not, GDACS simply shows SNAPSHOT.

body:
Both of these read as the platform refusing when it was not.

## 1. Having to save twice before "List on OnBuy" appears

A save advanced the sequence by **one** step. So somebody who had filled everything in had to save twice: the first save moved them from step 2 to 3, the second from 3 to 4, and only then did the listing panel — and its button — exist.

A save now opens **the first step still waiting for something**, which is step 4 when nothing is. Fill it all in, save once, and the option to list is in front of you.

Still only on a *save*, never on a keystroke. That distinction is load-bearing: opening on every render is what once made typing the "1" of "15" move the sequence out from under the cursor and save a price of 1.00.

## 2. Jinius only offered attaching to their listing

My inconsistency. I argued in #128 that creating our own product is not only for products they lack — and then showed it only when they lack one.

Attaching means a buyer reads **their** page, and their page can be thin or plainly wrong. `IT49693` is attached to a catalogue product whose barcode is not yours; matching cannot fix that, and no amount of re-checking will. Hiding the better road behind "they do not carry it" made it invisible exactly when somebody had looked at their entry and decided against it.

It is now offered either way:

- **they do not carry it** → open, as before;
- **they do carry it** → folded, under *"Or create your own product in their catalogue, instead of attaching to theirs"*.

Folded rather than absent, because attaching is still the right default when their entry is good — but the choice is now visible and yours.

## Checks

- 2,377 API tests pass; both apps build clean.
- I rendered the Jinius panel in the *carried* case and confirmed the create road appears alongside the offer.

author: k-taro56
body:
## What this is

The trial from the brief: **can an application use D1 / KV / R2 with no configuration at all, and is it any good to write?** Everything here is local — Miniflare only, no provisioning, no credentials, no deployment order.

**Yes, in `upwind dev` and in `upwind build`.** All eight checks pass, from an empty `.upwind/`, with no configuration file of any kind in the project.

## What was built

**1. `resourcesOf` moved to `@stayingupwind/core/paas`** — the part that was always going to stay. It could not be read from Node, because `packages/runtime/src/resources.ts` imports `cloudflare:workers` at the top, and this needed the published shape built the same way in two runtimes. The Function's behaviour is unchanged: `installResources` is still the only thing that defines the symbol inside one, and it now imports the moved function.

**2. One publisher, in the CLI** (`src/resources/publish.ts`). Same rules as the Function's: built by `resourcesOf` from the manifest rather than assembled by hand, published once, `configurable: false`. `upwind dev` calls it in the process Next.js runs in; `upwind build` reaches the process that renders pages through `NODE_OPTIONS=--import`, since a symbol in the CLI's own process is in nobody else's.

**3. Local storage** (`src/resources/local.ts`, `src/resources/listeners.ts`). One Miniflare per project, bound to `.upwind/`, published before anything is evaluated and proved readable before it is published. Two things it is careful about, both learned the hard way and both written down where they happened:

- **One runtime per directory.** A second runtime reads the same storage happily and then dies inside the first *write*, leaving that write unanswered for good — so the rule is kept rather than discovered: every run writes `.upwind/owners/<pid>` and stands down if anybody live is already there. A build started beside a dev server now says `another process (12345) is already using this project's local storage` and stops, instead of losing a write ten seconds later.
- **What the runtime does to a process it does not own.** Its exit hook takes the signals and — the one that cost a day — the IPC `message` listener, which in a render worker swallows the pool's first instructions and hangs the build.

`UPWIND_TRIAL_TWO_D1=1` adds a second database: the one deliberately throwaway knob, named so it is obvious.

**4. `@stayingupwind/sdk`** — `d1()` / `kv()` / `blob()` by name, and `/db`, `/kv`, `/blob` whose default export is the one of its kind. Decided **by count, never by name**, so the same rule serves a project that was handed storage and one that declared a single database of its own. It reads a global anything could have written, so it reads it defensively and says which of "nothing is published" and "this is not a shape I can read" happened.

## The checks

| | |
| --- | --- |
| 1. `upwind dev` → `db.prepare('select 1 as n').first()` | ✅ from a clean `.upwind/`, no config file written |
| 2. `kv` and `blob` | ✅ same run, same route |
| 3. data survives a restart | ✅ counter went 1 → 2 → **3** across a full stop/start |
| 4. delete `.upwind/` → empty | ✅ back to 1 |
| 5. two databases → bare `db` fails, naming both | ✅ `` `db` found 2 D1 databases published — UPWIND_D1, UPWIND_D1_2 — … name the one you mean, `d1('UPWIND_D1')` `` |
| 6. `kv('UPWIND_D1')` does not silently succeed | ✅ `undefined`; `d1('NOPE')` also `undefined` — no fallback to the one that exists |
| 7. `upwind build` prerenders from `db` | ✅ `generateStaticParams` reads **and writes** D1; `/posts/hello` and `/posts/world` come out of the database, exit 0 in ~15s, nothing left running |
| 8. plain `next build` says what to do | ✅ fails with the reader's message, which names `upwind dev` and `upwind build` |

Also measured, because each would have been found a week later: **five dev restarts leave one runtime process and then none**; a **mixed App + Pages Router** build prerenders from storage in both routers; a build **beside a dev server** refuses at startup; a claim left by a process that no longer exists is **taken over**; and storage works with workerd's install script **disabled**, which is what a project installing `upwind` under pnpm gets.

## What was actually in the way of a build

The first version hung at `Collecting page data`, forever, and none of the obvious explanations was the real one. Written down because the next person will start from the same suspicions:

1. **It was not the number of processes.** `experimental.cpus: 1` gives exactly one render worker, and the build still hung.
2. **It was not the storage conflict.** An app that never touches storage, built with a worker that merely *holds* a runtime, hangs just the same — 13s without the publisher, forever with it.
3. **It was Miniflare's `message` listener.** Its exit hook attaches one whenever `process.send` exists. An IPC channel is started by its first listener, so in a `jest-worker` child that listener receives the pool's `INITIALIZE` and `CALL` messages before `processChild.js` is listening — and drops them. Reproduced in four lines: a `--import` that attaches an empty `message` listener and waits two seconds hangs `next build`; the same wait without the listener does not.

Two things that looked like the answer and were not, kept in `local.ts` so they are not tried twice: `unsafeEnableSharedStorage` (works for two instances, deadlocks for six, and leaks a watcher and a timer that `dispose()` never clears, after which the process can never exit), and `ProxyClient` (exported, exactly the right primitive, and refuses anyone but the instance that owns the runtime).

## What it costs, and who pays

Only a project that can reach `@stayingupwind/sdk` — asked of the project, and of pnpm's store above it, since pnpm hoists nothing. For those:

- **Pages are collected by one worker rather than several**, because a directory of storage belongs to one runtime. The adapter arranges it and says so once; `experimental.cpus` set by the project wins. On the trial app that is 15s against 13s; on an application with hundreds of pages it will not be.
- **`upwind` grows by `miniflare` and `workerd`** — about 100 MB installed, a platform binary. No build script to approve: the `workerd` module finds the binary in the platform package as it loads, which was checked with the script off and the copied binary deleted.

A project without the reader gets the build it had before, unchanged.

## For maintainers

This adds a sixth published package, so the release that first includes it takes the `bootstrap` route `publish.yaml` documents — npm holds no trusted publisher for a name that does not exist yet, and a hand publish would leave a version no provenance covers. `CONTRIBUTING.md` now says that where the release steps are, and the provenance job's timeout grows with the sixth package as its own comment says it must.

## Not in here

Migrations, a Drizzle subpath, `upwind.config.ts` `resources`, `RESOURCE_TYPES` neutralisation (`r2_bucket` → `blob`), remote bindings, and adding the SDK to `create-upwind`'s template.

No rail code touched (PRs 2–4). This is the first consumer of `LayoutState::inputs`.

---

# #970 PR 1: completed Null text measurement

Class S. Base: origin/main 0e66ac51. Sources: frozen issues #970 and #965; workshop REFUTE-K2-codex.md sections 2, 3, 6, 7, 8.

## Gate 1 (before implementation brief)
1. Completed measurement parallels PaintFact only in completion, not purpose; no PaintScope belongs here. Use a small common MeasurementResult<Constraint, Extent> within the existing NullTextMeasurement table, replacing its aggregate width/height fields. One completion marker; no parallel cache.
2. Reuse and refusal checks are always on: omission causes stale or fallback geometry, so they are not diagnostics.
3. Context owns its measurement value; that value owns line frames and completed aggregate geometry. No borrowed native resources or new lifetime edge.
4. Commit lives at successful measurement construction, shared by both Null leaves. Both layout sites deliberately mirror the rail seam: skip build only, then place.
5. Counters/failure injection extend the Null testing door only, as explicitly requested; no production getter.
6. Completion cannot be derived from dimensions (zero is valid). Constraint cannot be derived from extent (intrinsic width differs). Test counters cannot be derived from geometry. No extra validity truth.

## Assumptions / implementation brief
Null ignores lineHeight; key logical short width only. Preserve its return-cursor layout contract, existing presentation invalidation, and fallback extent on the refused pass. Build only on marked inputs or unusable result; successful helpers publish the completed result, refusal leaves it invalid. Keep parked geometry; terminal retirement invalidates it. New headers in both mains. No native rail edits, push, PR, or golden edits.

## Review risk profile (forecast)
Three flags: multiple new member fields (encapsulated completed result and test counters); dirty/layout/lifecycle behavior changes; new explicit refusal outcome replacing optional outcome. Review completion/placement boundaries, lifecycle transitions and failure recovery with count/geometry/mutation pins. No new allocation owner or cross-boundary sharing.

## Result

An unchanged Null text leaf now skips its layout measurement build. Both leaf contexts consume `LayoutState::inputs` from #965 and compare their own logical width with the completed measurement's constraint. The existing table owns its aggregate geometry and completion; there is no parallel table-valid/cache-valid pair. Plain Null measurement and common `SyntheticTextExtent` return mandatory success/refusal outcomes. A refused Null helper replaces output with the existing fallback geometry in an uncommitted value. No extra caller invalidation is needed after that replacement. Placement and presentation handling still run on every layout.

Null's aggregate width is the existing maximum painted line width; height is the existing saturated sum of line heights. This PR does not change that to a sum of widths. `SyntheticTextLineWidth` has no refusal path; it remains a pure calculation over a completed line. `SyntheticTextExtent` now explicitly refuses an invalid breaker and leaves its output untouched; `AttributedString::estimateExtent` forwards the outcome.

## Candidate and evidence

- Branch: `feat/970-pr1-null-measure-owner`. HEAD and merge base: `0e66ac511149bce291f5661fa3ce67840fbf595b`.
- Candidate: **uncommitted working-tree snapshot**, enumerated and hashed in `/tmp/970-pr1/candidate.sha256`; changed files copied under `/tmp/970-pr1/review`. There is no new candidate commit SHA.

- Final `ctest --preset testing -E scriptNativeBuildPicker -j 6`: exit 0, 1,253 selected, 1,252 executed/passed, one existing expected-red skip (`testExpectedRedPartialTreeAttachRefusal144`).
- Final `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 ctest --preset testing-asan -E scriptNativeBuildPicker -j 6`: exit 0, same counts and skip.
- `python3 tools/ci/check_test_asserts.py`: exit 0, 610 files, 1,220 learned file/name pairs, no findings. `git diff --check`: exit 0.

Existing characterization expectations and all goldens remain untouched. Existing valid-measurement geometry pins pass unchanged in both presets; restored unconditional measurement is the red control for the new count pins.

代码侧（入版本）加三道守卫，避免同类问题再静默跑：

1. `util::ini::load_exp_list`：文件缺失、或曲线**疑似占位**（空表/全等）时 `warn!` 点名
   （带条目数与那个恒定值，并指明"C# 原版文件覆盖"这一处置）；
2. 新增纯函数 `exp_curve_looks_like_placeholder()` + 单测（占位/单元素/空 → true；真实曲线 → false）；
3. **修正一条老测试**：`test_load_real_exp_list` 此前断言 `list[499] == 100`
   —— 也就是**把当时那份占位数据钉成了期望值**，于是真缺陷一路绿灯。现在钉原版金标准
   （`Level1/2/111/500` 四个数据点）+ 显式断言"不是占位曲线"。

新增实机门禁 `tools/acceptance/l5ze_exp_curve.ps1`：
`A` 配置曲线存在且非占位（否则 exit 3，属本机数据缺失而不是产品红）；
`B` 客户端 `bag_probe` 的 `max_exp` 必须**逐值等于**配置里 `Level<当前等级>` ——
证明服务端真的把曲线应用到了运行时状态，而不是只躺在文件里。

## 验证了什么

- `cargo test --lib -- util::ini` = **15 passed**（含修正后的真实曲线测试与新增的占位检测器测试）；
- **阳性对照（实做）**：把检测器里的 `all(|v| v == first)` 改成 `false` → 检测器单测立即红；
- `cargo clippy --lib -- -D warnings` 通过；`rustfmt --check`（改动行）通过；
- 实机（重启服务端加载新曲线后）见 PR 评论 / 下方补充：`l5ze_exp_curve.ps1` 与 `l5g_quest_finish.ps1`
  的复跑结果。

## 未达成的点

- 该配置目录 **gitignore**，所以"数据对齐"这一步只在**本机**生效；干净检出/别人机器仍需从
  原版 C# 安装目录拷一份（这道守卫会 warn+红，能立刻发现）。
- 顺带发现 `HeroExpList.ini` 本机也缺失（服务端 #2418 会读它，缺失时英雄升级走 ×1.5 回退），
  已一并从金标准目录拷入本机数据；英雄侧**代码级**守卫/门禁未做，留待后续。
- 经验曲线只覆盖**玩家**：怪物经验、组队/行会经验分配等口径未对拍。

body:
## What and why

Stage 3 of `plans/refactor-in-stages.md` lists "`lib/http/action-state.ts` holds `ActionState`, `ok()` and `INITIAL`". Before this PR, the success state was built in seven places:

- `ok()` in four action files: the console's, the knowledge base's, the contacts', and the admin settings file;
- three more copies spelled out in the settings file: twice as `{ ...OK, nonce: Date.now() }`, and once as a literal.

All seven built `{ error: null, ok: true, nonce: Date.now() }`, under four names for one state shape.

This PR:

- adds `lib/http/action-state.ts` with the shape (`ActionState`) and the one `ok()`;
- keeps `KbState`, `ContactActionState` and `SettingsState` exported under their names, as aliases, because the client forms import them from those files;
- makes the console's `ActionState` the shared shape plus its own `message`;
- moves the comment on `nonce` word for word with the field, from the console's type to the shared one.

**`INITIAL` is left out on purpose.** In each of about 30 client forms it is `{ error: null }`, and the compiler already checks it against that form's own state type. A shared constant would change about 30 client files and prevent no bug. I will add this to the plan's Stage 3 text.

The `FormData` helpers (`text`, `uuidField`, `int`, …) are the other half of this plan item, and follow in their own PR.

## How it was verified

- `lib/http/action-state.test.ts`: with fake timers, `ok()` gives the exact object, and a new nonce for each success. The composer depends on the new nonce to clear after a second send.
- The existing action tests (`kb/actions.test.ts`, `admin/settings-actions.test.ts`, the console action tests) pass unchanged.
- `npm run typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `test` (2,050), `knip`, `build` and `repo-rules` (24 checks) all pass.
- `git merge-tree` against every open branch (#233–#239) shows no conflicts.

- [x] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm run test && npm run build`
- [x] A test covers this where the bug would actually hide. There is little to hide here; the test pins the one behaviour a form depends on.

## Risk

- [x] No secrets, tokens or connection strings in the diff or the description
- [x] Nothing here widens what an unauthenticated or unauthorised caller can reach. No `'use server'` module gains an export.

## Alongside other agents

- [x] Based on current `origin/main` (`7ecbfad`)
- [x] The row claim goes on the plan branch (#234), in a table-only commit.

author: ttlucian
body:
Adds a test suite for the websocket parsing path that needs no Mercedes account, no vehicle and no network, plus regression guards for defects that reached a released integration.

**Depends on #440 and #442** - the branch is stacked on both, because several tests assert on the behaviour those PRs introduce. If you would rather not merge the fixes first, the tests can be pointed at master and the relevant cases dropped; say the word and I will split them out.

## Why

The debugging workflow in `scripts/` works from recorded API responses, and those recordings come from a real car. That works for you, who has the car, but a contributor cannot reproduce a parsing bug without capturing a payload of their own - and capturing one puts a real VIN, plate and location into a file that then gets pasted into an issue.

The fixtures here are constructed in code instead. `tests/fixtures/build.py` builds `vehicle_events_pb2.PushMessage` objects from fabricated values, so the suite is self-contained and no real identifier reaches disk or a test report. The synthetic VIN keeps the correct 17-character shape so length validation still exercises properly.

**This does not change your workflow.** `scripts/` and the `save_files` debug output are untouched, and the debug dumps stay unredacted as you require. The fixtures are a separate artefact for a separate purpose - contributors reproducing a parse bug without a car.

## Coverage

`test_parser_offline.py` - the fixtures themselves. VEP and VSU use different envelope shapes: VEP carries a map of VIN -> `VEPUpdate` with a nested attribute map, while VSU carries flat named fields that `_build_car` folds into `Car` groups. Both are checked through the same serialise/re-parse boundary `websocket.py` applies to a live frame.

`test_regressions.py` - one guard per defect:

- a car missing from `self.cars` must be skipped, not dereferenced, on both the VEP and the pull path
- a listener that registers or removes another during `publish_updates` must not raise, in either direction
- `data_collection_mode` is only ever assigned inside the `None` guard
- `salesRelatedInformation` is walked with `or {}`, so absent, null and empty are all handled
- `capabilities` is pre-bound, so a failed request raises the original error rather than `NameError`
- no unused `ssl` import, no unsubstituted `%s` in exception arguments, shutdown task held in a reference

The `data_collection_mode` check parses `client.py` with `ast` rather than grepping, so a comment containing the same words cannot satisfy it, and it is parametrised per site so a failure names the line.

## Verified

- 20 tests pass; `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean
- **no production code is touched** - this adds only `tests/` and one line to `requirements.txt`
- the guards were checked against the unfixed shapes: reverting the pull guard in `client.py` fails two tests including the `ast` check, and reverting the listener snapshot in `car.py` fails both listener tests

## The one coupling to watch

`Client.__init__` needs a `HomeAssistant` instance and builds `Oauth`/`WebApi`/`Websocket` from it. The parsers read none of those, so `conftest.make_client()` reproduces the plain data attributes on a bare object. If `__init__` gains an attribute the parsers use, the helper needs the matching line and the tests fail with an `AttributeError` until it is added. Called out in `tests/README.md`.

Happy to split the regression guards onto master separately, or drop the parts that overlap with the open PRs - whichever is more useful to review.

author: colourbill-ctrl
body:
Part of #2563. No closing keyword: @xsscx decides when it closes.

PR 2 of the two ruled on the issue (PR 1 was #2656).

## The defect

`CheckHeader` ran its class-independent checks -- date, platform, profile flags, device attributes, version, preferred CMM, rendering intent, illuminant -- in the final `else` of a chain whose earlier branches were MultiplexIdentification, MultiplexLink and ColorEncodingSpace. So MID and MLNK never ran them: a MID or MLNK profile with rendering intent 9, or reserved profile flag bits set, was reported valid.

MultiplexIdentification also sat in the zero-data-colour-space exemption. ICC.2-2023 7.2.8 grants a zero data colour space to abstract, MultiplexLink and MultiplexVisualization profiles, not to MID, whose data colour space names the device space it identifies. #2656 left MID exempt and said so in the comment this PR replaces.

## Changes

The final `else` now ends after its PCS checks, and the class-independent block follows under `if (deviceClass != icSigColorEncodingClass)`. ColorEncodingSpace keeps its own test, which requires those fields to be zero. **The moved block is byte-identical**, so the diff is structural only. MID leaves the exemption.

The source comment now also records that the exemption list still differs from 7.2.8 in two places, left as they were: NamedColor is exempt with no 7.2.8 grant, and Abstract, which 7.2.8 does grant, is not.

## Corpus impact

All 243 tracked XML documents, each built from its own directory, every diagnostic line diffed against master: the `Testing/` corpus is unchanged. One negative fixture, `xml-spec-qa/mcs-channel-mismatch.xml`, gains three true warnings for its zero header date. No MID fixture has a zero data colour space.

## Verification

No tracked profile exercises either half, so the new `iccdev.mid-mlnk-header-checks` builds minimal v5 profiles in memory; every message it matches has one emitter.

| mutant | red |
| --- | --- |
| guard removed (ColorEncodingSpace runs the common block) | "ColorEncodingSpace is not run through the common intent check" |
| MID and MLNK excluded again | both intent cases and both reserved-flag cases |
| MID and MLNK skip only the flags check (a narrower fix) | both reserved-flag cases |
| rendering intent dropped from ColorEncodingSpace's zero-field test | "ColorEncodingSpace with only intent 9 set fails its zero-field test" |
| MID back in the exemption | "MID with a zero data colour space is refused" |

The ColorEncodingSpace cases clear the header fields `InitHeader()` fills in, so its zero-field test can only be reacting to the intent; an all-zero control passes.

## Gates

Run on all five open changes merged together onto `a9f56a236` (they merge cleanly in either order, to the same tree):

| lane | result |
| --- | --- |
| Strict Clang 18, `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`, strict warnings enabled | 0 warnings; 325/326 CTests |
| CI's GCC 15.2 image, same flags + LTO, strict warnings enabled | 0 warnings; 325/326 CTests |
| ASan + UBSan (Debug) | no sanitizer report in any test's output. Six tests fail locally, none from these changes: two environmental (a plain C program cannot `dlopen()` an ASan-instrumented library; `imagecodecs`) and four timeouts of a Debug sanitizer build (`pawg-report-regressions` case s10, `tool-coverage` RoundTrip CMYK, `hybrid-pipeline`, `applysearch-cli-args`). All four pass in both Release lanes; the slowest, RoundTrip on `CMYK-3DLUTs2.icc`, takes 1.1 s in Release on master and here, with identical output |
| New tests again with `detect_leaks=1` (CI runs with it off) | every new test, and the #2692 script driving each modified tool: 0 LeakSanitizer, ASan or UBSan reports |
| `shellcheck` 0.9.0 on every changed script | rc 0 |

The one failure differs by environment and is not from these changes: locally `iccdev.spectral-tiff-preview` needs the `imagecodecs` Python module, and fails identically on master; in the GCC 15 image, where that module is present, `iccdev.clusterfuzzlite-configuration` (added in #2719) timed out at its 30 s limit under parallel `ctest`. That script passes alone in the same image in 24 s, and on the host in 15.6 s on master and 10.6 s here.

The new C++ tests are registered in the POSIX CTest list, so the Linux legs (including the ASan+UBSan tool smoke tests) run them; it is not registered for Windows.

`ci-pr-action`, dispatched with `ci_scope=source` before this PR was opened: [run 36301132926](https://github.com/InternationalColorConsortium/iccDEV/actions/runs/36301132926), every job green (the manual thread-linkage job is skipped by design). In its GCC Strict Core (Debug) job, 316/316 CTests passed, including `iccdev.mid-mlnk-header-checks`.

author: danewarnick-source
body: Signup still collects the account, then asks the person to confirm their email. This change stops a bot from creating that account with a cheap trick, and moves the agency workspace so it is created only after that email is confirmed. Turnstile stays in the signup form. It still does nothing unless `VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` is set. No captcha service was added. ## What changed On the account step, before `supabase.auth.signUp`: - A visually hidden field named `company_website` (off-screen, not `type="hidden"`). If it is filled, the page shows the same “check your email” message and does not create a user. - The form remembers when it opened. A submit in under 3 seconds does the same thing. That check sits in `submit()` itself, so it covers both the normal Supabase client and the Cognito auth adapter (that adapter wraps `signUp` and does not create users today). After a confirmed sign-in, `ensureSignupWorkspace` creates the workspace if the person does not already have one. It runs from the signup page when the email link lands there, from login when a fresh agency is headed to the dashboard with no membership, and from the signed-in app shell on other pages when there is still no membership. Invite, manual add, roster import, training-only, and auditor logins are skipped inside that function so they do not get a personal agency. The owner membership is inserted with the service role. Row-level security only lets an existing owner insert members, so the new person’s own session cannot insert the first row. The trigger `trg_org_members_require_org_setup` still runs, and it allows the first member of an org. No extra SQL is required for that trigger. The workspace name uses, in order: the name typed on the business step, the name already on the profile, then `raw_user_meta_data.agency_name` saved at signup, then the email local part. A confirm on another tab or device can still name the workspace. One limit: the account step does not collect the real agency name yet, so the value stored at signup is still “<email>'s workspace” until the business step saves the typed name. ## What gets created today, and when This pull request does not change the live database. Today, `signUp` still fires `on_auth_user_created`, which calls `public.handle_new_user()`. That function inserts a profile, an organization, and an owner membership before the email is confirmed, and the org-create triggers seed presets and service codes. There is no trial row at signup. `ensureSignupWorkspace` finds that existing org and active owner row and leaves them alone. Three unconfirmed accounts already each own an auto-created org. A commented lookup for them is in the SQL file. It is not part of the paste. ## What gets created after the SQL is applied The trigger only inserts the profile (name split into first and last, plus `agency_name` from signup metadata). It does not create an organization, a membership, or a trial. The organization and the owner membership are created later, by `ensureSignupWorkspace`, after a confirmed session exists. These paths do not depend on the trigger creating an org or a membership, and they still will not: - Invite / team-member accept: `prepareInviteAccount` writes the profile with `created_via: invitation`. `accept_invitation` writes the membership on the inviting agency. - Add manually and roster import: `hireEmployeeInternal` writes the profile (`manual_admin` or `smart_import`) and upserts the membership itself. - Training-only: the login is an email invite with `created_via: training_only` and a profile row only. No organization is inserted. Until the SQL is applied, the live trigger can still open a leftover personal workspace for those people, because the live function does not skip `created_via`. The invite and hire code already deactivates that leftover. After the SQL, that update finds nothing to deactivate. ## Deploy order Merge and deploy this app first. Then the database owner applies the SQL. The reverse order is not safe. If the trigger stops creating the org before this app is live, a new signup only gets a profile and never gets a workspace. App first is safe: the old trigger still creates the org, and `ensureSignupWorkspace` is a no-op when that org and an active owner membership already exist. ## Needs database owner Paste `docs/SQL_HANDOFF_signup_after_confirm.sql` after this app is deployed. Do not run it from CI, and do not run it before that deploy. This pull request does not apply it and does not touch the live database. The file replaces `public.handle_new_user()` so the signup trigger only creates the profile row. It does not change `trg_org_members_require_org_setup`.

author: jizhi0v0
body:
## Problem

Muse's Sparkle feed (`https://www.facebook.com/endo/release/appcast.xml?channel=production`) usually answers `302 → https://www.facebook.com/login/?next=…`. `URLSession.updates` followed that redirect and downloaded Facebook's login page on every walled check. `SparkleAppcastSource` then threw `SparkleError.notAFeed` ("HTML with zero items"), and the checker fell through to the Homebrew-cask VendorProbe (#867). The page was never usable.

## Change

- New declarative recipe kind, `loginWalls: [bundleID: SparkleFeedCatalog.LoginWall]`. A wall is `feed` (matched on scheme + host + path, query ignored) plus `login` (matched on scheme + host + path prefix, trailing slash included, so `/login/` does not match `/loginfoo`). Muse declares `www.facebook.com/endo/release/appcast.xml → www.facebook.com/login/`.
- `CrossHostCredentialStripper` (the `URLSession.updates` session delegate) does not follow a redirect that matches a declared wall. It returns the 3xx. Every other redirect goes through the credential stripping exactly as before. No per-task redirect delegate is added, so the session delegate is never bypassed.
- `SparkleAppcastSource`: a 3xx whose `Location` matches a declared wall throws the same `SparkleError.notAFeed`, carrying the login-page URL. The error message is identical to the one the downloaded page produced (a test compares them), so the checker takes the same fallback. Any other non-2xx is still `badStatus`.
- Scope: this feed only. The evidence is n=1. A general rule such as "the redirect path contains `login`" would over-match: in the same request ledger, AweSun's `client-webapi.oray.com/softwares/SUNLOGIN_X_MAC_ARM` is a real download. If Facebook moves its login page, the match fails and we are back to today's behaviour: the page is downloaded and still reported as `notAFeed`.
- Plumbing for the new kind: `AppRecipeSet` (field, init, `bundleIDs`), `Codable` conformance, the hand-listed kind checks in `AppRecipeIndexTests` and `RecipeCodableTests`, and all 236 goldens re-recorded. Every golden except Muse's only gains `loginWalls = Dictionary(count: 0)`.
- `docs/app-audits/com-meta-endo.md`: detection section updated, and a dated history entry with the numbers below.

## Evidence

**Before (measured):**
- Request ledger (a read-only copy of `events.sqlite`), Muse / `www.facebook.com`, 2026-09-26 14:31Z → 09-27 06:33Z (16.0 h):
  - hop 0 `/endo/release/appcast.xml` → 302: 146 times
  - hop 1 `/login` → 200: 146 times, about 83,849 B each on the wire (460,047 B decoded), **12.2 MB** in total
  - hop 0 → 200, the real appcast: 36 times
- `curl -D -`, 8 times at 15 s intervals on 09-27: 2 × `302` (`location: https://www.facebook.com/login/?next=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Fendo%2Frelease%2Fappcast.xml%3Fchannel%3Dproduction`, `content-length: 0`) and 6 × 200 appcast (4.1 / 1077426479). The issue's premise holds.

**After:** a walled check is one request: the 302, with no body. This is shown by the tests below. I did not measure it on a live install.

**Tests** (`SparkleLoginWallTests`, loopback `NWListener`, `127.0.0.1` as the vendor and `localhost` as a second host, no real network):

- When the feed gets through (200 appcast), Sparkle still answers (4.1 / 1077426479), with the wall declared.
- A cross-host redirect that is not a wall is still followed, and `Authorization` does not reach the second host.

author: twdashenafi-beep
body:
Found while chasing a missing meeting in a real Proton export of 363 events. It turned out not to be the cause of that — the meeting was in a different calendar, and Proton exports one file per calendar — but the bug underneath is real and was hiding in plain sight.

## Recurring events older than five and a half years disappeared

They were expanded by walking from the first occurrence to the window, one period at a time, and giving up after two thousand steps. **A daily meeting reaches two thousand days in five and a half years** — so anything repeating daily since 2019 ran out somewhere in 2024 and vanished from a diary that had been keeping it faithfully the whole time.

The longer you had had a habit, the less likely the app was to know about it.

It now jumps most of the way and walks the last stretch. The walk is what gets the clock changes and the week alignment right, so it keeps a period in hand rather than landing exactly; the jump is arithmetic and only for daily and weekly, which are the two that can outrun the limit in a working life. Monthly needs a hundred and sixty years to hit the same wall and yearly two thousand. Counted series are never jumped: they are short by definition, and keeping the tally honest through a jump is a second piece of arithmetic to get wrong for no gain.

The margin is one period of slack in each direction. The tests bound it — two periods of overshoot loses the meeting and they say so — rather than pinning the exact number, which nothing outside the function can see.

## "Read 363 events" was no help to anybody

It counted what the file held, which says nothing about what the app can show. A file can parse perfectly and yield nothing for the next three weeks, and those are entirely different problems with entirely different fixes.

It now reports both — `Read 363 events from … · 12 in the next three weeks` — and the Account row goes on saying it.

Proton writes `X-WR-TIMEZONE` and no `X-WR-CALNAME`, so a calendar exported from it had no name to show. That is exactly when you need one, since Proton exports one file per calendar and the only way to tell which you picked is what it was called. The file's own name now stands in — and that, rather than anything else here, is what would have identified the original problem in one glance.

## Tests

- **Unit:** 29 suites, 1,511 checks, 0 failures — a new block on long-running recurrences, including a daily meeting from 2010, a weekly one from 2005, and the parity of an every-other-day series that a jump must not break.
- **Browser:** 31 suites, 698 checks, 0 failures, no uncaught page errors.
- Falsified by removing the jump, which lost both long-running meetings.
