body:
## What

Karan directive 2026-09-27 (he called the old behavior a bug): after successful name + email submit at the lead gate, the report **unlocks immediately** — real figures, working size stepper, cost breakdown, next steps, PDF. No blur anywhere, no "magic link is on its way" dead-end.

## How

- New `LoadLeadEstimate` NGXS action: runs the **public** `POST /api/v1/estimate` (auth: none by design — the figures were already in the API response; the blur was a nudge, not a boundary) and maps the full response onto the report snapshot.
- Report page dispatches `UnlockReport` (magic-link token) / `LoadLeadEstimate` (submitted lead) / `LoadPreview` (pre-gate) on init and retry.
- No-token `ReviseReport` re-runs the public estimate when a lead was submitted, so the stepper stays live post-gate.
- Persistent confirmation line below the disclaimer, using the `magicLinkSent` response flag:
  - Fresh: "Report saved — we emailed you a link to reopen it anytime."
  - Dedupe: "Report saved — your link is already in your inbox."
- The magic-link email stays as **return-access for other devices**; the token-gated extras (AI narrative, token revise, share, callback) still need it and fail honestly until the link is clicked.
- Guard unchanged: cold `/estimate/report` with no lead and no token renders the locked blurred preview, never unlocked numbers.
- No OTP (explicitly deferred by Karan). No API changes (frontend presentation only).

## Verification

- `npx tsc -b` (repo root, as CI runs): clean
- Full web suite: 84 files / 689 tests pass
- `npm run lint` (web): clean
- Production build: succeeds
- New specs: immediate unlock (fresh + dedupe variants), disclaimer persistence, active stepper, lead revise version bump, honest no-lead failures. One pre-existing test caught a real bug during development (lead-snapshot version was hardcoded to 1) — fixed.

## Follow-ups for Karan / parent

- **Browser QA still required** (delegated): desktop + mobile Safari — fresh gate submission, dedupe behavior, all sections, cold navigation.
- **Known limitation**: AI narrative content, share, and callback need the magic-link report token (production API is token-gated; frontend cannot mint one). They render visible/enabled but will prompt for the emailed link until clicked. If Karan wants these fully in-session too, that needs a backend change (e.g. same-session token on lead submit) — currently out of scope per "do not change the API".

author: julientalbot
body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `cron.reasoning_effort`, a fleet-wide default reasoning effort for cron jobs, in the same slot as `cron.model`.

Today a cron run resolves its effort as: per-job pin > `agent.reasoning_overrides` (per model) > `agent.reasoning_effort`. An operator who keeps chat at `high` but wants every routine at `low` on the **same model** has no config lever: `reasoning_overrides` is keyed by model, so it would lower chat too, and the per-job pin must be set job by job from the CLI/dashboard (the agent's `cronjob` tool deliberately cannot set it). On hosted deployments, users create frequent routines themselves ("check my inbox every 15 minutes"), so hand-pinning each job does not scale.

New fire-time resolution:

per-job pin > `cron.reasoning_effort` > `agent.reasoning_overrides` > `agent.reasoning_effort`

- Model-independent, like the pin and like `cron.model` winning over `model.default`.
- Empty (the default) falls through: existing configs behave byte-identically.
- An invalid value logs a warning and falls through; it never fails the job.
- `no_agent` jobs are unaffected (no LLM call).

```yaml
agent:
  reasoning_effort: high   # chat
cron:
  reasoning_effort: low    # every unpinned cron job, same model included
```

## Related Issue

Related to #23524 (per-job cron reasoning effort, now shipped as the per-job pin). This adds the fleet-level default that the pin alone does not cover.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `cron/scheduler.py` — `_resolve_job_reasoning_config`: consult `cron.reasoning_effort` between the per-job pin and `resolve_reasoning_config`. It is the only resolver for cron runs (the detached worker runs the same module; auth-fallback swaps the model after this point).
- `hermes_cli/config_defaults.py` — `cron.reasoning_effort: ""` with a short comment.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/cron.md` — precedence and example in the "Per-job reasoning effort" tip.
- `cli-config.yaml.example` — commented example under `cron:`.
- `tests/cron/test_cron_reasoning_effort.py` — 5 new tests: applies when unpinned; pin wins; wins over `agent.reasoning_effort` and `reasoning_overrides`; empty/None is byte-identical to config resolution; invalid value warns and falls back.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/cron/test_cron_reasoning_effort.py -q` → 25 passed (20 existing + 5 new).
2. Set `agent.reasoning_effort: high` and `cron.reasoning_effort: low`; a cron run logs `using cron.reasoning_effort 'low'` while chat stays on `high`.

Full `tests/cron` run, same partial environment, with and without this change on `b4410b4`: 1348 passed / 23 failed (baseline) vs 1353 passed / 23 failed (this branch). The 23 pre-existing failures are unrelated (media delivery, estop, desktop ticker) and fail identically on `main` in this environment.

author: erinable
body:
Closes SKIL-88

建任何 issue 之前先在整个工作区查重，防止同一个问题从两条路径各建一张票（D6 被做了两次：SKIL-79 → PR #54，SKIL-81 → PR #55）。

## 复盘：哪一步漏了查重

| 时间（UTC） | 谁 | 做了什么 |
|---|---|---|
| 05:21 | Scribe（SKIL-77 的 run） | 按票面「另建一张跟踪 issue」建了 SKIL-79，挂在 SKIL-77 下，`backlog`、无负责人。这一步没错 |
| 05:40 | 成员（聊天） | 「请按你的建议将 **SKIL-79** 指派给 Sleuth，挂到合适的父 issue 下」 |
| 05:40:49 | Mika（聊天 run） | 建父 issue SKIL-80，描述里写了 SKIL-79 |
| 05:40–05:43 | Mika（SKIL-80 首次路由 run） | 把 SKIL-79 移到 SKIL-80 Stage 1，指派 Sleuth，置 `todo`。这一路是对的 |
| **05:43:54** | **Mika（同一个聊天 run）** | **在 SKIL-80 下又建了 SKIL-81（`--status todo --assignee Sleuth`），这一步漏了查重** |
| 05:44 | Mika（聊天 run） | 发现建错，把 SKIL-81 置 `cancelled` |
| 05:44 起 | Sleuth | SKIL-81 的 run 已经起了，`cancelled` 停不下来；Sleuth 照常交付，把状态改回 `in_review`，出了 PR #55，后来又和 #54 冲突 |

漏掉的原因有三条：

1. 聊天 run 越过了「入口」只建父 issue 的边界，自己又建了子 issue，和首次路由 run 并发做同一件事。
2. 唯一的幂等检查是 `issue children <parent>`，而 SKIL-80 是刚建的，下面没有子 issue；SKIL-79 那时还挂在 SKIL-77 下，这个检查看不到它。成员原话里已经点名了 SKIL-79，也没有据此复用。
3. 票建出来就是 `todo` 并且已指派，Sleuth 的 run 马上就起了；事后置 `cancelled` 撤不回来。

## 改动

- `skills/delivery-contract/SKILL.md` 新增「建票前查重」。任何 `multica issue create` 之前都要走这一步，包括 Scribe「另建跟踪票」和 Mika 建票：
  - **先分清要建哪种票**：父 issue，还是执行票或跟踪票。点名的 KEY 只在两者是同一种票时才直接复用。建父 issue 时，点名的 KEY 写进父 issue 描述，照常查重，只和已有的父 issue 比。
  - **两组关键词**：问题关键词（`D6`、`Task N`）和来源锚点（`specs/<slug>/`、代码位置、来源 KEY）。
  - **判定**：同一张票同时满足 (a) 标题命中问题关键词、(b) 描述里有同一个来源锚点，才算重复。只满足一条的，在评论里记为「同号不同源」，不复用。看不出来时问成员，默认答案是「不算重复，新建」。
  - **处理**，只针对同源重复：未完成的复用；`done` 的不新建，确有遗留才建「续」票；`cancelled` 的可以新建。
  - **建后复查**：所有新票都先建成 `backlog`，复查确认没有更早的同源票，再置 `todo`。已经起了 run 的重复票，先用 `runs --active` 找到 run 并 `cancel-task`，再置 `cancelled`。
  - **完成判据**：评论里写出关键词、来源锚点和结论；同一个问题关键词加同一个来源锚点下，未完成的票只有一张。
- `skills/orchestrate/SKILL.md`：
  - 开头加总规则。
  - 入口：聊天回合只建父 issue（先建成 backlog，复查后置 todo），不建子 issue，也不改现有 issue 的归属。
  - stage 模板、修订票：一律先建成 backlog，复查后置 todo。
  - 拆票：来源锚点用 `specs/<slug>/`，别的 spec 的同号 task 照建。
  - Triager 和 Architect 两个交接入口也各自写明了查重的关键词和锚点。

## 验证

用双条件判定回放两个场景：

```
Task 1，来源锚点 specs/new-feature/（模拟下一个 spec 拆票）：
  SKIL-61/48/59/45  done  a=True b=False -> 同号不同源，照建
D6，来源锚点 state-root.ts:72（排除 SKIL-80/77/88/81）：
  SKIL-79           done  a=True b=True  -> 重复，不会再建 SKIL-81
```

`git diff --check` 无输出。只改了上面两个 skill 文件。

修改意见请评论在 SKIL-88 上

Slider drags in the builder were doing whole-scene work on every step. Measured on the latest save in a headless offscreen harness (median time from a slider step to the next drawn frame, 24 steps per slider):

| Slider | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inside, processor list, any slider | 355 ms | 23 ms |
| Inside, battery length | 146 ms | 57 ms |
| Inside, fan size | 117 ms | 57 ms |
| Surface, trackpad width | 225 ms | 37 ms |
| Surface, keyboard spend | 228 ms | 148 ms |
| Chassis, width | 153 ms | 144 ms (work in the input handler 68 ms to 22 ms) |

What changed:
- The option list's per-option solves (one per processor, battery, and so on) and the Chassis tray's per-body solves wait until the build holds still for 150 ms. A lone change, such as a click, still comes through at once.
- The shell surfaces, grill slots, bumpers and decal faces rebuild only when their content changes, not every time the build is re-solved. Shell edges are only built in x-ray.
- Dimension lines keep their material across a drag, and well linings are keyed by index, so three no longer recompiles their shaders on every step.

## 何を変えたか

2026年の重賞（障害を含む）のうち、結果が入っているのに出走頭数（`fieldSize`）が無かった **84 レース**（56 ファイル）に、頭数を1行ずつ足した。ほかの行は変えていない（84 行の追加だけ）。

- 頭数は出走馬の行から数えた。着順か通過順がある馬を「走った馬」とし、取消・除外は除き、中止は数える。`data:fetch result` の `fieldSizeOf` と同じ数え方
- 通過順も着順も無い4頭は、netkeiba の結果ページで確かめた

| レース | 馬 | netkeiba | 扱い |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-03-29 中山11R マーチS | ハピ | 取消 | 数えない（15頭） |
| 2026-04-04 中山11R ダービー卿CT | タイムトゥヘヴン | 除外 | 数えない（15頭） |
| 2026-04-26 東京11R フローラS | サムシングスイート | 取消 | 数えない（12頭） |
| 2026-08-15 新潟9R 新潟ジャンプS | ピーターサイト | 中止（通過順なし） | **数える**（11頭。YAML にコメントを残した） |

**マージすると `data-import.yml` が本番の D1 に投入する**（`race.field_size` が埋まる）。

## レビューで見てほしいところ

- 頭数を netkeiba から取り直さず、出走馬の行から数えた。今年の重賞は出馬表（`data:fetch entries`）から全頭を入れているので、行の数がそのまま出走した馬になる。数えから外すかどうかが分かれた4頭だけ、netkeiba で確かめた
- 新潟ジャンプS は頭数が 11 になり、上りの入った馬（10頭）＋通過順のある中止（0頭）と合わない。そのため、ふりかえり画面ではこのレースの上りの順位は出ない（[#98](https://github.com/Atoyr/keiba-note/pull/98) の決まりどおり、安全側）

[#98](https://github.com/Atoyr/keiba-note/pull/98) で、ふりかえり画面に上りの順位（1〜3位の色の札）を足した。順位を出すのは、走った全頭の上りがそろっているとき（頭数と一致するとき）だけにしている。出走馬を気にしている馬だけ入れたレースで、入っている馬の中だけで数えると嘘の「上り1位」になるためだ。ところが今年の重賞は、結果の入った 94 レースのうち頭数があるのは 17 レースだけで、残りでは順位が出なかった。「今年の重賞で出ればよい」と決まったので、頭数を埋める。

author: mishan
body:
`an_ng_client_that_stops_reading_is_dropped_and_resumes_into_a_resync` (from #127) failed about one run in five on a busy machine. The reader it expects to hear every line was cut off.

- **Cause:** the flood sent lines as fast as the server took them, so it raced the readers as well as the stalled client. A reader descheduled for a moment fell a whole connection's bound behind and was dropped along with the client that never read.
- **Fix:** the flood is paced by the clients hearing it, not by a clock. `listen` publishes the last line it has heard on a `watch` channel. The talker's own echoes are parsed and published the same way. The talker waits whenever it is more than a small window of lines (`WINDOW`) ahead of either one. The window is a small fraction of every bound in play: the classic writer's queue, the live channel, and the half of the average that the budget lets a queue that has kept up always hold. So no reader gets near a bound, however long it is descheduled. Nothing waits on the stalled clients, so they are still buried as fast as the others read. The sleeps are gone, and `flood_paced` folds into `flood`.
- **Why the echoes count too:** with only the reader setting the pace, the budget case cut the talker. While the talker's session is busy taking lines, its echoes queue up behind them. Against the 4 MB budget, a talker far enough ahead of its echoes holds more than the average once the stalled clients are gone.
- **No hangs:** if a reader dies or stops, its publisher is dropped. The talker then stops instead of waiting forever, and the reader's own timeout reports the missing lines.
- **Unchanged:** the reader hears every line in order. The stalled classic client is hung up on. The ng one is dropped while still silent and resumes into a resync. In the budget case, the budget alone cuts the stalled clients. Every case finishes well inside the 60 s limit.
- **Cost:** the suite takes about 2 s idle, and about 8 to 13 s with the machine's cores oversubscribed 1.25x to 2.5x by busy loops. The 1 ms pacing took about 13 s even when the machine was idle.

**Verified**
- The suite passed seven idle runs, five runs with 30 busy loops on 24 cores, and three with 60.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`.

author: shekharkadyan
body:
## Background

The nightly integration run brings up a full PipesHub stack in Docker and runs pytest against it. One of its suites covers the storage service, the part of the Node app that stores uploaded files: upload, download, versioning, placeholders, rollback and so on.

Since #3593 (merged 26 Sep), the storage routes no longer accept a user's login token. Storage only checks which organisation a file belongs to, not who may see it, so only other PipesHub services may call it, using a short-lived "service token" signed with a secret called the scoped JWT secret. The storage tests now make those tokens themselves, so they need to know that secret.

## What was wrong

Nothing told the tests what the secret was. The integration stack's Docker Compose files never set it, so the app made up a random one on first start, and the nightly workflow never passed any value to pytest. The storage fixture (`sc` in `integration-tests/storage/conftest.py`) saw no secret and skipped.

## What it meant

Every storage test that needs a token skipped every night: upload, download, buffer, versioning, placeholder, rollback, metadata and the change check. Only the authentication tests, which check that bad tokens are refused and need no secret, still ran. A skip reads like a pass in the nightly report, so the storage service had in effect no nightly coverage, and nobody would have noticed.

## The fix, and why this way

- **One fixed, test-only secret for the integration stack.** Both integration Compose files (Neo4j and ArangoDB) now start the app with `pipeshub-integration-scoped-jwt-secret-test-only`, written the same way as the other test values there, such as the encryption key: `${SCOPED_JWT_SECRET:-<test value>}`. Setting `SCOPED_JWT_SECRET` in the environment still replaces it, and so does an empty value.
- **The same value reaches the tests.** The workflow sets `SCOPED_JWT_SECRET` once, in the job's environment. Docker Compose picks it up when it starts the stack, and every pytest step reads it, including the nightly storage step and a manual run that picks the storage marker. A repository secret named `TEST_SCOPED_JWT_SECRET` replaces the built-in value if anyone ever wants a real one, but never on a pull request: that run executes the pull request's own code, which must not see a real signing secret, so it always gets the test value. Setting it once, not per step, means the stack and the tests cannot disagree.
- **A missing secret now fails the nightly instead of skipping.** The fixture now follows the rule the connector suites already use: `PIPESHUB_REQUIRE_CONNECTOR_SECRETS`, which the workflow sets on the nightly and on a manual run that picks one suite, turns "skip" into "fail". The failure says which variable to set and where. On a developer's machine without the secret, the suite still skips, as before.
- The local template (`integration-tests/env.local.template`) now carries the same test value, so a developer running the integration Compose files gets a working storage suite without looking anything up. Both it and the README explain that the app reads this secret only on the first boot of a fresh volume.

No other integration test makes service tokens: only `integration-tests/storage/` uses this secret.

## What changes going forward

The storage suite runs in full on the nightly again. If the secret ever goes missing again, whether from a removed line or a renamed variable, the nightly turns red and says why, instead of quietly skipping.

## How it was checked

- **The fixture decides correctly.** Calling the fixture directly gives: no secret on a local run → skip; no secret with the nightly flag set → fail; secret set → a working storage client.
- **The token is one the app accepts.** A token minted by the suite with the pinned value carries `orgId`, `userId`, `scopes: ["storage:token"]`, `HS256` and a one-hour lifetime. Checked in Node with `jsonwebtoken` 9.0.3, the same key setup and scope check as `AuthTokenService.verifyScopedToken`: accepted with the pinned secret, rejected ("invalid signature") with any other.
- **Compose resolves the value.** `docker compose config` on both files gives the test value by default, `real-override` when that is set, and the test value again when the variable is empty (the case of a blank repository secret).
- **The workflow is valid.** actionlint 1.7.12 on `integration-tests.yml` reports the same five shellcheck notes as `main` (single quotes and redirect style in untouched steps), and nothing new.
- The full stack was not brought up locally: that means building the whole PipesHub image. The first nightly after merge is the end-to-end proof. Its storage report should show the upload, download and versioning tests passing, not skipped.

No change to docs.pipeshub.com: this only affects the repository's own integration tests.

author: martianoff
body:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/release.yml` builds and uploads binaries for whatever tag is pushed. It does not check the tag against the version declared in `gala.mod` / `MODULE.bazel`, and it never runs the binaries it builds. So a tag pushed before the version bump, or one with a typo, ships a release whose `gala version` and Bazel module disagree with the tag. A binary that fails on a clean machine, for example because the embedded stdlib is missing a file, also ships unnoticed.

## Changes

- **`verify-version` job.** It runs first, and `build` and `intellij-plugin` depend on it. It fails the release, with an `::error` annotation on the offending file, unless the release tag equals both:
  - the `gala X` line in `gala.mod`;
  - `version = "X"` in the `module(...)` block of `MODULE.bazel`.

  Tags are bare versions (`0.83.1`), so a `v`-prefixed tag fails too. The workflow runs on `release: created`, after the release and its tag exist, so a mismatch does not un-publish anything. It stops binaries from being built and attached, and leaves a release with no assets for the maintainer to delete and recreate.
- **Smoke test** on every row whose binary the runner can execute natively: linux/amd64 (ubuntu-latest), darwin/arm64 (macos-latest) and windows/amd64 (windows-latest, under bash):
  - the first line of `gala version` must be exactly `GALA version <tag>`;
  - `gala run` of a hello-world program, with a fresh `GALA_HOME` and `GALA_CACHE` under `RUNNER_TEMP`, must print `Hello, GALA!`. This exercises extracting the embedded stdlib and compiling on a clean machine, which the Bazel suite never does.

  A failing `gala version` or `gala run` produces an `::error` annotation. linux/arm64 and darwin/amd64 are cross-compiled and not run.
- **Go setup in the build job.** It now runs `actions/setup-go` (1.25) and exports `GOROOT`, as `test.yml` does. The stdlib transpile actions use the host Go SDK for type inference; release builds previously relied on whatever Go the runner image had preinstalled. The smoke test needs a Go toolchain too. The Bazel disk cache key now includes the Go patch version, as in `test.yml`, because `GOROOT` is part of the transpile action keys.
- **Permissions.** The workflow default drops from `contents: write` to `contents: read`. Only `upload-release` gets `contents: write`.

## Type of Change

- CI workflow change only; no product code touched

## Checklist

- [x] `bazel build //...` passes
- [ ] `bazel test //...` passes (n/a: workflow-only change)
- [ ] `bazel run //:gazelle` run (n/a)
- [ ] Documentation updated (n/a)

## Test Plan

- `actionlint` (v1.7.12) reports no findings on the workflow.
- The version-extraction commands, run on master, both yield `0.83.1`. The `#`-comment inside `module(...)` that mentions `version = X` is not matched.
- The smoke program, run locally with a branch-built CLI and a fresh `GALA_HOME`, prints `Hello, GALA!`. `gala version` for a stamped build prints `GALA version <tag>` on its first line.
- The release workflow runs only on `release: created`, so this PR's CI does not execute it. The first real run will be the next release.

## AI Assistance

- [ ] No AI assistance
- [x] AI-assisted — tool/model: Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5)
  - [ ] I have read and understood the whole diff, and I will answer review questions about it
  - [x] The agent followed `AGENTS.md`, and commits it wrote carry a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer

author: sinity
body:
## Summary
Stream Hermes JSON snapshot messages and their per-message evidence into the sealed preparation artifact as each message is decoded. Retained replay uses a bounded taxonomy witness, preserves higher-priority Hermes dispatch, and keeps timestamp normalization to running extrema.

## Problem
A supported Hermes `sessions/session_*.json` snapshot with many `messages` followed the single-object fallback in `prepare_jsonl_blob`: `_iter_json_stream` decoded the whole object, `parse_payload` held all parsed messages and events, and retained timestamp normalization built a timestamp list proportional to the session. One large snapshot could exhaust the worker before prepared messages were durable.

## Solution
Validate the snapshot envelope, then decode `messages.item` one at a time into SQLite message and event sinks. Preserve the ordinary parser's identity, active leaf, event order, admission proof, and shard rows. Carry bounded root taxonomy evidence for retained classification and apply the existing state DB, verification DB, and ATIF predicates before the snapshot shortcut. Reject malformed suffixes and changed source bytes before sealing. Reduce message and event timestamp evidence with running minimum and maximum values.

## Verification
- `devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_prepared_jsonl.py -k 'hermes_snapshot or retained_hermes_extracted'`: 9 passed (`.cache/verify/runs/20260927T085950Z-focused-test-2191679-3d0e18fe/run.json`). Covers parser/shard parity, first-row spill, corrupt suffix, retained callback, source mutation, extracted transcript refusal, future-type priority, and ATIF/state/verification precedence.
- `devtools test tests/unit/storage/test_archive_tiers_write.py -k 'normalization_remains_derived or normalized_derived_repeat'`: 2 passed (`.cache/verify/runs/20260927T083953Z-focused-test-2090284-b7fa6dda/run.json`).
- `devtools test tests/unit/sources/test_parsers_local_agent.py -k hermes_snapshot`: passed before an unrelated master rebase (`.cache/verify/runs/20260927T082529Z-focused-test-2025202-229f2725/run.json`).
- `devtools verify --quick`: passed on the completed source tree before commit (`.cache/verify/runs/20260927T090130Z-quick-2199943-2dd9a6d8/run.json`). The hosted quick gate runs against the pushed head.

## Remaining bounds
The Hermes `tools` catalog is still one aggregate session-event payload. A giant tool catalog, individual message, or scalar string remains resident; this change bounds growth across the message array and its per-message events.

## Problem
A live walkthrough of DEMO.md means about 20 commands typed by hand: tokens, JSON bodies and ids copied between calls. One typo in front of an audience stalls the demo. Issue #40.

## Change
- `scripts/demo.ps1` (Windows PowerShell 5.1). It resets the demo database, starts the service and signs the four demo tokens. It runs scenes 1, 1b, 2, 6 and 8 through the real API and checks 11 results. It pauses between scenes (`-NoPause` skips the pauses) and stops only the service it started.

- Review fixes on the paused draft:
  - It reads 4xx bodies from `ErrorDetails.Message`, which is where PowerShell 5.1 puts them. Before this, the 403 detail was lost.
  - It drops the `PowerShell.Exiting` subscription, which failed on a second run in the same window. `try/finally` stops the service instead.
  - Its Postgres readiness check goes over TCP.
  - It stops on a compose failure or if the service exits early.
  - It leaves the caller's folder unchanged.

booyaka101
body:
`checkout.session.completed` fires when the customer finishes Checkout, not when the money arrives. With cards those are the same moment. With delayed methods (ACH, SEPA and BECS debits, Bacs, some bank transfers) the session comes through with `payment_status: 'unpaid'` and settles days later, or fails. Checkout uses whatever payment methods are switched on in the Stripe dashboard, so a studio only has to enable one of those for this to happen.

`fulfillCheckoutSession` never looked at `payment_status`, so an unpaid session still created the pass or membership and wrote a `paid` payment row. If the debit then bounced, the client kept the credits and the revenue report kept the money.

Unpaid sessions are now acknowledged with `awaiting_payment` and nothing is written. `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded` goes through the same fulfilment once it's paid, and the existing session-id idempotency covers both events. `async_payment_failed` needs no handler because nothing was granted.

Studios with delayed methods turned on need to add `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded` to their webhook endpoint, and the README setup step now lists it. Card-only studios see no change, because their sessions arrive as `paid`.

One thing I left alone: `/buy/thanks` still says the pass is active, which isn't true yet for a delayed payment. Fixing that means fetching the session on the thanks page, so it's a separate change if it's wanted.

The new test fails on main. 128/128 green.

author: zinsanjp
body:
### Summary
`POST /api/views/track` and `POST /api/views/track-bulk` trusted the client-supplied `x-user-id` header without any session verification. Since these routes are unauthenticated (anonymous visitors need to be able to view caws), an attacker could rotate `x-user-id` from a single IP to bypass Redis view-count deduplication entirely and manipulate `GET /api/views/trending`.

### Root cause
```typescript
const userId = req.header('x-user-id') ? Number(req.header('x-user-id')) : undefined
```
`ViewTracker.trackView`/`trackBulkViews` key the 24-hour Redis dedup set on `user:${userId}` whenever `userId` is present, falling back to `ip:${ipHash}` only when it's absent. An attacker sending `x-user-id: 1`, `x-user-id: 2`, `x-user-id: 3`, ... from one IP gets a fresh, never-before-seen dedup key on every request, so every request increments `caw.viewCount` — no session, wallet signature, or ownership check required.

### Fix
Added `resolveTrustedUserId(req)`, mirroring the two-layer verification `getAuthenticatedUserId` already uses in `bookmarks.ts`/`pins.ts`:
1. `extractSession(req)` resolves the session from the session cookie.
2. The requested `x-user-id` is only accepted if it's in the session's `authorizedTokenIds`.
3. Defense-in-depth: the token's *current* on-record owner address must still be in the session's `authorizedAddresses`. This closes the stale-session window between an L1 transfer and the watcher pruning the old session — without it, a previous owner's still-live session could keep attributing views to a token they no longer hold.

Unlike bookmarks/pins, failure here never 401s — these routes must stay usable by anonymous visitors. Any verification failure (no session, unauthorized token, stale ownership) falls back to the session's own primary token, or `undefined` with no session at all, which `ViewTracker` keys on `ip:${ipHash}` as before.

Also tightened `cawId` validation in `/track` to match the existing check in `/track-bulk` (reject non-positive/non-finite values with a 400, instead of only checking falsy).

### Verification
Manual script against a throwaway Postgres database and the real Redis session store (`ioredis`, same `caw:session:` key format as `sessionStore.ts`), calling `resolveTrustedUserId` directly with mocked requests. Five scenarios:

| Scenario | Input | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Anonymous, spoofed `x-user-id` | no session cookie, `x-user-id: <other token>` | `undefined` (falls back to IP dedup) |
| Valid session, own token | session owns token A, `x-user-id: A` | `A` |
| Valid session, unauthorized token | session owns token A only, `x-user-id: B` | `A` (falls back) |
| Stale session, transferred token | session's `authorizedTokenIds` still lists token B, but B's current on-record owner is a different address than the session's | falls back to the session's other legitimately-owned token |
| Stale session, still-owned token | same stale session, requesting a token it still legitimately owns | that token, accepted |

Before the fix (same mocked requests against the original header-only logic): the anonymous-spoofing and stale-session scenarios both returned the attacker-supplied tokenId directly — confirming the vulnerability and the fix.

`tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors.

### Not addressed here
- A repo-wide `grep` for `x-user-id` found it used, unguarded by a session check, in several other routes (`caws.ts`, `users.ts`, `search.ts`, `hashtags.ts`) for read-side personalization (e.g. "is the viewer following this user"), and behind `requireAuth`/`verifyOwnership` in write-side routes (`scheduled.ts`, `tips.ts`). I did not audit these as part of this PR — the blast radius and correct fix likely differ per route (some may already be adequately protected by `requireAuth`), and mixing that into a view-tracking fix would make this harder to review. Flagging it here as something worth a separate look.
- `sponsor.ts` also reads `x-user-id` directly (line ~2171); same caveat, not audited here.

zinsanjp

author: swkim86
body:
Add an opt-in REST harness that verifies the LambdaDB behaviors needed before PostgreSQL index execution: batched mutations, an indexed-write barrier, immutable Tags, vector/BM25 search, and large result downloads.

Each data request contains multiple documents and is acknowledged before the next request. A final marker with a unique revision must be visible through `consistentRead=false` fetch before creating a Tag; that marker and the expected data are then checked through the Tag. Per-request atomicity and serial acknowledgement ordering are recorded as owner-confirmed assumptions, distinct from live observations.

- 26 live checks/observations completed on fresh vector/BM25 collections; small cosine and BM25 reference comparisons passed, old Tags retained their data/scores, and all temporary resources were removed.
- Large data was sent as 52 + 52 + 6 documents. The offloaded result path required bounded gzip decoding; after that fix the entire live suite passed. Downloads carry no API key.
- For 110 known matches, query returned 100 with `total=100` and no ranked cursor. A local post-filter example missed ten eligible IDs. Immutable list pagination separately enumerated all 116 fixture documents.
- Marker-write through verified-Tag times were 48–103 seconds in this run, not a product SLO. Strict BM25 overlays, ranked continuation, production replay/fencing, and commit-wait latency remain open.

Review hardening: normalize HTTP protocol failures so cleanup continues and final reporting completes; use unique, exclusive report temporary files. Regression tests cover open/read failures, cleanup continuation, concurrent report saves, and preservation of existing files. These changes were tested offline; the live evidence remains pinned to `22c8281`.

Validation: 13 offline safety tests, shell/YAML checks, documentation link checks, and `git diff --check` passed. The [run guide and interpretation](https://github.com/lambdadb/pg_onesearch/blob/feature/live-compatibility/docs/live-compatibility.md) and [sanitized evidence](https://github.com/lambdadb/pg_onesearch/blob/feature/live-compatibility/docs/evidence/live-compatibility-2026-09-27.json) distinguish source-confirmed requirements from measurements. The tested harness matches commit `22c8281`; documentation and CI changes were prepared separately. [Full CI](https://github.com/lambdadb/pg_onesearch/actions/runs/36307517810) passed on PR head `43140df`: the 13 offline safety tests, existing product/protocol tests, 20 worker cases, 18 client cases, packaging, and clean installation. Authenticated live tests are manual and remain separate evidence.

Connection values and the private target fingerprint are absent from the public diff. This is a REST compatibility experiment, not an implemented PostgreSQL remote index or a completed production transaction protocol.

body:
## Summary

Playlists ビューのコンテンツ領域にある曲リストをテーブルにする、v1.3 の仕様書を `docs/specs/v1.3/` へ追加します。ソースコードの変更はありません。

- 曲リストを `<table>` にし、ヘッダー行 (`<thead>`) を上端へ固定する
- カラム幅のリサイズ、ヘッダーのクリックでのソート、表示カラムの切り替えに対応する
- 行の Virtualization (@tanstack/react-virtual) は維持する
- 先行例は [@akabeko/music-metadata-editor の GUI](https://github.com/akabekobeko/npm-music-metadata-editor/tree/main/packages/gui) のスプレッドシート

## Changes

| 種別 | ファイル | 内容 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 計画 | `README.md` / `scope.md` / `roadmap.md` | テーマ、やること・やらないこと、4 フェーズの分割 |
| アーキテクチャー | `architecture/table-library.md` / `table-library-candidates.md` | ライブラリー選定と候補の比較 |
| | `architecture/table-structure.md` | 要素の構成、ヘッダーの固定、Virtualization、横スクロール |
| | `architecture/column-settings.md` / `column-settings-types.md` | `AppSettings` への保存、sanitize、store、型 |
| 機能 | `features/playlist-table.md` | 行の操作と v1.2 からの変更点 |
| | `features/columns.md` | カラムの一覧、既定の表示と幅 |
| | `features/column-resize.md` / `column-sort.md` / `column-visibility.md` | リサイズ、ソート、表示の切り替え |

`docs/specs/README.md` に v1.3 へのリンクを追加しています。

## 主な判断

- **ライブラリー**: 独自実装とし、TanStack Table は次点。必要な機能が小さいこと、`data` / `columns` に安定した参照を求めるため useMemo を既定にしない方針と衝突することが理由
- **ソートの解除**: 「ソートなし」の状態は作らず、連番カラム (`#`) のクリックで登録順へ戻る
- **Drag & Drop での並べ替え**: 登録順の昇順かつ絞り込みなしのときだけ有効
- **タイトル カラム**: カラム幅の合計がコンテナーより狭いときは、タイトルが残りの幅を引き受ける
- **メニュー カラム**: 常に表示。ヘッダーは空欄で、横スクロール中も右端へ固定
- **永続化**: カラムの表示と幅は全プレイリスト共通で保存し、ソートは保存しない

## 確認してほしい点

依頼になかったものを仕様に入れています。不要なら外します。

- 連番とタイトルも常に表示するカラムにした
- カラムを 16 個定義した (既定の表示は v1.2 と同じ 5 つ)
- ハンドルのダブルクリックで幅を既定値へ戻す操作
- カラム メニューの「Reset columns」
- カラムの並び順の変更 (ヘッダーの Drag & Drop) は v1.3 の対象外とした

## Notes

PR 作成前の code-review の指摘 10 件にすべて対応しました。

| 指摘 | 対応 |
| --- | --- |
| タイトルを縮める方向へドラッグすると、表示が変わらず保存値だけが変わる | ドラッグの下限を「不足分を引き受けた幅」とし、開始値と同じなら保存しない |
| 非表示にしたソート カラムを再表示するとソートが復活する | 導出ではなく、レンダー中の検出で state を登録順へ書き換える |
| `scrollMargin` による行の二重のずれ | `translateY(start - scrollMargin)` と `scrollPaddingStart`、ヘッダーの高さの定数を明記 |
| scope の「Main に手を入れない」が他の仕様と矛盾 | Main の変更は設定の項目追加と検証だけ、と書き直した |
| 「値のない行」の定義が不足 | カラムごとの条件の表を追加 (`disc` と `duration` の 0 の扱いを含む) |
| `widths` の sanitize の順序と型が不正な場合が未定義 | 丸めてから 1 以上を判定、オブジェクトでなければ `widths` だけ空にする |
| Phase 1 だけでは広いウィンドウで右側に空白ができる | コンテナーの幅の取得と `fitTitleWidth` を Phase 1 へ移した |
| コンテナーの幅を適用する位置が未定義 | `resolveColumnWidths` → `useColumnResize` → `fitTitleWidth` の順序を明記 |
| `PlaylistHeader` の構成要素の記述が不一致 | 実装に合わせて統一 |
| テーマの「並び順」がカラムの並べ替えと読める | 文言を修正。キーボードでのソートは範囲内と明記 |

## Test

- 仕様書内の相対リンクがすべて存在することを確認
- ローカルのパスやユーザー名が含まれていないことを確認

author: jmtatsch
body:
## Problem

`SynologyAuth.login()` and `.logout()` call `auth.cgi` with `requests.get(..., params=payload)`, which puts `passwd`, `otp_code` and `_sid` in the URL. DSM writes the full request line to its own nginx access log, as does every proxy in between, so an account password outlives the session in plaintext in at least one file nobody treats as a secret.

Observed on DSM 7.3.2-86009 Update 4:

```
GET  /webapi/auth.cgi  query_keys=[account, passwd, session, ...]   PASSWORD_IN_URL=True
```

Neither call passed a `timeout`, while every other request in the codebase uses `timeout=15`. A NAS that accepts the connection then stalls hangs the startup auto-login loop indefinitely, and hangs `relogin()` while it holds `_relogin_lock`, wedging session recovery for every caller queued behind it.

## Fix

Both calls become `requests.post(..., data=payload, timeout=AUTH_TIMEOUT)`. `auth.cgi` reads the same parameters from a form body — that is what the DSM web UI sends — so this is a transport change only; the payload is untouched.

```
POST /webapi/auth.cgi  query_keys=[]  timeout=15                    PASSWORD_IN_URL=False
```

The timeout fix rewrites the same two statements, so it ships here rather than in a second PR that would conflict with this one.

## Verification

Tested against real hardware (DSM 7.3.2-86009 Update 4, RS822+), not just mocks: login succeeds, a SynoToken is issued, the session is genuinely usable (listed real shares), and logout succeeds. Confirmed no credential appears in any request URL.

The test harness now patches `requests.post` and makes `requests.get` **raise**, so a regression to the query-string form fails loudly instead of being quietly re-recorded.

## Notes

Independent of my other open PRs; applies cleanly in any order.

body:
## CI follow-up for #1053

The Playwright mobile gallery gate failed for the Standard/Filterable design because the newly fixed-position comment composer remained open after comment submission and intercepted the subsequent download tap.

The failing log shows Playwright resolving the download link correctly, but the `[data-comment-panel]` form/textarea intercepted pointer events until the 30s click timeout.

### Fix
- Close the Standard gallery comment panel immediately after its comment form is submitted.
- Preserve the asynchronous comment submission/count update behavior.
- Restore access to the photo action controls beneath the mobile fixed panel, including Download.

This PR is intentionally based on #1053's branch so it contains only the CI regression fix and can be merged into #1053 (or retargeted to `dev` after #1053 merges).

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a local-first, per-project coordination layer so autonomous agents can claim tasks, write durable inbox/outbox records, and hand off reviews without racing over a shared in-memory runtime.
- Prevent unsafe terminal injection by detecting shell prompt quiescence and gating synthetic nudges until an agent is idle.

### Description
- Add HIVE data models and JSON serializers under `app/src/main/java/com/jarves/mh/orchestrator/HiveProtocol.kt` representing canonical tasks, inbox items, and outbox reports.
- Implement `HiveCoordinator` in `app/src/main/java/com/jarves/mh/orchestrator/HiveCoordinator.kt` to manage `.hive/` layout, atomic write/rename persistence, single-claim assignment semantics, dependency checks, durable outbox writes, and automatic review-task creation/queueing.
- Add prompt quiescence detection and a `WorkerLifecycle` in `app/src/main/java/com/jarves/mh/orchestrator/AgentLifecycle.kt` to track agent states and withhold terminal nudges until the PTY is quiescent.
- Add unit tests covering assignment, double-claim protection, review handoff/outbox preservation, ANSI prompt readiness, and withholding/delivery behavior in `app/src/test/java/com/jarves/mh/orchestrator/*`.

### Testing
- Ran `git diff --check`, which produced no whitespace/errors and succeeded.
- Added unit tests for `HiveCoordinator` and `AgentLifecycle` but running `./gradlew testOnlineDebugUnitTest --tests 'com.jarves.mh.orchestrator.*'` failed during Gradle configuration due to the environment JVM (`25.0.2`) not matching the project's expected runtime/JDK configuration, so the test execution was blocked.

body:
## 问题

AUTO-MAS 的 `MumuManager.open()` 只判断 MuMu 的 Android 状态为 online，就立即写入 M9A 配置并启动 M9A。实际运行中 MuMu 仍可能处于 ADB `offline` 状态，M9A 自动探测失败后拿到空的 ADB 序列号，并记录“初始化控制器失败”和“M9A 已放弃本次任务”。

本机 2026-09-27 的日志同时证明：AUTO-MAS 启动时 MuMu ADB 返回 `device offline`；等待 ADB 就绪后单独启动 M9A，则成功识别 `127.0.0.1:16384` 并完成控制器初始化。

## 修复

- 在 MuMu 已在线和刚启动变为在线的两条路径中，等待 `MuMuManager.exe adb -v <index> get-state` 返回 `device`。
- ADB 在 `MaxWaitTime` 内仍未就绪时抛出启动异常，沿用现有 M9A 的模拟器失败处理路径。
- 移除无法解决启动竞态、且会掩盖真实就绪状态的配置回退注入。
- 增加回归测试，并更新版本修复记录。

## 验证

- 实机 MuMu 命令：`adb -v 0 get-state` 返回 `device`，`devices` 显示 `127.0.0.1:16384 device`。
- 实机单独启动 M9A：日志记录设备名称、ADB 路径和序列号 `127.0.0.1:16384`，控制器初始化通过；后续失败来自独立的 Agent 外部组件，不是 ADB 连接。
- `python -m py_compile app/utils/emulator/mumu.py app/task/M9A/AutoProxy.py tests/test_emulator_device_listing.py` 通过。
- `git diff --check` 和 `res/version.json` JSON 解析通过。
- pytest 当前环境无法收集测试：缺少 `truststore` 依赖。

## Sourcery 总结

改善模拟器就绪状态，并增强整个应用中的任务执行、通知、配置处理和自动化集成的稳定性。

新功能：
- 在依赖模拟器的任务启动前，增加可靠的 MuMu ADB 就绪状态检测。
- 改进通知投递、本地 webhook 代理处理以及 Windows 通知文本长度限制。
- 统一配置检查、基于 UI 的映射和运行时队列中的 HSR 引擎选择。
- 保留原生 MAA 任务选项，同时改进歼灭完成检测和任务配置。
- 更可靠地处理 MaaEnd 任务移除、资源缓存失效、启动失败和流终止。
- 为 MaaEnd 账户登录失败流程添加诊断截图。

Bug 修复：
- 通过等待 MuMu ADB 报告设备就绪来避免 M9A 启动竞争问题，并通过现有的模拟器错误路径显示超时失败。
- 修复 MaaEnd、MAA、HSR、通用脚本和日志监控中的过时或无效任务执行问题。
- 防止配置初始化失败、通知溢出、本地 webhook 代理错误以及更新包下载名称错误。

改进：
- 改进异步自启动任务的生命周期处理和错误报告。
- 改进外部脚本配置的清理与恢复，以处理文件被锁定或部分删除的情况。
- 为 Endfield 清单检查添加缓存失效机制，并持久化主页布局滚动提示设置。
- 优化 Endfield 登录账户选择，并在登录失败时捕获截图。

构建：
- 将发布下载构件名称从 Lite 包名称更新为标准 setup 包名称。

文档：
- 添加 MaaEnd 更新日志条目，说明无效任务筛选和无可执行任务的处理方式。

测试：
- 增加针对 MuMu ADB 就绪状态、通知文本裁剪、HSR 引擎回退、MAA 歼灭完成以及原生任务配置选项保留的回归测试覆盖。

日常维护：
- 更新版本元数据和默认任务配置字段。

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Sourcery 总结

确保 MuMu ADB 就绪后，再启动依赖它的 M9A 任务。

错误修复：
- 在继续初始化模拟器之前，等待 MuMu ADB 报告设备就绪，以避免 M9A 启动竞态。
- 如果 MuMu ADB 未能在配置的超时时间内就绪，则报告启动失败，以便现有的模拟器错误处理机制能够报告该失败。

增强功能：
- 对已在线和新启动的 MuMu 实例均应用 ADB 就绪检查。
- 添加从 ADB 离线状态恢复的回归测试覆盖。

测试：
- 添加回归测试，验证 MuMu 启动会等待 ADB 从离线状态转换为设备状态。

杂项：
- 更新发布版本元数据。

## Summary by Sourcery

Ensure MuMu ADB is ready before launching dependent M9A tasks.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent M9A startup races by waiting for MuMu ADB to report a ready device before continuing emulator initialization.
- Raise a startup failure when MuMu ADB does not become ready within the configured timeout so existing emulator error handling can report the failure.

Enhancements:
- Apply ADB readiness checks to both already-online and newly-started MuMu instances.
- Add regression coverage for recovery from the ADB offline state.

Tests:
- Add a regression test verifying that MuMu startup waits for ADB to transition from offline to device state.

Chores:
- Update release version metadata.

author: jmtatsch
body:
## Problem

The Dockerfile ends with `COPY .env* ./`, and `.dockerignore` does not exclude `.env`. On any machine where the developer followed the README and put `SYNOLOGY_PASSWORD` in `.env`, that password is copied into an image layer. `docker history` is enough to read it back, and deleting the file in a later layer would not remove it.

## Fix

Drop the `COPY`, and add `.env` / `.env.*` to `.dockerignore` so a future `COPY . .` cannot reintroduce it. `env.example` has no leading dot and is unaffected.

Nothing needs the copied file: both compose files already mount `~/.config/synology-mcp` read-only and pass configuration through `environment:`, which are the two supported paths. On a fresh clone there is no `.env` at all, so the glob matched nothing and the line did nothing — except on the machines where it did damage.

## Verification

Image builds clean; I ran it and confirmed `/app` contains no `.env`.

## Notes

Independent of my other open PRs; applies cleanly in any order.

body: A static daily digest of Elon Musk, built with Eleventy and deployed to GitHub Pages at `/elon/`. New days are added as `digests/YYYY-MM-DD.md` only. A push to `main` rebuilds and deploys; pull requests build and check without deploying. The home page shows the latest digest in full (date, covers line, and a Coming up panel taken from that file’s “Travel and what's coming up” list), then earlier digests. Each day has a permalink such as `/elon/2026-09-27/`, with previous and next links once more than one file exists. Search is client-side from a built JSON index, and `/elon/feed.xml` is an RSS 2.0 feed. Times are Nepal Time. **Pages setting:** in the repository, open **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment**, and set **Source** to **GitHub Actions**. That is the only setting required. It is not stored in the repo. Pages is not enabled on this repo yet (the Pages API returns 404). After the source is set to GitHub Actions, merging this pull request — or running the workflow by hand on `main` — publishes the site. The first digest is `digests/2026-09-27.md`. ## Walkthrough Home page, desktop width: [Home page at desktop width](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-42f2c648-298a-5f38-810d-29a5ec2416f5/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fhome_desktop.png) Home page, mobile width: [Home page at mobile width](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-42f2c648-298a-5f38-810d-29a5ec2416f5/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fhome_mobile.png) Digest page: [Digest page for 2026-09-27](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-42f2c648-298a-5f38-810d-29a5ec2416f5/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fdigest_desktop.png) Search for a word that appears only in the body: [Search results for Colossus](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-42f2c648-298a-5f38-810d-29a5ec2416f5/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fsearch_colossus.png) [elon_home_digest_search_and_theme.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-42f2c648-298a-5f38-810d-29a5ec2416f5/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Felon_home_digest_search_and_theme.mp4) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: geforcelegend
body:
Iris will always apply `iris_transforms.TextureMat` on `textureMatrix` and `gl_TextureMatrix[0]` if existing shader is core profile [here](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/b388d57491ca3bdf29c86bea79ba1f1b41dfcc92/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/pipeline/transform/transformer/VanillaCoreTransformer.java#L87-L89), unlike [what compatibility profile transformer do](https://github.com/IrisShaders/Iris/blob/b388d57491ca3bdf29c86bea79ba1f1b41dfcc92/common/src/main/java/net/irisshaders/iris/pipeline/transform/transformer/VanillaTransformer.java#L169). This will result in wrong texture coordinate for enchanted items, usually let them become invisible, as enchantment glint also use `iris_transforms.TextureMat` for transform.

This pr make the core profile transformer works like compatibility profile transformer, let `textureMatrix` be `mat4(1.0)` if it contains overlay or glint.

## Summary

The playtest guide assumed testers already had the Vega SDK. It now says what installing a playtest build needs. Part of #107.

- **The SDK.** A link to Amazon's "Install the Vega SDK", which covers macOS and Ubuntu.
- **Developer mode.** A Fire TV Stick needs an Amazon Developer account, signed in with `vega devmode login`, and the Stick on the same network as the computer. Amazon's developer-mode guide lists both.
- **The Virtual Device's package.** The example installs the Stick's armv7 package. The guide now names the aarch64 and x86_64 packages for the Virtual Device.
- **Upgrades.** A newer beta installs over the one there and keeps its saved game, results and settings.

## How it was checked

- **The Amazon pages.** Both open (HTTP 200) and say what the guide now says. The SDK page gives dependencies for macOS and Ubuntu. The developer-mode page lists the developer account, `vega devmode login` and the shared network.
- **The upgrade line** rests on the Vega Virtual Device. On 27 September, beta 3 installed over beta 2 resumed the saved game and kept the completed-games record and the music volume.
- **The checksum command** already in the guide was run on macOS with one package downloaded, and it passes.
- **Gates.** At the root, `npm run check`, `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, 161 tests and `git diff --check` pass. Native code is untouched.

body:
## Summary

The first live England run was a London smoke test with 10 places. It found 8 real Judaica shops, including Royal Judaica, Divrei Kodesh, Jerusalem The Golden, Hendon Judaica and Aisenthal. One email on the Outreach sheet was wrong.

- **Problem:** Torah Treasures was given `contact@martfury.com`. Martfury is the WooCommerce theme the shop's website is built on, and its placeholder addresses (`contact@`, `career@`, `customercare@`, `media@`) were left on the live site.
- **Fix:** demo addresses from common shop themes, and placeholder domains (`company.com`, `yourstore.com`, `demo-…`), are now discarded. That row moves to "No email found" and keeps its phone number, instead of carrying an address that would reach the theme vendor.
- **Kept:** `mail.com` addresses. It's a real email provider, and a second commit keeps it off the blocklist.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 70 pass. The new test uses the real addresses from the run, and checks that genuine shop and `mail.com` addresses still come through.

body: Новое мини-приложение собирается рядом со старым. Старые `app.html`, `boinya-c/app.html`, `boinya-c/app.main.js`, партнёрский миниапп, Goodboy и Varka по поведению не менялись. `Code.gs` и worker не трогались. Бот на `next.html` не переключается. Мержить этот черновик не нужно. ## Как открыть Файл `boinya-c/next.html` на GitHub Pages, в той же папке, что и старое приложение. Вход тот же: Telegram `initData`, `authMode=enforce`. Вне Telegram — экран «Откройте через Telegram». Нет доступа — «Запросить доступ», заявка уже есть — «Ожидание», сеть пропала — «Повторить». Справка для человека: `boinya-c/next/HELP.md`. ## Что работает Каркас: шапка (раздел и контекст), колокольчик со счётчиком только если задачи разрешены (`deferredScreen.none` прячет колокольчик), нижняя панель по дереву прав как в старом приложении. У владельца 6 вкладок: Заказы, Клиенты, Производство, Склад, Цели, Ещё. У остальных — только те разделы, на которые есть право. Обычный менеджер видит Заказы и Ещё; на скрине менеджера 5 вкладок, потому что в доступах выданы подписки, производство и склад. Курьер, нарезчик и склад без панели: заглушка и ссылка на старую версию. Нижний лист (крестик, свайп, тап по фону — ввод заказа не стирается), тост, каркас загрузки, пусто, ошибка с «Повторить», полоса «Идёт обработка…» после 8 секунд, кнопка «Сохраняю…» без второго нажатия. «Точно сохранено» только когда таблица подтвердила запись (`sheetsVerified`). До этого — «Вношу…». Заказы → Новый: типы ПП, БП, Розница, Партнёр; клиент, две собаки, телефон, адрес и координаты, подъезд, день включая субботу и воскресенье, «полный» от 6 заказов, «Будущая неделя», цена и слот, состав, крошки, чеклист, «Из подписки ПП», «На потом», вопрос «Перенести данные?» при смене типа. Сохранение — тот же `saveBooking`, что у старой формы. Расчёт цен скопирован из `app.main.js` без переписывания (`boinya-c/next/order-engine.js`). ## Заглушки Неделя, Месяц, Клиенты, Производство, Склад, Ещё и Цели («скоро»). На каждом экране кнопка «Открыть в старой версии» ведёт на `boinya-c/app.html`. Список задач по колокольчику тоже пока ссылка в старую версию. ## Прогресс по карте **44 из 171** перенесено, 127 заглушка, 0 не начато. Таблица: `boinya-c/next/PORTING.md`. ## Проверка `node --test boinya-c/next/order-parity.test.mjs` — 8 из 8. Одинаковый ввод даёт тот же `saveBooking` и те же цены: розница 42 (лёгкое 200 г = 18, трахея 3 шт = 24), с платной доставкой 51; ПП — цена из поля и слот `2/2`; БП — цена `0`. Две собаки пишутся в корзину с полем `dog`. Старые тесты не менялись: в diff только новые файлы `boinya-c/next.html` и `boinya-c/next/`. Скрины Playwright, 390×844, мок бэкенда и initData: [Заказы, новый, верх](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-699f508e-4e14-523f-8b85-20c06578a6d4/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fnext-orders-new-top.png) [Заказы, новый, низ](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-699f508e-4e14-523f-8b85-20c06578a6d4/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fnext-orders-new-bottom.png) [Лист смены типа](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-699f508e-4e14-523f-8b85-20c06578a6d4/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fnext-type-sheet.png) [Лист добавления позиции](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-699f508e-4e14-523f-8b85-20c06578a6d4/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fnext-add-item.png) [Состояния экранов](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-699f508e-4e14-523f-8b85-20c06578a6d4/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fnext-states.png) [Панель владельца, 6 вкладок](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-699f508e-4e14-523f-8b85-20c06578a6d4/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fnext-nav-owner.png) [Панель менеджера, 5 вкладок](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-699f508e-4e14-523f-8b85-20c06578a6d4/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fnext-nav-manager.png) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

body:
## What

Moves the pinned `cathedral` archive in the hash-locked reproduction environment from `cathedral-compute` to `cathedral-sandbox` at the same commit, `655c264421a1f5f2e625a372a40f595aa1e114ab`, with the archive's new digest.

| Site | Change |
|---|---|
| `requirements/sn39-reproduction.lock` | URL -> `cathedral-sandbox`, `--hash` `2384833b…` -> `98f4bf8c…` |
| `pyproject.toml` | `provenance` extra, same |
| `scripts/build_sn39_release_manifest.py` | `EXPECTED_CATHEDRAL_URL`, `EXPECTED_CATHEDRAL_ARCHIVE_SHA256` (+ comment) |
| `scaffold/sn39_public_reproduction.py` | `EXPECTED_RELEASE_PINS["reproduction_dependencies"]` `765f9042…` -> `8a04cced…` (sha256 of the lock) |
| `docs/SN39_MAINNET_RELEASE_20260724.md`, `docs/SN39_LAUNCH_CUTOVER_20260726.md` | component table; "Amendment 2" record |

## Why

The required `Two-mode provenance` check is red on every PR at "Build the hash-locked launch environment" (e.g. #435): `pip --require-hashes` rejects the archive. `cathedral-compute` was renamed to `cathedral-sandbox`; GitHub archives embed the repo name as the top-level directory, so the bytes changed while the commit did not. This is the second time; #421 fixed the first rename with the same five-site checklist, which this PR follows.

author: jmtatsch
body:
## Problem

`_handle_login` returns `"Session ID: {sid}"` followed by `json.dumps(result)`, which also carries `synotoken` and the long-lived trusted-device token. A tool result is written into the MCP client's conversation transcript, which outlives the session by a long way and travels wherever that transcript goes.

Verified on DSM 7.3.2-86009 Update 4: an ordinary password login, on an account with **2FA switched off**, still returns an 86-character device token. So this is not a 2FA-only exposure — every `synology_login` call leaked three live credentials.

## Fix

The SID is truncated to the same 10 characters `_handle_logout` already reports — enough to correlate with the server log, useless as a credential — and the raw response is dropped.

The device token is still printed for the **2FA bootstrap** (the call that supplied an `otp_code` and holds no `device_id` yet). The tool's own description promises the token back for exactly that call, and a legacy `.env` setup has no other way to obtain it. It is not printed on any other login, because DSM sends one every time.

The failure branch dumped the whole response too; it now reports the DSM error code with the decoding table, which is the part a caller can act on — 400 and 403 call for different responses.

## A related bug this turned up

DSM names the device-token field differently per API version, verified on the same build:

| `SYNO.API.Auth` version | field |
| --- | --- |
| **v7** (tried first by `login_with_session`) | `device_id` |
| v6, v3 | `did` |

This PR reads both. Worth flagging separately: `login_with_session`, `_login_nas` and `config.save_device_id` all read only `did`, so on v7 the token is never cached or persisted. That looks like the root cause of the v6-preference workaround at `synology_auth.py:111` (*"a v7 login with `enable_device_token=yes` succeeds but returns no `did`"*). Happy to open a follow-up.

## Verification

Confirmed against real hardware: an ordinary login now emits no SID, no SynoToken and no device token; the bootstrap path still surfaces the token.

## Notes

Independent of my other open PRs; applies cleanly in any order.

author: rabestro
body:
## Summary

The build packages everything under `native/assets/` into each `.vpkg`, but `generate-assets.mjs` cleared only `assets/sfx` and `assets/music`. Anything else survived from an earlier run, another branch or a hand copy. On 27 September a stray `assets/probe/` of test tones from `probe/76-music-player` would have shipped in all three v0.1.0-beta.3 packages. It was caught only because `native/assets` was deleted by hand.

Closes #122.

- **The fix.** `main()` deletes the whole of `assets/` before writing it.
  - The issue allowed two fixes: delete the directory, or refuse and name the strays. Deleting cannot trip over the generator's own earlier output, and it needs no list of expected entries to keep up to date.
  - The splash is still staged in `build/splash`, outside `assets/`.
  - The digest checks in `copySounds` and `copyMusic` are unchanged. Each still clears its own folder, so it stays correct when called alone.
- **An injectable root.** `main`, `copySounds` and `copyMusic` take the application directory as an optional `root`, defaulting to `native/`. The existing generator test, `test/splash.test.ts`, does not inject one: it runs `main()` on the real tree. So there was no pattern to follow, and this is the smallest one that works.
- **The test.** `test/assets.test.ts` copies the generator's inputs (`icon/`, `brand/`, `sounds/`, `music/`) to a temporary root and plants strays under its `assets/`:
  - a folder of its own, `probe/`, with a WAV and an MP3;
  - a loose file;
  - a file next to the icon and one next to the splash.

  It then runs `main(root)`. The files left must be exactly the icon, the splash archive, and the sounds and music the run reports, and `probe/` must be gone. The inputs are copied, not linked, so the deletion cannot reach the real ones. The real `native/assets/`, which `splash.test.ts` reads back, is never touched.
- **Docs.**
  - One sentence in `native/README.md`, under Icon and splash.
  - The `.gitignore` comment on `native/assets/`, which still named `generate-splash.mjs`.

**One consequence.** The probe branch `probe/76-music-player` writes its tones into `assets/probe/` with `generate-probe-audio.sh`, before `npm run build`. If it is ever rebased onto this, its build would delete them, so it would have to run the script after `npm run assets`. It is an unmerged throwaway branch, so this pull request leaves it alone.

## How it was checked

- **Gates.**
  - Native: `npm run check`, `npx eslint .` and `npm test` pass. That is 174 tests: the 173 before, plus this one.
  - Root: `npm run format:check`, `npm run check` and `npm test` (161 tests) pass, and `git diff --check` is clean.
  - Root `npm run lint` passes with `.claude/worktrees/` excluded. Locally, ESLint also picked up a git-ignored worktree nested in the checkout, which CI never sees.
- **The test fails without the fix.** With the `rmSync` line disabled, it fails and lists all five strays. With the line restored, it passes.
- **A Release build with strays in place**, with Vega SDK 0.24.12112.
  - Planted in the real tree: `native/assets/probe/tone_a.wav` and `tone_a.mp3`, `native/assets/notes.txt` and `native/assets/image/old-icon.png`. Then `npm run build --prefix native`.
  - Afterwards the strays were gone from disk. Each of the three `.vpkg` lists 33 entries, and none of them is a stray.
  - Unpacked with `tar -xf`, the aarch64 package matches the published v0.1.0-beta.3 one byte for byte, except `meta-info/signature/*`. Its `digest.json` holds the same digests in a different order, so the signatures differ.
- **Not run on a device.** Nothing the device runs has changed. The bundles, the manifest, the native library and every asset are byte-identical to beta.3, which was checked on the Vega Virtual Device.

author: blind-striker
body:
## 📝 Description

**What does this PR do?**

This is slice 2b of #87, the last declined operation. It makes `experimental.fs.write` generated. With it, no operation is declined: 134 are generated, and the two transport-owned WebSocket doors cover the rest, so **all 136 operations are usable**. The PR is stacked on #125 and retargets to `master` when #125 merges.

**The shape (decided 2026-09-27).**
- The body is `application/octet-stream` with a `string`/`format: binary` schema. The target is a required `path` query parameter.
- The binder binds the body as the caller's `Stream`. It is the last wire parameter, after a standalone query record. The query cannot ride a body that is not a model:

```csharp
using var source = File.OpenRead("logo.png");
var written = await client.Experimental.WriteFileAsync(
    new ExperimentalFsWriteRequest { Path = "assets/logo.png" }, source);
Console.WriteLine(written.File.Path);   // the resolved absolute path
```

**Stream semantics (`CallerStreamContent`).**
- The SDK reads the stream once, from its current position to its end.
- It never disposes, rewinds or fully buffers the stream.
- It declares `Content-Length` only when the stream can seek; otherwise the body is chunked.
- A second send (a redirect or a retry in a caller-supplied handler) is refused by name.
- **Each chunk written restarts the progress window.** Before this, the window armed before the send and nothing restarted it during an upload, so a slow but moving upload failed after 100 s. The canon already says the send must progress inside the window. It is now true for uploads.

**Other changes**
- The payload is named `File` (`envelopePayloadNames`). Curation already avoids the `Fs` abbreviation.
- The `CallerStreamContent` CA2213 arbitration: the content owns neither the caller's stream nor the pipeline message.
- Docs: `protocol-and-generation.md`, `client-runtime.md` (upload progress), ADR-0029 (request side), ROADMAP (surface completeness done), README, CHANGELOG.

**Related Issue(s):**

- Closes #87

## 🔄 Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## 🎯 Protocol & API Surface

- [x] Public API changed **deliberately**, and `PublicApi.verified.txt` is updated. The change is additions only: `WriteFileAsync`, `ExperimentalFsWriteRequest`, `ExperimentalFsWriteResponse`, `FileSystemWrite`, and the route builder.
- [x] Generated output changed, and it was produced by the generator — **not** hand-edited
- [x] `dotnet run --file tools/opencode-tool.cs -- generate --verify` passes
- [x] The pinned snapshot (`spec/`) is untouched
- [x] Nothing under `external/` was hand-edited

## 🧪 Testing

- [x] **Binder.**
  - A stream body binds beside its query record, whatever the query carries.
  - An optional binary body is refused.
  - The pinned profile declines nothing.
- [x] **Pipeline** (4 TFMs).
  - The SDK sends from the stream's position, and does not dispose or rewind the stream.
  - `Content-Length` is declared for a seekable stream and absent for a non-seekable one.
  - A second send is refused.
  - A trickling upload that outlives the window (12 × 250 ms against 2 s) completes.
  - A stalled upload fails at the window.
  - A mutation that removes the restart turns the trickling test red.
- [x] **Contract.** The route with `path` and `location`, the octet-stream content type, the exact bytes, and the typed 400.
- [x] **Live (simulated server, v2.0.15).** Bytes, including `0x00 0xFF 0xFE`, are written to a nested path. `ReadFileAsync` reads them back, and they are identical on disk. The source stream ends at its end position and is not disposed.

## ✅ Completion Gate

The full two-pass gate is green locally:
- slopwatch 0;
- build clean;
- both format checks;
- pass 1: 7258/7258;
- election pass: 32/32;
- `--help`, `generate --verify`, `refresh-spec --verify`.

author: victorpurmar
body:
Part of #1274 (PR 3b-2 of the convergence program). Builds on #1286.

Closes a whole requirement type in one action, and shows which types are open, closed or new.

What you see

- Violations tab, new **by-type** sub-tab: one row per requirement code, grouped by dimension and principle, with BASELINE (the count in the baseline run), NOW, DELTA and STATUS. A type that had findings and has none reads *closed* and stays listed. Rows sort by NOW, closed last. Click a row to open that type's findings. Group headers count open and closed types.
- Row menu on every open type: **Dismiss all N in this project** and **Dismiss all N in <principle>** (N counts that principle's findings), behind a confirm. One request, one dismissal per finding, all visible under *dismissed* and restorable. When the server dismissed a different number than the row showed, a notice says so. Hidden on shared (read-only) projects.
- Overview since-baseline panel: **see findings** opens the file page on the findings that are new in the scoped files, one list across the dimensions on show, labelled with its scope and count.
- Help: the Violations page documents the sub-tab and dismissing a type; the Overview page documents see findings.

Backend

- `POST /api/findings/dismiss-by-type` `{project, req, dimension, run_id, principle?, file?, reason?}`: selects the run's active findings of `req` in `dimension` (narrowed by principle or file) from the evaluation report, the same list the UI counts, so legacy runs without an event log work and nothing is written into the run directory; skips the ones already dismissed or deleted, and appends one `FindingDismissed` event per finding in a single batch (D7f: no new event type; the fingerprinted key applies to future runs too, D8). Returns `{ok, dismissed, scores, delta}` with delta kind `dismiss_many`, which the client folds like the other bulk kinds (invalidate, no splice). 400 `MISSING_PARAM` / `INVALID_PARAM`, 404 `NOT_FOUND`, constant messages.
- `services/dismiss_by_type.py`: `DismissScope` + `select_findings` + `dismiss_by_type`, idempotent.

UI

- Baseline counts come from the existing run-diff route (`types.perReq`), one request per distinct run the visible dimensions come from; requirement text and principle from the standard detail (`GET /api/standards/<dim>`), cached for the session.
- Clients `getRunDiff`, `dismissByType`; query keys `projectKeys.runDiff`, `standardsKeys.detail`.

Acceptance on the stored run: the maintainability diff lists 30 requirement types; dismiss-by-type on one type with 2 findings returns 2, a second call returns 0, the dismissed list shows both, and the diff then lists the type on neither side.

Tests: pytest 9546 passed; vitest 2512, node 959; every UI ratchet at its ceiling; build clean.

Known limits

- Shared (read-only) projects have no diff route yet: the by-type baselines read "-" there and the since-baseline panel shows no see-findings button.
- File scope exists in the API (`file` in the body) but has no menu entry: a type row has no single file. The file page is where that entry belongs.
- A type row opens findings from the dimension's own run (the accumulated view's run for that dimension).
- The diff lists are capped at 200 per dimension; the see-findings label says "first N" when a cap is hit.
- The by-type baseline is per dimension run; a dimension whose run has no baseline shows "-" and no closed rows.
- No visual check in a browser (the headless route does not get past the loader on the 4.6 GB clone); the components are covered by vitest and the layout wants a human eye.

author: dinwwwh
body:
`RetryLinkPlugin` no longer loops forever when `retryDelay` throws or rejects. Before, a call like `context: { retry: 1, retryDelay: ({ error }) => error.data.retryAfter * 1000 }` that hit a network `TypeError` (no `.data`) retried the delay error without using up an attempt, which froze the tab or process. Now the call rejects with the `retryDelay` error, the same way a throwing `shouldRetry` already behaves.

### Fixes

- A throwing or rejecting `retryDelay` fails the call right away instead of starving the event loop.
- `onRetry` is not called for a retry that never happens because `retryDelay` failed. `retryDelay` now runs before `onRetry` (after `shouldRetry`), so all the retry decisions come before the side-effect hook.

### Testing

- New test: a `retryDelay` that rejects once makes the call fail with that error. `retryDelay` runs once, `onRetry` never runs, and no second request goes out. It fails against the old code (which retries and throws `FAIL`) and passes with the fix, without hanging if the bug comes back.
- Client plugin suite passes (142 tests), plus eslint and tsc, including the test file.

author: miztiik
body:
Plan 54 group D1. The day-validation receipt is gone: the contract, the ledger member, the config registry entry, the key and rule, the retention knob and prune pass, the receipt-write path, and the 52 committed receipts.

## Why

The receipt let a run skip re-reading a published day whose recorded payload **length** still matched `os.stat`. That length was the whole of the skip's evidence, so a receipt earned over one tree settled a same-length day in another tree without opening it. The record that made the read cheap also made a wrong answer reachable.

It also removes a live double-prune claim. `state/day-validations/` was swept by the 90-day trial pass as well as by its own 14-month one, so it was emptied well before its own retention knob promised. Deleting the tree is the whole fix: `state.iterdir()` no longer yields it, so the trial sweep cannot reach it. **No prune logic changed.**

## What this does NOT do

`backend/idhazh/stages/validate_days.py` stays. Group D2 rewrites it into the discovered `publication_checks/` package. D1 only stops it writing.

## Two rulings baked in (Fowler, in debate with Carmack, 2026-09-27)

1. **`stage_validate_days` loses `state_dir` and `run_id`, and the CLI loses the `--state-root` pairing guard.** After the receipt goes, the verb reads `root` and `root.parent` only, so the guard's refusal describes a mechanism that no longer exists - worse than no guard, because the next reader trusts it. Plan 54's D2 row is corrected in this same commit to say so.
2. **`test_frozen_days.py` was not receipt-only.** Eight of its nine tests are; the ninth covers the console-payload gate, which survives D1 and moves to D2. It moves to `backend/tests/pipeline/test_console_payload_gate.py`, named for its own question. Deleting it would have left the only live coverage of that gate absent for D2's whole calendar.

## Coverage kept, not dropped

| Where | What would have been lost | What happened instead |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_frozen_days.py` | the only test of the console-payload gate | moved to a file named for that question |
| `test_migrate_to_day_shards.py` | coverage of the flat-ledger-to-day-directory migration shape, which other ledgers still use | the fixture is renamed to a surviving day tree |
| `state-ledgers.md` | the only record of WHY a config registry replaced a hand-written Python set | rewritten to keep the mechanism without the proper noun |
| `build-state.ts`, `malformed-day.spec.ts`, `gates-and-builds.md` | the recorded lesson about a producer dirtying its own build inputs mid-run (defect 20) | rewritten to keep the mechanism without the ledger name |

## Schema versioning (CLAUDE.md section 11)

**No surviving contract needs a version stamp or a changelog entry, and no read-side migration is owed.** No surviving persisted shape changed. The one knob removed, `retention.day_validation_keep_months`, lives in a config file this project authors, which section 11 scopes out. The only payloads of the removed shape are the 52 receipts deleted in this same commit, so no build can meet a payload it cannot parse.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `ruff check .` | clean |
| `mypy` | Success, 537 source files |
| pytest: `backend/tests/contracts` + the 4 affected modules | **1,294 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped** (under the shared gate lock) |
| `backend/tests/test_marks.py` | 2 passed - the new module is registered in `UNMARKED_MODULES` |
| `doc_load.py` before and after | bootstrap load unchanged; every page touched only lost text |

## Oracle

A whole-tree `git grep` over `backend/`, `frontend/`, `config/` and `docs/` finds **zero** `DayValidationReceipt` / `DAY_VALIDATION*` / `day-validations` references, and zero surviving receipt-machinery symbols. `config/ledgers.json` and `LedgerName` still agree - the registry's own load validator proves it on every config read.

### Motivation
- Expose environmental telemetry (Ecowitt weather station) and boiler temperatures (eWeLink MCP) on the dashboard for operational visibility.
- Provide a minimal MCP client and diagnostics to read temperatures from eWeLink Premium MCP endpoints without committing tokens.
- Automate weather-based maintenance alerts (SMS) during the active season.

### Description
- Added new environment configuration keys in `config/env.php` for `ewelink.mcp_*` and an `ecowitt` section to configure MCP access URL, boiler names, cache/timeouts and Ecowitt API credentials.
- Implemented `core/ewelink_mcp.php` which contains a small MCP JSON-RPC client, helpers to discover devices, extract boiler temperatures and a diagnostic function `ewelink_mcp_test_device_raw` for safe debugging without exposing tokens.
- Implemented Ecowitt integration in `core/ecowitt.php` to fetch and cache current weather readings, and `core/ecowitt_alerts.php` to evaluate alert thresholds and send one-shot SMS notifications to the Maintenance department using existing SMS plumbing.

author: zifangsky
body:
## 概要

本 PR 包含两轮改动，均围绕首页查词的**输入校验**与**结果区状态一致性**。

### 1. 输入校验放宽（口径按入口分叉）

- 首页手输字符集由「仅英文字母」放宽为「英文字母 + 连字符 + 撇号」，现支持 `well-known`、`don't`、`state-of-the-art`、`'em`
- 仍要求**至少含一个字母**，故 `-`、`--`、`''` 等无字母纯符号输入会被拒绝
- **匹配指令路径保持不变**（纯字母），受 `public/plugin.json` 的 `over.exclude` 约束
- 新增 `HAS_LETTER_PATTERN` 判定；提示文案更新为「请输入英文单词（可含连字符或撇号）」

### 2. 校验失败清空旧结果

- **修复问题**：输入非法字符后，结果区仍残留上一次查询的详解，形成「红色错误提示 + 旧详解同屏」的怪异形态
- 根因是非法分支只 `setError()` 未清 `result`，而 UI 的降级渲染分支 `result && (loading || error)` 会把残留内容照常渲染
- 明确两类 `error` 的语义边界：**校验失败须清空** `result`；**AI 调用失败须保留**已收到的流式内容（降级展示）
- 未改动 UI 降级分支，避免破坏「调用失败保留部分内容」的既有行为

## 测试与门禁

| 项 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | **227 passed**（218 → +21，14 个文件） |
| `npx standard` | 退出码 0 |
| `npm run build` | 成功 |

两轮均遵循 TDD：先复现 RED（`expected '上一次查询的详解内容' to be ''` 等），再写最小实现。
其中「AI 调用失败时保留已收到的流式内容」一条是特意的**回归锁**，防止后续把两类 `error` 统一成同一种处理。

## 文档

- `CLAUDE.md` / `README.md` / `CONTEXT.md`：测试计数与输入契约（含清空要求）
- `.codexspec/memory/constitution.md`：**1.2.0 → 1.2.1**（原则 3 补充清空条款；原则 2 / 6 计数）
- `.codexspec/specs/2026-0927-1312iz-word-match-command/requirements.md`：追加复验第 8 / 9 轮变更记录，`OPEN-002` 关闭

## 已知边界（未处理）

- 流式查询**进行中**提交非法输入时，旧请求的回调仍会回填 `result`；合法→合法的并发查询存在同类既有缺陷。根治需引入请求代次或 abort 机制，属独立迭代
- 从网页复制的弯引号 `don’t`（U+2019）仍会被拒绝，本次未做 Unicode 引号归一化

author: jmtatsch
body:
## Problem

`_handle_message` logs the raw JSON-RPC request and response at DEBUG. A `tools/call` for `synology_login`, `synology_create_user` or `ds_create_task` carries a live password in its arguments, so at `LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` those passwords are written to `./logs` — a mounted volume, reached through a documented setting rather than an obscure one.

Confirmed by driving a real `synology_login` through the bridge: the account password appeared verbatim in the DEBUG log line.

## Fix

Frames go through `_redact()`, which masks the value of any key naming a credential. It masks rather than drops, so the log keeps the shape that makes it worth having — you can still see that a password was sent, and where.

```
before:  "arguments": {"username": "svc", "password": "<real password>"}
after:   "arguments": {"username": "svc", "password": "***"}
```

## Known limitation, stated in the docstring

The approach is key-based, so it cannot mask a secret embedded in a free-text value — notably a `tools/call` **result**, whose content is a single JSON string. Those are still logged verbatim; DEBUG logs remain sensitive.

In practice the remaining exposure there is the login result, which my `_handle_login` PR removes at the source. Verified: with both merged, a live login through the bridge leaves password, SID and SynoToken all absent from the DEBUG log. Neither PR alone is sufficient — they are complementary, but independent and safe to merge in either order.

author: chitranshjoshi99
body:
Adds `https://chitransh.dev/bob`, the single redirect URI registered on Bob's Google OAuth client.

Google can only redirect to one fixed https address, but every Bob (the Mac app server) lives at its own: `https://bob-<user>.<tailnet>.ts.net` or a Wi-Fi address. Bob puts its own origin in `state`; this static page forwards the phone to `<origin>/_auth/cb` with Google's answer untouched. The code is useless without the PKCE verifier and client secret that only that Bob holds.

- `apps/portfolio/public/bob/index.html` + `relay.js`: allowlist is `bob-*.<tailnet>.ts.net`, private IPv4 ranges, `*.local` and localhost.
- `vercel.json`: `/bob` rewrite ahead of the SPA catch-all, plus a strict CSP, `no-referrer` and `noindex` for it.

Host side: chitranshjoshi99/Builder, branch `feat/google-sign-in`.

- the bottom tab bar still showing;
- a grey band under the header;
- big outlined radio cards;
- long paragraphs between controls;
- an inline API Key input, with small 保存/清除 buttons at the left;
- a floating 「已配置 ✓ …」 label.

This PR fixes it for **all** phone sub-pages, not only the voice page in the screenshot.

## What

- **`src/settings-kit.tsx`** (new): the shared building blocks.
  - `SettingsGroup`: grey header, a white rounded card with **16dp gutters**, and a grey footer note.
  - `SettingsRow`: label, value on the right, and a ›. Rows are **≥ 48** tall (`max(48, ds(52))`), with hairlines inset to the label.
  - `SettingsChoiceRow`: the ✓ sits in the **same 18px column as the ›**.
  - `SettingsSwitchRow`, `SettingsTextField`, and `SettingsButton` (primary / destructive / plain).
  - Text goes through `ui-text` and sizes through `ds()`, so 字体大小 and 界面密度 both apply.
  - Colours come only from theme tokens, so dark mode is covered.
- **`src/SettingsPhonePages.tsx`** (new): every phone sub-page, drawn only with the kit. It uses the same state and handlers as the wide pane; only the presentation changes.
- **`src/SettingsEditPages.tsx`** (new): the third-level edit pages. These are the only place inputs appear (API Key, 高级 / 旧版控制台, 免打扰时段).
