author: skyphusion-rollins
body:
Step 8 of the v1.25.0 cut, plus two procedure notes the cut earned.

## The row, both cells DERIVED

| field | value | derived from |
|---|---|---|
| `source commit` | `e82db9a` | `git rev-list -n1 vivijure-core-v1.25.0` -- the commit the TAG points at, not HEAD |
| `published` | `2026-09-27` | **the registry**, `2026-09-27T08:39:27.043Z` |

Neither was typed from memory. I wrote it as a script that derives both and **refuses rather than guessing**: non-zero if the tag will not resolve, non-zero if the registry timestamp is not an ISO date, and a **distinct exit** for "the registry reports no publish time yet" whose message says explicitly that this is *the absent-version window, not a failed publish*. That last branch is the one that matters, because the comfortable misreading is available exactly there.

That is effectively the derive-half of **core#318** prototyped on one row. Say the word and I will generalise it there and backfill the 11 rows that still have both cells empty.

## Note 1: the absent-version window is NOT converging, and 20 seconds was the outlier

| cut | time to visible |
|---|---|
| v1.23.0 | ~2 min |
| v1.24.0 | ~20 s |
| **v1.25.0** | **~2 min 40 s** |

Six consecutive polls returned E404 for `1.25.0` with `dist-tags.latest` **still reading 1.24.0**, beside a green workflow and a signed publish. Then it appeared.

**Anyone treating the v1.24.0 figure as typical would have called this cut a failed publish three times over.** So the note now carries all three readings and says plainly not to derive a timeout from any single cut: the step log is the evidence and the clock is not. The markers that actually proved success, as ever:

```
npm notice Publishing to https://registry.npmjs.org/ with tag latest and public access
npm notice Your package is being processed and may take a few minutes to become available.
```

## Note 2: three version slots, individually, before AND after the assemble

Written down because I did it on instinct and it is not in the procedure. There are **three** slots, not two: `package.json`, the lock's top-level `version`, and the lock's `packages[""].version`.

Read each on its own with `node -p` rather than grepping for the old string, because **a count cannot tell you WHICH slot it found**, and a bump that moved two of three looks identical to one that moved all three. RELEASES.md already records that the lock going stale was caught only by a test; this is the check that makes it visible before the test has to.

And again **after** the assembler runs: it does not touch `package.json`, and confirming that is cheaper than discovering it did.

## Gate

`npm test`: **118 files / 1232 tests pass**. Docs-only change, so no `changelog.d/` fragment is owed.

body:
Small follow-up (job_dcf75e2bb93e). No migration; nothing deployed.

Stage 2 capped each post-list refresh at 20 bodies, sized for the Workers Free limit of 50 subrequests. Carrel is on Workers Paid.

- **The limit, confirmed:** Workers Paid allows **10,000 subrequests per invocation** by default (up to 10 million if configured). Workers Free stays at 50. A D1 call counts as one ([Workers limits, Subrequests](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/#subrequests), and the [2026-02-11 changelog](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-02-11-subrequests-limit/)).
- **Named constants with the doc cited** (`app/lib/index.server.ts`): `SUBREQUEST_LIMIT = 10_000`, and `REFRESH_SUBREQUEST_BUDGET`, a tenth of it, so the cron's other work in the same invocation (the health check, other sites) always has room. `MAX_BODY_FETCHES` goes from **20 to 200**, and `REFRESH_MAX_SUBREQUESTS` is derived from it: up to 10 list pages + 2 D1 calls + 2 per body = **412**, about 4% of the limit.
- **Tests:** one asserts the worst case sits inside the budget. The other refreshes 250 posts that all need bodies and **counts** every site fetch and every D1 call through a counting proxy, rather than assuming them: 202 + 202, under 412 and far under 10,000. With the cap raised to 600 as a plant, both tests fail.

A trade-off to know: a manual Refresh that has 200 bodies to read makes 200 sequential calls to the site, so on a large first sync it takes longer than it did before (the cron does the same work in the background).

69 → 71 tests, all green; typecheck passes.

Needs Dustin: review and merge; it takes effect at the next deploy.

body:
Part of #253 (Discovery Hint 4.0, OD-DH4-4). This is Lane C: a docs/data/tools-only audit of the ingredient taxonomy for the 105-ingredient / 172-recipe populations.

**Owner review only. Do not merge automatically.**

## Scope

Three new files. There are no `src/**` changes.

- `docs/reports/TETO_DISCOVERY-HINT-4_INGREDIENT-TAXONOMY-172_Fresh-Audit.md`: the Fresh Audit, with the approved Owner Decisions OD-TAX-1…9
- `docs/reports/data/TETO_INGREDIENT-TAXONOMY_172_FRESH-AUDIT.json`: the machine-readable audit
- `tools/ingredient_taxonomy_audit.py`: a deterministic generator (`--check` reports drift). It is docs tooling only, not in CI, and nothing in production imports it.

**Not changed:**
- DH4-1 (merged via #254), including `ingredientTaxonomy.ts` and `deductionHint.ts`
- the reducer, persistence, HintSheet and `App.css`
- Dinner, #252 and #243
- the canonicalizer tables and PROJECT_HANDOFF

There is no DH4-2 work and no new canonical id.

## Audit

- **Ingredient universe:**
  - runtime: 29 ingredients, 25 recipes;
  - progression: 105 ingredients, 101 recipes;
  - 172 evidence: 169 canonical ids + 13 unresolved tokens;
  - union: 179 ids.
- **Classification status:** 132 PROPOSED and 47 NEEDS_REVIEW. The 13 unresolved tokens are UNKNOWN.
- **Taxonomy layers:**
  - L1 group and L2 family are DH4-1's own ids.
  - L3 subfamily is internal only.
  - At 172, every L2 family has at least 8 ingredients.
- **Machine checks:**
  - The generator fails when a row lacks evidence, when a category disagrees with the evidence, or when a family disagrees with DH4-1.
  - It found no mismatch.
- **DH4-1 guard simulation over the 101-recipe pool:**
  - With all 105 ingredients owned, every topping is answered at family level.
  - Coarser answers are needed only early in progression.
- **Privacy findings:**
  - Two axes together can name a single ingredient. For example, 「肉 + ピリ辛」 identifies pepperoni among the 105. Any multi-axis hint therefore needs k ≥ 2 on the intersected set (FR-3).
  - Selling the full taxonomy signature pins 5 recipes to a single composition early on. This supports the one-fact-per-hint rule.

## Owner Decisions recorded (2026-09-27)

- OD-TAX-1: adopt 3 layers (group, family, subfamily).
- OD-TAX-2: keep the 7 DH4-1 family ids and do not rebuild the algorithm.
- OD-TAX-3: players see at most the L2 family.
- OD-TAX-4: keep k ≥ 2, re-checked on the intersected set for any future multi-axis hint.
- OD-TAX-5: never sell the whole signature; one fact per hint.
- OD-TAX-6: identity is separate from role, timing and technique.
- OD-TAX-7: the Human Review Queue and a Human Classification Gate come before any production authority.
- OD-TAX-8: 「その他系」 is not used as player copy; the candidate wording 「ちょっと変わった材料があるよ」 goes to the DH4-2 UI audit.
- OD-TAX-9: subfamily, sauce and cheese families and multi-axis hints are future requirements, not DH4-2 scope.

Proposals from the first revision that these decisions do not cover are listed as **open**, not assumed. They include the garlic / capers / black-olive boundary and the canonicalization clusters.

## Re-audit on latest main

- The first audit ran on `22658f7`. `origin/main` `5a33d85` (DH4-1 merged) was merged in with no conflict and no shared file.
- The generator now reads the merged `src/data/ingredientTaxonomy.ts`. Its family and group ids and labels match exactly.
- `--check`: OK. Two regenerations produced the same SHA-256.
- All audit values are identical to the first audit. Only metadata changed (the SHAs, the DH4-1 source and `ownerDecisions`).

Verdict: **A. TAXONOMY OWNER DECISIONS RECORDED — READY FOR DOCS PR REVIEW**

No UI or gameplay change, so the Human Verification policy does not apply.

## 관련 이슈

Related to #(issue-3 PR 번호) — 리뷰 [P2] "여러 이미지의 잠금 순서를 요청 배열 순서와 분리" 반영

## 변경 내용

`attach_many`가 요청 배열 순서대로 이미지 행에 `FOR UPDATE`를 걸고 있었습니다. 같은 새 업로드 두 개를 `[A, B]`, `[B, A]`로 보내는 요청 두 개가 동시에 들어오면, 각자 첫 이미지를 잠근 채 상대가 쥔 이미지를 기다리다 교착에 빠집니다. 이때 한 요청은 명세의 409가 아니라 `DeadlockDetected`(500)로 실패합니다. 장소 생성과 서로 다른 장소의 PATCH가 모두 `replace_images → attach_many` 경로를 탑니다.

- 검증 전에 `SELECT ... WHERE s3_key IN (...) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE`로 대상 이미지 전체를 `id` 순서로 한 번에 잠급니다.
- 이 조회 결과로 key → image id를 찾으므로, key마다 따로 날리던 id 조회를 없앴습니다.
- 검증, 반환, 저장 순서는 전과 같이 요청 배열 순서를 따릅니다.
- 나중에 온 요청은 먼저 온 요청이 commit할 때까지 기다린 뒤 `ATTACHED`를 보고 409 `IMAGE_ALREADY_ATTACHED`로 거절됩니다(명세 §4.6).

공유 이미지 서비스(`images/service.py`) 수정이라 issue-3 PR과 분리해 develop 대상으로 올립니다.

## 변경 유형

- [x] 버그 수정
- [ ] 기능 추가
- [ ] 리팩터링
- [x] 테스트
- [ ] 문서 또는 설정
- [ ] 기타

## 검증

```bash
uv run pytest apps/backoffice/tests/test_image_attach_race.py   # 3회 반복, 4 passed
uv run pytest                                                   # 791 passed
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .
```

- test_reversed_arrays_conflict_instead_of_deadlocking: 두 트랜잭션이 첫 이미지를 잠근 뒤 검증(store.head) 단계에서 서로를 기다리게 맞춰, 반대 순서 배열을 동시에 연결합니다. 수정 전에는 DeadlockDetected로 실패했고, 수정 후에는 한쪽만 IMAGE_ALREADY_ATTACHED로 실패합니다.
- test_attach_many_returns_images_in_request_order: 잠금 순서와 관계없이 반환 순서가 요청 배열을 따르는지 확인합니다.

## 영향 범위

- API 계약: 없음 (동시 요청 시 500 대신 명세대로 409를 반환)
- 데이터베이스 또는 마이그레이션: 없음
- 환경 변수 또는 배포 설정: 없음
- 하위 호환성: 없음

## 스크린샷 및 참고 자료

issue-3 브랜치는 foundation 기반이라, 이 PR이 develop에 머지된 뒤 develop을 반영해야 장소 라우트에 적용됩니다.

body:
Phase 6-iii, tasks 6.9–6.13: the last of Phase 6's three stacked PRs. You can publish a pattern to the community library, anyone signed in can report one, and a moderator can act on the reports.

**Stacked on #23** (`phase-6-public`), which is stacked on #22. Merge in order: #22, then #23, then this, retargeting each at `main` as the one before lands.

## 6.9: publishing
- `POST /api/v1/breaks/:id/publish` with `{ confirm: true }` (the "I wrote this" tick) is the only way a pattern becomes `published`. It refuses in this order, each with its own code:
  1. the `PATTERN_PUBLISHING` flag is off (403) — the flag is seeded on, and a missing flag reads as off;
  2. you have no username (409);
  3. the title or description contains a blocked word (422);
  4. the notes are the same as someone else's published pattern, or as a famous break (409 `DUPLICATE`);
  5. you have already published 10 patterns for the first time in the last 24 hours (429).
- **Edits to a published pattern are held to the same word and duplicate checks** (`assertPublishable`, run by PATCH). Republishing keeps a pattern's first `publishedAt`, so it neither jumps the Newest list nor counts against the cap twice.
- The Studio has a publish dialog. It asks for a username first if you have none, shows a retry if it can't read yours, and gives the username field ⓘ help. The share card gets Unpublish, which keeps the link working, next to Stop sharing.

## 6.10: reports
- A `BreakReport` model (migration `break_reports`). `reporterId` and `resolvedById` are hand-written, drift-probed `ON DELETE SET NULL` keys, so a report outlives both the reporter and the moderator.
- `POST /api/v1/public/patterns/:slug/report` (signed in): each person has at most one open report per pattern, you can't report your own, and there is a daily cap.
- `/p/` has a Report button, and the export gains a `reportsFiled` section.

## 6.11: moderation
- `/admin/patterns` (in the admin nav) and `/api/v1/admin/patterns[/:id]` offer three actions, all audit-logged:
  - **unpublish:** makes the pattern private and emails the owner. The email goes out after the write, and only when a pattern was actually taken down.
  - **strip links**
  - **dismiss**
- Reporters are never shown to the owner.

## 6.12: the Studio and Home
- The Patterns drawer has a **Community** tab (newest or most saved) that opens a pattern in place.
- Home has a **Published** section and a _Browse the community library_ link.

## 6.13: erasure, Privacy and Terms
- The Privacy page says what publishing makes public and what erasure does: your published patterns are deleted, copies others made stay with them without your name, and reports you filed are kept without it.

The generator uses that id to join each lineage to the existing conference row. The id stays in the script and is not added to `logo_ref`.
- The keys come from name kinds `name`, `short_name`, `abbreviation` and `code`, from every source (espn, cfbd, sdv, ncaa, kenpom). Slugs are left out. Keys are `toupper()`ed with whitespace trimmed and collapsed, the same way `match_team_abbrs()` matches.
- A key is added only when exactly one lineage in that sport uses it and sdvplotR doesn't already map it (team keys, conference keys, crosswalk names and curated aliases all count). Skipped keys are logged. Existing keys are never overwritten, and the curated-alias clash `stop()` and the conference self-resolve assertion still pass.
- Upstream drift: sportsdataverse-py's NCAA/ESPN crosswalks changed today (24f154cb, bcb09617). author: deep-sixed
body:
Stacked on Deep-Sixed/InferenceDeck#34 (history + graphs), which is stacked on Deep-Sixed/InferenceDeck#31. Retarget it down the stack as those merge.

## What's added
- **llama-server gets `--metrics`**. It is on by default; a profile can set `"metrics": false`.
- **Server metrics collector** (`telemetry.py`):
  - Reads each live, unpaused server's `/metrics` with a 1 s timeout. Paused servers are skipped, since a SIGSTOPped process would only time out.
  - Maps llama.cpp counters (and vLLM-style `vllm:*` names, in case vllm.cpp follows them) to `requests_active`, `requests_deferred`, `prompt_tokens_total`, `tokens_generated_total` and `kv_cache_usage_percent`.
  - Works out rates from how InferenceDeck's own readings change:
    - `tokens_per_second` and `prompt_tokens_per_second`: tokens over the time the server spent on them. Absent while idle, not zero.
    - `throughput_tokens_per_second`: tokens per wall-clock second.
  - A counter reset produces no rate rather than a negative one.
  - It deliberately does not use llama.cpp's `predicted_tokens_seconds` and `prompt_tokens_seconds` gauges, which reset on every scrape.
- **Prometheus**: `inferencedeck_server_requests_active`, `_requests_deferred`, `_prompt_tokens_total`, `_generated_tokens_total`, `_generation_tokens_per_second`, `_prompt_tokens_per_second`, `_kv_cache_usage_ratio`, plus `inferencedeck_benchmark_tokens_per_second{profile}` from the latest benchmark per profile.
- **Benchmarks** emit a `benchmark.completed` lifecycle event carrying tok/s. It shows in the event list and on the chart markers.
- **History and UI**: the new fields are sampled into history, with four new charts: generation speed, prompt processing, active requests and KV cache used. Isolated readings (short bursts) are drawn as dots, and the active-requests axis uses whole numbers.
- README: a Requests and tokens section, including the note that scraping llama-server resets its bucket gauges for other scrapers.

## Testing
- New `tests/test_telemetry_requests.py` covers:
  - text parsing (labels, `}` inside label values, NaN, comments);
  - fetching llama.cpp and vLLM-style metrics from a live fake server, plus 501, unrelated metrics and dead ports;
  - rates (first reading, busy vs wall time, idle, counter reset, no time counter, forgotten servers);
  - paused servers not being asked, combining counters with rates, latest benchmark per profile;
  - Prometheus and history export, and `--metrics` on and off in the launch args.
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests`: 240 tests, OK.
- Rendered the new charts in headless Chromium with synthetic data: no page errors.
- Not yet run against a real llama-server. Field names follow llama.cpp's `/metrics`. `kv_cache_usage_ratio` is absent on newer builds and is then left out.

body:
### What does this PR do?
Adds a global, dismissible cookie-consent banner that appears on every route except `/privacy` (and its locale-prefixed variants), offering "Accept all" / "Reject non-essential", persisted in a `cookie_consent` cookie (mirroring the `lang` cookie's write pattern: `Path=/`, one-year `Max-Age`, `SameSite=Lax`, conditional `Secure`). Links to `/privacy#cookies`.

Exports a `hasOptionalConsent()` helper that future analytics code can check before loading anything non-essential — no such script exists yet, so this has no caller today. That's intentional groundwork per the approved plan, not dead code.

Depends on the companion `oniwebsite_bk` PR (hfleury/oniwebsite_bk#28) for the new `cookie_banner_*` locale keys — without it the banner falls back to rendering raw key names.

### Related tickets
https://oniweb.atlassian.net/browse/FOWO-88

### How to test
- `cd oniwebsite && npm run lint`
- `cd oniwebsite && npm test` (includes new `CookieConsentBanner.test.tsx`)
- `cd oniwebsite && npm run build`
- Manual: after building, run `cd ../oniwebsite_bk && go run ./cmd/server -port 8090` (no `-dev`) with both branches checked out, then in a browser confirm the banner appears on `/`, the "Cookie Policy" link lands on `/privacy#cookies` scrolled to that section, Accept/Reject each hide the banner and survive a reload, `/privacy` never shows it, and `/pt/`, `/sv/` show translated copy with locale-prefixed `/privacy` suppression.

### Additional notes
Verified manually via Claude-in-Chrome against the built `dist/` + Go server: banner shown on `/` and `/pt/` with correct copy, Accept hides it and survives reload, and it's suppressed on `/privacy` and `/pt/privacy`.

author: admintokohadashop-art
body:
### Motivation
- Ensure program files are separate from user data by moving the production `tiktok_seller.db` and avatars out of `.dart_tool`/`build`/executable folders into a deterministic persistent application-support `CountCat/` root. 
- Safely bootstrap legacy development databases (sqflite_common_ffi) without overwriting or deleting user data, and migrate legacy avatar references into the persistent avatars folder. 
- Provide a local, portable backup/restore flow that produces consistent SQLite snapshots and protects live data via staging and safety backups. 
- Surface the current active account identity in the left sidebar while keeping the existing active-account source of truth.

### Description
- Added a single `CountCatDataPaths` abstraction to centralize persistent paths (`root`, `tiktok_seller.db`, `avatars/`, `backups/`) and to produce a candidate legacy path derived from the working-directory `.dart_tool/sqflite_common_ffi/databases/` layout. (`lib/core/storage/countcat_data_paths.dart`).
- Reworked `AppDatabase` to open a persistent database at the `CountCat/` path using platform-appropriate factories (Windows uses `sqflite_common_ffi`, others use `sqflite`), with startup order: use persistent DB if present → else copy legacy DB into persistent location (copy, do not move/overwrite) → else create new DB; avatar migration runs once after open. (`lib/data/database/app_database.dart`).
- Updated `AvatarStorage` to use the shared `CountCatDataPaths` avatars directory and to maintain `isOwnedPath`/`deleteOwned` semantics pointing to persistent storage. (`lib/core/profile/avatar_storage.dart`).
- Implemented `CountCatBackupService` that creates ZIP-based backups with `manifest.json`, uses `VACUUM INTO` to produce a transactionally consistent snapshot, includes avatar files under `avatars/`, validates archive contents and SQLite header, and stages/restores archives with a safety backup and rollback on failure. (`lib/core/backup/countcat_backup_service.dart`).
- Exposed backup and restore actions in Settings (`BACKUP DATA` / `RESTORE DATA`) using `file_picker` and surfaced results via `SnackBar`, while preserving existing account/profile/HPP workflows. (`lib/features/settings/settings_page.dart`).
- Added a desktop sidebar identity widget that reads the active account via `AccountRepository.activeAccount()` and refreshes via a lightweight `ValueNotifier` event when the active account or profile is updated; the widget shows a circular avatar and account name beneath it. This does not introduce a second active-account state. (`lib/app/app_shell.dart`, `lib/data/repositories/account_repository.dart`).
- Added dependency additions for `archive` and `file_picker` and a focused regression test covering persistent path layout and idempotent legacy bootstrap (`pubspec.yaml`, `test/milestone_three_storage_test.dart`).

### Testing
- Added a focused test file `test/milestone_three_storage_test.dart` covering: persistent `CountCat` root layout and the legacy-database-copy bootstrap behavior being non-destructive and idempotent; the test uses `sqflite_common_ffi` and `AppDatabase.forTesting` to exercise the legacy copy logic. The test file was added but not executed in this container. 
- Static and runtime checks could not be executed here because the Flutter SDK is not installed in this environment, so `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` failed with `/bin/bash: flutter: command not found`; these checks must be run in CI or a dev environment with Flutter installed. 
- Local repository checks (`git diff --check`) were run and no whitespace errors were present before committing changes.

author: vincemakes
body:
The owner's call on finding 0430-B1, before 0.43.0 ships: withdraw the raw-text replay, keep `rawInput` on the context and the block.

## Why

The 0.43.0 rc replayed a tool call's arguments as the model's own text. The paired bench read more requests on that arm — 18 pairs: median cost +3.3% (within the margins), requests 591 vs 557, the pre-registered expensive shape 6 times on the rc side and never on the control's — and a byte check on the rc legs' own logs found that every one of the 455 replayed calls differed from `JSON.stringify(input)`: the provider streams `{"path": "x"}` with spaces after colons and commas; 0.42.3 replayed the compact form. The one change the model could read; the direction consistent; not settled as variance. Withdrawn rather than shipped.

## What changes

Both openai adapters send `JSON.stringify(input)` whether or not the block carries `rawInput`. Kept: `ctx.rawInput`, `AssistantToolUseBlock.rawInput`, the lossless projection round-trip, the cold-resume parity — what the hosts asked for. The two rig tests now pin the withdrawal; `docs/extensions.md`, the block's JSDoc and the 0.43.0 release report say why. Kernel unchanged (2,195).

## After this merges

Rebuild and repack the rc, install it isolated, and run six more interleaved pairs against the published 0.42.3 on the corrected artifact before any publish.

## Evidence

`npm run check` on `b5171151`, the exit read before this PR was opened: unit 374 files / 3,565 tests, PTY 183 / 853, packed smoke + demo, exit 0.

author: samilazreg-eng
body:
Investigation report for #61: [`docs/parser-regeneration.md`](https://github.com/samilazreg-eng/DaedaluX/blob/docs/61-parser-regeneration/docs/parser-regeneration.md). Documentation only. The build is not changed.

## Findings

- **Ninja** (the documented generator) regenerates `lex.yy.cpp`, `y.tab.cpp` and `y.tab.hpp` on the first build of **every new build directory**. `-d explain` reports `command line not found in log`. This also happens when the tracked outputs are newer than their inputs.
- **Unix Makefiles** regenerates only `lex.yy.cpp`. Git checks it out just before `promela.l`, so it is slightly older (30/30 fresh clones). This is the #33 observation.
- **Differences** are paths only: `#line` directives with absolute paths, plus the `y.tab.hpp` include guard that Bison derives from the path. After path normalization, the regenerated files are identical to the tracked ones and identical across two checkout paths.
- **Second build:** no work to do, both for `promela_parser` and for the full target. Touching `promela.y` or `promela.l` regenerates only its own outputs.
- **Undeclared outputs:** `y.tab.hpp` and `lexer.h`. Deleting either one is not repaired by a rebuild. Flex writes `lexer.h` into the **build directory** (`header-file` is relative), while `promela_loader.cpp` compiles against the tracked copy (checked with `ninja -t deps`). That copy is stale since `ec82629`, but only by one `#line` directive.
- **Role:** in practice the tracked files are cached outputs committed after a local build. The documented Ninja build fails without flex/bison even when the tracked outputs are newer than their inputs. The original intent is **UNKNOWN**.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Regeneration triggers identified (Q1)
- [x] All parser inputs and generated outputs identified (table in the report)
- [x] Differences from tracked files identified and explained (Q3)
- [x] Second unchanged build tested (Q4)
- [x] Role of the tracked files established (Q5, with the intent marked UNKNOWN)
- [x] Fixes deferred: 5 proposed follow-up issues listed in the report. None have been opened yet; they are waiting for your decision.

## Validation

WSL Ubuntu 26.04, CMake 4.2.3, Ninja 1.13.2, Bison 3.8.2, Flex 2.6.4, commit `410b514`, fresh `git clone` per experiment. Also includes one full default-target Ninja build: `184/184`, rc 0, second build `no work to do`.

Refs #61

* **Documentation**
  * Added an investigation report describing when fresh CMake builds regenerate parser files, how behavior differs between Ninja and Unix Makefiles, and which generated files are used.

author: eugenena
body:
Closes #13. Part of release 1.3.0 (still unreleased; tag after merge).

## Dialect items
- **Oracle `FLOAT`** is compared by binary precision (`FLOAT`/`DOUBLE PRECISION` = 126, `REAL` = 63). Before, any float declaration matched any live `FLOAT`. Snapshots keep `FLOAT(n)`, and `FLOAT(n)` outside 1..126 fails validation.
- **Lock release after commit:** if releasing the lock (or restoring auto-commit) fails after a successful sync, the failure is logged and the result is returned. After a failed sync it is still attached to the original exception as suppressed.
- **Already fixed on `main`, now covered by integration tests:** Oracle `TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE` folding, SQL Server bare `DATETIME2` (precision 7), and MySQL national-type collation drift.

## Tokenizer
`SqlTokenizer` splits SQL into typed tokens and statements for each dialect, and `NonDestructiveSqlPolicy` and `ChangeSetSchemaScope` now use it instead of regexes over masked text.
- A routine body is one statement, but its inner statements are still checked.
- Input that can't be parsed is rejected.

It closes every guardrail gap listed in #13: quoted admin function names, forbidden statements in bodies, `TOP`/alias write targets, three-part name false positives, verification false positives, multi-statement bodies, and escape forms.

Local review also found and closed:
- SQL Server batches that run a second statement without `;`, including number-glued keywords (`1EGRANT`) and `ADD SIGNATURE`.
- `--` comments that PostgreSQL and SQL Server end at a bare carriage return.
- MySQL `/*+ SET_VAR */` hints.
- PostgreSQL routines in languages other than `sql`/`plpgsql`, and `CREATE EXTENSION` (listed under breaking changes).
- Role and global-setting changes.
- Additional side-effecting functions.

## Applied change sets
The guardrails now check only change sets that are not yet in history. An applied change set whose checksum still matches never runs again. Without this, upgraders would be stuck on a change set they can't edit whenever a check gets stricter.
- Checksum mismatches still fail first.
- Every rejection happens before any DDL or verification SQL runs, in dry-run too.
- Offline `validate` still checks every change set, as documented.

## Testing
- 456 unit tests.
- Integration suites all pass on PostgreSQL 16, MySQL 8.4, MariaDB 10.3, SQL Server, and Oracle XE.
- New contract suites: `SqlTokenizerTest`, `GuardrailTokenizerContractTest` (cells per gap and per dialect, plus benign look-alikes), and `ChangeSetHistoryPolicyTest`.
- Independent Grok review in two parallel areas (bypasses; correctness and false rejections) over five rounds, with differential probes on live engines. The final verdict from both is SHIP.

body:
## Data
- **MOJ tribunals, April to June 2026** (published 10 Sep): receipts 21,762 (−21%), disposals 16,786 (+30%), open caseload 155,798 (+48%), mean 65 weeks to clear, allowed rate 38% against 40%. MOJ's Q4 2025/26 revisions are picked up.
- **Small boats to 24 Sep 2026:** 18,609 arrivals in 2026 so far, against 32,188 at the same point in 2025 (−42.2%).
- **HO spend over £25k, July 2026:** +£15.7m asylum, all in 2026/27. The ledger is now £4.33bn / 17,103 payments / 369 suppliers. No earlier year moved.

## Fixes
- **Tribunal parser:** MOJ now marks rows `Q4ʳ` / `Q1ᵖ`. The parser only knew ASCII `r`/`p`, so those quarters were read as annual totals. The reconciliation guard stopped it; a new check asserts no quarter is read as a year. On Q1–Q3 editions the annual comparison now uses the latest complete financial year. The provisional note is built from MOJ's markers. Anchors were re-read by hand from the published tables.
- **HO spend timezone bug:** `toISOString()` on SheetJS local-midnight dates moved four 2012-13 ODS files back a day under BST, which broke their dedupe. A laptop run put 2013/14 £16.5m above CI. Output is now identical across four timezones. The published figures were never affected, because CI runs in UTC.
- **Small boats file choice:** it picked the newest file alphabetically (28 Aug > 25 Sep). It now picks by the date in the filename.

## Pages
- `/entities/` and `/spending/` meta descriptions now read the ledger instead of typed-in totals.
- `/routes/` "took in far more appeals than it cleared" (written against an 81% gap) is now computed: "took in 30% more…".
- Release diary entry added.

## Checks
- `npm run build`: 487 pages
- `npm test`: 420 passed
- `npm run check`: 0 errors
- Tribunal, small boats and spend text checked in the dev server.

## 목적
대표 결정 35(2026-09-27)에 따라 적격 판정 기록 기능을 만든다.
- 사람이 리드를 적격·보류·거절로 판정하고 사유 코드와 함께 기록한다.
- 이 기록으로 R6 보고서의 '적격 리드당 비용'을 채운다. R6a·R6b는 이 값을 비워 두었다.
- 보고서는 문의 월 코호트 기준으로 적격 수와 적격 리드당 비용을 계산한다.

- 기준 SHA: `efee922`(origin/main, #200 결정 36 병합 뒤)
- 레인: R(맥 세션, 대표 결정 구현 담당). #200(결정 36)의 다음 PR이다.

## 수용 기준(사례 번호는 `tests/franchise-qualification.test.mjs`)
- 판정(QL-R·QL-A·QL-H): 작업 `qualify_lead`. 받는 값은 `verdict`(qualified·hold·rejected), 판정별 사유 코드 `reason`, 지금 적격 기준 버전 `criteriaVersion`이다.
  - 권한은 R4b 리드 패턴이다. 대표·관리자는 모든 리드를 판정한다. 직원은 본인 담당 리드만 판정한다. 담당 없는 리드는 가져온 뒤 판정하고, 다른 직원의 리드는 403이다.
  - 계획 역할 표에 판정 행이 없어 지시대로 정했고, 역할 표에 행을 더했다.
- 이력: 리드 `qualifications`에 추가만 한다(덮어쓰지 않음, 50건 한도). 현재 판정은 마지막 행이다.
  - 한 행에는 판정·사유 코드·기준 버전·판정 때 적격 점수·시각·행위자가 있다.
  - 이벤트 `qualification_recorded`와 감사 `qualification`에는 코드만 남긴다.
  - 가맹희망자 활동이 아니라서 마지막 활동과 보존 기한은 바뀌지 않는다. 새 kind는 없다.
- 거부(QL-V·QL-S):

  | 경우 | 응답 |
  |---|---|
  | 적격 기준 없음 | 409 `QUALIFICATION_NO_CRITERIA` |
  | 화면을 연 뒤 기준 버전이 바뀜 | 409 `QUALIFICATION_CRITERIA_CHANGED` |
  | 판정에 맞지 않는 사유나 자유 문구 사유 | 400 `QUALIFICATION_REASON` |
  | 정해진 칸 밖 입력(메모 등) | 400 `QUALIFICATION_TEXT`(값은 어디에도 저장하지 않음) |
  | 같은 판정 | 400 |
  | 한도 초과 | 409 |
  | 버전 불일치 | 409 STALE |
  | 스위치 꺼짐 | 409 OFF |
  | 연락처 파기·삭제 리드 | 409 |

  같은 요청 번호로 다시 보내면 결과를 재생하고 판정은 1건만 남는다.
- 화면(QU-*, RU-8, E2E):
  - 리드 상세 '적격 판정' 칸:
    - 현재 판정과, 지금 기준보다 이전 기준으로 한 판정인지 표시한다.
    - 판정과 사유는 선택으로만 고르고 자유 문구 칸은 없다.
    - '판정 기록 (기준 vN)' 버튼과 이력(최근 것 먼저)이 있다.
  - 보드: '적격 판정' 필터(적격·보류·거절·판정 없음)와 '판정' 열.
  - 성과 탭: '적격 판정(문의 월 코호트)' 표.
- 보고(`fr-report@2026-09-27.4`, RM-Q1~Q4):
  - 코호트마다 적격·보류·거절·판정 없음 수, 기준 버전별 적격 수, 적격 리드당 비용(코호트 지출 합 ÷ 적격 수)을 낸다.
  - 집계 시점(asOf)까지의 마지막 판정을 센다.
  - 1~4건 칸은 억제하고, 적격 20건 전에는 적격 리드당 비용을 숨긴다. 결정 36의 계약 예외는 적용하지 않는다.
  - 주간 비용 칸의 빈 `cost.qualified`와 '비움' 줄을 지웠다.
  - 사유 코드와 행위자는 보고에 싣지 않는다.
- 모델 경계(QL-M1): 합성 워크스페이스에 적격 기준과 리드마다 판정 2번(사유 코드 `timing_unconfirmed`·`region_unavailable`)을 심었다. 그 상태로 역할·회의를 모의 HERMES로 실행했다. 제출 본문·`hermes_submission`·콘솔에 사유 코드 0건이다.

## 명세와 다르게 한 것
- 계획 R6 지표 표는 적격 리드당 비용을 채널 단위로 적었다. 대표 결정에 따라 문의 월 코호트 기준으로 계산하고 채널별로는 나누지 않는다. 계획 표를 고쳤다.
- 사유는 코드만 받는다. 자유 문구 칸은 두지 않았다. 그래서 '자유 텍스트를 목록에서 가린다'는 해당하지 않는다.
- 증빙 묶음(리드별 여정)에는 판정 이력을 넣지 않았다. 판정 이력은 리드 상세·이벤트·감사에 있다.
- 작업 이름은 `qualify_lead`다. `record_*`는 증빙 작업 접두어이고, 직원에게 `record_*`가 없다는 기존 검사가 있어 피했다.

author: cjohnsonpeart25
body:
Closes #5.

**Favourites** now land in the **Library** folder, and stop being there when they stop being **Favourites**. The mechanism is the part worth reading: the **Library** is *derived* from the **Decision log** — one idempotent operation makes the folder agree with the log — rather than being written as a side effect of a click. That is what makes a failed download a non-event, and what gives **Clearance** at #7 the removal half for free.

## What changed

**Core service.** `reconcile_library()` writes a file for every **Wallpaper** whose *resolved* **Verdict** is **Favourite** and which has no recorded **Library** file, and removes the recorded file of every **Wallpaper** that has one and is no longer a **Favourite**. Nothing else. It is a condition over the **Decision log**, not a queue of pending work, so there is no second account of what the log already says and nothing that can drift out of step with it. Calling it twice writes once.

It runs at the tail of `submit_batch`, **after** the transaction has committed and never inside it. Downloading is a ten-second network call to `w.wallhaven.cc`; holding SQLite's write lock across it would block every other writer, and a failure inside it would roll back **Verdicts** the user actually gave. A **Favourite** is a fact about taste, not a claim that a download succeeded. Failures are collected into a returned `LibraryReconciliation` rather than raised, because a raise would turn a **Batch** that *was* recorded into an error page telling the user it was not.

Migration 4 adds `library_files (wallpaper_id PRIMARY KEY, path, written_at)` — the deferred decision #4 left here. `path` is the absolute path the writer returned, and deletion only ever targets it, never one recomputed from the **Library** setting, which can have changed since (invariant 9). The destination for a *new* file comes from the setting as it is now; those are deliberately different sources.

**Writer.** `DownloadingLibraryWriter` streams the full-resolution image to a temp file **inside** the **Library** folder and `os.replace`s it into position (invariant 10), creating the folder on its first file — #4 stores the path without touching the filesystem, so the first **Favourite** is what makes it. `remove` is `unlink(missing_ok=True)`: "**Library** file deleted in Explorer" is a state the spec guarantees is reachable, and an existence check would still race with the user's file manager. Not an **API call** (invariant 11) — the image hosts are separate from `wallhaven.cc/api`. The protocol shape is unchanged. `UnbuiltLibraryWriter` is gone; `main.py` wires the real one.

**Shared.** The atomic write moves out of `core.py` into `files.py` rather than being duplicated. The **Thumbnail cache** and the **Library** want it for the same reason and are deliberately separate concerns (invariant 8), so neither should import the other. It grows a chunked form so a multi-megabyte wallpaper is never assembled in memory.

**Docs.** ADR 0006 for the derived **Library**, the placement of the download, the reported failures and why a file deleted in Explorer is not noticed. `CONTEXT.md` gains **Library reconciliation**. `AGENTS.md` loses the two deferrals that land here and gains one for surfacing a failed write.

## Checks

`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `pyright` strict and `pytest` all clean. 121 tests, 14 new. No test touches the network — the real writer is driven against `tmp_path` with `httpx2.MockTransport`. Built test-first; the seam tests were red at import before any of this existed.

See the review note below for the three places the reading was chosen rather than forced.

## Deliberately not here

Any UI for a failed **Library** write — the report exists, nothing renders it (deferred to #15). Rebuilding the **Library** from scratch, or repairing one the user has been deleting from: both would need the folder read back, which the **Library** is defined not to allow. Closing the writer's `httpx2.Client` on shutdown — that belongs with the lifespan #6 is building. **Clearance** (#7) calls the operation but is not this ticket.

author: gdelgiovine
body:
## Summary

Evolves the 0.5 singleton broker to 0.6 without changing the established Razor/MVC ↔ Blazor communication invariant.

The core `RazorBlazorDataExchange` remains the same singleton, session-aware, bidirectional in-process broker. Version 0.6 is additive and introduces two optional infrastructure layers:

1. ordered completion lanes for workflows that require deterministic publication/update completion order;
2. a transport SPI and serialization-safe wire envelope for future multi-process adapters.

## Ordered exchange

Adds `RazorBlazorOrderedDataExchange`, registered as a singleton facade over the existing broker.

Ordering can be selected as:

- `SessionAndProperty` — one property lane per session; unrelated properties/sessions remain concurrent;
- `Session` — exclusive writer for the complete session.

The final implementation uses a writer-preferred asynchronous reader/writer coordinator per session:

- property-scoped ordered operations enter as readers and can run concurrently on different property lanes;
- session-scoped operations enter as writers, wait for all active property readers, and block new readers until the writer completes.

This means `Session` genuinely serializes against **all** ordered operations in that session, not only other calls that also selected `Session`.

The ordered facade awaits complete async broker dispatch before releasing its lane. Property lanes and session coordinators are reference-counted and retired when no active/waiting operation remains.

Reentrancy rules prevent lock-order deadlocks:

- same-property reentry executes causally inside the currently held property lane;
- any nested ordered publication while a session writer is held executes inside that writer;
- property → session escalation is rejected with a clear exception;
- property → different-property nested ordering is rejected and the caller is directed to use `Session` scope for cross-property workflows.

The AsyncLocal held-order snapshot is cloned per async flow so sibling subscriber flows cannot mutate each other's ordering context.

## Transport abstraction

Adds `IRazorBlazorDataExchangeTransport` and the default `InMemoryRazorBlazorDataExchangeTransport`.

`RazorBlazorTransportEnvelope` is designed for a future process boundary and contains:

- OriginNodeId
- SessionId / PropertyName / ActorId
- MessageId / CorrelationId
- SourceVersion / Timestamp
- ValueTypeName
- JSON payload

The wire envelope deliberately does not contain live object references or `System.Type` instances.

Custom transport registration is infrastructure-only:

```csharp
services
    .AddRazorBlazorDataExchange()
    .UseRazorBlazorDataExchangeTransport<MyRedisTransport>();
```

This does not require Razor/Blazor publishers or subscribers to depend on Redis, Service Bus or another external technology.

## Important scale-out boundary

0.6 introduces the transport contract but does **not** claim transparent distributed broker replication yet. Cross-node ingress/egress still needs explicit policies for deduplication, version reconciliation, replay/reconnect, delivery guarantees, distributed ordering, origin filtering and authorization. This is intentionally deferred rather than silently changing the proven 0.5 semantics.

## Compatibility

- Existing `RazorBlazorDataExchange` API is unchanged.
- Existing `Publish`, `PublishAsync`, `Update`, `UpdateAsync`, `Subscribe`, `SubscribeSession` and legacy APIs retain their behavior.
- Session partitioning remains an isolation boundary only; it does not restrict Razor → Blazor, Blazor → Razor or same-session cross-circuit communication.
- The ordered layer is opt-in.
- Core version becomes `0.6.0`.

## Validation

Adds `RazorBlazorDataExchange.V06Tests` and keeps all existing 0.5 stress/browser E2E validation.

0.6 tests cover:

- same-route completion ordering;
- concurrency of independent property lanes;
- session-wide writer ordering across different properties;
- session writer waiting for active property readers;
- new property readers waiting for an active session writer;
- same-route reentrant publication without deadlock;
- rejection of unsafe nested cross-property property ordering;
- ordered concurrent atomic updates;
- in-memory transport broadcast fan-out;
- transport subscriber failure isolation;
- JSON transport-envelope round-trip;
- DI registration and custom transport replacement.

Existing stress tests continue to cover session isolation, bidirectional fan-out, 24,000 atomic updates, loop suppression, fault isolation and cleanup. Existing Playwright tests continue to validate real Razor Pages + Blazor Server + SignalR + JS interop, including same-session cross-circuit fan-out.

Current PR CI result: restore PASS, solution build PASS, broker stress tests PASS, 0.6 ordering/transport tests PASS, Playwright Chromium/browser E2E PASS.

Documentation: `docs/v0.6-ordered-transport.md`.

## Summary

Removes the unused port for writing a review outcome onto a stored task version, as agreed on 2026-09-27 ("未使用の口は削除します").

Approval now adopts a draft (ADR 0019, #522). Since #526 nothing outside tests called `record_review`.

**Removed**
- `TaskRepository.record_review`, from the protocol, `InMemoryTaskRepository` and `SqlTaskRepository`
- `Provenance.reviewed` (core), used only by those two implementations

**Kept**
- `REVIEW_FIELDS`: `substantive()` still leaves the review outcome out of "same content", so saving the same version as approved is not refused. Its comment now describes that job rather than the removed write path.
- `list_versions_in_review`: the console overview still counts in-review versions.
- The rule that a rejection needs a reason: it is also enforced by `Provenance`'s validator in core.

**Tests.** `test_review_state_rules.py` keeps the rules that still hold:
- in-review versions are listed
- a stored statement cannot change
- the review outcome is not content
- a rejection needs a reason

The tests of the removed write path (approve publishes, deciding twice is refused) go with it. The conformance test (both stores satisfy their protocols) passes unchanged, since the method left all three places together.

Full suite: 2695 passed, 25 skipped (18 `[runsc]`, run in CI). ruff, format, mypy (5 packages) and lint-imports (29 kept) are clean.

## Fase 5 — Automatizaciones

- **Tasas** (`app/worker/taux.ts`): cron `0 19 * * *` (06:00 Nouméa). BCE (Frankfurter, secours open.er-api) × 119,332 → KV `taux:latest`, `taux_historique` y una operación `taux.definir` por divisa en `sync_journal`, así cada teléfono recibe las tasas del día en su siguiente pull. Botón «Actualiser maintenant» en `/admin`.
- **Clôture en PDF** (`app/worker/pdf/cloture.ts`): plantilla HTML autónoma con el diseño de la app (cabecera night, KPIs, encaissements, top, conteo, ventas) → Browser Rendering (binding `BROWSER`, solo `env.production`) → R2 `clotures/AAAA/AAAA-MM-DD_<id>.pdf`, generado con `waitUntil` al recibir la clôture por sync; sin navegador se archiva el HTML. Servido y regenerable desde `/api/admin/journees/:id/pdf`.
- **Panel `/admin`** (`app/src/ecrans/Admin.tsx`): pestañas que cargan al abrirse — ventas del mes (CA, jornadas, panier moyen, por mercado, encaissements, top), jornadas con clôture (ver / regenerar), horas por vendedora (total, a pagar, pagado), exportes CSV de ventas y horas (BOM + «;», Excel), tasas, archivos, emparejamiento y dispositivos.
- **Archivo mensual** (`app/worker/archive.ts`): cron `0 20 1 * *` → R2 `archives/AAAA-MM.json` con todas las tablas (sin hashes); listado y descarga desde el panel.
- `wrangler.jsonc` (producción): binding `browser` y `triggers.crons`. Sin migración.

Tests (`app/test/automatisations.spec.ts`, runtime real de Workers): clôture sincronizada → archivo en R2 visible y descargable (HTML sin navegador); KPIs, detalle y CSV del mes; tasas con fuente simulada → KV + historial + diario recibido por un teléfono; fallo sin fuente; archivo mensual. Panel probado en el navegador contra la API local.

author: alsotoes
body:
💡 What:
Replaced inefficient list comprehensions used within loops (e.g., `x in [y.attr for y in elements]`) with precomputed sets outside loops or generator expressions combined with `any()`.
Refactored `is_host_unreachable`, `is_host_schedulable`, and `is_host_draining` in `inventory.py`. Refactored `get_placement_hosts` and `place` in `schedule.py`. Precomputed `osdspec_ids` in `module.py` and simplified a nested list comprehension.

🎯 Why:
Python's list comprehensions create a full list in memory. When used on the right-hand side of an `in` operator inside another loop or comprehension, it creates a new list and performs an O(N) linear scan for every iteration, resulting in O(N*M) complexity. Precomputing into a `set` changes the lookup to O(1) and reduces memory overhead. For single evaluations, `any()` with a generator allows for early short-circuiting.

📊 Impact:
Improves execution time of scheduling logic, osdspec preview fetching, and inventory state evaluation by reducing time complexity from O(N*M) to O(N+M) and avoiding redundant list memory allocations.

🔬 Measurement:
Run the cephadm unit tests via `tox -e py3 -- cephadm/tests/test_scheduling.py cephadm/tests/test_cephadm.py` to ensure scheduling and inventory logic performs identical state tracking but slightly faster. No regressions should occur.

body:
From APP · Paint sync's regression report: `refresh_paints` only re-applied riders whose paint was **missing** when the refresh began (`g_paintMissing`). A rider who rejoined already has their paint in the table, but the game re-adds them through its reuse path, which does not re-paint. So they rode stock.

A paint refresh now re-applies every remote rider's **installed** bike and gear paints. It never touches the local rider (the name matched against the session rider), and paints that aren't installed are still skipped. It's cheap: `0x4DC50` / bus `0x9E` per rider. A full reload (R) keeps the old behaviour (missing paints only).

This is v0.39.2's second fix, alongside #90 (whose rejoin fix sends rejoiners down the fresh path anyway). App side: mxb-app#879 sends `refresh_paints` on every room "joined".

author: etibarhasanov
body:
The flashcards put Estonian in front of people who have never heard any of it. Reading a word only gets you half of it: *leib* and *leiba* are one thing on the page and two when spoken. The README listed "no pronunciation" under what the page does not do. The owner asked for it, the shape was described in the session, and they agreed it with Mari as the voice.

**What a visitor gets.** A row of quiet `.alt` presses under the card, each with a speaker beside it:
- **Front:** *Hear it*, which says the word.
- **Back:** *The word*, plus *The sentence* on the 772 cards that have one.
- **S key:** says the same thing as the last button in the row.
- **Stopping:** a second press stops the sound, and the speaker turns into a square while it plays. If the button leaves the screen (the card was answered or undone, the deck was left, or a lesson was opened), `render()` stops the sound.
- **Lessons:** the grammar lessons have no speaker, because their Estonian is in prose and tables rather than on a card.
- **When the voice fails:** the press goes quiet and a toast says so. The run carries on unchanged.

**Where the sound comes from.** A new route, `GET /api/say?text=`, asks the University of Tartu's Estonian text-to-speech (speaker `mari`, speed 0.9) and returns the WAV.
- **Nothing is stored:** no database, no bucket, no file. Cloudflare's cache keeps the answer for thirty days, keyed on the voice and the words, so each word goes to Tartu once per data centre a month.
- **Only shipped cards are spoken:** the route speaks the front of a card or the Estonian of a card's sentence in `data/decks.json`, exactly, and answers anything else `404 not-a-card`. That keeps it from being an open text-to-speech proxy running on a university's goodwill.
- **When Tartu does not answer:** the route returns `502 no-voice` if nothing has come back within fifteen seconds.

**It honours `Range`, because iPhones need it.** Safari's first request for any media is `bytes=0-1`, and [Apple's guide](``https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/AppleApplications/Reference/SafariWebContent/CreatingVideoforSafarioniPhone/CreatingVideoforSafarioniPhone.html)`` says a server hosting media for iOS must answer that with those two bytes. The route answers `206` with the slice, whether the recording came from the cache or fresh from Tartu. It also waits for the cache to store a new recording before answering, so Safari's second request, which follows the probe at once, finds it already there instead of sending the same words to Tartu twice. I added this after the first push, when I was checking the change for merge.

`VOICE` is one constant and the cache key carries it, so offering Albert as well is a small second step. That step needs its own description first, since the voice switch would be a new control.

**Docs moved with it.** A new README section, **Hearing it**, under **Flashcards**. New rows in **Files**, **Taking it out**, **What it does not do** and **Analytics** (`flash_say`), and a `/api/say` row in the api skill's route table. The `flash*` key count goes from eighty-two to eighty-seven. While editing **What it does not do**, I fixed two lines there that had gone stale: it said there was no undo (undo has since shipped), and it pointed "below" for the three forms, which are above. **Taking it out** counted five flashcard lines in **Files** where there were six; with this change there are seven. I left `CLAUDE.md`'s "twenty-five Cloudflare Functions" alone because I couldn't find what it counts.

**Rebased** onto the two flashcard commits that landed while this was open (the grammar lessons, and the door that reopens where you were). The conflicts were stamps, key counts, the api skill row and README placement. I re-stamped and re-validated, and the share card redrew identical.

**What was run.**
- `node tools/stamp.mjs`, `node tools/ogcard.mjs`, `node tools/validate.mjs`, `node tools/qrperf.mjs --check`, `node .claude/hooks/d1-write-gate.mjs --check`: all clean on the rebased tree.
- **Browser, stubbed:** Chromium at 390 px in both styles, with `/api/flashcard` stubbed from the real *Pronouns* deck and `/api/say` stubbed. Checked:
  - idle, loading and playing
  - a second press stopping the sound, and the sound carrying across the turn
  - answering the card stopping the sound
  - the S key on the back saying the sentence
  - the 502 path and its toast
  - the back of the card in Russian at 390 px
- **Browser, real route:** after the rebase, the page ran against the real route, served from Node with Cloudflare's cache and Tartu mocked.
  - Chromium sent `bytes=0-`, got `206` and played.
  - A second pass over the same words never reached the voice.
  - A grammar lesson drew no speaker and sent nothing on S.
- **Route on its own:**
  - a two-byte probe gets `206 bytes 0-1/66194`, and the follow-up comes from the cache
  - suffix, middle, past-the-end (`416`) and multi-range requests all answer correctly
  - text that isn't on a card gets a 404
  - a dead voice gets a 502, and a hanging one gets a 502 at fifteen seconds

**What could not be checked.** This sandbox has no network route to `api.tartunlp.ai`, and no WebKit to play Safari's probe in a real Safari. So nobody has heard a word yet, and an iPhone hasn't been tried. If Tartu wants a different field name or voice id than `speaker: "mari"`, every press will show the error toast. That is quiet and harmless, but it would be the first thing to look at. After it lands, `curl -sS -o t.wav 'https://tallinntastebuds.ee/api/say?text=Tere'` shows whether the route or Tartu is the problem, and `curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null -H 'Range: bytes=0-1' 'https://tallinntastebuds.ee/api/say?text=Tere'` should show `206` and `content-range: bytes 0-1/…`. Driving the page reported into the live GA and Clarity as usual; the analytics tags were blocked in the stubbed runs.

Nothing to apply by hand: no schema, no load, no secret.

Correction to the original report: Spotlight does **not** call `/api/chat`. It already reasons through CORE (`executeAgenticLoop` → `/v3/cognition/agent`). It then ran `parseAIResponse` on CORE's `final_message` and executed any `[[MORA_ACTION:{...}]]` it found (highlight, point, navigate, pulse, pane). That text-derived execution is the injection path: any document, mail or web text the model repeats could drive the shell.

Env key: in this repo, `NEXT_PUBLIC_AI_*` appears only as placeholders in `.env.local.example`. No workflow, Dockerfile or GitHub secret references it; repo secrets are SSH deploy credentials only. The production server `.env` was not inspected (no server access by design).

## Change
- New `lib/mora/coreUiActions.ts` executes CORE's structured `ui_actions` through an allowlist: `navigate_department|space|folder`, `highlight`, and `open_pane` for `search` (query only) and `document` (nodeId only). It handles at most 5 actions per response and ignores unknown types.
- Spotlight uses `response.ui_actions` and shows `final_message` as-is. It no longer parses markers.
- Deleted `lib/ai/cursorBridge.ts`, `lib/api/aiClient.ts` and `app/api/chat/route.ts`, removed the unused import in `apps/chat`, and dropped the provider-key block from `.env.local.example`.
- `AgentResponse` type gains `ui_actions?`.

Companion: Saimor-world/saimor-core#65 removes the MORA_ACTION instructions from the CORE prompts.

## Tests
- New: `__tests__/lib/mora/coreUiActions.test.ts` covers the allowlist, sanitised pane data, ignoring unknown or marker input, and the cap.
- New case in `Spotlight.navigation.test.tsx`: a CORE response carries both `ui_actions` and a `[[MORA_ACTION:highlight]]` marker. Navigation follows `ui_actions` and no presence event fires from the marker.
- Removed obsolete `cursorBridge` mocks from 4 chat/ChatPane suites.
- `jest` (Spotlight, coreUiActions, aura, ChatPane agentic/dispatch-parity/pill, os/shell): 12 suites / 54 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

Behaviour note: until the CORE PR deploys, a model that still emits a marker would show it as literal text in Spotlight rather than executing it. That is intended, and CORE's agent prompt path (`core/cognition/external.py`) does not teach markers anyway.

Not merged or deployed.

author: abbra
body:
pyo3 ships wasm/emscripten/runner.py, executable and starting with #!/usr/local/bin/python.  rpm turned that into a requirement of rust-pyo3_0.29-devel on /usr/local/bin/python, which no package provides.  The pyo3 build passed; the next package that needed it failed in COPR with "nothing provides /usr/local/bin/python".

regen now lists executable files of the crate whose #! interpreter is outside /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin and /sbin, unless the prep scripts in rust2rpm.toml name them (removed, or made non-executable), and says how to handle them.  Of the crates in my tree, it finds exactly this one.

## Summary by Sourcery

Flag crate executables with nonstandard shebang interpreters and provide guidance for handling them before package dependency generation.

New Features:
- Detect executable crate files whose shebang interpreters are outside the standard system binary directories.
- Report such files during dependency regeneration unless packaging prep scripts explicitly handle them.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent generated RPM dependencies on unavailable nonstandard interpreters such as /usr/local/bin/python.

Enhancements:
- Document how to resolve executables with nonstandard interpreters in Rust package metadata.

Documentation:
- Add packaging guidance for removing or disabling unneeded executables with foreign shebangs.

Tests:
- Add coverage for detecting foreign shebangs and recognizing files handled by prep scripts.

author: mairat
body:
**Stacked on Broiler-Platform/Broiler.Layout#29**, whose commit this branch includes. Its own change is the last commit. Merge #29 first: see "Why stacked" below.

## Summary

A percentage margin or padding was resolved against the box's own width. CSS 2.1 §8.3 and §8.4 resolve it against the width of the box's containing block. The two agree only for a box that fills its container. In a 320 px block:
- a 100 px wide box with `padding-top: 50%` (the intrinsic-ratio pattern of responsive embeds, given a width) was 50 px tall; browsers make it 160;
- a box with `margin-left: 50%` started 50 px in; browsers start it 160 px in.

Found by Broiler-Platform/Broiler.Layout#29, which lists it as found alongside.

## Why

`CssBoxProperties` resolved every margin and padding against `Size.Width`, because it has no box tree to find a containing block in.

Resolving against the containing block exposes a cycle that the old basis hid:
- A float or an absolutely positioned box of `auto` width first takes the width it has room for, then measures its content.
- A percentage in that content, resolved against that width, grows the box by that much. In a 320 px block, a float holding a block with `padding-left: 10%` around a 100 px box came out 132 px wide; browsers make it 100.
- CSS Sizing 3 §5.2.1 resolves such a *cyclic percentage* against zero for intrinsic size contributions.
- The old code got zero at measurement only because the boxes inside were still 0 px wide. A side padding then kept that 0 for good.

## Changes

- `TryGetPercentageBasisWidth`, which `CssBox` overrides, gives the containing block's width:
  - for a box in flow or a float, the content width of `ContainingBlock`;
  - for an absolutely positioned box, the padding-box width of its positioned ancestor, from `GetAbsoluteContainingBlockPaddingBox`;
  - for a fixed box, the viewport's width.

  These are the widths `ResolveBlockUsedWidth` resolves the box's own width against. The root, the parts of a table, and grid items keep their own width.
- All four margins and all four paddings resolve a percentage against that width. A length resolves as before.
- A percentage `padding-left` or `padding-right` is now resolved on every read, as top and bottom have been since #29. #29 left the sides cached because they took part in the width they resolved against. They no longer do, and that width changes when the container is laid out again. A margin with a percentage inside a `calc()` was cached like a length; it is now resolved on every read too.
- While a box's content is measured for its intrinsic width, a percentage margin or padding inside it resolves against zero. That covers `GetMinMaxWidth`, `GetContentMinMaxWidth`, `GetMinimumWidth`, `ComputeShrinkToFitWidth` and `ComputeIntrinsicInlineSize`.
- Under the native zoom lever (off by default), the percentage takes the box's own zoom, as a percentage of the containing block already does for widths and insets.

## Why stacked

#29 made a percentage `padding-top` or `padding-bottom` resolve on every read. This branch extends that to the sides and changes what all of them resolve against. Both rewrite the same padding getters in `CssBoxProperties.cs`.

## Tests

`PercentageContainingBlockTests`, 17 new. Words are 8×16 px, in a 1024×768 viewport.
- A 100 px wide block, or inline-block, with `padding-top: 50%` in a 320 px block is 160 px tall (2).
- In a 320 px block, a 100 px wide block with `margin-left: 50%` starts 160 px in, and a float with `margin-left: 10%` starts 32 px in (2).
- A block with 20 px side margins in a 320 px block gets 32 px from `padding-left: 10%`.
- A 100 px wide item with `padding-top: 50%` in a 320 px row flex container is 160 px tall.
- In a positioned block 300 px wide with 10 px side padding, a 100 px wide box with `padding-top: 50%` is (2):
  - 150 px tall in flow, half the content box;
  - 160 px tall when absolutely positioned, half the padding box.
- A fixed box with `padding-top: 10%` is 102.4 px tall, a tenth of the viewport.
- A float, an absolutely positioned box and an inline-block of auto width each hold a block with `padding-left: 10%` around a 100 px box. For the float there is also a `margin-left: 10%` case. Each is 100 px wide, and the box starts 10 px in (4).
- After the container goes from 100 to 320 px and the tree is laid out again (2):
  - `padding-left: 10%` goes from 10 to 32 px;
  - `margin-left: calc(10% + 2px)` goes from 12 to 34 px.
- Controls, which pass before and after (2):
  - a box that fills its 320 px container is 160 px tall with `padding-top: 50%`;
  - a 20 px padding stays 20 px.

Negative controls:

| Engine | New tests failing |
|---|---|
| #29's `CssBoxProperties.cs`, `CssBox.ContainingBlock.cs`, `CssBox.Sizing.cs` | 15 of 17; the controls pass. 50 px for 160, 28 for 32, 10 for 102.4, and 0 for 10 in the shrink-to-fit boxes |
| The containing block's border box instead of its content box | 1: the box in flow, 160 for 150 |
| Out-of-flow boxes resolved as boxes in flow | 2: 150 for 160, and 32 for 102.4 |
| Side paddings cached as before | 4: the three shrink-to-fit boxes with a padding, 0 for 10 (the padding keeps the zero it measured); the second layout, 10 for 32 |
| A `calc()` margin cached as before | 1: 12 for 34 |
| No zero while measuring | 3: the float and the absolutely positioned box, 132 px wide for 100 |

`Broiler.Layout.Tests` 1714/1714 (1697 on #29). The solution builds with the same 305 warnings as before. Merged with the sixteen other open branches (#27, #28, #30 to #43), the suite passes 1872/1872.

## In the browser

#29 and this branch were each packed locally and pinned in a scratch Broiler.Browser worktree, and `Broiler.Cli` was built against each. `--evaluate-page` read `getBoundingClientRect`. Every case is in a 320 px block:

| Case | #29 | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| 100 px wide block with `padding-top: 50%` | 50 px tall | 160 px tall |
| Same, as an inline-block, a row flex item, or an absolutely positioned box | 50 px tall | 160 px tall |
| `margin-left: 50%` on a 100 px wide block | 50 px in | 160 px in |
| `margin-left: 10%` on a float / on an inline-block | 10 / 0 px in | 32 / 32 px in |
| `margin-left: 25%` on a column flex item | 0 px in | 80 px in |
| `padding-left: 10%` on a block with 20 px side margins | 28 px | 32 px |
| `padding-left: 10%` on a span | 0 px; text at 0 | 32 px; text drawn 32 px in |
| `margin-left: 10%` in a block 300 px wide with 5 px side borders and 10 px side padding | 20 px in | 45 px in |
| 50% wide block with `padding: 0 5%` | 160 px wide | 192 px wide |
| 100 px wide inline-flex with `padding-top: 25%` | 25 px tall | 80 px tall |
| 100 px wide list with `padding-left: 10%` | 100 px wide | 132 px wide |
| Absolutely positioned box in a 100 px block with `margin-left: 50%`, under a 320 px positioned ancestor | 50 px in | 160 px in |
| Float, absolutely positioned box, inline-block, or inline-flex of auto width, holding a block with `padding-left: 10%` around a word | 34.68 px wide; word 0 px in | 34.68 px wide; word 3.47 px in |
| Inline-block holding a block with `margin-left: 10%` around a word | word 3.12 px in | word 3.47 px in |

- Without the zero while measuring, the float and the absolutely positioned box in that row were 66.68 px wide.
- Unchanged:
  - an auto-width block with `padding-top: 50%`;
  - a responsive embed's wrapper with `padding-bottom: 56.25%`, 112.5 px tall in a 200 px block.
- Merged with the open branches, each of these measures the same.
- `--analyze` gives the same fragment tree and display list with this branch as with #29 alone. That covers the DuckDuckGo-shaped page from #16 and 23 other probe pages.
- `Broiler.Browser.Core.Tests` 207/207 and `Broiler.Cli.Tests` 180/180 with this branch.

## Found alongside, not fixed here

- **A grid item's percentage padding.** An auto-width grid item with `padding-top: 50%` in a 100 px column is 0 px tall, both on #29 and with this branch; browsers make it 50. Gri

author: rahmat-ullah
body:
**Agent-2**

Closes #649.

## What
`SogdaApp` read `followsPlatform` from `settingsProvider`, which never notifies, and it rebuilt only when `Theme`'s resolved mode changed. That fails in one case:
1. *Dark* is chosen on a dark phone, from *System*.
2. It resolves to the mode *System* already had, so the root never rebuilt and kept `ThemeMode.system`.
3. When the phone went light, the app went with it, despite the explicit *Dark*.

The fix:
- **A new `ThemeFollowsPlatform` notifier** (autoDispose, watched by the root) follows the setting through `settings.changes`, the way `LearnerName` does. Settings, import and reset all write it, so it reaches every writer.
- **The root watches it** instead of reading the setting once.

The provider is autoDispose, so the keepAlive table doesn't change. `settings.md` (FR-M3-02) says this.

## Tests
In widget_test's host-driven group, the phone's own switch:
- **`#649`:** *Dark* chosen on a dark phone, from *System*, stops the app following the phone. The phone then goes light, and the app stays dark.
- **`#649`:** *System* chosen from *Light* follows the phone from then on.

**Basic check:**
- `dart analyze --fatal-infos` clean; `dart format` 0 changed.
- 167 passed: widget, app_providers, settings, the settings golden, bootstrap and architecture.

## Plants (2 of 2 caught)
1. The root reads the setting once, which is the bug.
2. The provider doesn't follow changes.

## Device check
Not run. The bug needs a phone switch after a theme choice, which the widget tests drive through `platformBrightnessTestValue`. #644's device check already showed the switch path working on emulator-5558.

Workflows use scoped permissions, do not persist checkout credentials, have time limits and concurrency controls, and check dependency changes for high or critical vulnerabilities. Dependabot now covers Node and Python tooling as well as Gradle and Actions. The Gradle distribution has an official checksum, and CI validates wrapper JARs. Gradle caching uses the basic GitHub cache provider. A main-only workflow submits the resolved Java dependency graph to GitHub for vulnerability alerts.

Updating release-it and its dependency lock resolves the reported Node-tooling vulnerabilities. Node tooling now requires the versions declared in `package.json`; Minecraft, NeoForge, Java, and gameplay behavior are unchanged. A redundant ModDex string replacement identified by CodeQL is removed.

GitHub settings enable private vulnerability reporting, dependency alerts and security updates, and CodeQL scans for Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and Actions. Main-branch rules require pull requests, trusted CI, and resolved conversations with no mandatory approval. The owner retains a release bypass; separate rules prevent deletion, force-pushes, and merge commits on `main`. Squash merging and merged-branch cleanup are enabled.

Validation: `ciCheck`, repository and ModDex checks, strict MkDocs build, Actionlint, workflow Bash/version validation, clean `npm ci`, `npm audit` (zero vulnerabilities), and release-it dry run all passed. The existing wrapper JAR also matches Gradle's official validation catalog. No release or tag was created.

author: zkochan
body:
The `resolutionMode: time-based` section said subdependencies are resolved only from versions published before the last direct dependency. Both pnpm 11 and pnpm 12 behave differently in two ways:

- The cutoff is the newest direct dependency's publish date plus one hour.
- If no version before the cutoff satisfies a subdependency's range, pnpm installs the lowest version that does.

The section now also says that with `minimumReleaseAge` set, pnpm resolves subdependencies against the earlier of the two cutoffs. Updated in `docs/` and `versioned_docs/version-11.x/`.

Raised in pnpm/pnpm#13569 and in review of pnpm/pnpm#16207. That PR also makes only the `minimumReleaseAge` cutoff decide which versions are reported as too new. It has not been released yet, so this PR leaves that out.

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified that time-based resolution considers subdependency versions published up to one hour after the newest direct dependency, and falls back to the lowest version that satisfies the range if none qualify.
  * When `minimumReleaseAge` is also set, the earlier cutoff applies. If the fallback version is newer than that cutoff, `minimumReleaseAgeStrict` determines whether pnpm installs it or fails.

## Goal

Booth Actions Enablement PRD, Phase 3 ("Punch from here"): finish wiring the already-gated "Punch from here" button (`ReaderFlagsPanel.tsx`, gated behind `CapabilityGate('punch')` since DAW port PRD Phase 7 / #705) to the real `dawport.Puncher` role, and do the same for the pickup list's own punch action — closing out Teleprompter Manuscript Integration PRD Phase 12's remaining scope (host anchors, the pre-roll setting, the real click wiring).

## What changed

**Go (`internal/teleprompter`, `apps/desktop`)**
- `internal/teleprompter/anchors.go`: the punch anchors file (word index → REAPER project time), resolved by exact match, interpolation between two anchors, or an extrapolated pace-based estimate labelled `alignment` (a documented stand-in for a real offline re-decode with word timestamps, which this phase does not build — see Open follow-up below).
- `Service.CurrentWord`/`CurrentChapter`: what a live session is reading now, for the poll loop and the punch binding.
- `apps/desktop/teleprompterpunchpoll.go`: a background loop (alongside the existing `backgroundCheckLoop` etc.) that polls REAPER's play position through `dawport.Role[dawport.Puncher]` every 3s while a session is live, and records an anchor. Read-only, silent no-op whenever there's nothing to anchor.
- `Teleprompter.punch_preroll_seconds` setting (0–10s, default 3s; `apps/desktop/app.go`, `settings_number.go`, `config/defaults.json`, `internal/settings/store.go`'s `builtinDefaults` mirror). Reading REAPER's own pre-roll preference first is the owner-gated spike this phase does not run (`docs/operations/reaper-verification-pass.md`); the setting is the only source until it does.
- `TeleprompterPunchPreview(word)`/`TeleprompterPunch(word)` (`teleprompterpunch.go`): resolve the live session's own chapter (no chapter id ever comes from the UI), the word's time/source/pre-roll, and — for `TeleprompterPunch` — call `dawport.Role[dawport.Puncher](resolver, CapPunch).PunchTo`, never `bridge.Actions` directly. A successful punch drops every anchor at or after the punched word.
- `PickupsPunch(position)` (`pickupspunch.go`): the same `Puncher` role, but no resolution step — a pickup marker's position is already a project time.
- `hostAPIVersion` 63 → 64 (main's tip when this branch was cut).

**UI**
- `ReaderFlagsPanel.tsx`: "Punch from here" now previews (no REAPER mutation) then opens a confirm dialog naming the resolved time, its source and the pre-roll before moving; a refusal (no anchor yet, no live chapter, no DAW) shows inline.
- `apps/ui/src/components/tracks/PickupsDialog.tsx`: added "Punch from here" next to "Mark this pickup done", gated the same way, moving the cursor straight away (no preview needed — see note below).

**Note on the PRD's own file list.** This phase's Parallel-session row names `components/manuscript/PickupsDialog.tsx`, which doesn't exist. The real pickup list dialog is `apps/ui/src/components/tracks/PickupsDialog.tsx` (REAPER Automation Follow-Through PRD Phase 9) — that's where the punch button landed; the PRD's row is corrected in this PR.

**Docs.** `booth-actions-enablement.prd.md` Phase 3 → `complete`, its Parallel-session row corrected. `teleprompter-manuscript-integration.prd.md` Phase 12 updated to record what's delivered and what's still owner-gated (spike 1, the REAPER pre-roll read) or unbuilt (a real offline-alignment mode).

## Two things worth a second pair of eyes

1. **Hand-computed Wails bindings and goldens.** This container has no GTK4/webkitgtk-6.0 (its package mirrors are unreachable here), so it can't build the `wails3` CLI even as a static-analysis tool (it transitively needs the same libs) — `pnpm --dir apps/desktop run bindings` couldn't run. The three new `host.ts` exports were added by hand, with their FNV-1a-32 method IDs (`main.Host.<Method>`) computed locally and cross-checked against six of the file's own already-known IDs before trusting the formula. Likewise the two new golden payloads (`teleprompter-punch-results.json`, `pickups-punch-results.json`) were produced by reproducing `contractfile.Check`'s exact encoder locally rather than via `UPDATE_CONTRACTS=1` (same root cause — the owning Go tests are in `apps/desktop`'s main package). Everything here passes `wireContracts.test.ts` and `go vet` (cross-compiled for `GOOS=windows`, this container's only path to that package), but a run of `pnpm --dir apps/desktop run bindings` on a real toolchain should confirm the diff is a no-op, and `UPDATE_CONTRACTS=1` should confirm the two goldens.
2. **The `alignment` fallback is a pace extrapolation, not a real re-decode.** Phase 12 of the sibling PRD calls for "offline word-time alignment" as the fallback when no anchor covers a word; building a real one needs a sidecar mode with per-word timestamps this phase doesn't add. What's shipped instead: when a word falls outside every recorded anchor's range, its time is extrapolated from the anchors' overall pace, labelled `alignment` so the UI is honest about it being an estimate. Flagged as a follow-up in the sibling PRD's Phase 12 row rather than silently left off.

## Local checks run, with results

- `go vet ./internal/teleprompter/...` and `go test ./internal/teleprompter/...` — native, all pass.
- `go test ./internal/settings/...`, `./internal/dawport/...` (and subpackages) — native, all pass (includes `TestBuiltinDefaultsMatchRepoDefaultsFile`).

- `node scripts/ci/bump-host-api.test.mjs` — passes (confirms the three `hostAPIVersion` locations agree).
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` on every touched file — clean.
- `npx vitest run` (the whole `apps/ui` suite) — 3155 tests, all pass except one pre-existing flake (`App.test.tsx`'s "the host is busy" test, unrelated to this PR, reproduces on `main` under the same parallel load and passes cleanly alone/isolated).
- Playwright visual suite, targeted: every `manuscript / read-aloud*` state (31 tests) and `tracks / pickups-next*` (2 tests) — all pass; PNGs reviewed at all three viewports for the two new states plus the two existing ones whose rendered content changed. (This container's pinned `chrome-headless-shell` build wasn't installed; verification used the pre-installed `chromium` build via a local, uncommitted symlink at the pinned path — not part of the repo.)
