author: thuupx
body:
<!--
Title: a conventional prefix (feat:, fix:, deps:, docs:, refactor:), lowercase,
imperative, and about the why rather than the what.

Delete any section that does not apply. Three honest lines beat thirty empty ones.
-->

## What and why

<!-- What changes, and what problem it solves. The "why" is the part a reader
     cannot recover from the diff. -->

Until now the only way to upgrade an installation was to re-run `install.sh`
(`curl | sh`) or rebuild from source. This adds `hive update`, so a running
installation can move to a release by itself.

```
hive update [-version <x.y.z>] [-dir <path>] [-force]
```

It mirrors `scripts/install.sh` deliberately, so a self-update lands the same
shape as a fresh install:

- **The checksum is verified before the archive is opened.** An archive that is
  never extracted cannot do anything, whatever is in it.
- **Each binary is staged beside its target and renamed**, because a rename is
  atomic within one filesystem — writing over a binary the daemon is running does
  not work, and Linux refuses it with "Text file busy".
- **The target directory is the running binary's**, resolved. The plugins ship
  next to `hive` and the daemon resolves them from there, so `hive` and its
  plugins move together. `-dir` overrides it.

The version comes from `-version` or, by default, from the redirect on
`/releases/latest` (one request, not rate-limited like the API; the API is the
fallback). A running service is restarted so the new build is the one running;
without a service it says to restart `hive serve`.

Edges are stated plainly, as the installer does: `darwin/amd64` has no published
build, an unsupported platform is refused, a development build always updates,
and an already-current version is a no-op unless `-force` is given.

## Verification

<!-- How you know it works. `make ci` is the floor, not the answer.

     Anything that crosses a wire — the protocol, a transport, a plugin — needs to
     have been run against something real, and what you saw needs to be in this
     box. Unit tests have never once caught a malformed permission response, a
     replayed conversation, or a message Slack refuses to accept. -->

- [x] `make ci` passes
- [x] Run against a real agent or platform, and here is what I saw:
  - **Against the published v1.1.0 release**, into a throwaway `-dir`:

    ```text
    hive: development build -> 1.1.0
    hive: downloading hive_1.1.0_darwin_arm64.tar.gz
    hive: verified the sha256 checksum
    hive: installed hive, hive-plugin-acp, hive-plugin-slack, hive-plugin-zalo to /tmp/hive-update-test
    ```

    The installed binary reports `hive 1.1.0`.
  - **Already current** (a version-stamped build): `hive: 1.1.0 is already the
    current version`, exit 0, nothing downloaded.
  - **`-force`** reinstalled over the same version.
  - Unit tests drive a local release server for the install, the checksum
    refusal, the up-to-date no-op, and both latest-version paths.

## Tests

<!-- A bug fix carries a test that fails without the fix, and saying you checked
     is what makes it a regression test rather than a description of one. -->

- [x] Added or updated tests
- [ ] Confirmed the new test fails against the old behaviour

This is a new command, so there is no prior behaviour for a test to fail
against. The tests cover: asset naming and the platform errors, checksum parsing
(`./`, `*`, `\r`), version comparison, tag parsing, extraction (a symlink is
refused, an escaping path is ignored), and `performUpdate` for install,
checksum-refusal, and the current-version no-op.

## Semantics

<!-- Hive owns orchestration and context; agents own execution; transports own
     presentation. A change to a semantic, to `protocol/hive/v1`, or to the
     configuration format is a compatibility decision — say which, and whether the
     design document (`docs/hive-solution-design.md`) agrees or is silent. -->

- [x] No semantic, protocol, or configuration change
- [ ] Described above, and consistent with the design document

A new CLI command only: no configuration key, no wire method, no change to
`protocol/hive/v1`. It consumes the existing release assets, so nothing about a
release changes.

## Layering

- [x] `protocol/hive/v1` still imports only the standard library
- [x] Domain packages (`internal/agent`, `internal/command`, `internal/event`,
      `internal/session`) still do not import `internal/storage`
- [x] No platform-specific command registry or vendor semantics reached the core
- [x] Read-modify-write goes through `UpdateAgentRunWith`, `UpdateSessionWith`, or
      `UpdateHandoffWith`

Unchanged. The command lives in `cmd/hive`, and touches no domain package.

## Reaching the machine

<!-- Hive runs agents that read and write files, and asks users to approve what
     they do. If this changes either, a reviewer needs to know. -->

- [x] Does not change what an agent can reach, or what a user can approve
- [ ] Does change it, deliberately, and the bound is described above

It replaces Hive's own binaries and may restart the daemon, but it does not
change what an agent can reach or what a user can approve. The update's own
safety is the checksum (verified before extraction) and the staged rename; it
does not run anything it downloaded.

## Dependencies

<!-- A new dependency is a decision, not an implementation detail. -->

- [x] No new dependencies
- [ ] New dependency, and why it beats what is already here:

Standard library only (`net/http`, `crypto/sha256`, `archive/tar`,
`compress/gzip`). `go.mod`/`go.sum` are unchanged.

## Follow-ups

<!-- What this deliberately leaves out, so a reviewer does not have to guess
     whether it was forgotten. -->

- **`hive update` ships in the next release.** A user on v1.1.0 cannot run it
  yet, because v1.1.0 was built before the command existed; they run `install.sh`
  once, then update with `hive update` from then on.
- **No signature or provenance.** `checksums.txt` proves integrity against the
  release, not who made it — the same gap `docs/releasing.md` already records.
- **No downgrade guard.** `-version` installs any release, including an older
  one.
- **No check-only mode.** There is no `-check` that reports an available update
  without installing it.
- **`install.sh` and `update.go` duplicate the download/verify/place logic.** A
  shared package would remove the drift risk; today they are kept in step by a
  note in `AGENTS.md`.

body:
## What

**S5 · One review queue.** A single session now covers every due flashcard and every due vocabulary word, interleaved, following the Anki and Duolingo pattern of one study button.
- Open it from the new `▶ REVIEW n` chip on the TODAY panel, or from `/command.html#review`, which both study pages now link to.
- Controls: Space reveals the answer, 1–4 grades (AGAIN / HARD / GOOD / EASY), Esc closes.
- Each grade re-reads the store and saves that one item by id, so a page open in another tab is never overwritten with an old copy.
- Words reviewed here count toward the vocabulary page's stats and streak.

**One SM-2 scheduler (`omega-srs.js`).** The two pages each had their own copy of the scheduling algorithm, and the copies had drifted. Both pages and the queue now use the one module. Each bug below was confirmed by testing the previous version:
- **Flashcards: HARD acted like AGAIN.** HARD was mapped to quality 2, a failing grade, so a 6-day card went back to 1 day. GOOD was mapped to 3, which lowered the ease on every correct answer. The four buttons now map to 1 / 3 / 4 / 5.
- **Vocabulary: mastered words never came back for review.** The due drill and the library's DUE filter both excluded them.
- **Vocabulary: wrong SM-2 order.** It updated the ease before computing the interval. It now follows the original algorithm, like flashcards.
- **Vocabulary: unescaped text.** Terms, definitions, examples and etymology were inserted into the page as raw HTML. They are now escaped.

## Verification
- Every scheduling result in the browser test matched the SM-2 value worked out by hand:
  - HARD on a word at 6 days → 15 days, ease 2.36;
  - EASY on a mastered word at 30 days → 78 days, ease 2.70.
- The queue alternated card and word as intended.
- Injected HTML in a card rendered as plain text.
- The chip disappears when nothing is due.
- No overflow at 375px or 1280px, and 0 page errors.
- `verify-runtime` passes on command, flashcard and vocabulary.
- 435 unit tests pass (13 new in `test_review_queue.py`), and `ci-local.sh` passes 27 of 27 checks.

**Not changed:** in original SM-2, HARD, GOOD and EASY give the same next interval and differ only in the ease they leave behind. FSRS, the scheduler Anki now uses by default, is recorded as proposal S15 in `FEATURE_IDEAS.md`.

body:
Evaluate the one concrete benefit of moving to nightly: `std::simd` for
8-wide BVH nodes in safe, portable code. Done as an opt-in feature, not a
toolchain switch; stable stays the default and the only gate.

- bvh/: traversal, collapse and tests are written against a `LANES`
  constant. `lanes4.rs` (default, glam Vec4, stable) and `lanes8.rs`
  (`bvh8`, std::simd::f32x8) supply the lane type, RaySlab and slab test.
  forbid(unsafe_code) still holds.
- `bvh8` feature on crust-rt, forwarded by crust-core and crust-render.
  Stable rejects it with E0554.
- Non-blocking CI job on a pinned nightly (clippy + crust-rt tests).

Results:
- Images bit-identical to BVH4 (cornellbox, veach_mis, stress, 16 spp).
- Default path: -0.3% instructions (callgrind, ray_throughput).
- Kernel: BVH8 12-37% slower by min-of-10 (same nightly, x86-64-v3 both
  sides), even though node visits fall 7-36%: a 256-byte node and an
  8-lane sort cost more than the visits saved.
- End to end: within noise.

Verdict, recorded in docs/simd.md: not worth a nightly toolchain.

author: danbruder
body:
## Why

The goal is that someone can paste one prompt into a coding agent and get a verified deploy. Walking that path turned up several places where an agent (or a person) would get stuck or get the wrong answer:

- **`lh deploys --wait` reported the wrong deploy.** It waits on the newest deploy, and right after a `git push` that's still the *previous* one, so it returns the old result immediately. It was only correct for an app's first deploy.
- **A failed GitHub Actions build never registered a deploy**, so `--wait` sat until its 10-minute timeout.
- **There was no way to install `lh` on a laptop.** `install.sh` is server-only (root + domain), and releases shipped only Linux binaries.
- **Non-root users on Linux couldn't use the CLI.** The client config defaulted to `/opt/litehouse/config`.
- **The admin token leaked to stderr** through the `#[tracing::instrument]` on `ClientConfig::save`, which puts it in agent transcripts.
- **`lh connect` saved without checking anything**, and there was no env-var config for cloud/CI agents.
- **App names weren't validated.** `My_App` breaks the subdomain/TLS, and it also fails the backup's name safety check, so no backup day would ever be marked successful.

## Changes

**Deploy verification** (`src/deploy_wait.rs`, shared by the CLI and MCP)
- `lh deploys <app> --wait --sha <ref>` waits for that commit's deploy. `<ref>` can be a full or short sha, or a git ref like `HEAD`.
- With a GitHub token available, it also polls that commit's `litehouse-deploy.yml` run and exits 1 with the build-log URL as soon as the build fails.
- Exit codes are unchanged: 0, 1, 2. Without `--sha` the old behavior is kept.
- MCP `list_deploys` takes `sha` and returns an error result unless that deploy succeeded.

**Getting connected**
- `install-cli.sh`: installs only the CLI into `~/.local/bin`, verifies the checksum, and needs no root. Works on Linux and macOS.
- The release workflow now also builds `litehouse-darwin-{aarch64,x86_64}` (CLI only).
- `LITEHOUSE_URL` / `LITEHOUSE_TOKEN` override the client config through `ClientConfig::load_effective`. The overrides are never saved to disk.
- `lh connect` checks the URL and token against `/api/server/info` before saving, and `--token` defaults to `$LITEHOUSE_TOKEN`.
- The client config moves to `~/.config/litehouse/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). An existing legacy `/opt/litehouse/config/client-config.toml` still takes precedence, so root's `lh` on existing servers is unaffected.
- `ApiClient` now uses the token it was constructed with instead of re-reading the file on every request. This is what lets `connect` test a candidate token.

**Preflight**
- `lh doctor [--app] [--json]` checks the server connection, GitHub token scopes (`repo` + `workflow`, needed to commit the workflow; fine-grained tokens get a warning), the GitHub `origin`, the Dockerfile, and the port the final stage `EXPOSE`s.
- It exits 1 if anything blocks a deploy, and every failure includes its fix.

**Agent guide**
- `docs/agents.md` covers the rules, the app contract (`/data`, port, `LITEHOUSE_BLOB_PATH`, memory, env), the first-deploy and redeploy steps, and a table of failure meanings.
- It's compiled into the binary (`src/agent_guide.rs`) and exposed three ways: `lh agent-guide`, the MCP `agent_guide` tool, and a short `instructions` field in the MCP `initialize` response.

**Hardening**
- **Validation:** new app names must be DNS labels (1–63 chars, lowercase letters, digits, hyphens) and can't be the admin label.
- **Logging:**
  - `ClientConfig::save`/`ServerConfig::save` no longer log `self`.
  - Client commands default to `warn`; `serve`, `install` and `upgrade` stay at `info`.
- **Fixes:**
  - Fixed the stale `lh server s3-config set` hint.
  - `lh install` now points to `install-cli.sh`.

**Site**
- New "For agents" section: step 1 is you installing and connecting the CLI (so the token stays out of the agent's transcript), step 2 is a paste-in prompt, step 3 is the MCP line.
- Also adds `site/llms.txt` and nav/hero links.

**Docs / e2e**
- Updated README, CLAUDE.md, and the messaging doc.
- `acceptance.sh` waits on the pushed sha, and both e2e scripts retry `lh connect`, since it now verifies and the admin certificate can take a moment after install.

## Testing

- **New unit tests:** sha matching and target selection, the exit-code contract, and timeout messages (they never claim "no run found" unless GitHub was actually asked). Also run lookup, Dockerfile `EXPOSE` parsing, token-scope checks, `api_base_url` / env overrides, app-name validation, MCP `instructions`, and the `agent_guide` tool.
- **End-to-end wait tests** against a scripted HTTP server. The key one: the previous deploy has already succeeded, the new commit's deploy then appears and fails, and the wait reports the new failure, not the old success.
- **Against a local `lh serve`:**
  - `connect` rejects a bad URL or token without saving, and succeeds with a good one.
  - `doctor` reports both pass and fail cases, in text and `--json`.
  - A real MCP stdio handshake works with env-only config.
  - An invalid app name gets a 400.
  - `deploys --wait --sha` times out with exit 2 and an accurate hint.
- **`install-cli.sh`:** real download and install from the current release, plus the missing-release error path.
- **Landing page:** checked visually in light, dark, and mobile, with no horizontal overflow.
- **Full `cargo test`:** 251 passed, 4 failed. Three of the failures also fail on unmodified `main` in this sandbox (volume init permissions). The fourth is Docker Hub rate-limiting a pull (429); it passed on an earlier run.
- **Clippy:** 53 warnings, the same as `main`; none are new.

**Needs a release to verify:** the macOS release jobs (x86_64 is cross-built from the Apple Silicon runner) and `install-cli.sh` on macOS. The Rust code only uses `std::os::unix`, which compiles on macOS.

author: 1lck
body:
## 问题与修复

Windows 虽然已注册 Monaco 语义高亮 provider，但 `lsp_get_semantic_tokens` 被适配器列为不可用，客户端总是提前返回 null。现在映射到 Rust Core 已有的 `semanticTokens` 操作，复用现有语言服务器能力协商、图例解码、请求超时和取消路径。

Closes #675

## 功能点

- 接通 `lsp_get_semantic_tokens → lsp.request(operation: semanticTokens)`，客户端仅在会话 ready 且已协商该能力时请求；未支持时继续保留基础语法高亮。
- 转发 Core 的 `semanticTokensRefresh` 为前端刷新事件，当前窗口拥有该会话时通知 Monaco 重新请求颜色。
- 在语义请求前冲刷编辑器待发送的文档变更，避免防抖期间用旧文本的位置给新文本上色。
- 同步前后检查取消、模型版本、模型销毁、路径、文档打开状态和适用性；文件与会话的 attachment 被替换后丢弃旧响应。
- 复用共享 semantic-tokens fixture 和已有 Monaco 编码器，不新增 Rust 语义实现、依赖或资源下载；现有设置开关与大文件降级选项保持生效。
- 增加路由/客户端/provider 回归测试与 Windows CI 单测计时入口，覆盖图例转换、null、取消、刷新、能力缺失、归属替换和过期模型。
- 更新 LSP 归属笔记、契约的 Windows 转发说明，以及独立的语义高亮功能矩阵行和生成文档。两平台实机验证状态均保留 pending。

## 验证

Linux 服务器通过：

- `bun run typecheck`（windows/tauri）。
- `node .agents/skills/write-stable-tests/scripts/run-bun-tests-with-timing.mjs --suite-timeout-ms 60000 --report .artifacts/test-stability/windows-semantic-tokens.json -- src/platform/lsp-core-adapter.test.ts src/features/editor/lsp/lsp-client-semantic-tokens.test.ts src/features/editor/engines/monaco/semantic-token-provider.test.ts`：47 项通过，新增测试最慢 7 ms。
- `bun test src/platform/tauri-core.test.ts --timeout 15000`：4 项通过。
- Windows 测试稳定性静态检查、`verify-windows-boundaries.sh`、`verify-shared-contracts.sh`、`verify-agent-notes.sh`、`verify-platform-feature-matrix.sh`、`git diff --check`。
- HTML/JUnit 本地报告：`.artifacts/test-stability/index.html`、`windows-semantic-tokens.junit.xml`。

扩大验证 `bun test src/platform --timeout 15000` 为 78 通过 / 4 失败。临时恢复 preview 原版适配器、客户端和测试后重跑，为 75 通过 / 同样 4 失败；失败均在 tauri-core.test.ts，独立运行全部通过，属于原有合跑隔离问题，本 PR 不扩大修复范围。

当前没有 Windows 实机，未验证 WebView2/JDTLS 实际上色、原生构建和 PowerShell harness。Windows 验收步骤见功能矩阵：普通 Java 文件开启语义高亮，编辑/切换/关闭/重连及服务器 refresh 后确认颜色正确；关闭开关与大文件降级保留基础高亮。

不等待 CI，不自动合并。

author: claude
body:
When a long article or page was translated DE→EN, some blocks came back still in German. Separately, the AI SEO buttons in the EN editor produced German SEO text.

### Translation pipeline (`EditorJsTranslationPipeline`)
- **Root cause:** a segment that came back empty was silently replaced with the German source, and one returned unchanged was accepted as the translation. An incomplete or invalid batch response aborted the whole block.
- **Batch splitting:** if a batch response is incomplete or invalid, the batch is split in half and each half is retried, down to single segments. Only known payload/contract errors trigger this; other errors are still re-thrown. The match on those errors now uses `mb_strtolower`, so `Übersetzungs…` messages are recognised.
- **Retry of untranslated segments:** a segment that comes back empty or identical to the source is sent again on its own, once. Sources shorter than 20 characters or without letters (brand names, numbers, codes) are not treated as failures.
- **Remaining gap:** if the single retry also fails, the segment still falls back to the German source with no warning. Mixed blocks should become much rarer but can still happen.
- **Oversized segments:** a single segment may now be up to 8000 characters (was 2400) and is sent in its own batch. Longer segments are still rejected.
- **Quota:** every split or retry is an extra provider call and counts against the call quota through `QuotaAwareAiProvider`.

### SEO metadata (`SeoMetadataGenerationPipeline`)
- The locale was already passed to the server, but the prompt never told the model which language to write in.
- The payload now includes `output_language` (`English` / `German` / the locale code in upper case).
- A strict rule is added to the system prompt, including when a custom SEO template is configured in the AI settings: all generated text fields must be written only in that language.

body:
## Summary

This PR implements meeting agenda topics, boxed deferred action glyphs, and pixel-perfect font baseline alignment.

### 1. Agenda Topics Tokens (\o \, \. \, \, \)
- **Tokens**:
  - \o \: To Discuss / Open topic (renders circular outline \○\ with \--glyph-open-color\).
  - \. \: Discussed topic (renders fisheye circle with inner dot \◉\ in \--glyph-done-color\).
  - \, \: Not Discussed / Postponed topic (renders dashed circular outline \◌\ in \--glyph-progress-color\).
- **Strict Non-Action Invariant**: Topics are discussion items, not tasks. They are completely excluded from task counts, completion percentages, calendar heatmaps, and \F2\/\Shift+F2\ action jump navigation.
- **Smart Enter Continuation**:
  - Numbered topics: \o 1. First\ -> pressing Enter creates \o 2. \.
  - Bulleted topics: \o - Item\ -> pressing Enter creates \o - \.
  - Plain topics: \o Topic\ -> pressing Enter creates \o \.
  - Pressing Enter on an empty topic line cleanly exits the list.
- **Resolved Line Dimming**: Lines starting with discussed (\. \) or skipped (\, \) topics are dimmed with \--muted\ when unfocused, matching completed actions.

### 2. Boxed Deferred Glyph (Option 1)
- The deferred action glyph (\> \) previously rendered as a bare chevron \»\, visually mismatched with the boxed square glyphs \☐\, \☑\, and \☒\.
- It now renders with a matching box around a centered chevron (\☐\ containing a centered \›\), achieving visual parity with action checkboxes.

### 3. Pixel-Perfect Font Baseline Alignment
- Outer glyph containers use \	ransform: translateY(0)\ and dynamic line-height \calc(var(--editor-line-height, 1.6) * 1em)\.
- Topic glyph ink uses \	ransform: translateY(0.20em)\.
- The bottom edge of all action boxes (\☐\, \☑\, \☒\, \>\) and topic circles (\○\, \◉\, \◌\) sits directly on the font baseline (the bottom of lowercase letters like \d\), verified down to 0px across all supported line-height steps (.3$ to .8$).

### 4. Keyboard Shortcuts & UI Parity
- **Shortcuts**:
  - \Mod+5\: Set line/selection to To Discuss (\o\).
  - \Mod+6\: Set line/selection to Discussed (\.\).
  - \Mod+7\: Set line/selection to Not Discussed (\,\).
  - \Mod+Space\ / \Ctrl+Space\: Close item (\# -> v\, \o -> .\).
  - \Mod+Shift+Space\ / \Ctrl+Shift+Space\: Reopen item (\ -> #\, \./, -> o\).
- **Command Palette**: Added commands for setting line/selection to To Discuss, Discussed, and Not Discussed.
- **Shortcuts Modal**: Documented the new agenda topic tokens, glyphs, and shortcuts.
- **Mobile Accessory Bar**: Added quick-insert buttons for \○\, \◉\, and \◌\.
- **i18n**: Full translation coverage across English (\en\), German (\de\), and Dutch (\
l\).

author: wangi
body:
Half of item 4 built, and measurements saying the other half can't be built the way the spec described it.

## Fresh ground — done

The drawn mask belongs to the build and the fill is told not to reach outside it, so a contour drawn beyond the drawn envelope moves **nothing** in the preview — 0 of 25 cells. A mapper extending coverage sees nothing at all until a rebuild, and with the ten-second backstop that's ten seconds of a surface that looks broken. It asks for a rebuild immediately now.

**The test is the contour, not the patch, and that distinction is the whole of it.** The mask is the fill's reach *from* the contours rather than a solid blob, so it's full of holes an ordinary patch straddles:

| | |
|---|---|
| of each **patch** outside the mask, 12 gobras edits | 1.9% – 28.3% |
| of the moved **contour's own cells**, same 12 edits | **0.0%** |

As a trigger, the patch version fires on almost every edit and is worse than the timer it replaces.

## The second detector doesn't discriminate

It was to be: a preview whose solved box has unanswered ground touching its own boundary is one to distrust — F3's residual, and the classes are already computed for R20.

| reading | result |
|---|---|
| any unanswered cell on the boundary | flags 43–53% of the boundary on **every** edit, right and wrong alike |
| the connected region the edit lands in | flags 8 of 11 wrong previews **and the 1 right one** |

Neither is a detector.

## And the premise was the golden square's

*"Seventeen of twenty-one previews already right to 0.013 m"* is one sparse square. Repeated on the gobras 3×3, with the exact build re-adopted after each edit as the editor does:

> eleven of twelve previews are **0.085 m to 0.877 m** out; one is 0.003

Not accumulation — each measured on its own. Previews on a real working set are simply less exact than on that fixture.

That weakens the case for the ten-second backstop without overturning it: 0.877 m against a 25 m contour interval is nothing a hillshade shows, and F3 measured zero grey-level difference at 0.268 m. But the 0.013 m figure is quoted in three places and now carries the correction.

**What would detect the bad previews is not known. It is not the classes.** The spec says so rather than leaving a specified-but-unbuilt detector looking like remaining work.

Two tests, both falsified — including one that needed its fixture moved, because my first version placed the mask hole one column outside the patch and so wasn't testing the distinction at all.

446 passing, 216 with `osgeo` blocked.

author: pixnop
body:
Meant for beta.11, off the pre-release sweep against dev.

## Symptom

The sweep found the Author filter failing four times out of ten with "check your connection", even though ModDB was reachable the whole time. QUERY_URL routes every allow-listed API call through one 15s wall clock, and `/api/mods` and `/api/authors` are both several megabytes, uncompressed, with no Content-Length. At ordinary slow ModDB speed the transfer itself takes longer than 15s while bytes are still arriving throughout, so the wall clock cut it mid-flight.

## Measurement

A scratch script drove `requestBoundedText` (the same function QUERY_URL calls) against the real `https://mods.vintagestory.at/api/authors`, once, outside any test double. It took 16.6s to bring back 4,223,116 bytes: already past the old 15s ceiling on an otherwise healthy connection, which is what the sweep's 4-in-10 failure rate was catching.

## Fix

`requestBoundedBuffer` (src/ipc/network.ts) now runs two timers instead of one: an inactivity window, reset on every chunk received, that still cuts a connection after 15s of silence, and the overall wall-clock ceiling every caller already had. A `UrlRule` can widen that overall ceiling on its own now (src/ipc/validation.ts's new `timeoutMs`, read back by `getApiUrlTimeoutMs`), the same way `maxBytes` already widens the byte cap. The mods/authors rule does, to 90s, six times the generic timeout, in step with how far its existing 16 MiB byte cap already sits above the generic 4 MiB one. `queryUrl` (netHandlers.ts) now passes that resolved timeout alongside the byte ceiling it already passed.

Every other endpoint keeps its 15s ceiling exactly as it was: both timers still default to that same 15s there, so the overall timer fires first regardless of activity, same as before this change. `requestBoundedTextViaNode` (the login transport) is untouched; nothing on that path answers with a large, slow-trickling body.

## Tests

`tests/ipc/moddb-slow-transfer-timeout.test.ts` drives `queryUrl` against a fake `net.request` that trickles a chunked body on a schedule vi's fake timers control:

- a transfer that stays under 90s with no gap past 15s resolves for `/api/authors`
- one that goes quiet for 15s is rejected once the inactivity window elapses, well before the 90s ceiling
- an ordinary endpoint (`/api/tags`) still fails at 15s even though no single gap in that same slow response would have tripped the inactivity window on its own

`tests/ipc/api-url-ceiling.test.ts` gets a matching unit test for `getApiUrlTimeoutMs`. The full existing suite (`network.test.ts`, `networkProxy.test.ts`, `netHandlersDispatch.test.ts`, `mod-catalog-cache.test.ts`, `fetchReleaseNotes.test.ts`, `moddbListingArchive.test.ts`) passes unchanged.

author: mateusvillain
body:
Closes #116

## Resumo

- Traço com `tool` = marca-texto é desenhado com **16 unidades** de espessura e **opacidade 0,35** (`HIGHLIGHTER_WIDTH` em `stroke-geometry.ts`, `HIGHLIGHTER_OPACITY` em `Strokes.tsx`). São valores de partida, ajustáveis na revisão.
- A opacidade fica no `<polyline>` inteiro, não na cor. Com isso, o ponto em que um marca-texto cruza a si mesmo não escurece, enquanto dois marca-textos diferentes sobrepostos escurecem.
- Dentro da camada de tinta, o marca-texto é pintado **antes** de todos os outros traços, qualquer que seja o `z`, e entre marca-textos o `z` continua valendo. Os post-its já ficavam por cima da camada inteira.
- `STROKE_WIDTH` saiu de `Strokes.tsx` e foi para `stroke-geometry.ts`, junto com `strokeInkWidth(tool)`. A espessura passa a ter leitores geométricos: o alvo de clique e a borracha da #118.
- A prévia do gesto (`StrokePreview`) aceita `tool` e pinta com a mesma espessura e opacidade. O `Viewport` ganha `drawingTool`. Com o marca-texto, a prévia é desenhada **dentro da camada de tinta**, entre os marca-textos existentes e o resto dos traços, que é a altura em que o traço vai ficar ao soltar.
  - O `Viewport` entrega a prévia por contexto (`HighlighterPreviewContext`), e só o slot que a lê re-renderiza a cada movimento, não a pilha inteira. O Provider fica sempre montado, para não remontar o board ao trocar de ferramenta.
- O teste de atalhos nas dicas (`tooltips-i18n.test.tsx`) ganhou um timeout explícito de 20 s. Ele levava ~3,5 s sozinho, mas beirava os 5 s padrão no suíte paralelo e falhava de vez em quando.
- O lápis não muda. A caneta tinteiro continua saindo como lápis até a #113.

Ainda não há como desenhar com o marca-texto pela interface; o modo e o atalho H chegam na #117 (PR empilhada sobre esta).

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run`: 1094 testes. Casos novos:
  - espessura e opacidade do marca-texto;
  - lápis inalterado;
  - caneta ainda como lápis;
  - opacidade no elemento, não na cor;
  - ordem com `z` misto;
  - ordem entre marca-textos;
  - prévia com o estilo do marca-texto;
  - altura da prévia no `Viewport`: lápis por cima de toda a tinta; marca-texto sobre os destaques e sob os rabiscos, com uma prévia só.
- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npx eslint src`
- [ ] Conferência visual em tema claro e escuro, nas sete cores. Só dá para testar pela interface depois da #117.

## Pendências conhecidas (fora do escopo)

- Durante um redimensionamento, a escala não uniforme do `<g>` estica a espessura da tinta num eixo, que volta ao normal ao soltar. O efeito já existia no lápis, mas lá era imperceptível; com 16 unidades ele aparece.
- A moldura de seleção usa só os pontos e corta a tinta larga do marca-texto. Fica para a #118 (seleção pela largura).

author: int19h
body:
Closes #128.

The deploy rebuilt every published version on each run. The 1.3.5 deploy took about 5 hours 40 minutes for four versions. The Actions cache for the versions did not help: its key covered the whole version list, and GitHub drops unused entries after seven days.

## What the deploy does now

`scripts/build-versions.sh` replaces the cache step and the build loop of the workflow. It follows the maintainer's policy:

- A published version serves the book files of its release, unchanged. The HTML (`xhtml_section_chunks`, `xhtml_no_chunks`) comes from `cll-<version>-html.tar.gz` on the release, and `cll.pdf` and `cll.epub` come from the release's own assets. A published release that lacks any of these three files stops the run.
- For a published version, only the comparison pages (`diff_from_*`) and the landing page are made again, with the current tooling. For this, `scripts/build-site.sh` gets a `DIFFS_ONLY` mode. So the diff pages can improve while the book files stay equal to the release.
- A version without a published release is built from source, as before.
- The deploy never changes a published release.

## Draft releases and the release procedure

A draft release `v<version>` gets the HTML archive, the PDF, and the ePub of each run. So the release procedure changes:

1. Create the release as a draft, with its notes.
2. Add the version to `pages/versions.tsv`. The deploy attaches the files to the draft.
3. Check the draft, and publish it.

## The build cache

The result for each version is cached as `cll-<version>-html.tar.gz` in a draft release named `site-build-cache`. If this draft is missing, the deploy creates it. If the release is no longer a draft, the deploy stops. Drafts are not public, so the deploy replaces the cache freely: a failed upload costs at most one rebuild.

The deploy uses a cache entry only if its `BUILD-INFO` matches this run in all fields. It records the version's commit, the sha256 of `scripts/build-site.sh`, the previous version's commit, and the baseline commit. For a published version, it also records the names and sha256 digests of the release files that it serves.

The `workflow_dispatch` input `force_rebuild` ignores the cache. Unpublished versions then build from source, and published versions rebuild their diffs. Published releases stay as they are.

Every download and unpack checks its own result, and any error of the GitHub API fails the run. The job needs `contents: write`.

## One-time correction of v1.3.2

v1.3.2 was released before the book had a PDF and an ePub. Its release now also carries the `cll.pdf` and `cll.epub` that the site serves for 1.3.2 ("Version colojban-1.3.2"). They were built in the 1.3.5 deploy (run 36278151590). Nothing that the release had before changed. The HTML archives on v1.3.2 to v1.3.5 come from the same run.

## Tests

- Run 36322116489, of the first version of this PR, restored all four versions from their releases in 7.5 minutes.
- Run 36330370148 tests head ecfcd329: it serves the four published versions from their releases, rebuilds only their diffs, and fills the cache. It started before the v1.3.2 correction.
- The deploy jobs of branch runs fail by design, because the `github-pages` environment allows only the `pages` and `docbook-prince` branches.

body:
## Summary

Adds the Claude Code agent arm. skillc can now install a declared skill collection into Claude Code's own skills directory in the trial container. It runs one real Claude Code agent per collection on the Level 1 slug-fix task, through the same contract and grader #11's Codex runs used, and records the evidence with its limits.

- **`materialize.SURFACES`** declares two surfaces, each bound to one client and one install dir: `codex-skills` → codex, `~/.codex/skills/`; `claude-code-skills` → claude, `~/.claude/skills/`. A surface/client mismatch is refused by name. There is no subject-name branch; the #94 genericity guard stays green.
- **Discovery, stated honestly.** Claude Code has no model-free listing, so discovery is read from the real agent transcript's `skill_listing` attachment (`transcript_adapter.claude_code_skill_listing` → `observation.skills_listed`). It is reported `listed`/`not-listed` and labelled `source=transcript skill_listing`. It is `UNMEASURED` with a reason when no complete initial listing was readable, and that includes every codex run. `collection-run` exits 1 on a measured `not-listed`, even after a PASS. `demo --subject` reports Claude discovery NOT EXERCISED, and the host `skillc materialize` refuses a Claude subject.
- **`collection-run`** takes its client and default argv from the subject: claude runs `claude -p --dangerously-skip-permissions` as the non-root trial user.
- **New subjects:** `cpp-claude-code` (CPP's native `.claude/skills`, 18 skills, same pin) and `mattpocock-skills-claude-code` (`tdd`, `diagnosing-bugs`, both model-invoked; the 14 `disable-model-invocation` skills are reported incompatible before selection).
- **Fixed, found on the live run:** the paste-back read `refresh_observed_in_container`, but the record key is `credential_refresh_observed_in_container`, so it printed `None` on every run, #11's included. The regression test was red on the old key.
- **Folded into the issue during the run** (owner edit, from the Nit Store): `find_client` now searches PATH for a bare `--client` name (red on the old code). #11's evidence is annotated for the refresh key bug, with the verbatim blocks untouched, and #98's accounting relied on it; correction posted: https://github.com/cooneycw/skillc/issues/98#issuecomment-5856264322

## Live evidence (`evals/claude-code-agent-arm/`)

Claude Code 2.1.283 in `skillc-trial:latest` (`sha256:d1b2ced9…`), on the operator's normal Claude subscription login (ADR 0005 rule 6):

|---|---|

| `collection-run cpp-claude-code` | captured, 18/18 listed, graded PASS, EXIT=0 |

| #98 transfer: host `claude -p` after the trials (13:08:54Z) | `OK`, EXIT=0; `refresh_observed_in_container=False` in both captured records |

`tests/test_claude_code_agent_arm.py` fails if a cited line is not in its own collection's block. Its negative controls cover a borrowed line, an empty or partial discovery map, and a control that exits 0 or belongs to another subject.

## Red cases (ADR 0001)

- A skill whose files are withheld from the container → `not-listed`, exit 1 (`test_a_skill_that_was_not_installed_turns_discovery_red`, `test_cmd_collection_run_exit_follows_measured_discovery`).
- An installed skill the listing omits → `not-listed`.
- No listing, a delta-only listing, or an unreadable attachment → UNMEASURED, never an absence. The delta and unreadable cases were shown red on the pre-fix code.
- Surface/client mismatch → refused. A claude subject lands under `.claude/skills/`.

| REPLACE-FIRST | 72 | 49k | guards a REAL invariant only textually — behavioral home lands first, then it dies |
| MERGE | 60 | 14k | folds into a named sibling (e.g. 3 append-only-id evals → 1; ~65 ADRs → `docs/DECISIONS.md` entries) |

**How it was built:** mechanical inventories → two-key classification (independent classifier + verifier per batch; neither sees the other's reasoning; 79% path-level agreement) → 89 mismatches settled by adversarial arbiters with fresh evidence → an adversarial false-negative hunt over all 83 risk:high destructive rows both keys agreed on (**0 unsound**, 30 rows gained explicit preconditions — chiefly: `native_host_tests.rs` must gain insert/update, a settable sender, and a `database_identity` stub before the privacy/economy replacement tests are buildable; that is now a Phase-2 entry task).

## 18 suspected bugs found along the way (`kind:bug` rows; fixes are Phase 3, test-first, adjudicated against the original specs)

Gameplay-visible:
- **`inventory` table is world-readable** — declared `public` with an unfiltered client subscription; every player receives every other player's item counts, contradicting the original owner-private intent. (The later `monster_pub`/`my_battle` privacy pattern was never applied to it.)
- **Practice-XP predicate drift** — docs say practice = "opponent is not wild"; code uses `player == opponent`, so PvP wins appear to grant full XP.
- **"To Party" with a full party is a silent no-op** — client sends slot 255 and nothing happens, no feedback.
- **Auto-evolution forecloses branches** — the lowest-level evolution edge wins the race and shuts out sibling branches, contradicting care-dependent branching in the design doc; one species also spawns wild above its own evolution gate.
- **`heal_party` owner check is tautological** — `require_owner(ctx, "heal_party", me)` where `me = ctx.sender()` always passes (benign today because the lookup is sender-scoped, but the guard guards nothing).
- **Evolution eligibility is re-implemented in TS** (`evolutionModel.ts`) against the original "rules live in game-core only" decision — drift risk; the plan replaces the text-parity guard with an executable wasm-parity test.

Stale-label / doc-truth class (fix = correct the doc/label): reduced-motion "KNOWN DEFECT" title is stale (defect was fixed; the title survives only because a gate pins it byte-for-byte), PLAYTEST.md still says "no accounts yet", the ADR digest still calls the battle table public, a dead `shouldToggleBox` guard is still documented as live, plus a predictor outstanding-count undercount pinned as current behavior, an a11y token-length contradiction, a missing promised migration smoke check, a content-version `--update` flag the eval advertises but doesn't implement, and `client-test` missing its `wasm` dependency in the justfile.

## Policy calls to ratify (or veto) with this review

1. **Drop semgrep + SBOM from CI** (keep gitleaks, cargo-audit, dependency-review).
2. **Coverage gating → report-only** (the 96% ratchet incentivizes assertion-stuffing).
3. **Drop the changelog-freshness nightly** (regenerate via git-cliff on demand).
4. **Plan divergence, decided on ground-truth evidence:** the plan draft said keep the `i18n-export`/`i18n-import` recipes; arbitration found the original M24 spec explicitly puts TMS vendor interchange **out of scope**, so they are DELETE (the i18n *feature* — catalogs, lint, completion data — stays).
5. `a11y-e2e` nightly recipe DELETE: plain `just e2e` already runs the full a11y + reduced-motion Playwright projects per PR; the recipe added only count-floors on other checks.
6. One **user-review flag**: `docs/research/SEED-DOMAINS.md` is operator-provided (cited by harness memory) — kept for now; relocate it yourself if you want it out of the repo, the program won't write outside the project.

## How to review

- Skim `DELETE` rows with `risk:high` (`jq 'select(.disposition=="DELETE" and .risk=="high")' docs/debloat/ledger.ndjson`) — each has an adjudication answering "what breaks if the claimed invariant is false".
- `REPLACE-FIRST` rows name their behavioral `new_home`; rows with `fn_verdict:"NEEDS-CONDITION"` carry the precondition in `condition`.
- The EXTRACT per-test splits are in `docs/debloat/worksheets/` (README explains which key governs).
- `node docs/debloat/check-ledger.mjs` re-validates everything.

Approving/merging this PR releases Phase 2 (Commit A severs the gate-of-gates loop, then batched deletions per this ledger, production source bit-identical throughout).

author: fatal10110
body:
## Summary

**#93: an uncaught `error('ERR x', 0)` lost its leading `ERR`**
- `src/codec.ts` `stringScriptError` no longer strips a leading `ERR `. A string script error (or any script error in the `redis-6.2` model) is `{ code: "ERR", err: <whole message> }`, so `error('ERR x', 0)` → `err: "ERR x"`. The host writes `-ERR ERR x` like Redis 7.0+ / Valkey, and Redis 6.2 keeps `ERR x` too.
- The strip was hiding the engine's own `ERR ...` string errors. They now go through the profile's error path (`raise_api_error`): an `{err='ERR ...'}` table in the Redis 7 model (flagged `SCRIPT_ERROR_FROM_TABLE`), a bare string in Redis 6.2's. Sites converted:
  - `wasm/src/redis_api.c`: `reached lua stack limit` (host reply decode depth), every `reply decoding failed`, `unknown reply type`, `empty reply from host` (was `ERR ...` in both models), `host callback failed` (was a plain `ERR ...` string in both models), `sha1hex failed`.
  - `wasm/src/runtime.c`: the fuel kill (`Script killed by fuel limit` bare in the 6.2 model, like Redis 6.2's `luaMaskCountHook`; `ERR`-coded table in the Redis 7 model as before), the `unknown error` fallback for an error table with no string `err` (bare in the 6.2 model), and the unreachable `script load failed` / `script execution failed` fallbacks.
  - Left unchanged: the `REPLY_ERROR` (non-script-error) replies (`ERR reached lua stack limit` for a too-deep return value, `ERR Lua VM not initialized`, ...). They are split by code and never went through the strip.
- In the `redis-6.2` model, a host command error that `redis.call` raises as a string now keeps its code in the message (`ERR unknown command` → `err: "ERR unknown command"`). Redis 6.2 does the same: its `luaRaiseError` raises the reply text as it is, and the error handler only prefixes the position.

**#95: `redis.sha1hex` arity**
- `l_redis_sha1hex` raises `wrong number of arguments` when `lua_gettop(L) != 1`, through the profile's error path. The Redis 7 model raises `{err='ERR wrong number of arguments'}`. The `redis-6.2` model raises the plain string with no `user_script:N:` position. This is ported from `luaRedisSha1hexCommand` in Valkey 8.0 (BSD) and Redis 6.2. A single argument is still read with `luaL_checklstring`.

Docs: `docs/errors.md`, `docs/compat.md` and `docs/abi.md`. The wire format is unchanged; `abi.md` only rewords how the host reads a flag-less script error and the text raised for a `{0,0}` host import result. `CHANGELOG.md` has new Unreleased entries.

Closes #93
Closes #95

## Tests

New tests in `test/error-model.test.ts` run on `redis-6.2`, `redis-7.0`, `redis-8.0` and `valkey-9.0`:
- #93: `error('ERR x',0)`, `error('x',0)` and `error('WRONGTYPE x',0)` check code and err. `pcall(error,'ERR x',0)` still returns `ERR x`.
- #95: `redis.sha1hex()` and `redis.sha1hex('a','b')` fail uncaught. `pcall(redis.sha1hex)` returns `ERR wrong number of arguments`, or `wrong number of arguments` on 6.2. The xpcall error type is checked. One argument, string or number, still hashes.
- Engine errors are never `ERR ERR`: a too-deep host reply (both uncaught and caught), `error({})`, the fuel kill, and the `redis.setresp` / `redis.log` errors.

`test/host-boundary.test.ts`: the heap-exhaustion test now runs on the default and `redis-6.2` profiles. It checks the exact code and message for `empty reply from host`, `host callback failed` and `sha1hex failed`, uncaught and caught.

Existing tests updated for the new behavior: a script's own `ERR` is kept, and 6.2 host errors are kept whole.

- `npm run build`: ok
- `npm run test:skip-wasm`: 473 tests, 473 pass, 0 fail
- `npm run smoke`: all 6 native smoke binaries OK
- `tsc --noEmit`: ok

## What changes

Collection logging tests now use the same card catalog view as DeckPal, so they check real logging behavior again. Deck-E also gives each approved collection change a stable write key: sending the same approval back after a short delay returns the first result without adding the cards twice.

## Why it matters

The Pocket filtering change left 13 logging tests failing on main even though ordinary cards should still log correctly. A separate test caught a real edge case: if an approval and its replay crossed a 15-minute boundary, the same change could be applied twice.

## How we know it works

- The 13 failing logging tests now pass with their original assertions; all 243 agent-tools tests pass.

## What could go wrong

A repeated approval must still be recognized when it arrives later. The write key uses the conversation, the approved call, and its signed input; a separate call gets a separate key. The Pocket browsing rule and the signed approval input remain unchanged. The key excludes conversation metadata that the approval does not sign.

Nothing, just merge after checks pass. No migration or setting change.

body:
Package G2 of the local backend roadmap ([spec](docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-27-local-backend-completion-design.md) §5, [plan](docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-27-local-backend-g2-chunked-batches.md)).

## What changes

- `lib/core/database/id_chunks.dart`: `idChunks(ids, {size = sqliteIdChunk})` splits an id set into chunks of 30 000, under SQLite's 32 766 bind limit.
- Every batch read or write over a caller-sized id set runs per chunk:
  - `CardDao`: `liveRows`, `deckRows`, `exportRows` (chunks re-sorted by `created_at`, then `id`, BR-TRANSFER-010), `rootIdsOf`, `moveCards`, `setFlagged`.
  - `TagDao`: `liveCardCount` (summed), `cardsCarrying` (union), `tagCounts` (per-card maps joined), `unlink`.
  - `TrashDao.purgeCandidates`: chunked reads merged by id, ordered by `deleted_at`, then `id`.
  - `CardListDao.tagsOf` (an export's tag read; found by the final review).
- Records:
  - WBS BE-C2 is `xong`.
  - BE-C1 is `cắt`: the owner chose to keep the current order. The legend gains the `cắt` status.
  - The two blocker rows are removed.

## Rulings

- **Task 2:** the limit test sets both sub-decks to `content_type = 'card'` before seeding cards. Cost if wrong: none, since the repository's rules are unchanged.
- **Task 3:** `tagCounts` counts the tags of each card, not the cards of each tag. The chunks are disjoint by card id, so their maps are joined, not summed. Cost if wrong: none.
- **Task 4:** the WBS legend's "Hoãn hoặc cắt" rule keeps a row and changes its status, so BE-C1 reads `cắt`. The plan's own relative link was also fixed. Cost if wrong: one word.
- **Final review:** the tag filter's `tagIds`, a study session's cards and the lapse actions stay unchunked. Cost if wrong: a bind-limit error on a filter over more than 30 000 tags.

**Final review fix:** `CardListDao.tagsOf` was unchunked, so an export of more than 32 766 cards failed. The new test "a whole-deck and a selected export of more cards than SQLite binds carry every card with its tags" went RED, then GREEN.

**Deferred minor:** `cardsCarrying`, `tagCounts` and `rootIdsOf` build their result with `await` inside nested collection-for loops. That is denser than the accumulator loop that `liveCardCount` uses.

## Verification

Run on the head, after merging `origin/master` (#113, #115) and regenerating l10n and build_runner output:

- `dod_check.sh`: generated code, format, analyze, guard, architecture and docs (0 errors, 45 warnings) all pass; 2429 tests pass.
- `TZ=UTC flutter test --tags golden`: 351 pass.
- The limit tests in `test/features/{card,tags,trash}/data/*_batch_limit_test.dart` seed 33 000 rows through a recursive CTE.

author: blackn-l
body:
`minWidth` and `maxWidth` are documented as numeric-only, but their types currently accept strings and allow percentage constraints that Yoga resolves against the wrong ancestor. This narrows both properties to `number` and removes their explicit percentage conversion branches, while preserving percentage support for the other dimensions.

The existing `test.failing` layout cases remain as checks for a future Yoga fix. A compiler-backed AVA test verifies that both JSX and the exported `BoxProps` reject percentage width constraints, while numeric values, omitted constraints, and supported percentage dimensions still compile. Restoring the original types makes all four negative type assertions fail.

Compatibility: TypeScript callers passing strings to these two properties will now receive an error, matching the documented API. This does not fix Yoga's percentage layout behavior or add runtime validation for JavaScript callers.

Validation:
- `npm run typecheck` passed.
- XO and Prettier passed for all five changed files. Full-repository XO reported 65 project-service parsing errors in unchanged configuration, example, media, and benchmark files.
- Targeted AVA suite: 45 passed, 2 existing expected failures.

body:
Fills `modelo130.lines`, `modelo303.lines` and `modelo349` in `2025.example.json` and `2026.json` from the orders that approve each form, so a future form mapper places figures by semantic key instead of hard-coded casilla numbers. Only what SPEC-003 computes for this profile is mapped (Profesional with EU B2B and US clients).

**Sources** (read on boe.es and the AEAT sede, 2026-09-27; each map has `boe` provenance):
- Modelo 130: Orden EHA/672/2007 anexo I, replaced by Orden HAP/258/2015, and the AEAT instructions. Casillas 01–07, 12–17 and 19. 08–11 are agrarian and 18 is complementaria, so neither is mapped.
- Modelo 303: Orden EHA/3786/2008 anexo I, in the design of Orden HAC/819/2024 for 2025 and 1T 2026 and of Orden HAC/27/2026 from 2T 2026, plus the AEAT 2025/2026 instructions. The map covers:
  - devengado 01–13 and 27, including 12/13, reverse charge on services bought from outside the EU (LIVA art. 84.Uno.2.º)
  - deducible 28/29, 36/37 and 45
  - results 46, 59, 120, 64, 65, 66, 110, 78, 87, 69, 71, 72 and 73

  Page 4 is not mapped, because this profile files the 390.
- Modelo 349: Orden EHA/769/2010 art. 2.d, art. 10 (in the wording of HAC/174/2020) and the anexo (in the wording of HAC/1274/2020):
  - claves S (services supplied) and I (services acquired)
  - tipo-2 record field positions
  - `quarterlyFilingCap` 50,000 € per quarter. This replaces the old `periodThresholdEurPerYear: null`, which had the wrong period.

**Shape and rules.** Each map goes from a semantic key to a casilla. A declared gap is `lines: { "_todo": ... }`, and a `_todo` beside filled lines is rejected. C# rules check four things: a casilla appears once per form, a clave appears once, 349 positions run forward without overlap, and every filled map has provenance. Each rule was broken once to confirm its mutation test fails, including the three added here (a 303 `_todo` beside lines, a missing 303 12/13 entry, a missing 349 field).

**Validation only.** Nothing in C# reads the maps yet, so there are no parser or `TaxYearConfig` types. They would be dead code until the form mappers exist.

**SPEC-003 corrections** from the sources:
- Services to US clients go in casilla 120 (not subject by location rules), not an "exentas" line.
- The 349 also needs clave I for services bought from EU suppliers.
- Reverse charge on non-EU services goes in 12/13.

body:
## Summary

Repo prose (`src/**` comments and `ui/README.md`) cited "the instrument that proves the other half" by file name — jsdom probes, Python compile gates, edit sheets. Those instruments live outside the repository and never entered it (there is no JS runner in CI), so every such citation is a dead link for every reader.

The repo had already written the convention down — `state_gate.rs`'s R165 block says *"the instrument lives outside the repo, so no file name here (#606)"* — but nothing enforced it. Recon measured **62 occurrences** violating it, one of them in that same file, three lines after that very sentence.

This PR keeps the statement and drops the file name at all 62 sites, and adds `src/citation_gate.rs` so the rule has an enforcer.

## Related Issue

No issue was open; this came out of repository recon.

## Changes

- [x] 62 prose sites stop naming out-of-repo instruments — `src/state_gate.rs` 42, `ui/README.md` 17, `src/i18n_pack.rs` 2, `ui/js/app.js` 1. The surrounding sentence is preserved; exactly one line changes per site (62 insertions / 62 deletions).
- [x] New gate `src/citation_gate.rs` (test-only, registered as `#[cfg(test)] mod citation_gate;`). Corpus = the repo's text files, walked at runtime from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` so new files enter scope automatically; for `.rs` only the comment text is scanned (the citation sites live in comments, while this gate's own synthetic fixtures live in string literals). Site = a backticked, file-shaped token; verdict = basename matches the session-instrument naming (`^[rc][0-9]+[-_]`) **and** no file of that name exists.
- [x] `ui/README.md` records the convention (new section) together with its exact scope.
- [x] `ui/js/app.js` was touched, so its cache-bust token was bumped: `app.js?v=20260927-1` → `-2`.

## Tests

- [x] `cargo test` — **413 passed / 0 failed** (baseline 409; +4 new tests)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — rc=0
- [x] `clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — rc=0
- [x] New tests — four: the rule itself; a **positive control** asserting the corpus really contains ≥200 backticked file-shaped tokens (so "0 violations" cannot be confused with a blind scanner); a synthetic **teeth** set (comment citation → flagged, string literal → not, present file → not, runtime path → not by declared scope, Markdown → flagged); and the naming predicate's precision (no real repo file name is caught).

**A/B on the live tree**: injecting one citation into a `.rs` comment and one into `ui/README.md` makes the rule fail, naming both `file:line` locations, while the other three tests stay green.

## Scope (stated honestly)

The predicate is *naming shape + presence*, not "any out-of-repo reference". It deliberately does not flag runtime artefacts (`<data>/config.toml`), negated statements ("the repo has no `ui/package.json`"), historical changelog entries ("Removed `data/models.example.json`") or output-file placeholders (`aitokenpool-transactions-YYYYMMDD.csv`) — those are either runtime facts or true precisely because the file does not exist.

## Checklist

- [x] 分支命名符合约定（`fix/<描述>`）
- [x] Commit message 使用 Conventional Commits 格式
- [x] 单一职责，改动最小化

author: miroslav-jokovic
body:
APPLICATION-FLOW-V2-PLAN.md §6.6.4, AW5. C3b is split in two (recorded in §12). This is **C3b1**, the barcode. **C3b2** is AW4: the wizard, browser metrics, the upload fallback, the desktop QR, the `captureMode` label, and the server confirm. It follows off `main`.

## What it does
- **`parseAamvaBarcode`** (`packages/shared`, pure) reads the header, subfile designators and Table D.3/D.4 elements. It fills licence no., DOB, expiry, address, and the issuing state from the IIN. Every field is optional. Anything that is not an AAMVA card barcode returns `null`.
- **Sources committed, not remembered:** `docs/plans/recruitment/aamva/` holds Annex D §D.12–§D.13 of the AAMVA 2020 standard (PDF pinned by sha256) and AAMVA's IIN table. The web test reads §D.13's own example byte for byte against its header's offsets. It also checks every element ID against Tables D.3/D.4 and the IIN table row for row.
- **Found in the sources:** the extracted §D.13 example came out one byte short, because `DAK` is F11 and the text layer collapsed its padding. Padded to its fixed width, both header offsets match exactly. AAMVA lists Colorado as `GM`, so the issuing state is derived by *name* through `jurisdictions.ts`.
- **`readLicenceBarcode`** (web) loads `zxing-wasm/reader` 3.1.4 through a dynamic `import()` and reads PDF417 only, in `Plain` text mode. The default `HRI` mode loses the separators; the real-barcode test failed with it. The 931 KiB binary is served from our own origin, not jsDelivr. It decodes the **original** photo, not the 1568-px upload. It never throws.
- **Bundle:** `ApplyPage` is 39.6 KiB gzipped. The reader chunk (12.3 KiB gz) and the wasm (416 KiB gz) are reachable only through the dynamic import.
- **CSP:** `script-src` gains `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`. It allows WebAssembly compilation only: no `eval`, no new origin. Pinned in `appHttp.test.ts`.
- **Prefill:** it fills only blank boxes. The address and the current licence fill as whole blocks or not at all. It runs only while Part 1 is unbegun, so a begun link never downloads the decoder. The date of birth is fill-only after it is written. Each prefilled screen says so. The first write's order (answers → licences → DOB) is unchanged.
- **Q-AW31 (new, default built):** the CDL's two photos now come *first*. It is the only order in which §6.2's own "prefilled from the barcode" can fill anything. Changing one array (`PART_ONE_SCREENS`) reverts it.
- **CPU per photo measured** before any server gate is built (§10, §12): 34.7 ms median for a web upload, 78.9 ms for a raw 12 MP JPEG.

## Not built, named in §12
The name (Part 1 has no name box), and class and endorsements (`DCA`/`DCD` hold jurisdiction-specific codes).

## Checks
All 32 `ci.yml` lint gates, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `lint:secrets` (run again after the commit), and the shared, ui, web, api and `test:rls` suites pass, as does the full build. **25 mutants, all killed**, plus one extra for the rewritten separator split.

author: sebauf
body:
## Symptôme

La tâche `purge`, tout juste ajoutée au DAG, échoue au lancement en production alors que l'image publiée est correcte.

## Cause

`_build_k8s_task` ne réglait pas `image_pull_policy` : Kubernetes retombe alors sur `IfNotPresent`. Les images `scrapper` et `pipeline` portent le tag **mobile** `main`, réécrit à chaque push sur `main` — le nœud garde donc la couche déjà téléchargée et rejoue l'image de la veille, indéfiniment.

Tant que les étapes du DAG ne changeaient pas, le symptôme restait discret : du code publié qui met un jour à s'exécuter. `purge` l'a rendu franc, puisque le DAG appelle un module (`src.maintenance.purge_dead_products`) qui n'existe pas dans l'image en cache.

Vérifié côté registre pour écarter l'autre hypothèse : `ghcr.io/sebauf/item_scrapper-pipeline:main` contient bien `src/maintenance/` et le module s'importe (`PURGE_AFTER_DAYS = 15`). Les deux images ont été publiées à 09:14:43, le run manuel a démarré à 09:17:22 — le registre était à jour, le nœud non.

## Correctif

`image_pull_policy="Always"` sur les Pods éphémères, soit la même politique que tous les Deployments de `k8s/base`.

`k8s/README.md` annonçait déjà ce comportement (« récupèrent toujours la dernière image `main` (`imagePullPolicy: Always`) ») : la doc décrivait une intention que le code n'appliquait pas. Elle dit maintenant où le réglage vit, et sa liste de tâches suit le DAG (`train` avait disparu, `purge` est arrivée).

## Après merge

Attendre la republication de l'image `airflow` (elle embarque les DAGs), puis :

```bash
kubectl -n price-tracker rollout restart deployment airflow-scheduler
```

Le prochain run prendra l'image `pipeline:main` fraîche.

## Reste à traiter, hors périmètre

L'erreur visible dans l'UI n'était pas celle de la tâche mais un échec de lecture du log (`Could not read served logs: ... Failed to resolve 'airflow-scheduler-<pod>'`) : le webserver cherche le log sur le pod scheduler par son nom d'hôte, que le DNS du cluster ne résout pas. Le vrai message reste donc invisible depuis l'UI. À corriger séparément (Service headless + `hostname`/`subdomain` sur le scheduler, ou logging distant).

author: bobleer
body:
## Summary

Remote workspace transfers no longer inherit one 30s frontend request deadline, and both providers (SFTP and container) now stream, stage, and publish the same way.

Root cause of the reported failure: the shared `ApiClient` applied its default 30s deadline to every Tauri command, including `remote_download_to_local_path` / `remote_upload_from_local_path`. A slow-but-healthy transfer was aborted client-side with `Request timeout` while the host kept transferring, and the progress listener was torn down at the same moment, so the UI reported a failure for a transfer that could still complete. The same single deadline also hid whole-file buffering on both sides, an inconsistent cancel path, and a stop action that never reached drag-and-drop uploads.

No upstream issue: this was reported directly against 1.0.2 behaviour ("文件传输失败：Error: Request timeout" while receiving files from a remote workspace).

## Type and Areas

Type: bug fix / robustness fix.

Areas: desktop/Tauri, web UI, Rust core (remote SSH services), docs.

## Motivation / Impact

For users:

- a transfer runs to completion instead of failing at 30s, and the stop button on the transfer card actually cancels the operation it displays (before this, a drag-and-drop upload could not be cancelled at all and a peer download could not be stopped);
- a cancelled or failed upload/download leaves the previous destination unchanged instead of truncating or half-writing it;
- large files no longer have to fit in memory on the client or the host.

For developers:

- `ApiRequestConfig.timeout <= 0` now means "no deadline" (previously `0` silently fell back to the default), so a long-running command can opt out explicitly; the two transfer commands use it, commands without a stop surface keep the default;
- the SFTP per-request timeout went from the dependency default 10s to 60s, because 10s for one 256 KiB chunk is a ~25 KiB/s throughput floor that turned a slow-but-healthy link into a failing one;
- the cancellation registry is now an RAII guard, so it cannot leak an entry on an early return.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p openbitfun-services-integrations --no-default-features --features remote-ssh-concrete --lib remote_ssh::` — passed (163 passed, 5 ignored)
- `cargo test -p openbitfun-desktop --lib api::ssh_api::tests` — passed
- `cargo test -p openbitfun-desktop --lib api::local_file_download::tests` — passed
- `cargo test -p openbitfun-desktop --lib remote_workspace_policy` — passed
- `cargo check -p openbitfun-services-integrations --no-default-features --features remote-ssh-concrete` and `--features remote-ssh` — passed
- `cargo check -p openbitfun-desktop --lib` — passed (needs the same Linux GTK/webkit build packages CI installs)
- `pnpm run type-check:web` — passed
- `pnpm --dir src/web-ui run test:run src/tools/file-system src/features/ssh-remote src/infrastructure/api` — passed (50 files / 440 tests)
- `pnpm run fmt:rs`, `pnpm run i18n:audit`, `pnpm run check:core-boundaries`, `pnpm run check:repo-hygiene`, eslint on the changed files — passed
- `git diff --cached --check` — clean

AI assistance: this change is AI-assisted. Automated testing level is fully tested according to the list above (unit/integration plus the repository's static checks); it was **not** manually exercised against a real remote host in this environment (no live SSH/container target was available), so an end-to-end transfer check on a real workspace is still worth doing during review.

## Reviewer Notes

- Remote scenarios: everything here is local to the desktop host and its Web UI. No wire shape, Tauri command name, event payload field, Product Operation Registry row, `workspace_file_upload` chunk protocol, or relay-service/mobile-web code changed — so no relay or mobile-web redeploy is involved, and no cross-version negotiation changes.
- Behaviour change worth confirming: an upload now replaces its destination (new inode; the mode comes from the staging file) instead of truncating in place. That is the publish semantics the container path and the chunked `workspace_file_upload` already used, and it is what makes a cancelled upload non-destructive. Documented in `docs/architecture/remote-workspace-transport.md`.
- Known gaps deliberately not bundled in this PR: peer-proxied transfers are still capped at 120s by the peer RPC policy and the peer host-invoke bridge, and commands without a progress/stop surface keep the default deadline on purpose (that bound is what ends a wedged host). Both are called out here rather than silently half-fixed.
- New tests: streamed SFTP upload (progress, cancel, channel reuse), streamed container upload through the local shell fixture, desktop staging/registration units, `ApiClient` deadline opt-out, `sshApi` deadline boundary, drag-and-drop multi-file stop, peer-download stop.

## Checklist

- [x] This PR is focused and does not include secrets, temporary prompts, generated scratch files, or unrelated artifacts.
- [x] Relevant verification is recorded above, or skipped checks are explained.
- [x] User-facing strings, docs, and locales are updated where applicable.

author: jason-easyazz
body:
## What this does

`mempalace migrate` would corrupt recall on Zoe's palace. Its `extract_drawers_from_sqlite()` takes every row in `chroma.sqlite3` with no collection filter and adds all of them to a new `mempalace_drawers`. The palace is almost all audit rows:

| collection | rows |
|---|---|
| drawers | 365 |
| `mempalace_audit` | 21,389 |
| `mempalace_audit_sec_*` leftovers (9 collections) | 11 |

So the tool would put ~21k audit summaries into recall and drop the audit collection.

`scripts/maintenance/chroma_migrate_rehearsal.py run` migrates **one collection at a time, on a copy**, and never opens the live store:

- **copy:** `rsync` the segment dirs, then snapshot the SQLite with the online-backup API and run `integrity_check`.
- **export:** read each collection from the copy's SQLite in `mode=ro`, using the same SQL as `export_memory_store.py`. It never loads the 0.6 HNSW.
  - Collection policy is fail-closed: drawers are re-embedded, audit gets the constant vector, `_sec_` leftovers are skipped and listed. Any other collection aborts the export.
- **rebuild:** runs in a throwaway `uv venv` with `chromadb==1.5.9`. ORT, numpy and tokenizers are pinned to the zoe-data venv's versions; the aarch64 abi3 wheel installs. It builds a **new** store:
  - drawers are re-embedded with MiniLM; archive SHA256 `913d7300…` is asserted, and it is the same in 0.6.3 and 1.5.9
  - audit rows get `memory_service._AUDIT_NULL_EMBEDDING`, pinned equal by a unit test
  - the EF identity is `"default"`, the same identity mempalace 3.10 persists
  - the source HNSW settings are kept: **the live drawers are `l2`, resize 2.0, not cosine**
  - `config.json` gets `embedding_model: minilm`
- **prove:** every proof runs in its own subprocess (chroma#1218), and mutating proofs run on scratch copies.
- **finish:** writes `manifest.json` and deletes the venv.

Heavy steps run at `nice 15` inside a `MemoryMax=700M, MemorySwapMax=0` user scope. Before each one the script waits for `MemAvailable ≥ 1.2 GB`, and refuses if it doesn't come.

## Proofs: run for real on the box, on a copy (2026-09-27 21:20)

| proof | result | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| a. counts: 1.x API **and** export-SQL on the 1.x sqlite; HNSW space and resize kept | **PASS**: 365 = 365, 21,389 = 21,389 | 158 MB |
| b. per-id document+metadata hash (type-preserving) | **PASS**: 0 mismatch / 0 extra | 237 MB |
| b-neg. one mutated metadata value on a scratch copy | **PASS**: caught | 188 MB |
| c. write round-trip on each collection (write → fresh proc sees+deletes → fresh proc sees gone) | **PASS** ×3 | 311 MB |
| d. embedding cosine, 200 drawers, stored 0.6.3 vectors vs rebuilt | **PASS**: min 1.0000; 15 `embeddings_queue` vectors also 1.0000 | 114 MB |
| d-neg. same vectors paired with the wrong ids | **PASS**: caught (min −0.053) | 36 MB |
| e. recall parity, `demo_b08_*` user only, 20 queries top-10 | **PASS**: 20/20 identical order, 0 demo rows left | 282 MB |
| f. 0.6.3 client on the migrated store | **PASS**: fails loudly (`KeyError: '_type'`) | 96 MB |

- **RAM:** peak RSS 372 MB, in the rebuild. `/usr/bin/time` isn't installed on the box, so RSS is `wait4` `ru_maxrss`, the same number `time -v` reports.
- **Wall:** 266 s end to end, under contention: copy 2.3 s, export 2.1 s, rebuild 156 s, proofs about 100 s.
- **Artifacts:** kept in `~/.zoe/chroma-migration-rehearsal/2026-09-27/` (0700): `src/`, `export/`, `dst/` and `manifest.json`.
- **Unit tests:** 24 `ci_safe` tests pass offline (`unshare -rn`) under `TZ=UTC`, and they go red when the script is mutated. `validate_structure.py` passes, and the `tests/unit -m ci_safe` lane is green (1331 passed).

## Findings beyond the brief

- **The live drawers are `l2`, not `cosine`.** The research and the tracker assumed cosine. Distances feed `1/(1+dist)` in `_semantic_search`, so the space is carried over, not changed.
- **The EF call size sets RSS.** chroma pads every text to 256 tokens, so RSS was 706 MB at 32 texts per call and 264 MB at 4. The first attempt was OOM-killed at the 700 MB cap. The rebuild now embeds 4 texts per call.
- **`check_memory_tombstones.py` is silently wrong on a 1.x store.** It reports audit `0/0 ok` and doesn't see drawers. It needs a port before cutover.
- **`~/bin/nightly-training-cycle.sh` (`zoe-training.timer`, 02:05, `/usr/bin/python3`) opens the palace with chromadb.** It is an extra 3.10 opener the plan didn't list.
- **The drawer count is climbing:** 333 → 344 → 365 in about 20 minutes. Something writes drawers continuously, so the final copy must come from a stopped store.
- **mempalace 3.10.0 was uploaded 2026-09-16,** so it clears the 14-day rule on 2026-09-30. The rehearsal doesn't need it.

## Cutover checklist (🧑 operator, one window, outside 01:45–03:15)

Full detail is in `docs/knowledge/chroma-1-5-migration.md` §4–§6.

1. Stop `zoe-training.timer zoe-dreaming.timer zoe-memory-export.timer zoe-backup.timer` and then `zoe-data`. Confirm no opener process is running.
2. Run `chroma_migrate_rehearsal.py run --fresh --date cutover-<date>` against the stopped store. All 10 proofs must PASS.
3. `mv ~/.mempalace ~/.mempalace.pre-b08-<ts>`, then `cp -a <rehearsal>/dst ~/.mempalace`.
4. `uv pip install chromadb==1.5.9 mempalace==3.10.0` into the py312 venv, with the numerics constrained. Re-point the 3.10 callers (tombstones, nightly-training, hand-run checks) at the venv; don't install into the 3.10 user-site, which holds Kokoro's CUDA ORT. Land the requirements pins, the ~line 82 comment fix and the `_skip_name_check` audit in the same PR.
5. `mempalace palace set-embedder` to record the MiniLM identity. Check `--help` first; this step is unrehearsed.
6. Start zoe-data and poll `/readyz` until `memory_capture` reports `self-recall ok`. Then check `/health` recall, run `check_emotional_thread.py` under the venv, do one real recall turn, and compare zoe-data RSS before and after.
7. Re-enable the timers.

**Rollback:** stop everything and restore `~/.mempalace.pre-b08-<ts>`, then reinstall 0.6.3 / 3.3.1. Never just re-pin: proof f shows 0.6.3 can't read the migrated store.

## Not verified

- The mempalace 3.10 runtime path. The rehearsal never installed mempalace; EF name compatibility was checked from source only.
- The `set-embedder` step.
- Installing into the 3.10 user-site.
- zoe-data steady-state RSS on 1.5.
- A real `/readyz` self-recall on the new client.

All of these belong to the operator cutover.

## Summary

- **SSH / headless login**: when `SSH_CONNECTION`/`SSH_CLIENT`/`SSH_TTY` is set, or on Linux with no `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, `wk login` prints the sign-in URL instead of silently "opening" a browser nobody can see (`--no-browser` forces this anywhere).
- **Paste-back**: the browser's final redirect to `127.0.0.1:<port>` can't reach the remote host, so the user can paste that redirect URL at a `Redirect URL:` prompt. The token is extracted (CSRF state checked) and raced against the loopback listener — whichever lands first wins. SSH port-forwarding still works too.

- README **Headless / SSH** section and AGENTS.md auth + quirks updated.
