| Stepping exp 2 from t=400 through the turn at t=500 to t=530 keeps h_max near 1330 m and no beyond-front cell thicker than the ice inside (campaign reached ~2500 m) | ⏸️ untested | no | The 130-year run on 8 ranks takes about 2 hours and had only reached t=408 when this step had to report (h_max 1330 m, max beyond-front 244 m so far). Read the finished exp2_t400_530_target.log/.csv i… |
| Front radius drift vs the prescribed 750 - 47.75(1 - cos 2 pi t/1000) km stays small with this commit where the base reset pulls the front back | ⏸️ untested | no | Only one reinitialisation had run (at t=408: this commit -3843 m vs base -3904 m, both -3829 m at t=400). The direction matches the intent, but a drift rate over several decades needs the finished run… |
| A reinitialised convex disc one cell in radius survives and loses less than 3 % of a cell per reinitialisation | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload established this only through the unit test test/levelset_test.py::test_reinitialisation_keeps_a_convex_front (serial and 3 ranks, passed), not a live product run. |
| A gated band advances with its ice to within 0.5 of a cell | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload established this only through the unit test test/levelset_test.py::test_a_gated_band_advances_with_its_ice (passed), not a live product run. |
| Adversarial: a one-cell water pocket inside the ice and a one-cell ice island are healed by reinitialisation, not made permanent | ⏸️ untested | no | The prior payload established this only through the unit test test/levelset_test.py::test_reinitialisation_heals_isolated_cells (serial and 3 ranks, passed), not a live product run. |

author: ulanproger
body:
## Summary

PR #9 merged without its last two commits — they were pushed while diagnosing the manual re-run path live, right around when the merge happened:

- **`ci: pass head_sha/base_ref to OpenCodeReview on manual dispatch`** — dispatched a real review for PR #7 to test it and got "Review skipped: no items were selected" after 0 files, ~60ms. Root cause: on `workflow_dispatch` the action has no `pull_request` event payload to read `EVENT_HEAD_SHA`/`EVENT_BASE_REF` from, and does not resolve them from `pr_number` itself — both end up empty, its merge-base command fails on the empty ref, and it silently "succeeds" having reviewed nothing. `fork-check` now also fetches `headRefOid`/`baseRefName` and passes them through.
- **`ci: stop interpolating pr_number directly into the fork-check script`** — OpenCodeReview's own review of the PR that added the fix above caught this: `${{ inputs.pr_number }}` was embedded straight into the `run:` block, so a workflow_dispatch input's raw text lands in the shell source before bash parses it — quotes or a command substitution in it would run as this job's own commands, with `GH_TOKEN` (and, a step later, the App/OpenAI secrets) in scope. Now passed through `env:` as `PR_NUMBER`, read as a shell variable, with a numeric check before it ever reaches `gh`.

**Confirmed live, not just by inspection:** dispatched from this branch reviewing PR #9 itself (same-branch — the one case `workflow_dispatch` reliably supports) after the first fix, got a real review back (1 finding — the injection bug above). Cross-branch dispatch (reviewing a PR on a different branch than the one you dispatch from) still doesn't fetch real diff content — that appears to be a limitation in `alibaba/open-code-review`'s own checkout logic, not something fixable from this workflow; noted for awareness, not fixed here.

body:
## Change

Consumers currently have to assemble raw vLLM connector arguments and account for CPU cache memory themselves. Add opt-in `spec.serving.kvCacheOffload.cpuMemoryGiB` to render native KV-offload flags and reserve the cache allocation in serving-pod memory requests and limits.

The budget is per data-parallel engine, shared across its tensor-parallel ranks. For example, a 4 GiB cache with two data-parallel engines adds 8 GiB to both baseline memory values. Admission and reconciliation require explicit baseline memory and reject conflicting raw arguments. Removing the field restores the baseline resources and removes the generated flags.

Includes the generated operator/Helm CRDs, admission and rendering tests, an illustrative model manifest, and an offload-on/off validation worksheet. The guide records source compatibility with the pinned serving runtime and explains how to measure latency, concurrency, cache reuse, correctness, and host-memory tradeoffs for each consumer profile.

Refs #196.

## Validation

- `go test ./... -coverprofile=cover.out` in `operator`, including Kubernetes envtest admission.
- `golangci-lint v2.4.0 run`: no issues.
- Documentation: 29 tests passed; static site build passed.
- `helm lint charts/nebari-llm-serving/` passed; packaged and operator CRDs match.
- Rendering tests cover tensor/data parallelism, per-pod replica accounting, overflow, input immutability, conflicting arguments, and disabling offload.

## Draft status

GPU inference and offload/reload validation remain outstanding. No model/hardware combination or performance improvement is claimed as validated. The available local GPU is already substantially occupied and this environment has no vLLM installation; no serving deployment was changed. Keep this draft until a compatible GPU environment completes the documented paired benchmark and runtime checks.

author: francescok
body:
Fixes #5163.

`&:to_s` becomes `{ |_spx| _spx.to_s }` in the parser, so both forms in the issue take the same path through `infer_block_params` (`src/analyze_pass.c`). In the first round `stage.outcomes` has no type, so `h = stage.outcomes || {}` reads as the `{}` arm's StrPolyHash, and the Hash arm (`hash.transform_keys { |k| } binds key`) types the param `ty_hash_key` of that, a String. In later rounds `h` is boxed: the Hash arm no longer matches, and the list of iterators whose params a boxed receiver binds as poly (`each`, `select`, `sort_by`, ...) has no `transform_keys`, so nothing widens the param and it stays `const char *`. Codegen was already right: it walks `sp_poly_as_pp_hash(...)` and binds each boxed key. The inline form and the method-parameter form in the issue are poly from the first round, so their param never becomes a String.

`transform_keys` joins that list, with the other walks of a Hash that had the same gap. Each of them fails on master:
- `delete_if`, `keep_if`, `select!`, `filter!` and `reject!` with `|k, v|` stop the C build the same way.
- `each_key` unboxed a Symbol key as a String: two keys crashed, one printed nothing.
- `transform_values` and `each_value` fail the same way when the fallback literal has String values (`x || { "x" => "y" }`).

Widening fits the monotone fixpoint, and codegen does not change:

```c
sp_RbVal lv__spx = sp_box_nil();
...
  sp_PolyPolyHash_set(_t8, sp_box_str(sp_poly_to_s(lv__spx)), _t7->vals[_t7->order[_t9]]);
```

`transform_keys!` and `transform_values!` desugar to the forms above, so they need no entry of their own.

Tests: `test/boxed_hash_local_walk_params.rb` runs each walk over a local holding `stage.outcomes || {}` (or `|| { "x" => "y" }` for the value walks), against a two-key hash and against `Stage.new(nil)`. It fails to build on master and matches CRuby 4.0 with this change. `make test` is green (4170 pass). `make gate-props` is clean apart from the two #4847 `infer-test` rows, which fail on master too.

Not covered, all failing the same way on master in the inline form too, so not this gap:
- `h.each_with_index.map { |(k, v), i| k }` on a boxed hash answers `[]`.
- `h.fetch(:zz) { |k| k }` raises KeyError instead of calling the block.
- `h.transform_keys!(&:to_s)` on a local holding a boxed Symbol-keyed hash now compiles but raises "can't store String as a key in a Hash of Symbol keys through a boxed receiver", the limit the inline form already reaches.

Found while compiling a small macOS CLI with spinel.

author: danielhanchen
body:
## Summary

K-EXAONE-2.0-750B sets `swiglu_limits` (a SwiGLU clamp on layers 62-77) and per-layer `sliding_windows` (128 on the sliding layers, with no `sliding_window`). Stock transformers' `exaone_moe` modeling never reads either field, and the config defaults `sliding_window` to 4096. Loading the checkpoint therefore silently builds a different network: every sliding layer gets a 4096 window instead of 128, and the clamp is dropped. It loads and trains with no warning. The upstream support is huggingface/transformers#47802, which is still open. The model card installs a fork.

This PR adds `_raise_if_modeling_ignores_config`, called in both `FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained` and `FastModel.from_pretrained` right after the model types are resolved. For `exaone_moe` it raises when the config sets these fields in a way that matters (non-zero `swiglu_limits`, or `sliding_windows` that disagree with the single `sliding_window`) and the installed transformers modeling source does not mention them. The error names the fields and the upstream PR. `UNSLOTH_ALLOW_IGNORED_CONFIG=1` turns it into a warning.

The check reads the modeling source, so it switches off by itself once transformers supports the fields. K-EXAONE 236B (one window that matches its list, no clamp) is unaffected.

## Who hits it

Anyone loading K-EXAONE-2.0-750B-A37B(-FP8) through Unsloth on a stock transformers. Before this PR they trained a model that is not the released one. All other models skip the check (it is keyed on `model_type`).

## Evidence

- New `tests/test_modeling_only_config_fields.py`:

| transformers | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 5.17.0 | 5 failed | 5 passed |
| 5.5.0 | 5 failed | 5 passed |
| 4.57.6 | module skipped | module skipped |

  On 4.57.6 the module skips because there is no `exaone_moe`. On main, one test fails on behaviour and the rest fail because the helper does not exist; the behavioural before/after is the end-to-end repro below.
- `tests/test_optimized_precision_conflicts.py` runs `FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained` over a stub namespace. It gains a stub for the new helper, the same way it stubs the other loader helpers. Without the stub its 18 tests fail with `NameError`.
- Existing loader tests (35 files) have identical failing test IDs on main and this PR:
  - 5.17.0: 804 passed, 29 skipped, 11 failed.
  - 4.57.6: 756 passed, 80 skipped, 8 failed.
  - All failures are pre-existing on main.
- End-to-end repro on a tiny random model with the 750B config shape:
  - main loads silently, and every layer's attention `sliding_window` is 4096 while `config.sliding_windows` is `[0, 4096, 128, 128, 128, 0, 128, 128]`;
  - with this PR, loading raises and names `swiglu_limits`, `sliding_windows`, the installed transformers version and huggingface/transformers#47802.
- `test_k_exaone_1_still_loads` covers the K-EXAONE 236B config shape (one window that matches its list, no clamp), which is not refused. On main, that model's real (truncated) weights load and train through Unsloth with forward parity against transformers, and this check does not change that path.

author: francescok
body:
Fixes #5164.

`table` never settles a return type, since its last expression is the raise from the missing `Styler`, so `method_is_void` emits it as a `void` C function and the call `table([1])` is typed TY_UNKNOWN. An untyped argument to a typed parameter goes through `emit_arg_or_default_fill` into `emit_unresolved_coerced` (`src/codegen.c`), which only recognized the raise tokens an unresolved call emits (`sp_raise_nomethod(`, `sp_raise_cls(`) and passed anything else through raw, so the void call landed in the `const char *` or `sp_int` slot. `puts(table([1]))` worked because `emit_boxed_text` already renders TY_UNKNOWN as `(expr, sp_box_nil())`. The element slots of a typed Array never reached the coercion at all, which is why an inline unresolved call stops there too.

`call_answers_no_value` decides whether a call is bound to a void user method, resolving it the way the direct-call emitters do: a receiverless call through the enclosing self (`comp_self_call_mi`), `Const.m` through the class-method chain, and an object receiver through its class, where every override below that class must be void too. A yielding method is not counted, since its call is spliced and gives the splice's value, and parentheses around the call are peeled (`unwrap_parens`). `emit_unresolved_coerced` gains one arm for such a call, the same evaluate-then-give-the-slot-its-nil form as #4661:

```c
const char * _t8 = ((void)(sp_table(_t7)), NULL);
```

`emit_unresolved_coerced` is where a typed slot fed an untyped value already goes, so this one arm covers a user method's parameters of any type, typed locals, ivars through a writer and Struct members. The typed Array element slots now send an untyped value through it too: `emit_typed_elem_value` (String `unshift` and `insert`, and Integer `unshift` of a void call), statement `[]=`, statement `push`/`<<`, the value form of `push`, and array literal elements. The numeric element forms already discarded a raise token, so they are only routed there for a void call. Both arms only rewrite spots where the raw emission put a void or poly value in a typed slot, which never built, and every other untyped value emits what it did before.

Tests: `test/no_value_call_typed_slot.rb` covers a String parameter typed by another call site, an Integer parameter, an instance method on an object receiver, a class method, an implicit-self call inside a class, a Struct member, a typed local that keeps its old value, and String and Integer Arrays through `push`, `<<`, `[]=`, `unshift`, `insert` and literals, with both the void call and an inline unresolved call, and parenthesized calls in an element, a `<<` and an argument. It fails to build on master and matches CRuby 4.0 with this change, also under `--int-overflow=promote`. `make test` is green (4170 pass). `make gate-props` is clean apart from the two #4847 `infer-test` rows, which fail on master too.

Not covered, also on master: `def t; Styler.new(rows).render; end` raises NoMethodError where CRuby raises NameError.

Found while compiling a small macOS CLI with spinel: its flattened source stopped the C build at three sites of this shape and builds with this change.

author: greg-weber-claude-agent[bot]
body:
## What this does

The dispatcher could only decide *which model* an agent runs on. It now also
writes a `thinking:` line beside the `model:` it chose, because the model a
budget can afford is often one that should think at a different effort.

There is no originating issue — this came out of a design conversation. The
reasoning and the rejected alternatives are recorded in
[`docs/adr/0004-thinking-levels.md`](../blob/thinking-levels/docs/adr/0004-thinking-levels.md).

```json
{
  "models": { "openai-codex/gpt-6-sol": { "thinking": "low" } },
  "agents": {
    "planner": {
      "thinking": "xhigh",
      "primary":    { "model": "claude-bridge/claude-opus-5-5", "rail": "claude" },
      "alternates": [{ "model": "openai-codex/gpt-6-sol", "rail": "codex", "thinking": "off" }]
    }
  }
}
```

## The mental model

Three places can state a level; the most specific wins:

| Place | Spelling | What it is about |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate | `agents.<name>.primary.thinking`, `.alternates[i].thinking` | This destination |
| Route | `agents.<name>.thinking` | The work — "planning thinks hard" |
| Model | `models.<provider/modelId>.thinking` | The model, wherever a route names it |

Resolved level = candidate → route → model → **nothing**. "Nothing" is a real
answer: no line is written and the agent file's own `thinking:` line is left as
it is.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `model:` rewritten only; `thinking:` was whatever you last hand-edited | `model:` and — when the config states one — `thinking:` written together |

## How it works

**Config** (`src/config.ts`) — `thinking` is a new optional field on `Candidate`
and on `AgentRoute`, and a new `models` table keyed by `provider/modelId`.
`thinkingFor()` is the single place the precedence lives, so the decision, the
write and the printed provenance cannot disagree. Levels are validated for their
*spelling* only, and each one carries provenance like every other value, so
`/quota-dispatch` shows where a level came from.

**Policy** (`src/index.ts`) — an assign-decision now carries `thinking`, resolved
from the same candidate it carries a `model` for. Every assign path (pinned,
primary-ok, winning alternate, no-alternate-won) goes through one `assign()`
helper; holds carry no level.

**Writing** (`src/index.ts`) — `upsertThinking` mirrors `upsertModel`: written
unquoted beside the `model:` line, replaced only when the decoded value differs,
and `src` returned byte-for-byte when there is nothing to change, so a pass that
changes nothing still reports `unchanged` and writes nothing.

**No restore** — this is the deliberate part of the design. The dispatcher keeps
no record of what a file said before, and does not put anything back when an
agent moves to a candidate that states no level. So a level written on the way
out survives the trip home. A guarantee about what a file *used to hold* cannot
be kept without owning the file, and the file is shared across sessions and
projects. If you want a level on the way home, state one.

## Technical decisions

- **Three places, not one.** A per-model map alone cannot say "planning thinks
  hard on whichever model it ends up on" without repeating itself on every model;
  a per-route level alone cannot say "Sol is a low-thinking model wherever it
  appears". Rejected options and the reasoning are in the ADR.
- **No capability check.** An unknown model id is *known bad* and holds the
  agent, because it makes the spawn fail. A level the model cannot do is not:
  pi clamps it at spawn time. Treating the two the same would put a second,
  quieter copy of the model catalogue in this extension.
- **A level is not checked against the consumer either.** `thinking:` is read by
  the installed subagents plugin from the agent file, which needs no new API —
  the same seam `model:` already uses.

## Verification

- `npm test` — **270 pass** (29 new), `npx tsc --noEmit` clean,
  `scripts/check-runtime-deps.js` clean, `npm pack --dry-run` resolves the pi
  manifest.
- End-to-end against a real agent file in a temp dir: planner resolves `high`
  from the route while on Opus (beating the model's `low`), and `off` from the
  candidate on the codex alternate.
- The new `alternates[i].thinking` provenance clearing was **verified by
  reverting it** — three tests fail with the old loop and pass with the fix.
- Adversarial review of this branch found and this branch fixes: stale
  `thinking` provenance after an `alternates` list replacement (plus two tests
  that were passing vacuously), a type named after a term `CONTEXT.md` forbids,
  an over-claimed "cannot drift" in `src/index.ts` and the README, a
  self-contradicting ADR bullet, a comment that disagreed with its code, and a
  misleading test name.

## Follow-ons, not in this PR

- A replaced `alternates` list drops the candidate levels the old list carried,
  so a level can silently fall back to the route or model default. Correct per
  the documented "a layer that mentions `alternates` replaces it whole" rule,
  but worth deciding whether a replacement should carry levels over per model.
- `upsertThinking`/`upsertModel` share a shape that could be one
  `upsertScalar(head, key, rendered, decoded)` helper. Left alone: the symmetry
  is deliberate and the two differ in quoting, value type and return.
- Pre-existing: the insert-after-`name:` path writes a bare `\n` into a CRLF
  file, producing mixed line endings. `upsertModel` already did this.

author: jenspytlichpersonal
body:
## Summary

Reconverting a book ("Convert again") rewrites its section files under unchanged URLs, and the reader caches those hard: `Cache-Control: max-age=86400` in the browser cache, and indefinitely in the service worker's cache-first offline store once the app runs over https. So after the reflow improvements in #5, devices kept showing the old text.

Changes:
- **Conversion stamp.** `writeBundle()` records `convertedAt` in `book.json`; the conversion queue stores it in a new `books.converted_at` column; the API returns it as `convertedAt`. A small startup migration adds the column to existing databases.
- **Versioned URLs.** The reader requests sections, images and the book stylesheet as `.../sections/12.html?v=<convertedAt>`, and the library's cover URL uses the same stamp. New conversion, new URLs, no stale copies.
- **Offline cache cleanup.** On opening a book the reader deletes offline-cache entries for that book that carry an older stamp, so the cache doesn't grow with every reconversion.

No change to the service worker: its cache keys already include the query string.

## Testing
- `npm test`: 20 pass. The API test now asserts that reprocessing bumps `convertedAt` and that the manifest and API agree.
- Migration verified against a database created with the previous schema: the column is added and existing rows read `0`.
- Headless Chromium: cover, stylesheet, sections and images are all requested with `?v=<stamp>`; images load; no page errors.

## After merging
```
cd /opt/ereader && git pull && npm install --omit=dev
sudo systemctl restart ereader
```
Then reload the reader once; already-reconverted books show their new text without another conversion.

author: qigao
body:
Closes #137
Advances #122

## Why this is required

A Wasm `funcref` denotes a **function instance**, not merely a module-local function index.

Before shared table linking, TurboWasm represented refs as:

```
{ is_null, function_index }
```

That becomes ambiguous as soon as a consumer can observe a provider-created ref: raw index 0 in the provider is not necessarily function 0 in the consumer.

## New identity

```
funcref
  = owner instance token
  + function index in that owner
```

Internal table entries carry the same owner identity.

The public owner token is opaque and borrowed. Callers must not dereference or manufacture it.

## Runtime semantics

- `ref.func` captures the current instance + function index
- const-expression refs and element items capture their creating instance
- `table.get` returns the same owner identity
- `table.set/grow/fill/copy` preserve it
- `call_indirect` resolves the actual function type in the **entry owner** module and dispatches to the **entry owner** instance
- null refs carry no owner
- legacy host-created non-null refs with `owner == NULL` normalize to the executing instance at the interpreter boundary
- host-provided non-null owner tokens are never dereferenced until they match the current instance or a known linked provider

## Qualification

A real cross-module scenario proves the identity is semantic, not cosmetic:

```
provider.getref() -> ref.func(provider.target)
        |
        v
consumer local table
        |
        +-- set/get
        +-- grow
        +-- fill
        +-- copy
        |
        v
consumer call_indirect
        |
        v
provider.target() == 42
```

Additional coverage:

- runtime-produced refs expose non-null owner tokens
- `table.get` preserves the exact owner token
- legacy ownerless host refs normalize on entry
- C++ standard-layout ABI check for the enriched `turbowasm_funcref`
- section/body framing statically qualified before CI

This PR intentionally does **not** add shared table imports yet; it establishes the identity model they require.

author: davidmarsden
body:
Improves opponent dossiers when the latest tactical family is a recent switch rather than an established setup.

- keeps latest-setup evidence and thresholds unchanged
- detects volatility when the latest family is under 60% of the last five and differs from the longer-run dominant family
- independently builds evidence for the longer-run dominant family
- shows an established-setup contingency without promoting it as the current plan
- uses the same 3-match / 2-club recommendation floor for both scenarios

CSKA is the motivating case: its latest family is only 1/5 and 2/10, while its longer-run family has substantially more history. The dossier should prepare for both rather than manufacture confidence in the latest switch.

Stacked on #3585 (cluster B). The skill side of cluster D in UiPath/flow-builder-sdk (`feat/bpmn-cluster-d`).

Measured across the 97 real artifacts to hand, every public `uipath:input` is scoped to the manual start event and every public `uipath:output` to the end event whose mapping writes it. The SDK now defaults to that placement; this adds the guidance that goes with it:

- `bpmn.variables.public-scope`: declare the contract with `.input()` / `.output()`, not `.var()`; the compiler scopes them like the canvas.
- `bpmn.variables.read-inputs-directly`: `vars.<id>` reads an input directly; the start-event bridge is one spelling, not a requirement (the engine seeds by id).
- `bpmn.variables.input-name`: input values are matched by display `name` at run start.
- Router row for variables now points at the new section.

No grader changes: `check_script_jint_guidance.py` (#3585) already accepts either scoping, and `check_variable_scopes.py`'s start-event requirement is now what the SDK writes.

author: omardev29
body:
## Summary

`./pyt` could not start at all on Android (Termux) or the BSDs: uv has no CPython builds for those platforms, and the launchers' `uv run --script` followed `.python-version` (`python.cpython`, 3.14), so every command, `help` included, stopped inside uv before the runner started. Termux's own Python 3.13 was never used.

This PR makes the runner start in two steps and documents what each platform supports.

## What changes

**Launchers and the Neovim plugin** (`pyt`, `pyt.cmd`, `pyt.ps1`, `init.lua`, mirrored by `project.launcher_python` and `proc.runner_argv`) now run
`uv run --quiet --python=REQUEST --python-preference PREF --script .pytemplate/pyt.py ARGS`:

| The project | REQUEST | PREF | The runner starts on |
|---|---|---|---|
| has its environment (`.venv/bin/python`, `.venv-wsl/bin/python` or `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` is there; a dangling link does not count) | empty: no request (verified with uv 0.10.12 and 0.12.19) | `only-managed` | `python.cpython` from `.python-version`, as uv installed it: exactly as before this PR |
| has no environment yet (a fresh clone, Termux) | `>=3.11` | `managed` | any CPython 3.11 or newer uv finds, a system one too |

One word (`--python=`) because Windows PowerShell 5.1 drops an empty argument. The environment's interpreter is not passed as a path: on Windows that file is there even when its base Python was uninstalled, and uv would stop every command on it. `only-managed` makes uv build the runner's cached environment again when a system Python built it (`managed` kept a system 3.14's for good).

**Runner** (`cli._restart`): `help`, `doctor`, `new`, `install` and `uninstall` run on whatever Python started the runner. Every other command (and every `[tasks]` entry) runs on the `python.cpython` uv manages: when the runner started on another Python (a system one of that very minor too: `cli._runs_on_python_cpython` asks uv which interpreter is its own while the project has no environment), it runs itself again on it, in the same folder with the same arguments and exit code. `envs.ensure_python` finds that CPython or installs it (`uv python install --no-bin --no-registry`: nothing outside uv's folder), or exits 3 with the reason (`envs.no_download_problem`):

```
error: python.cpython = "3.14": uv installs no CPython on this platform (Android (linux aarch64)).
  The project's commands run on the CPython of python.cpython, which uv installs: here pyt
  runs help, doctor, install and uninstall only, on any Python 3.11 or newer.
  Work on the project on Windows, macOS or Linux (README: "Where pyt runs")
```

- `new` asks for the new project's `python.cpython` before it copies anything (the new `uv.lock` is made with it); on Termux it stops there, nothing written.
- `doctor` gets a `python.cpython` line; where uv cannot install it, that line is the one problem, and the environment and `uv.lock` checks that need it are skipped with a note.
- `pytemplate.toml`: `python.cpython` below 3.11 is refused (it never worked: the runner needs 3.11).
- `.pytemplate/pyt.py`: its "Python older than 3.11" message also covers a hand-made `.venv`.

**Docs**: README ("Where pyt runs", requirements, troubleshooting with the exact messages, the plugin paragraph), the plugin README, and CLAUDE.md (4.1, 5.2, 5.4, 11, 12.2, 13.1, new 15.1 and 15.2 entries).

## Behaviour by case

- Windows, macOS, Linux with a `.venv`: unchanged (uv follows `.python-version`, its own CPython only).
- Fresh clone: the runner may start on another CPython 3.11+ first; project commands pay a `uv python find` and, on another Python, a restart on `python.cpython` (about 50 ms more on Linux) until `setup` makes `.venv`.
- Termux/BSD: `help`, `doctor`, `install`, `uninstall` work on the system Python; the rest exit 3 with the message above, also when `python.cpython` names the system Python's own minor. By design: environments, `uv.lock` and builds stay on uv's managed CPython. A `.venv` made there by hand makes every command stop in uv (README troubleshooting: delete it).
- Windows only: the first start after `.venv` appears rebuilds the runner's cached environment when another Python built it; while a runner started before still runs from it, that start fails in uv (access denied) until the earlier command ends (CLAUDE.md 15.2).
- Older runners (a project made before this PR) started by a newer installed `pyt` in a project without `.venv` run on the Python uv picked (they have no restart); with `.venv` nothing changes. Noted in CLAUDE.md 15.2.

## Commits

- bacc96c: a one-line CLAUDE.md 13.3 correction pushed after #4 merged.
- fd3e8d8: the two-step start, `new`, `doctor`, docs and tests.
- 66a7293: findings of an adversarial review of fd3e8d8: `only-managed` with the environment, the check that a Python of the right minor is uv's own (a regression test fails with the old minor-only rule), and the real restart test moved into a throwaway copy (uv rebuilds a script's cached environment in place, and the checkout's is the one `./pyt selftest` runs in: Windows cannot delete it).

## Tests

New and updated tests in `test_cli_core` (which commands restart, the second runner's command line, folder, environment and exit code, a system Python of the right minor, faked and for real through uv on another CPython in a throwaway copy), `test_envs_core` (find, install, the three no-download messages, doctor lines), `test_launcher_sh` / `test_launcher_win` / `test_nvim_render` (the request and preference of every launcher against `project.launcher_python`, dangling links, `.venv-wsl`), `test_presets` / `test_global` (`new` asks for the Python first), `test_config_rules`, `test_docs` (the manual quotes the exact Termux message).

Local validation (Linux): `./pyt selftest` 4170 passed, 78 skipped; mypy --strict clean for linux, win32 and darwin; `selftest --shells` 60/60 (sh, bash, dash, zsh, ksh, mksh, yash, busybox, fish, pwsh 7.6); `selftest --nvim script`; `selftest --e2e script --quick`; `render --check`; `shellcheck -s sh pyt`. Termux simulated with an empty uv install folder, a downloads list without this platform and a system Python 3.12: `help` works; `tasks` and `new` exit 3, also with `python.cpython = "3.12"`; `doctor` shows one problem. CI on fd3e8d8: all 51 checks green, Windows (`pyt.cmd`, Windows PowerShell 5.1) included.

The site at itcoachen.netlify.app was returning a "Page not found" error on its home page. The project's only page had been uploaded with its display title as the filename (with spaces and special characters) instead of `index.html`, so Netlify had no root page to serve.

This PR will resolve the following CVEs: | Issue | Severity           | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | 
[CVE-2026-45736](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/35680437/detail?groupId=118975#CVE-2026-45736)

HIGH
| [ws] is an open source WebSocket client and server for Node.js. Prior to 8.20.1, the websocket.close() implementation is vulnerable to uninitialized memory disclosure when a TypedArray is passed as the reason argument. This vulnerability is fixed in 8.20.1. |
🤖 Remediation details Fix CVE-2026-45736: upgrade `ws` to ≥ 8.20.1 across all instances ## Short summary This PR remediates a high-severity vulnerability in the `ws` package (CVE-2026-45736) by ensuring every resolved instance of `ws` in the `8.x` line meets the patched floor of `8.20.1`. `ws` appears only as a transitive dependency in this project. Changes touch `stakecraft-frontend/package.json` (new override entry) and `stakecraft-frontend/package-lock.json` (lockfile refresh). ### ws `ws` is pulled in transitively by many dependencies (`ethers`, `viem`, `engine.io-client`, `@reown/appkit*`, `@walletconnect/utils`, `@polkadot/x-ws`, `rpc-websockets`, `smoldot`, and others). A first-pass `npm update ws --package-lock-only` resolved instances whose parent specs were wide enough (e.g. `^8.18.0`, `^8.5.0`) to reach `8.21.3`. The remaining instances were held below `8.20.1` by exact or tilde pins in their parents (`ethers` at `8.17.1`, `viem` at `8.18.3`, `engine.io-client` at `~8.18.3`, and several nested `isows`/`viem` copies at `8.18.0`); bumping those parents is forbidden by policy, so a selector-style override `"ws@<8.20.1": "8.20.1"` was added to `stakecraft-frontend/package.json` to floor every sub-`8.20.1` instance at the patched version without disturbing already-patched copies. ## Version changes | Package | From | To | Why updated | |---|---|---|---| | `ws` (multiple nested instances: `@polkadot/x-ws`, `rpc-websockets`, `@solana/web3.js` → `rpc-websockets`, `@trezor/websocket-client`, `@xrplf/isomorphic`, `smoldot`, `web3-providers-ws`) | `8.18.3` | `8.21.3` | Transitive CVE fix — lockfile refresh via `npm update` | | `ws` (nested under `ethers`, `viem`, `engine.io-client`, `@reown/appkit*`, `@walletconnect/utils` nested copies) | `8.17.1` / `8.18.0` / `8.18.3` | `8.20.1` | Transitive CVE fix — override `"ws@<8.20.1": "8.20.1"` (parent specs were exact/tilde-pinned) | | `ws` (root `node_modules/ws`, shared by `@cosmjs/socket`, `jayson`, `isows`, `isomorphic-ws`, etc.) | `7.5.10` | `7.5.13` | Lockfile refresh only — `^7` range; not in vulnerable `8.x` line |

author: 9takdanai007
body:
## Summary
T-201: database data sources (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server). You can connect, test, browse tables, preview rows and share a source. Decisions are in ADR-027; spec 03 describes what was built.

**Connectors** (`apps/api/app/connectors`)
- `ConnectorType` does not depend on FastAPI. Pydantic config and secret models produce the form's JSON Schema, with th/en labels and UI hints (`x-secret`, `x-rebinds-secret`, `x-visible-when`, ...).
- Drivers:
  - psycopg 3 connects through `hostaddr`.
  - PyMySQL and python-tds get a socket we open ourselves.
  - All three connect to the address the guard checked, and check the certificate against the name the user typed.
- python-tds 1.17 is hardened:
  - routing redirects are refused
  - certificate names are checked by SAN per RFC 6125 (the library's own check accepted CN and stripped `DNS:` badly)
  - retries, pooling and instance names are off
  - the patches fail at import on any other python-tds version
- TLS is required and verified by default (PG `verify-full`). A server without TLS fails before any credential is sent. `tls: disabled` must be chosen explicitly; the UI warns and the audit log records it.
- Error codes are safe to show: driver messages are never kept, and refused, reset and non-database answers all return `connection_failed`.

**SSRF guard** (`HostGuard`)
- The host must be host-name or IP syntax, and not one of our compose services. `make compose-check` fails if a service is missing from `DATA_SOURCE_BLOCKED_HOSTS`.
- Every resolved address is checked. Blocked: loopback, link-local (including metadata), 0.0.0.0/8, multicast, reserved, IPv4 inside IPv6, our services' current addresses, and `DATA_SOURCE_BLOCKED_NETWORKS`.
- The connection goes to the checked address and the name is never resolved again, which stops DNS rebinding.
- With `APP_ENV=production`, the api does not start while `DATA_SOURCE_BLOCKED_NETWORKS` is empty.

**Data sources API**
- `data_sources` table: `WorkspaceItemMixin`, names unique per workspace ignoring case, secret sealed with a key id bound into the AAD (HKDF purpose `data_source_secret`).
- Permissions:
  - Create needs EDIT on the workspace and a `data_source` ceiling of at least edit.
  - Browse and preview need EDIT, because raw rows bypass RLS.
  - VIEW sees no config. Delete and share need MANAGE.
- Secrets are never returned (`secrets_set` only) and are replaced whole:
  - Changing host, port, username, TLS or CA needs the password again (`secret_required`).
  - Testing unsaved settings uses only the password in the request.
- Test, browse and preview run in the request (ADR-027's exception to rule 8):
  - timeouts: connect 5 s, query 10 s, plus an overall budget
  - a separate thread pool of 8, read-only sessions
  - per-user rate limits: test 10/min, browse 60/min
  - preview caps: 50 rows, 100 columns, 1,000 characters per cell
- Audit:
  - create, update and delete are recorded in the same transaction
  - tests record where they went
  - a preview is not returned when its audit record fails
  - never a password

**Web**
- `/sources`: list with status, TLS-off mark and workspace.
- `/sources/new`: a wizard that goes type and workspace → connection → name.
  - The connection form is generated from `config_schema`, with advice to use a read-only account.
  - "Next" needs a passing test of the settings currently on screen.
  - Warnings for `account_can_write` and TLS off.
- `/sources/:id`:
  - Tables load only on request; the preview shows raw source values, not formatted through `Intl`, with a note above the table and NULL marked distinctly from an empty string.
  - The connection tab has write-only secrets and asks for the password again when the target changes.
  - Delete for manage.
  - Viewers see only the name and status.
- Sharing uses the existing `ShareDialog` (`origin: "api"`) with the inheritance switch; the share button shows only for manage.
- The audit log page has labels and a filter for `data_source.*`.

**Dev environment**
- Root cause of the blank login page: `make images` (run by test and lint) rebuilt `bi-api:dev`, but the running `api` container kept the old image and crashed on the new driver import.
- Now `make images` and `make build` recreate running services whose image changed; stopped ones stay stopped.
- Default build attestations are off (`BUILDX_NO_DEFAULT_ATTESTATIONS=1`). With the containerd image store they gave every cached build a new image id, which would have recreated everything each time.

## Configuration
New variables in `.env.example`:
- `DATA_SOURCE_BLOCKED_HOSTS`
- `DATA_SOURCE_BLOCKED_NETWORKS`
- `DATA_SOURCE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`
- `DATA_SOURCE_QUERY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`
- `DATA_SOURCE_TEST_RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS`
- `DATA_SOURCE_BROWSE_RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS`

New api dependencies:
- `psycopg[binary]`
- `pymysql`
- `python-tds` (pinned to 1.17)
- `pyopenssl` (used by python-tds for TLS)

## Existing dev stacks
Run `make up`, then `make migrate`. Demo sources are in the compose profile `sources`: `source-postgres`, `source-mysql` and `source-mssql`.

## Carried to T-801
- A weekly CI run of `make test-connectors-mssql`.
- Production subnets in `DATA_SOURCE_BLOCKED_NETWORKS`.
- A rotation job for `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

## Test plan
- [x] `make lint`
- [x] `make test`:
  - api: 894 passed, 12 skipped (the SQL Server tests)
  - web: 249
  - realm: 170
  - compose: 30
  - worker, ml, pipelines and renderer pass
- [x] `make test-connectors-mssql`: 12 passed against a real SQL Server 2022
- [x] Tests check that passwords never appear in responses, logs, SQL or `audit_log` rows.
- [x] SSRF is tested through the API, including DNS rebinding.
- [x] Every new endpoint has a forbidden test.
- [x] `make ui-snap`: 12 data source shots × th/en × light/dark, reviewed.
- [x] A second `make images` recreates no container.

body:
Part of #1 (landing the local work, PR 2 of 5). Groundwork for #5 (stable player identity).

## What
- **Time-based player ID recovery** (existing local commit): the IoU tracker keeps a lost player dormant for up to 3 s and reassociates a returning detection by centre distance, instead of issuing a new ID. Replaces `--max-missing-frames` with a time window.
- **Detector hardening** (`detectors/`):
  - Roboflow calls retry transient failures with exponential backoff, so one timeout on a long clip no longer kills the run.
  - Confidence and overlap are configured on the hosted client (fixed in this PR after review: they had stopped reaching the API), and confidence is also applied locally.
  - `filter_player_detections(max_players=...)` and `expected_player_count` (2 tennis, 4 padel) let the pipeline drop extra "players" such as spectators. Not wired into the pipeline yet; that lands with PR 5 of #1.
- **Tracker stats**: `SimpleIouTracker.last_update_stats` counts IoU matches, dormant recoveries and new tracks.
- **Experimental Kalman IoU tracker** (`tracking/kalman_iou_tracker.py`): constant-velocity Kalman filter over box centre and size, with one-to-one matching by the Hungarian algorithm (`scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment`). **Not used by any pipeline**: on the tested padel clip it created more tracks and ID switches than the simple tracker. Kept for comparison and for #5. Adds `scipy` (BSD-3).
- **`scripts/compare_trackers.py`**: runs both trackers on the same clip and reports their matching stats.

## How it was tested
- Fresh virtualenv: `pytest -q` 31 passed (8 new), `ruff check .` clean, CI green.
- New tests: Kalman prediction across a missed detection, dormant expiry, Hungarian assignment picking the globally best pairing, confidence filtering, player cap, retry on a temporary failure, thresholds reaching the hosted client.

## Review
Two-axis review done. Fixed here: thresholds not reaching the API, Kalman tracker marked experimental, changelog moved from a premature "v4.0" to "Unreleased". Tracker design findings (drift of the predicted box while a player is hidden, noise parameters, duplicated tracker logic, stats that mean different things per tracker) are recorded on #5.

Replaces #21: same final code, rebuilt so every commit passes the tests and uses the author's personal email. The threshold fix now comes first, so hosted detection never breaks at any commit.

author: drellem2
body:
When the witness store is missing, `OrphanedPolecats` returned `(nil, nil)`, which is the same result as a clean fleet. So `ReportOrphanedPolecats` returned 0 and logged nothing, and `/agents/drain` reported nothing unreachable.

Changes, following the approved triage packet's proposed_approach:
- **`ErrWitnessAbsent`** (new sentinel, `internal/agent/orphan.go`). When `WitnessedAlivePolecats` returns nothing, `OrphanedPolecats` now asks `WitnessStoreExists`. An absent store returns a wrapped `ErrWitnessAbsent` that names the path. A stat error is returned as an error. A present but empty store is still `(nil, nil)`, a real zero.
- **Reporter:** `ReportOrphanedPolecats` returns `OrphanSweepAbsent` (-2) for an absent store and `OrphanSweepUnreadable` (-1) for an unreadable one, as before. The absent state is logged once when it starts ("reporting absent, NOT zero") and once when it ends ("present again"), not on every heartbeat. Unreadable still logs on every sweep, unchanged. It sends no event and no mail, per the scope ruling.
- **`/agents/drain`:** `UnreachableErr` is now set for an absent store too. `pogo-self-deploy` already prints `unreachable_err` as "cannot tell whether any polecat survived", so the script needs no change.
- **Tests:** a three-state matrix (absent / present-empty / unreadable) across `OrphanedPolecats`, `/agents/drain`, and `ReportOrphanedPolecats`'s return value, plus a log-cadence test for the transitions. Positive control: with the absent branch disabled, all three matrix tests fail.

The limit from the issue reply still applies: the store is created by the first agent start. So this removes the silent zero, but polecats left by a pogod that never wrote a witness stay invisible once the store exists.

`./build.sh` passes.

Refs drellem2/pogo#197

author: micka420-collab
body:
## Why

The event journal kept its last 5,000 events of **all** types (`store.pruneEvents(EVENT_RETENTION)` every 2 s tick). `task_progress` is written at every agent milestone, so one night of work pushed out the proofs of a production that was still waiting for a human:

- the ingested CI (`validation_recorded`) → the Miellerie fell back to "missing evidence" on a proven production;
- the counter-review launch (`contre_expertise`) the Evaluator reads to count reviews in flight;
- a retry's critique (`task_retry`) → a reopened task waiting in `ready` restarted **without** its critique, silently (the "Limite connue" in `docs/PROTOCOLE-CRITIQUE.md`);
- routing reasons (`task_assigned`), Genome facts, delivery provenance.

Five ad-hoc exceptions had been grafted onto the blind prune, one per reader that complained. This PR replaces them with **one retention owner** (Notion cards: Evaluator durable evidence; routing "honest Genome window"; Time Travel depends on missions' events surviving).

Regression test proven on the pre-fix code: with `src/orchestrator/{server,store}.ts` from `origin/main`, the tick-boundary test fails on the critique (`expected undefined to deeply equal [ 'le jeton vide passe' ]`), and with soft assertions also on the CI evidence (`'missing'`), the Genome facts (`[]`), the truncation flag and the missing prune record.

## What

**Policy (pure, `src/shared/retention-journal.ts`)**
- **Traces** keep the window: the last 5,000 events, unchanged (live catch-up via `/api/events?since=`).
- **Proofs** (`TYPES_PREUVE`, composed from the Genome / routing / chronology reader lists, plus Evaluator, delivery, retry/critique and Worker facts) live **with their task** (`payload.taskId`):
  - kept while the hive can still decide something about the task (`clotureDe` → `null`): in flight, or done and awaiting review, delivery (`en_cours`/`echouee`) or merge (open PR: the Evaluator gates auto-merge);
  - kept **30 days after closure** (failed; merged; human-rejected without retry; a review or delegated child handed back), even if a dependent keeps the task row alive;
  - dropped with the task (orphans).
- **Facts bounded by their own owner** are never touched: current `council_decided` per kept Council session; last counter-review verdict of each Aiguillage-corpus production (its `producteurModele` is the only proof of the exact model).
- **Hard cap (50,000 rows)**, last resort: closed tasks first (oldest closure), then open tasks idle the longest, **one whole task at a time** (never half a dossier), never the window.

**Owner (`HiveStore.pruneEvents(politique, now)`)**: gathers rows under the window + each cited task's closure from the ranked tables (tasks, livraisons, reviews, contre_expertises, task_delegations), lets `planDeRetention` decide, deletes in batches of 900, in one IMMEDIATE transaction. Returns a `BilanJournal`.

**Journaling the prune**: every pass that removes something emits `journal_elagage` (counts per reason and per type — bounded to 12 types + total, cap-hit tasks bounded to 20 + total) shown in the dashboard Journal (cap and still-open tasks named apart), and adds to the new side table `journal_elagages(type, motif, supprimes, dernierA)`.

**Honest Genome window**: `faitsElagues(types)` replaces the global `journalElague()` for `/api/genome`: "truncated" only when facts of a still-known task were removed (expired or capped), when removals predate the ledger (`avant_registre`, seeded once from `sqlite_sequence` on an existing DB, cleared once pre-upgrade tasks are gone), or when removals are unexplained.

**Cadence**: every 500 new events or hourly (not every tick), so the journal does not narrate its own pruning every 2 s.

**Readers of a larger journal**
- `idx_events_type` + guarded expression index `idx_events_tache` (`json_extract(CASE WHEN json_valid(payload) …)`, so a malformed payload can never break startup). Per-task evidence readers (`latestValidation`, `crossReviewForResult`, `contreRevueImpossible`, `lastEventFor`, `evenementsDeTache`, worker usage) use it.
- Thermal window pinned with `INDEXED BY idx_events_ts` (the planner started preferring the type index and would have re-read all retained outcomes each tick).
- The Aiguillage corpus SQL is now one shared definition for learning and retention, reading the last verdict per production in one grouped pass instead of a correlated subquery per production.
- `/api/projects/:id/essaim/cycles` reads the latest `essaim_cycle` events by type (`evenementsParTypes`) instead of `listEvents(0, 800)`.
- `/api/replay`, `/api/waggle`, `/api/ghost`, `/api/pulse`, `/api/chat` read the window through one helper (`lireJournal`, dedupes four copies of the paging loop) instead of "the first 5,000 from id 0", which would now return sparse old proofs.

**Measured** (bench, 3,500 productions ≈ 43.5k retained events): old per-tick DELETE ~250 ms every 2 s at that scale → new pass ~140 ms per 500 events; per-task lookups 3–7 ms → ~0.05 ms; `observationsAiguillage` ~130–160 ms → ~35–75 ms.

## Decisions taken autonomously

- **One owner, two families**: the window stays 5,000 for traces; proofs follow their task. "Delivered/closed" = failed, merged (`livraisons.etat = 'fusionnee'`), human-rejected without retry, or review/delegated child handed back. An open PR, a failed delivery and an approved-not-delivered task are **not** closed (the Evaluator still reads their evidence).
- **Bounded window = 30 days** after the latest closing fact, equal to `TACHES_RETENTION_MS` (a test locks the equality).
- **Hard cap = 50,000 rows**, removing whole tasks (closed first by closure age, then open by inactivity). A test locks `plafond > fenêtre + CONSEILS_CONSERVES + CORPUS_AIGUILLAGE`. A task that still has proofs **inside the window is never taken by the cap** (the window is untouchable, so taking its below-window proofs would split its dossier). Accepted tradeoff: the cap can be exceeded by the below-window proofs of such tasks until their last proof leaves the window.
- **A human rejection closes only the result it judged**: a `rejected` review older than the task's last update (re-run by a path that does not clear the review) leaves the task open.
- **A PR closed without merge is not a closing fact here**: the stored `livraisons.etat` is only ever `en_cours`/`ouverte`/`echouee`/`fusionnee`; `fermee` exists only in the GitHub-derived view (`shared/retour.ts`). Such a task stays open until `pruneTasks` or the cap; making the table record `fermee` is delivery-batch territory.
- **Genome `tronquee`**: an expired/capped Genome fact keeps the flag on only while a task created before the latest such removal still exists (same rule as `avant_registre`); the tick now runs `pruneEvents` after `pruneTasks`/`pruneConseils` so tasks deleted this tick count as orphans.
- **New side table `journal_elagages`** and **two new indexes**, all `IF NOT EXISTS` at startup, tested on a DB created by the previous schema (already-pruned AUTOINCREMENT journal): index + table created, `avant_registre` seeded once with the exact count, idempotent on reopen. Declared in `tests/bornes-doctrine.test.ts` as bounded by construction (one row per type × reason).
- **Cadence 500 events / 1 h** rather than every tick.
- Evidence events whose payload names no task (e.g. project-level `delivery_merged`) remain traces.

## Tests

- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:dashboard`: green.
- `npx eslint` + `npx prettier --check` on all changed files: clean.
- New `tests/retention-journal.test.ts` (35): pure closure cases; the plan (traces/orphans/expired/kept, ranked facts untouched, cap order and whole-task removal, excess computed on remaining rows); type coverage (every per-task reader's types are proofs, chatter is not); bounded payload; policy inequalities; store owner (open task keeps proofs, closed task expires after 30 days even if kept in table, merge dates closure, orphans, cap never touches the window, ranked facts survi

## Summary

Implements #624: Analyze reasons now carry measured evidence, a new digital-silence check flags gated dialogue stems and proposes VAD, and the CLI gets `pipeline analyze`, `pipeline config`, and `pipeline run --set`.

- `suggest_pipeline_tuning` (`services/pipeline_config.py`): every reason now includes an `evidence` dict (measured values + the threshold compared against); `report_summary.tracks` lists one row per dialogue track's health numbers, even when no reason fires. `pre_aligned` now also carries `suggested_skip_steps: ["align_tracks"]` — a hint that `apply` does not act on (config patches only; `enabled_steps` stays a separate, explicit choice).
- New `digital_silence` check reuses `engines.asr_silence.peak_envelope` to measure the share of a dialogue track's source audio below `transcribe.silence_filter.peak_dbfs` (new `engines/asr_silence.silent_fraction` / `digital_silence_fraction`). At or above `DIGITAL_SILENCE_VAD_FRACTION` (0.8) it flags the track and proposes `transcribe.vad.enabled=true` only when VAD is currently off.
- New `parse_config_assignments` / `config_assignments` in `services/pipeline_config.py` parse and format `path=value` overrides (YAML/JSON scalars and flow values), validated against `ALLOWED_CONFIG_TOP_KEYS` and the shipped defaults (outside free-form `effects.*`).
- CLI (`cli/pipeline.py`):
  - `podcast pipeline run` gains a repeatable `--set path=value` (run-only override, never persisted, same lifetime as `--realign`/`--force`).
  - New `podcast pipeline config [--set ...] [--json]` previews the effective config (defaults + `--set`), `PARAM_FIELDS` values (marked `*` when overridden), and step states — a preview only, no new persistent store.
  - New `podcast pipeline analyze --project P [--set ...] [--json]` runs heuristic Analyze against that config and prints each reason with its evidence, any `suggested_skip_steps`, per-track evidence, and a ready-to-paste `podcast pipeline run ... --set ...` line built from the patches.
- `gui/web/src/types/pipeline.ts`: typed `PipelineAnalyzeReason` (`evidence`, `suggested_skip_steps`); `report_summary.tracks` added to `PipelineAnalyzeResponse`. `PipelinePanel.tsx` is unchanged (still renders `message`).
- Docs: `docs/pipeline.md` (new `--set`/`config`/`analyze` CLI bullets + an Analyze checks table), `docs/gui-integration.md`, `docs/audio-engineering.md`, and the `podcast-pipeline-tune` / `podcast-pipeline-run` skills.

**Note:** `scripts/check_progress.py` lists `pipeline.analyze` / `pipeline.config` as warn-mode "unexempted", the same as the existing `pipeline_analyze_tool`. No exemption was added — that needs explicit user approval per `docs/progress.md`.

author: mandakan
body:
Closes #1072.

`/api/sync/fingerprints` returned `(doc_count, version_sum)`. A hosted delete of a v1 doc plus an insert of another v1 doc between two polls left both unchanged, so the desktop didn't pull the new doc.

**Change.**
- `sync.state.versions_digest(versions)`: 16 hex chars of sha256 over the sorted `identity=version` lines. `local_fingerprint` returns `(count, sum, digest)` from `doc_versions`.
- Hosted: `ProjectStateStore.list_doc_versions` (identities and versions, no payloads) replaces the grouped `list_fingerprints`. The route builds per-match maps keyed by `doc_identity_key` (the same keys `doc_versions` uses) and adds `digest`.
- Client: `get_fingerprints` returns the triple when `digest` is present, the pair otherwise.
- Driver: compares the pair only when hosted sent no digest, so a desktop on this release against an older hosted doesn't see a phantom difference. An older desktop ignores the new field.

**Tests.** The route returns the digest the desktop computes for the same docs; the digest differs for the delete-plus-insert swap while count and sum match (the case in the issue); a digest-only change triggers a pull; a digest-less hosted compares on the pair.

Merge note: #1090 (the `/fingerprints` 404 fallback) computes a pair from manifests. Whichever lands second gets rebased so the fallback also produces the digest.

author: pobed2
body:
### WHY are these changes introduced?

`shopify app deploy` reports unchanged events configuration as updated when a subscription omits `api_version` and inherits `[events].api_version`. The server stores the inherited version on each subscription, while the CLI compares it with a local config that still omits the field.

### WHAT is this pull request doing?

Resolve inherited subscription versions in the existing local-to-remote events transform, alongside relative URI resolution. Deploy comparison and upload then use the same effective versions as the server, without modifying the local TOML or requiring a server change.

Explicit overrides remain intact. Regression tests cover unchanged inherited and explicit versions, changing or removing an override, and changing the default version.

### How to manually test your changes?

Use an app whose TOML sets `[events].api_version` and omits `api_version` on an event subscription:

```sh
pnpm shopify app deploy --path /path/to/app
pnpm shopify app deploy --path /path/to/app
```

The second deploy should show no events update. Setting a different subscription version, or removing an override that differs from the default, should still show an update.

### Checklist

- [ ] I've considered possible cross-platform impacts (Mac, Linux, Windows)
- [ ] I've considered possible [documentation](https://shopify.dev) changes
- [ ] I've considered analytics changes to measure impact
- [x] The change is user-facing — I've identified the correct [bump type](https://github.com/Shopify/cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#choosing-the-right-bump-type) (`patch` for bug fixes · `minor` for new features · `major` for [breaking changes](https://github.com/Shopify/cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#what-counts-as-a-breaking-change)) and added a changeset

author: h0verin
body:
## Problem

The LC76G on the -G variant can wedge: its I2C output stops and the driver sees `chars=0` indefinitely (socquique/capsule-radar#24). The only known cure has been a full power cycle, because:

- the module's `VCC` is the board's main 3V3 rail, so an OTA update, **Save & restart**, or any soft reboot never power-cycles it; and
- `gps_poll()` only drains while "Use GPS for location" is ticked, so switching it off lets the module's NMEA queue overflow, which is the #24 wedge.

Before this change it wedged on my device after an OTA-update session, and it took a USB unplug plus power-off to recover.

## What the schematic offers

From the official [Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75 schematic](https://files.waveshare.com/wiki/ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75/ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75.pdf):

- LC76G `RESET` (pin 9) is on net `GPS_RST`, which goes to **EXIO7 (P7) of the TCA9554 I/O expander at 0x20** (A0–A2 tied to GND). The firmware never touched it.
- The other EXIO pins are **inputs**: P3 `RTC_INT`, P4 `SYS_OUT`, P5 `AXP_IRQ`, P6 `QMI_INT1`. So only P7 is ever changed, with a read-modify-write of the output (0x01) and config (0x03) registers.
- `V_BCKP` is on `VCC-RTC`, which stays up, so ephemeris survives a reset and the module restarts hot.

## Changes

**1. Hardware reset (`src/gps.cpp`, expander defines in `src/boards/board_amoled_175.h`)**
- Pulse `RESET` low for 100 ms **at every boot**. That catches a module that wedged before an OTA or soft reboot.
- Pulse it again **whenever no NMEA has arrived for 30 s**, at most once a minute. This covers a module that stops mid-run, and "Use GPS" being switched back on after the module sat undrained.
- Release by returning P7 to an input, its power-on state (the module's own pull-up holds `RESET` high), with a retry so `RESET` is never left asserted.
- Boards that don't define `I2C_ADDR_EXPANDER` (the 1.43) compile the reset out.

**2. Less NMEA over I2C**
- Adds the Quectel I2C **write** path: free-space query at `0x50`/`0x54` (`04 00 51 AA …`), length announcement at `0x50` (`00 10 53 AA` + len), then the command bytes to `0x58`. It uses the same 100 ms settles as the existing read path. The sequence matches two independent LC76G drivers ([LC76G_Pico](https://github.com/musicaJack/LC76G_Pico), a port of the vendor demo, and [opendash](https://github.com/landracer/opendash), an ESP32 driver for this board).
- Once per reset, it sends `$PAIR062,{1,2,3,5},0` in **a single write**, which turns off GLL, GSA, GSV and VTG. TinyGPS++ only reads GGA and RMC, so the other sentences were pure I2C volume: GSV bursts are what overflowed the queue in #24, and they lengthened every blocking drain on the core that serves the web page.
- `$PAIR001,062,0` replies are counted from the stream and logged. It retries up to 3 times per reset. Writes stay rare because opendash reports that about 88 cumulative command writes can corrupt the module's parser.

**3. Diagnostics:**
- The `[gps]` status line gains `resets=`.
- Every reset checks itself: the TCA9554 input register (0x00) reports the real pin level even for an output, so P7 is read back while `RESET` is held (expect LOW: the writes reached P7 and it drives the line) and after release (expect HIGH: the module's pull-up took it back), then logged as `[gps] reset pulse: P7 low=ok released=ok`.

## Testing (1.75 with GPS, OTA-installed)

```
[gps] reset via expander; module answered after 401 ms
[gps] LC76G detected on I2C
[gps] sentence config (GGA+RMC only) sent: ok, try 1/3
[gps] sentence config acked (4/4)
[gps] chars=2557 sent=6 csErr=0 sats=14 fix=1 resets=1
```

- Identical results across two boots: 401 ms to answer, config acknowledged 4 of 4 on the first try, and a fix 7–17 s after boot (indoors).
- NMEA volume: default output scales with the satellites in view (GSV). With 25 in view it was about **9.2 KB per 8 s**; with GGA+RMC only it's about **1.3 KB per 8 s** (roughly 86% less), still `csErr=0`. Indoors with 0 satellites the default was about 3.5–4.5 KB per 8 s.
- **Stall recovery:** I unticked "Use GPS", waited 2+ minutes and re-ticked it, without restarting:
  ```
  [gps] no NMEA for 142 s: resetting the module
  [gps] sentence config (GGA+RMC only) sent: ok, try 1/3
  [gps] sentence config acked (4/4)
  [gps] chars=24467 sent=254 csErr=0 sats=21 fix=1 resets=2
  ```
- Both the 1.75 and 1.43 environments build.

**Reproducing the wedge, then clearing it with only the reset:** I used a local diagnostic build (not part of this PR) with the automatic resets disabled, the default NMEA output restored, a manual reset URL, and per-read outcome counters (`rd=` data/empty/dead):

1. **Baseline:** a manual reset on a healthy module logged `P7 low=ok released=ok`. `sats` went 25 → 0 → 24 over about 30 s (a real restart; the fix returned within seconds thanks to `V_BCKP`).
2. **Wedge:** with "Use GPS" off for 10 minutes and then back on, the leftover queue drained (about 6 KB) and then the module **stayed wedged, answering I2C but with nothing queued**:
   ```
   [gps] chars=365217 sent=661 csErr=0 sats=22 fix=1 resets=1 rd=0/4/0(data/empty/dead) lastdata=28s
   ...
   [gps] chars=365217 sent=661 csErr=0 sats=22 fix=0 resets=1 rd=0/4/0(data/empty/dead) lastdata=124s
   ```
   It answers, so v1.4.3's dead-module backoff never sees it. That's why this PR triggers on *no data*, not on *no answer*.
3. **Recovery with only the reset**, after 2 minutes wedged:
   ```
   [gps] reset pulse: P7 low=ok released=ok
   [gps] chars=367235 sent=661 csErr=0 sats=0 fix=0 resets=2 rd=2/2/0(data/empty/dead) lastdata=0s
   [gps] chars=374433 sent=674 csErr=0 sats=17 fix=1 resets=2 rd=4/0/0(data/empty/dead) lastdata=0s
   ```
   Data returned within about 5 s and a fix within about 13 s, with no power cycle.

**Not tested:**
- A 1.75 **without** GPS. It should just probe, find no module, and wait at most 1.5 s (`GPS_BOOT_WAIT_MS`) once at boot.
- A single OTA update (about 16 s without draining) did *not* wedge the module in my testing. The wedge I originally hit came after a longer OTA/reboot session. The boot-time reset covers that path regardless.

**Blocking cost** (on the loop core, like the existing drains): about 0.4 s at boot on -G boards, a 100 ms pulse per runtime reset, and about 300 ms per config write (once per reset).

Based on v1.4.5 (after socquique/capsule-radar#28). I tested it on hardware together with that fix.

Text, surfaces, focus rings and the other controls keep the system colors, and orange is removed from the scene palette so it only marks the playhead. ```css /* fframes-editor/src/main.css */ --color-brand: #fb6a22; /* IconButton.Brand → play/pause */ --color-brand-hover: #e25507; ``` ```rust // fframes-native-player/src/controls.rs: play button, played range and thumb ring const BRAND: Color = Color::from_rgb(0xfb, 0x6a, 0x22); ``` ### Web editor - System font stack; the bundled Inter and Virgil fonts are removed - Colors, radii, type scale and shadows come from the SDK tokens (`bg-surface`, `text-secondary`, …); no gradients - Light and dark follow the OS, and the timeline canvases use the same palette (`Theme.res`) - ChatGPT's monochrome icons are bound from ReScript (`Icons.res`); esbuild drops the unused ones (+25 KB of JS) - The dock is a floating pill of round ghost buttons with one solid primary action (`IconButton.res`). Every control has a label and a tooltip that shows its shortcut. - Media thumbnails are `` with alt text and `object-cover` - The back/forward buttons now use `rewindStepInSeconds` (they were hardcoded to 2 s and their labels were swapped); the speaker icon toggles mute ```ts renderEditor(bridge, { theme: "dark" }); // "system" (default) | "light" | "dark" ``` ### Native player The thin red progress bar and pause glyph are replaced by a Skia-drawn control bar with the same icons and dark tokens: back, play/pause, forward, time, seek slider, loop and full screen (`f`). While playing it hides after 2.5 s without mouse movement. ```mermaid flowchart LR resize[Presenter::resize] --> layout[ControlsLayout] layout -->|draw| canvas[Skia canvas] layout -->|hit / progress_at| app[App pointer events] app --> state[ControlsState] --> canvas ``` ### Landing page and brand `landing/` is a static page: the motion trail logo, a light editorial layout with film grain, the demo video, and a get started section (`npx skills add dmtrKovalenko/fframes` or `cargo fframes new`). | Landing | Link preview | App icon | |---|---|---| | ![](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/blob/pr-assets/chatgpt-design/landing.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/blob/pr-assets/chatgpt-design/brand-og.png?raw=true) | ![](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fframes/blob/pr-assets/chatgpt-design/brand-icon.png?raw=true) | - `landing/brand/` has the outlined SVG wordmarks, favicons (`.ico` and PNG), app and maskable icons, the X header and avatar, and Open Graph and GitHub social preview images - Link-preview tags need absolute URLs once the page has a domain (marked `TODO`) ### Tooling - `just run ` no longer loops: `cargo watch` now ignores the `pkg/` output of `wasm-pack`

body:
## 背景

堆叠在 #106 之上，继续 Opus Tier-2 复验修复序列。本 PR 落地 Medium 项 B-5。

## 变更

`extend()` 之前只看 DB 里的 `status` 列，一个 TTL 已经到期但还没被 `sweep_expired` 扫描到的预留（`status` 依然是 `'active'`）会被当成正常预留续期——这会让一个逻辑上已经失效的预留重新复活。现在额外检查 `expires_at_ms <= now_ms`，命中就按 `ReservationNotActive` 拒绝。

新增两个上限：
- 单次 `extend` 的 `additional_ttl_ms` 不能超过这个 ledger 自己的 `ttl_ms`——一次续期最多给和一次全新 `reserve` 一样长的时间，不能无限续。
- 预留从 `created_at_ms` 到续期后的新 `expires_at_ms`，总寿命不能超过 4×`ttl_ms`——限制能连续 `extend` 的次数，不能靠反复续期让一个预留（和它占用的额度）无限期活下去。

`find_reservation` 补上 `created_at_ms` 字段（之前只在 `INSERT` 里写，读取时没选出来）。两个新上限都复用已有的 `InvalidTtl` 错误变体，`checked_mul`/`checked_add` 防止 4x 乘法和加法溢出。

新增三个测试：已过期但未 `sweep` 的预留续期被拒绝；单次超过 `ttl_ms` 被拒绝、恰好等于 `ttl_ms` 放行；连续 4 次合法续期后，第 5 次会把总寿命推过 4×`ttl_ms` 而被拒绝（精确推演了每一步的时钟/过期时间数值）。同步修正既有的 `extend` 测试（原来一次性续期 10 倍 `ttl_ms` 现在会被单次上限拒绝，改成分两步：先推进时钟到接近原定过期时间，再用单次上限内的续期把新过期时间推到原过期时间之后）。

## 精确行数

2 files changed，113 行。

## 机械门禁

```
$ bash idoris-precheck.sh origin/fix14-b6-b7-gate-semantics
✅ 工作区干净
✅ 改动 113 行 ≤300
✅ 未发现密钥模式
✅ 无 todo!/unimplemented!/dbg!
✅ 提交署名齐全
✅ cargo fmt
✅ cargo clippy -D warnings
✅ cargo test
✅ cargo deny
PRECHECK=PASS
```

定级：`GRADE=B`（113 净改动行 >100），3 轮评审。

## 评审：本地模型评审（Codex 不可用，额度耗尽至 2026-10-04）——3 轮

**第 1 轮·正确性**：总寿命上限测试的每一步时钟/过期时间数值都手工推演过（第 4 次续期落在 3997ms，第 5 次会推到 4996ms，超过 4000ms 的上限），实际跑测试验证过数值吻合；单次上限的边界值（恰好 `ttl_ms` vs `ttl_ms+1`）分别有正负测试。

**第 2 轮·溢出安全**：`self.ttl_ms.checked_mul(4)` 和 `row.created_at_ms.checked_add(max_lifetime_ms)` 都做了溢出检查，映射到 `InvalidTtl`/`InvalidTimestamp` 而不是 panic。

**第 3 轮·检查顺序**：`additional_ttl_ms` 的范围校验在查库之前就做（不合法输入不产生数据库往返）；"状态/是否已过期"的检查先于"总寿命上限"检查，所以一个已过期的预留会拿到 `ReservationNotActive` 而不是被总寿命上限的错误掩盖，优先级符合直觉。

结论：3 轮均未发现需要修复的问题。

body:
Phase 2 of the UI plan: the dashboard now knows which car is yours and uses it everywhere. Four commits, one per part.

## 1. Store the player's car (`c5c41b8`)
- Migration 6 adds `sessions.player_car_index` (nullable), set from `PacketHeader.PlayerCarIndex` when a session starts (null while spectating).
- Old sessions are **not backfilled**: they stay null and fall back to the comparator's saved driver name.
- Export/import carry it; a re-save never clears a stored value.

## 2. List summaries and the player's debrief (`de36736`)
- `GET /api/sessions` returns `SessionListItem`: the session plus a `summary` (leader, fastest lap, laps completed, and `player`: position, grid, places gained, best lap, DNF/DSQ). `?driver=` finds you in old sessions; `player.source` says how you were found.
- Participants and laps for every listed session load in two queries (~50 ms warm for 32 sessions).
- The AI session debrief leads with your result, marks your line `(YOU)` and always includes the cars around you.

## 3. UI (`66af08a`)
- Session list: a "Your result" column/card row; the format badge shows only when it differs from the rest.
- Session detail: highlighted YOU row, a "Your race" card (result, grid, best lap and gap, pit stops, cars ahead/behind, compare with the fastest lap), and charts that start with you and the cars around you.
- Comparator: defaults to your best lap, and waits for the session list so both slots can't pick the same lap.

## 4. Progress page (`306d855`)
- `GET /api/progress?track=&driver=` and a new `/progress[/:track]` page with its own nav tab: personal best, theoretical best, gap to each session's fastest lap and consistency (std dev of clean laps), charted over time with a session-type filter, plus a sessions table (cards on phones).
- The nav now fits four tabs on tablets and phones.

README and `.agents/AGENTS.md` cover the new API fields and the route; wire types are regenerated.

## Testing
- `gofmt`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues), `go run ./cmd/tsgen -check`, `go test ./...`
- Frontend: lint, 832 tests, build
- Browser checks at 1440, 768 and 375 px against a copy of a real database: an old session found by driver name, a simulator session with a stored car, and the fallback with no saved name.

## Known, unchanged
- When you set the session's fastest lap, the comparator's "next fastest lap" rule for slot B can pick your own second lap.

author: patshub65
body:
Closes #112

## Summary

The `ActionFeedbackProvider` toast was pinned at a hardcoded `safe-area-inset-bottom + 5.75rem` offset that tracked nothing, and it covered the map sheet's "N flares near you" header in the mini and peek states.

- Added `--sponti-bottom-occupied`: the distance from the viewport bottom to the top of whatever is docked at the bottom, published on the document root the same way `BottomNav` publishes `--sponti-nav-h`.
- The map view (`spa/components/map-view.tsx`) is the only writer, via a small pure `bottomOccupiedCss(state)` helper:
  - **mini**: nav height + mini sheet height (sheet sits above the nav)
  - **peek**: just the peek sheet's own height (it sits at `bottom: 0`, so the nav is already behind/inside it)
  - **expanded**: just the nav height (the toast floats above the nav rather than fighting the tall sheet for space)
  - Resets the variable on unmount so other routes fall back cleanly to `--sponti-nav-h`.
- `ActionFeedbackProvider`'s toast container (`spa/components/action-feedback.tsx`) now reads `calc(var(--sponti-bottom-occupied, var(--sponti-nav-h, 64px)) + 12px)` instead of the old fixed `5.75rem` offset. No safe-area term is added separately since `--sponti-nav-h` already bakes it in (see `BottomNav`'s own comment).

Out of scope, unchanged: toast look/copy/duration/z-index, map sheet heights/snap behaviour.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npm run test` — 25 files / 210 tests pass (207 pre-existing + 3 new for `bottomOccupiedCss`)
- [ ] Manual: post a flare on the map with the sheet in peek — toast sits above the sheet's top edge
- [ ] Manual: same in mini
- [ ] Manual: sheet expanded — toast sits just above the bottom nav
- [ ] Manual: calendar/circles/settings — toast sits just above the bottom nav
- [ ] Manual: navigate away from map — no stale sheet offset lingers on other routes

<!-- Branch flow: feature/* → develop, and only develop → main. -->

## What & why

The knowledge-base structure block in the understanding prompt (`render_knowledge_base_structure()` in `app/agent/prompts.py`) listed every field, then repeated the limited-value fields in a separate list with all their values. This PR merges the two:

- Each field's values now appear on that field's own line, after `Values:` (still separated by semicolons, since some values contain commas).
- `item_type`, `category`, `category_slug` and `category_path` no longer list their values there (new `LISTED_VALUE_FIELDS`). The item-type line and the group/category tree further down already name every one of them, and `category_slug` is only `category` in kebab-case.
- The `dietary_tags` and `portion_unit` descriptions no longer hard-code their values, which now come from the corpus.

The result is a shorter prompt with no repeated values, still built from the live corpus so it cannot drift from the data (rule K-01).

## How to verify

- `uv run pytest`: 424 passed.
- `tests/test_catalog.py`: the structure-block test now checks that values sit on each field's own line, and a new test checks that values the tree already names (including category slugs) are not repeated.
- `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .` and `uv run mypy scripts app` pass.

**Not verified live:** this changes the understanding prompt, so it changes model behaviour. It has not been run against Groq, and `notebooks/03_evaluation.ipynb` sections 5–8 have not been re-run.

- [x] Target branch is correct (`feature/* → develop`; `develop → main` only)

- [x] `uv run mypy scripts` passes (plus `app` once it exists)

body:
Parent: #5679

`e2e/login-sent-state.spec.ts` asserted `expect(errors).toEqual([])` over every console error the page emitted. Under `page.clock.install()` the real Turnstile widget — the only third-party script on /login — mis-measures time and logs `"%c%d font-size:0;color:transparent NaN"` from `challenges.cloudflare.com`, failing the spec on both widths (run 36339331784) with noise the app does not own. The collector now records `{text, url}` per `console-clean.spec.ts`'s paved shape and drops entries whose URL origin differs from the page's; an entry with no source URL still counts, and `pageerror` stays unfiltered.

## Changes
- `e2e/login-sent-state.spec.ts:7-14` — `errors: string[]` splits into `consoleErrors: {text, url}[]` (records `message.location().url`) and `pageErrors: string[]`; the pageerror listener is unchanged apart from the target array.
- `e2e/login-sent-state.spec.ts:43-50` — the gate filters `consoleErrors` to entries with an empty URL or an origin equal to `new URL(page.url()).origin`, maps survivors to `"text @ url"`, appends `pageErrors`, and labels the assertion with `testInfo.project.name` since it runs at two widths.

## Verification
- Reproduction before the change (`PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_BASE_URL=https://0509.io npm run e2e -- e2e/login-sent-state.spec.ts`): red at the assertion — `+ "%c%d font-size:0;color:transparent NaN"` ×2 on desktop-1440 and phone-390 across all retries; a temporary print showed 12/12 error entries carried `message.location().url` on origin `https://challenges.cloudflare.com` (issue's step-2 stop condition checked: not 0509.io).
- Acceptance after the change, same command: `Running 3 tests using 2 workers / 3 passed (4.3s)`.
- Negative check (local, reverted): injecting `page.evaluate(() => console.error("deliberate same-origin error"))` before the gate failed the test with `"deliberate same-origin error @ "` — the entry carried an empty location URL and the `!entry.url` guard kept it, so a real app-side error still cannot pass.
- `npx eslint e2e/login-sent-state.spec.ts`: no output, exit 0.
- Diff-scoped semgrep `--config p/default --baseline-commit $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)`: no findings, exit 0.
- §C1: no workaround (rejects only proven foreign-origin entries), no comments added, no second path (the collector shape is copied from `console-clean.spec.ts`, which never runs under `page.clock` and needs no change).

run-proof: the playwright output above (3 passed against https://0509.io at head d26cb41c), plus eslint and semgrep exits 0 on the diff.
in-run review: litellm/senior (same-family review — xai-oauth grok-4.6:high returned 402 balance exhausted); pass 1 0 findings.

encoded: codebase (rung 1) — the same-origin gate lives in the spec itself: any console error attributable to 0509.io (or to no origin) still fails the test at both widths, while `challenges.cloudflare.com` noise under the mocked clock cannot.

Closes #5682
