author: skibkitty
body:
Reverts #37 (`2fa53c3`) and returns `main` to its state before the notification
service was merged.

## Why

#37 was merged without a human reviewing or approving it, which is not a
decision an agent should make on its own. The work itself was not wrong —
CI was green on it — but merging is a human decision, and the branch
protection that should have stopped this (`required_status_check:
build-and-test`, `enforce_admins: true`) is there now.

## What this does and does not do

**Does:** remove the notification service and its docs from `main`, restoring
the pre-merge tree exactly (`git diff 666d4a3 e80dd16` is empty).

**Does not:** erase the merge from history. `2fa53c3` stays on `main`; this
adds a revert commit on top of it. That is inherent to a revert and is why
it is a reviewable PR rather than a history rewrite.

## Sequencing — read before merging

This PR is the first half of a two-PR change. It is **not** meant to leave
`main` without the notification service for long:

1. **This PR** — revert #37. After it merges, `main` is back to the
   pre-merge state.
2. **#39** — re-lands #11 with the three review findings already addressed
   (bounded pagination, Kafka topic ownership, loopback-only port
   bindings), plus the original work. It is already open; it only needs to
   be brought up to date with this revert, because it currently branches
   from `666d4a3` and so conflicts with `main` until this lands.

So this is not a decision that the notification service should not exist —
it is unwinding an unreviewed merge so the reviewed version can land in its
place. If you would rather not have the intermediate state at all, closing
this and landing a fixes-only PR against `main` is the alternative.

## Verification

This revert restores a tree that was previously green: `666d4a3` passed
`mvn verify` (236 tests) and this PR's tree is identical to it. CI will
confirm.

author: turer73
body:
## Why

Follow-up to the Codex review on #523, which completed after that PR was merged. All six findings (1 P1, 5 P2) were verified against master and are fixed here.

## What changes

**Migration 214 (`community-quality@2`, no threshold, floor or version change).**

- **P1, retention.** 213 retained an already taken quarantine or confirmation only inside the branch where the gated and ungated decisions differed. Contrary model evidence (or lost reporter trust) can lower **both** rules to `suspected`; that branch was skipped, `compute_question_quality_consensus` returned `suspected` for a quarantined case, and `record_question_quality_consensus` raised `cannot regress automatically` from the call the worker makes outside its catch block. The same gap existed for `confirmed` cases once the ungated rule no longer said `confirmed`. Retention is now keyed on the previous state alone: confirmed stays confirmed (terminal); quarantined stays quarantined unless the new decision is quarantine or confirmed. Lifting stays a human decision. `modelGate` still says `held_for_human_review` only when the gate changed a decision, and `retained_existing_action` only when retention did.
- **P2, exact thresholds.** 213 rounded `posterior_without_model` to nine decimals before comparing it, so a value just below a boundary could be rounded onto it (`0.9799999996` → `0.980000000` permits quarantine). Decisions now use the exact value; only the snapshot field is rounded, so the recorded rationale stays bounded and the snapshot keys are unchanged.

`src/lib/question-quality/consensus.ts` (the TypeScript policy spec) applies the same retention rule.

**`scan-question-text-defects.mjs`** (four P2 findings):

| Finding | Fix |
|---|---|
| bare `şekilde` ("olacak şekilde") reported as a missing figure at error severity | `figure_reference_without_media` matches only demonstrative references: `şekildeki`, `yukarıdaki tabloda`, `grafikte verilen`, `Şekil 1`, `ok yönünde`; bare nouns and topic mentions (`Grafik nedir?`) no longer match |
| `Mn`, `Zn`, `Cu`, `Kc`, `Aa` reported as mid-sentence capitals | rule requires three letters; two-letter mixed-case tokens are element symbols, genotypes or constants |
| option strings not scanned for lost superscripts | `superscript_loss` also runs over each option |
| superscript rule disabled for the whole `fen` game | skipped only for category `kimya` (reaction equations such as `2H2 + O2`); `fizik` and `biyoloji` expressions like `x2+y2=1` are caught. Categories are stored lowercase (`fizik`/`kimya`/`biyoloji`) |

## Verification

- `question-content-governance-postgres.integration.test.mjs` on a disposable PostgreSQL 16 with the full chain plus 214: **15/15**. The gate scenario now continues with a `supports_clean` verification on the quarantined case and asserts `ungatedDecision: suspected`, `decision: quarantine`, `modelGate: retained_existing_action`, and that `record_question_quality_consensus` returns `quarantined` without raising.
- **Mutation check:** with 214 removed from the chain, exactly that scenario fails (1 failed | 14 passed).
- New SQL contract test for 214 (5 tests); 2 new TS spec tests (contrary model evidence on a quarantined case; confirmed stays confirmed); 4 scan tests updated or added for the false-positive cases above.
- `npm run test:db` 686 passed; `npm test` 4360 passed; eslint on changed files, `tsc --noEmit` and `lint:migrations` clean. Pre-commit and pre-push hooks passed.

## Branch note

The head branch of #523 was auto-deleted after the squash merge, so this branch was recreated from its last tip with `origin/master` merged in (`8b37816`, tree identical to master) and the fix on top. Merge-base with master is `2f40223`; the diff is only this change.

## Rollout

Apply 214 after 212/213. It replaces only `compute_question_quality_consensus`; no data migration, no worker change.

body:
This pull request introduces the full booking window ("slot") management API, including controller, DTOs, repository, and service contract changes. It enables CRUD operations for booking windows on microgrid nodes, exposes endpoints for both operators and backoffice, and adds supporting data access and business rule hooks. It also adds activate/deactivate endpoints for nodes and extends the reservation query interface for referential integrity checks.

**Booking window (slot) management API:**

* Added new `SlotsController` with endpoints for creating, updating, deleting, and querying booking windows (slots) on nodes, including role-based authorization and detailed documentation. (`SlotsController.cs`)
* Introduced DTOs for slot creation, update, and response: `SlotCreateRequest`, `SlotUpdateRequest`, and `SlotResponse`, with validation and clear separation of client-editable and server-managed fields. (`SlotCreateRequest.cs`, `SlotUpdateRequest.cs`, `SlotResponse.cs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9e5e5d92b62d3d86282fd219231b7d497ee03fceba2cb9a2075e77ee2fffdec9R1-R38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b7d9784d69dd30c65b86490d69df455fc7d0f7e9e78c91348760391c0a23e193R1-R35) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4ebf1e7541839d6a57f919183357eb213ffae50f1f3a5c7a48798f31c432a1d2R1-R59)
* Registered the new `ISlotService` and its implementation in DI. (`Program.cs`)

**Repository and data access:**

* Extended `ISlotRepository` with methods for finding, inserting, updating, and deleting booking windows, as well as advanced queries for overlaps and bookable slots. (`ISlotRepository.cs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ab793ff811842707a615fdc0c70b96d790758e35166a6d9d36919d5aedeb78ebL5-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ab793ff811842707a615fdc0c70b96d790758e35166a6d9d36919d5aedeb78ebR30-R56)
* Implemented the new repository methods in `SlotRepository`, including efficient MongoDB queries for all new use cases. (`SlotRepository.cs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0236c18bbfbf65772cfce0b3fea819bf7d7352429a06cbae6d1d8bf893139f17L6-R8) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0236c18bbfbf65772cfce0b3fea819bf7d7352429a06cbae6d1d8bf893139f17R72-R209)

**Node activation/deactivation:**

* Added `Deactivate` and `Activate` endpoints to `NodesController` and corresponding service methods, with business rules to prevent deactivation if active reservations exist. (`NodesController.cs`, `INodeService.cs`) [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9473724c5ef4cd457e20417891d86106143c06d9dc31bb55c0e2791ab0b625efR76-R98) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8add3187270ac05f2419829a5c27e65304c9144307a92535663971db8fbebd88R30-R38)

**Reservation referential checks:**

* Extended `IReservationQueries` with a method to count all reservations referencing a slot, supporting safe slot deletion. (`IReservationQueries.cs`)

These changes establish the foundation for booking window management, enforce business rules at the service layer, and ensure safe modification and removal of slots and nodes.

## Summary

Implements the STEM AI Portfolio Agent for the Axioms AI System.

The agent creates a reviewable portfolio case-study blueprint for academic and industry audiences. It translates author-supplied, verified research evidence into:

- Repository structure and documentation plan
- README sections with evidence-to-claim traceability
- Reproducibility and test checklist
- Dataset-provenance and public-release checks
- Evidence-bound impact summary
- DOCX export
- FastAPI endpoints, Streamlit controls, and Axioms Core routing support

## Governance and safety controls

- Portfolio claims require an author-verified evidence record and source reference.
- The agent does not infer novelty, performance, publication, citation, GitHub-star, H-index, or impact claims.
- Public repository plans reject proprietary, restricted, and unknown-access data.
- Public and de-identified datasets require recorded licence/permission and attribution.
- Reproducibility planning includes pinned dependencies, deterministic controls, tests, provenance, expected outputs, and limitations.
- API keys, credentials, student data, unpublished material, and non-public data are explicitly excluded from public portfolio packages.
- The agent cannot create, modify, push to, or publish a GitHub repository. Explicit human approval is required before any external repository action.

## API

- `POST /portfolio-packages`
- `POST /portfolio-packages/docx`

## Validation

- 47 tests pass.
- Ruff linting passes with no issues.
- The deployment ZIP archive passed integrity verification.

author: noallrightokay
body:
## What

New mail now appears within seconds of arriving. Before this it could take up to five minutes, because RATA only checked on a timer.

**Engine (`rata-mail`)**
- `watch(resolver, acct)` signs in, checks the server supports IDLE, and opens the inbox. It returns a `Watch`, which reads no messages and keeps no password.
- `Watch::wait(IDLE_FOR)` waits up to nine minutes per round, well inside the 29 minutes servers allow, and reports one of:
  - `Arrived` or `Quiet`: the connection stays open for the next wait;
  - `Unsupported`, `Auth`, `Host` or `Net`: the connection is gone.
- `idle_until` wakes only when the inbox grows past what it held. It tracks the message count down on EXPUNGE and up on EXISTS.
- Any other server news, such as a flag change, starts a fresh IDLE instead. This matters because RATA marks messages read over its other connection; without it, every read would trigger a refresh.

**App**
- `watch.rs` checks once a minute which mailboxes to watch, using `Rata::watchable`:
  - every linked mailbox not set aside for a refused password;
  - none at all without a licence, so a lapsed licence or an unlinked mailbox closes its connection.
- `Rata::watch` runs the same checks as a refresh (`readable`). A refused password sets the mailbox aside the same way a refresh does, so a wrong password is never sent twice.
- A failed connection is retried after 30 s, doubling each time up to 15 minutes. A server without IDLE isn't tried again until RATA restarts.
- When new mail arrives, Rust calls the page's `window.__rataMail({email})`, passing a JSON literal, the same way links do.

**Interface**
- `__rataMail` waits 1.2 s so a burst of mail is one refresh, then runs `autoSync`. That is the same quiet refresh as the 5-minute timer, so fetching, display and notifications are still handled in one place.
- A wake that comes in during a refresh (`MAIL_AGAIN`) gets exactly one more refresh afterwards.

The 5-minute refresh keeps running regardless. A server without IDLE, a connection lost when a laptop sleeps, or any other failure here only makes mail slower, never lost.

## Version

0.1.34 in `tauri.conf.json` (version and window title), `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`. The `sw.js` cache is bumped to v37. CLAUDE.md, README and BETA are updated.

## Checked

- Engine tests: 175 pass. Four new ones run against a scripted IMAP server:
  - new mail wakes the watch and keeps the connection;
  - a flag change doesn't wake it, and it starts a fresh IDLE;
  - one message removed and another added counts as new mail;
  - a server without IDLE isn't watched and has no folder opened.
- App tests: 61 pass. `watchable` and `watch` return nothing when unlicensed, unknown or set aside for a refused password. Clippy is clean.
- Desktop harness (`beta-fixes.mjs`):
  - a burst of wakes makes one refresh;
  - that refresh brings the mail and sends a notification;
  - a wake during a refresh gets exactly one more;
  - without a licence, a wake fetches nothing.
- The website suite passes.
- The packaged build launches as "RATA 0.1.34 beta".

Not tested against a real mail server. The network guard refuses private addresses, so no local IMAP server can stand in.

body:
**PILLAR: MATCHING · SHIP:** an NHL game stops appearing on two days. `/search?q=golden knights` stops showing Chicago @ Vegas a second time ("Sep 30 2:30 PM · 71/29").

Refs #9187, refs #2693. (Issue stays open until the after-check on production.)

## What was wrong
The Odds API lists **two** Chicago @ Vegas events: its real `deceabd9…` (2026-09-30T02:40Z) and a phantom `ec5a4b4a…` at **21:30:10Z**. ESPN lists **one** game (401891775, 02:30Z = the 29th in ET). Our row 15320181 mirrors the phantom (no ESPN id, no markets), so search printed the game on two days. Ruling 048 correctly created it (no shared id); nothing labelled it afterwards.

## The change
- `utils/mlb_reschedule_ghosts.py`: new **adjacent-day arm** (off unless the caller asks). ESPN lists the pair exactly once on D and exactly one row carries that game's id, dated D. ESPN's board for D±1 must be **read and non-empty** and list **no** game for the pair in either orientation. The one same-home/same-away row on that day must have no ESPN id and no score. When all of that holds, the row gets the existing `provenance:duplicate-of:<canonical>` label. Postseason and unreadable season types are never asked. `BoardGame` now carries ESPN's `season.type`.
- `tasks/mlb_reschedule_ghost_sweep.py`: takes `sport_key`; `ADJACENT_DAY_SPORTS = {icehockey_nhl}`. New task `nhl_adjacent_day_ghost_sweep`, beat `nhl-adjacent-day-ghost-sweep` hourly :56 on `background`, enrolled in the task-verdict contract. It uses the same fold guard, the same D51 backup table and the same undo: `python3 scripts/restore_8547_mlb_reschedule_ghost_tags.py --apply`.
- The background census was **run** on the branch and printed `explicit 89 implicit 43 total 132`; pins moved to match.

## Reach, measured on production rows (read-only) + live ESPN boards, −7d/+3d
- NHL, arm on: 74 rows, 66 board games, 66 anchored → **1 label: 15320181 → 15168035**. Arm off: 0.
- MLB control, arm forced on: 129 rows, 115 board games → **0 labels** (the ALWC games 1/2/3 are all on ESPN's boards; the postseason gate is tested separately).
- Checked the only other future Odds API event with a non-zero-second clock (Carolina v Florida 21:00:47Z): it is real (ESPN 401891773) and is a single row. So seconds are **not** a phantom signal and the rule doesn't use them.

## Gates
- Focused band: every `tests/` file that names `beat_schedule` (90) + the four ghost suites + startup + task_verdict: **4065 passed, exit 0**.
- New `test_nhl_odds_phantom_adjacent_day_9187.py`: 28 tests (specimen, every refusal incl. empty/dark/unread neighbour, home-and-home, postseason, doubleheader, scored/anchored ghost, the sweep passes the sport through to SQL and to ESPN).
- Mutation: 10/10 killed (season gate removed, postseason admitted, empty board admitted, neighbour-pair check removed, one-sided neighbour, arm always on, canonical-date check removed, MLB added to the arm set, board read hard-coded to MLB, sport not passed to the board read).

**Class:** production data write (a reversible label on `events.event_tags`), so it goes to review under 49(d). Not migration-class. Not a heavy task: it runs on the main app's `background` queue.

author: aikido-autofix[bot]
body:
Upgrade nanoid to fix integer overflow vulnerability that corrupts CSPRNG pool, causing session tokens and API keys to become predictable. ✅ There are no breaking changes
✅ 1 CVE resolved by this upgrade
This PR will resolve the following CVEs: | Issue | Severity           | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | 
[CVE-2026-73086](https://app.aikido.dev/issues/43573144/detail?groupId=118975#CVE-2026-73086)
| 
HIGH
| [nanoid] A signed integer overflow in the size parameter allows attackers to corrupt the CSPRNG pool, causing all generated IDs to become predictable ("uuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuu") until process restart, compromising session tokens, CSRF tokens, and API keys. This enables authentication bypass and token prediction attacks. |
🤖 Remediation details Fix CVE-2026-73086: upgrade nanoid to patched versions (3.x and 5.x) ## Short summary This PR remediates **CVE-2026-73086** (HIGH) in the **nanoid** package. Two separate resolved instances of nanoid existed in `stakecraft-frontend/package-lock.json`—one in the 3.x line pulled in by `postcss`, and one in the 5.x line pulled in by `@meteorwallet/sdk` (nested under `@near-wallet-selector/meteor-wallet`). Both instances were updated to patched versions via a lockfile-only refresh and a new `overrides` entry in `stakecraft-frontend/package.json`. ### nanoid Two transitive instances required separate remediation strategies. The 3.x instance (`node_modules/nanoid`, resolved by `postcss@8.5.6` via a `^3.3.11` range) was updated from `3.3.11` to `3.3.19` using `npm update nanoid --package-lock-only`, since the existing range already permitted the patched version. The 5.x instance (`node_modules/@near-wallet-selector/meteor-wallet/node_modules/nanoid`, resolved by `@meteorwallet/sdk@1.0.24`) was pinned at exactly `5.1.5` by its parent and could not be updated via a lockfile refresh alone; two selector-style overrides (`"nanoid@<3.3.12": "3.3.12"` and `"nanoid@>=5.0.0 <5.1.11": "5.1.11"`) were added to `stakecraft-frontend/package.json` to force both lines to their respective patched floors without bumping any parent dependency. ## Version changes | Package | From | To | Why updated | |---|---|---|---| | nanoid | 3.3.11 | 3.3.19 | CVE-2026-73086 fix — lockfile refresh (postcss transitive) | | nanoid | 5.1.5 | 5.1.11 | CVE-2026-73086 fix — override (@meteorwallet/sdk transitive) |

author: spyder007
body:
## Summary
Supersedes #7 (closed — that PR's source branch had already been squash-merged as #6, so re-pushing to it and opening a new PR replayed the whole old diff against current `main` and conflicted). Same underlying problem, but the actual root cause (and fix) turned out to be different from what the first two iterations of this PR assumed — see below.

## Root cause
A real CI run on [spydersoft-consulting/audit#4](https://github.com/spydersoft-consulting/audit/pull/4) (build 6830) failed:

```
MSBUILD : error MSB1001: Unknown switch.
    Full command line: '.../MSBuild ... --target:VSTest --nologo ... --report-trx --coverage ...'
```

This is **not** a `DotNetCoreCLI@2` limitation. Reading the task's actual source
(`Tasks/DotNetCoreCLIV2/dotnetcore.ts`): since 2.256.3 (April 2025 — well before the
2.279.0 that actually ran), `command: test` detects Microsoft.Testing.Platform itself by
reading the repo's `global.json`, and when detected, automatically passes
`--project`/`--solution` (picked by file extension) instead of a bare positional project
path — that's what makes `dotnet test` invoke MTP's own discovery instead of falling back
to the legacy VSTest-via-MSBuild path that chokes on MTP-only flags like `--report-trx`.

Detection failed for audit because its `global.json` lived under `src/`, and the task's
search only walks **up** from the pipeline's working directory (normally the repo root)
— it never looks into subdirectories. Confirmed by reproducing the exact `MSB1001`
failure locally (invoking `dotnet test` from the repo root with `global.json` left in
`src/`), and confirmed fixed by moving it to the repo root and re-running the identical
command.

## What changed
`mtp` mode is now the exact same `DotNetCoreCLI@2` `command: test` task as `vstest` mode
— no `pwsh` step, no custom command, no script of any kind for test execution. Only the
`projects` input (`buildProject`, the solution, instead of `testProjects` — the CLI does
its own test-project discovery from there) and `arguments` (MTP-native flags) differ.
`--max-parallel-test-modules 1` is the one non-obvious flag: `--coverage-output` is a
fixed filename, and MTP's own results-subfolder naming for that isn't reliably
collision-free when modules run in parallel sharing one `--results-directory` (a coverage
report was silently dropped without it during validation).

The README calls out the `global.json`-must-be-at-repo-root requirement prominently,
since it's an easy trap for any other repo adopting `mtp` mode.

## Test plan
- [x] YAML parses cleanly (`js-yaml`)
- [x] Clean diff against current `main`, no conflicts (`mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`)
- [x] Reproduced the exact CI failure locally, then confirmed the fix resolves it: `dotnet test --solution <path> --configuration Release --no-build --no-restore --max-parallel-test-modules 1 --report-trx --coverage --coverage-output-format cobertura --coverage-output coverage.cobertura.xml --results-directory <dir>`, invoked from the repo root (matching the pipeline's actual working directory) — 100/100 tests, 8/8 correct trx + coverage files, exit 0
- [ ] Real CI run on spydersoft-consulting/audit#4 once this merges (companion commit there moves `global.json` to the repo root)

body:
## Summary
- Adds a deterministic PRNG-based mission generator (`src/config/missions.js`) that offers 1-3 `ONE_WAY_PASSAGE` (2-8 hex) or `RESEARCH_EXPEDITION` (2-6 hex, round trip) charters per station/node/hour, sized to the pilot's ship `passenger_capacity` (0 capacity → no offers).
- Adds `GET/POST /game/missions/{available,accept,active,complete,abandon}` (plus a `/missions/types` convenience endpoint), registered in `src/app.js` alongside the other `/game` route modules — following the mock-vs-persisted dual path already used by `ship` and `trade` routes (in-memory for dev-login pilots, Prisma-backed for real players via new `PlayerMission` / `MissionCooldown` models).
- Payout is `baseFare * passengers * distanceHexes` plus a time-based bonus for beating the expected pace; completing a mission activates a per-player, per-station cooldown (15-30 min, itself deterministic per station) before that station offers passage again.
- Refactors the trade route's in-memory dev-login ledger into a shared `src/lib/mock-accounts.js` so mission payouts and trade credits land in the same mock ledger and both show up via `GET /game/credits`.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test` — 30/30 passing (18 pre-existing + 12 new in `tests/missions.test.js`)
- [x] New tests cover: deterministic/seeded generation, capacity-0 → no offers, party-size/distance bounds, full accept → active → complete → cooldown lifecycle, wrong-destination rejection, credit payout accrual, abandon freeing the slot without a cooldown, and rejecting an unknown mission id.

author: jonyardley
body:
## What changed

A lane's generated anchor never shows as a card in its own lane any more, even with an agent running in it: its status dot and unread count sit on the lane header, and tapping them selects that workspace (#49). Empty lanes fold into one quiet line at rest and open as drop zones while a card is being dragged; dropping on a zone files the card there, including a lane with no cmux group yet (#50).

Closes #49
Closes #50

**Anchor heuristic.** The renderer's data has no "generated" flag (#7), so a group's anchor whose title matches the group name counts as the placeholder, agents or not. It gets two cases wrong: a real workspace titled exactly after its lane (say "Parked") hides as the placeholder, and a placeholder Jon renames shows as a card.

**Calls I made.**

- A waiting anchor still appears in Needs you, since hiding its card would otherwise lose the ask.
- An empty lane whose anchor has an agent or unread messages keeps its header rather than folding, so they stay visible.
- A lane's placeholder never moves out of its group, even from the card menu on its Needs you row.
- The folded line sits after the last lane. Unsorted folds into it too when empty.
- The renderer has no dashed stroke, so a zone is a quiet solid edge that turns ink under the pointer.
- Each empty lane is always a row, shown as a zone mid-drag and folded to nothing at rest, so the rows never change as a drag starts or ends and the drop index always counts the same rows.

## Look at after reload

1. With a lane empty (Background, in a fresh window), the lanes end with one grey line reading "Empty: Background" (plus any other empty lanes), and no "0" header for it.
2. Start dragging a card: each empty lane opens in its own place as an outlined box with its name; the one under the pointer fills darker and says "Drop here". Let go of the drag without dropping and the boxes fold back into the grey line.
3. Drop a card on the Background box: it lands in Background (cmux makes the group if it did not exist), and the box becomes a normal lane with the card under it.
4. Start an agent in a lane's own placeholder workspace (the one named after the lane): no card named after the lane appears, the lane's count does not go up, and the header shows a status dot beside the name. Tapping the dot selects that workspace and shades the dot; tapping elsewhere on the header still folds the lane, and tapping the dot does not.
5. At rest, the folded-away drop zones leave no visible gap between lanes (a few points of spacing is the most there should be).
6. A real workspace that is the only member of a lane group (a group made from one tab) still shows as its own card.

Unverified until then: that a zone row folded to zero size really draws nothing at rest, and that the dot's tap does not also reach the header (the project header's "+" relies on the same thing).

## Review

`/code-review high`, nine findings:

1. Drop index could be measured against the folded rows while resolveDrop used the zone rows, filing a card one lane off. Fixed: the rows no longer change with the drag; zones and the folded line show or hide by drag instead.
2. The row list rebuilt on every pointer move because it read drag(). Fixed by 1: the list no longer reads drag().
3. Needs you's card menu could move a lane's placeholder out of its own group. Fixed: moveToLane ignores a lane's generated anchor, with a test.
4. A tap on the header's dot might also fold the lane. Not changed: the project header's "+" already nests an onTap the same way and works; listed under Look at after reload.
5. A placeholder with unread messages but no agent vanished. Fixed: unread alone puts it on the header, with a test.
6. A real workspace titled exactly after its lane now hides even with a live agent. Not changed: issue #49 asks for this rule; the trade-off is written up above.
7. A cancelled drag left a stale row snapshot. Fixed by 1: the snapshot is gone.
8. The anchor lookup was duplicated between the hidden anchors and the header. Fixed: one helper serves both.
9. Selecting the placeholder showed no selection anywhere. Fixed: the header's dot is shaded while it is selected.

## Checklist

- [x] `npm run check` passes locally
- [x] New or changed logic in `model.ts`, `status.ts`, `drop.ts` or `shared/` has a test
- [x] No edits to `sidebars/*.js`, and `config/projects.json` is not committed

author: angelolamonaca
body:
## What and why

The lore the owner and co-admin approved, told by the world itself, plus a second region to walk it in. One logic for the whole map, so signs, people, items and the roadmap never contradict each other.

- **The story** (docs/DESIGN.md, "The story: NAPO and Napoland"; a short version in the README): N.A.P.O., the National Anomalous Phenomena Observatory, came for the hum of the Old Stone, built down the south road, and one night answered it. The woods lit up, the Old Stone cracked, and the woods have surged on the Tower's 40-minute clock ever since. NAPO closed the road at its checkpoint, drew the Napoland Zone and told everyone to leave. The 23 who stayed or came back are the residents, and every player is one of them. "Still open" lists what nobody knows yet, and new facts go into DESIGN first.
- **One logic for where things are:** the world gets deeper to the north, toward the stones that hum back. The Old Stone is the other end of the hum, not a door (the owner's call: the old "a new region will open there" line is rewritten). The South Road is the other way, calm, and it ends at the quarantine line. The Old Stone sheds shards, and the stones that hum back pull them in: deep in the woods, at NAPO's field site, and by the poles in storms.
- **The South Road** (depth 1, 72x96), down Stonebrook's south road through NAPO's old grounds, north to south:
  - NAPO's first warning sign.
  - The NAPO Bunker, where Ruth, NAPO's nurse, keeps a fire that never goes out: the road's safe fire, like the old cabin's in the woods.
  - The leavers' camp, with a fire in the open.
  - The cars left on the shoulders.
  - The research station: the NAPO Laboratory, where Vera still listens, the dormitory and the stores.
  - The NAPO Tower with its shed and panel.
  - The sinks (a bog) and the field site.
  - The checkpoint on the quarantine line, where a barrier and a truck close the road.

  It is calm: no surges, storms, flashes, watchers or skulkers. Its danger is the distance, about 90 steps to the checkpoint. Its finds lean on what people left. NAPO's buildings are concrete with yellow rims, and NAPO's desks (`console`) are read like signs.
- **People:** Walt Pruitt by the lodge fire, the one lineman (the owner's call). He kept the north line for the power company and then NAPO's, strung the wire to the Tower, went with the others when NAPO said two weeks, and came back for his truck.
- **NAPO in town and in the Near Woods:** its evacuation notice by Stonebrook's south road, the Zone warning where the woods' road comes in, and a listening post (a mast and a sign) by the ring of stones.
- **One map button, for where you are** (the owner's call):
  - The bag's header shows your maps as one button (M on a keyboard), and it opens the paper map of the area you are in; indoors, the area outside.
  - Every area has one for now, so everyone carries three: Stonebrook (new: the lodge, the Old Stone, the notice board and the pond), the Near Woods and the South Road (traced from NAPO's own).
  - An area without a map, as there will be farther out, says "No map of this place".
  - Maps now draw masts, fences and NAPO's flat roofs, and write in the names of their `places`, each moved until it covers no other.
- **Made to fit what landed today:**
  - Nothing comes into the Zone from outside any more, so the woods' supply drop is now a NAPO cache the creek washed out of its bank.
  - A live shard broke loose while the woods grew restless: it turns up before the surge, not after it.
  - The roadmap reads in the order things landed: live shards 190 (it had 63, between sign-in and survival), the South Road 200.
  - NAPO's two rooms are "The NAPO Bunker" and "The NAPO Laboratory", so board lines read "the NAPO Laboratory".

author: andrewnicolalde
body:
Since our existing CNSA 1.0 uses `echd-secp384r1` for key establishment, it is not secure against "harvest now, decrypt later" attacks, so we should select a post-quantum-secure algorithm for key establishment. Fortunately, Apple devices on versions at or after 26 (e.g. iOS 26, macOS 26 etc.) [have added support for `X25519MLKEM768`!
](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/guide/security/sec100a75d12/1/web/1#:~:text=1%2E3%2E-,On,TLS%2E)


Sadly, this PQ-ready version of our NAC infrastructure isn't quite up to CNSA 2.0 standards, which mandate `MLKEM1024`, apparently tolerate hybrids like `SecP384r1MLKEM1024` but categorically do not allow for `X25519MLKEM768`. I'm forced to use `X25519MLKEM768` though, since `SecP384r1MLKEM1024` and bare `MLKEM1024` aren't supported by the version of BoringSSL that Apple uses in `eapolclient`.

I'd happily switch to `SecP384r1MLKEM1024` only if Apple adds support for it in `eapolclient`, but frankly I am more than happy with `X25519MLKEM768`.

Also harden VLAN assignment on the CNSA 1.0 setup.

author: grumpyoldgandalf
body:
Closes #295. The design is the one posted on the issue ([comment](https://github.com/codelisperer/ouranos/issues/295#issuecomment-5858418957)).

**README row:** from dispatched run 36346098035 at `e6f5046`, rebased onto `643a2c2` (#310). The gate passes at **6369** checks, axes base+uv+tls+view. 6269 + 100 = 6369, and only the aion row moves (1124 → 1224). `AION/HTTP-CLIENT/TESTS` is 134: the 122 described below plus 12 from the review of this PR (the IPv6 regression cases, `parse-address` on non-addresses, and the port fallback).

## On the request

Four new slots. Each defaults to what the client did before.

- **`:follow-redirects`** is the most redirects dexador may follow. NIL follows none and returns the 3xx as the response. The default stays 5, dexador's own.
- **`:max-body-bytes`**, when set, reads the body as a stream and stops at the limit. A longer body signals **`response-too-large`**, a subclass of `http-error`. So does a `Content-Length` over the limit, before the body is read.
- **`:connect-address`** is an IP address, as text or octets. The client opens the socket to that address itself. For https it runs TLS with the **URL's host name**, so SNI and certificate verification use the name. Then it hands the connection to `dex:request`, so the `Host` header keeps the name too.
- **`:ca-path`** gives trust roots for verification. It is passed to dexador, and used by the pinned path as well. Unset means the system store, which is what dexador does.

`add-header` now copies the request and changes one slot. Before, it rebuilt the request slot by slot, which reset any slot it did not list.

## `fetch-public`

For a URL an admin typed.

- **Scheme:** only http and https. Anything else is refused as `:scheme`.
- **Addresses:** the host is resolved once. If **any** address it resolves to is not `:public`, the fetch signals **`fetch-refused`** without connecting, and names the URL, the host, the address and the reason.
  - It does not pick a public address and connect to that, because the same name could resolve differently for the next caller.
  - `address-category` returns the reason: `:loopback`, `:private`, `:link-local` (169.254.0.0/16, which contains 169.254.169.254, and fe80::/10), `:shared` (100.64/10), `:unspecified`, `:multicast`, `:broadcast`, `:documentation`, `:benchmarking` or `:reserved`.
  - An IPv6 address that carries an IPv4 one (IPv4-mapped, NAT64, 6to4) is classified by the IPv4 address, so `::ffff:127.0.0.1` is `:loopback`.
- **Pinning:** the connection goes to the address that was checked, through `:connect-address`.
- **Redirects:** followed here, never by dexador.
  - Each hop is resolved and checked again.
  - A hop to another origin drops `Authorization` and `Cookie`.
  - A 301, 302 or 303 after anything but GET or HEAD becomes a GET without a body.
  - More than `:max-redirects` (default 5) signals **`too-many-redirects`**.
- **Body:** capped at `*fetch-public-max-body-bytes*`, 10 MiB, unless `:max-body-bytes` says otherwise.

`:resolve`, `:address-policy` and `:perform` are arguments so that tests can set them.

## Windows

dexador uses WinHTTP on Windows, and WinHTTP ignores a connection handed to it. So `:connect-address`, and with it `fetch-public`, signal **`pinned-connect-unsupported`** there instead of connecting without the pin. Redirect control and the body cap work on every platform. The Windows leg skips the pinned tests with that reason.

## Tests

`aion/http-client/tests` goes from 34 to 122 checks, and to 134 after the review fixes. None reaches the network. The transport tests run a small HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 in the test image, and a TLS server presenting a self-signed certificate for the made-up name `pinned.test` (`aion/tests/fixtures/http-client/`, with a README).

- **Addresses:** 34 cases across every category and the embedded-IPv4 forms. Parsing refuses junk.
- **Redirects:** refused (the 3xx comes back, one request), capped at 1 (stops at the second 302, three requests), and followed by default.
- **Body cap:** refused with and without `Content-Length`. Control: a body exactly at the cap comes back whole.
- **Pinned http:** `http://pinned.test:PORT/` pinned to 127.0.0.1. The name resolves nowhere, so the request can only have gone through the pin, and the server received `Host: pinned.test:PORT`.
- **Pinned https:** pinned to 127.0.0.1, the `pinned.test` certificate is accepted for `https://pinned.test` and **refused for `https://other.test`**, so verification used the URL's name. It is also refused without `:ca-path`.
- **`fetch-public` refusals, with no connection made:** a private address, 169.254.169.254 by name and as a literal, loopback in IPv4, IPv6 and IPv4-mapped form, a name resolving to a public **and** a private address, a name that does not resolve, and `file:` and `gopher:` schemes.
- **Every hop is checked:** a real 302 from the test server to a name that resolves to 169.254.169.254 is refused, and the server saw only the first request. Control: a redirect to an allowed host is followed.
- **Pinning, stopping and rewriting:** the checked address is the one pinned. `too-many-redirects` comes after the limit. A 303 turns a POST into a GET and drops credentials across origins. Control: a same-origin 307 keeps the method, the body and `Authorization`.

**The hang found while writing these was in the test, not the client.** The first version of the test server looped on `socket-accept` and was stopped by closing the listening socket. On SBCL that does not wake a thread blocked in `accept()`, so every test using it hung in its cleanup. The server now waits for input with a timeout and checks a stop flag, and it is joined through `aion/test-threads:join`.

## Evidence

- `check-deps`: in sync after documenting `usocket` and `cl+ssl` (26 distinct third-party systems, up from 24). Both were already loaded as dexador's dependencies; `aion/http-client` now names them. `check-source-deps` is clean.
- `check-compile`: 41 of 47 systems ok. The 6 failures are the `aion/windows*` systems, which do not compile off Windows. The same check fails the same way on a tree without this change (`7cf8d72`).
- Cold gate, Linux/WSL, commit `a785dc6`, in a fresh detached worktree with `OURANOS_WITH_UV=1` and Postgres 18.6: **6242 checks, VERDICT: PASS**. `AION/HTTP-CLIENT/TESTS` is 122. The TLS axis was declined, so its 43 checks are not included. Predicted +88: 6242 + 43 = 6285 = 6197 + 88.

https://entire.io/gh/jdx/hk/trails/91
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The docs site favicon drew the cyan hook on a solid dark (`#071019`) square, which showed up as a dark tile in the browser tab. The favicon now has a transparent background, and it switches colour to suit light and dark browser themes.

**Theme-aware SVG favicon (Chrome, Edge, Firefox):** the new `docs/public/favicon.svg` draws the hook in the light theme's brand teal `#08768b`. Under `prefers-color-scheme: dark` it switches to the logo cyan `#4adef0`. The hook reuses the showreel's `ICON_HOOK` geometry. In headless Chromium at 512 px it overlaps `android-chrome-512x512.png` by 98.9% (the showreel's own logo test requires 98%). The SVG is the last `<link rel="icon">` in the page head and the only scalable one, so browsers that read SVG favicons choose it. The ICO's `sizes` now lists its actual frames (`16x16 32x32 48x48`) rather than `any`, so Chrome doesn't pick it over the SVG.

**Transparent raster fallbacks (Safari and others):** browsers that don't use SVG favicons fall back to `favicon.ico` (16, 32 and 48 px) and `favicon-16x16.png` / `favicon-32x32.png`. A single colour has to work in both themes there, and the logo cyan measured only 1.6:1 against a white tab. So the fallbacks draw the hook in `#088ca0`, a teal between the two brand colours. Its contrast is about 4:1 on white and `#202124` tabs, and 3:1 on Chrome's grey `#dee1e6` and `#35363a` tab strips. On dark tabs it is more muted than the SVG's cyan. Each icon's transparency was worked out from how much background each pixel held, because every pixel in the old icons was a straight mix of the two colours (residual under 1/255). So the anti-aliased edges are exact.

**Unchanged:** `apple-touch-icon.png` and the `android-chrome-*` manifest icons keep their dark background. iOS fills a transparent background with black, and Android launchers expect an icon with a background.

**Validation:** `mise run docs:build` passes, and the three icon links appear in the built page head. I also rendered the SVG in headless Chromium in both schemes, on white and on `#202124`, at 16 and 32 px. The ICO frames were checked on all four tab colours.

author: world-swap
body:
Two commits: a career record page, and public boards built from the same numbers.

## `/stats` — Your record

Reached from a row under the three cards on Play. `GET /api/game/stats` was expanded from a thin summary into the full record — it had no caller in `web/`, so it was grown rather than duplicated: rounds, 18-hole rounds, holes, distinct courses played, rounds under par and the rate, best round and best 18 (with course and date), aces, eagles, birdies, birdies a round, average vs par per 18, days played, XP from play, challenges won, and the five courses played most with a best score each.

New `GET /api/tournament/career`: played, wins, podiums, best finish, best score, average finish, the current week's standing, and the last ten weeks with where you placed.

Every figure is an aggregate over `game_rounds` / `tournament_entries` — nothing is a stored counter, so none of it can drift from the rounds behind it.

## `/ranks` — three boards, 17 tabs

| Board | Ranked by |
|---|---|
| Training | XP · Lessons · Streak · Daily |
| Throw Lab | XP · Best round · Best 18 · Aces · 18-hole · Courses · Birdies · Under par |
| Tournament | This week · Wins · Podiums · Weeks played · Best score |

`?metric=` decides an `ORDER BY`, so it never reaches SQL: it only selects an entry in `GAME_METRICS` / `TOURNAMENT_METRICS`, whose fragments are written in the repo source. An unknown metric falls back to XP rather than erroring — a board is a read, so a stale link should still show something. Both are tested, including with an injected string.

Each metric carries its own `HAVING`, so the Aces board lists the players with an ace rather than everyone with a zero.

New `GET /api/game/metrics` and `GET /api/tournament/records?metric=`; `GET /api/game/leaderboard` gained `metric`.

Ranking by XP rather than raw score is unchanged and deliberate — it is the one number comparable across a 3-hole and an 18-hole round.

## Two bugs fixed on the way

**`is_me` was read by `ranks.html` and never sent by the API**, so the "· you" highlight had never once worked. It is now computed from `req.player?.id` on both boards, and pinned by a test on a row that is deliberately *not* rank 1 — the shape that would have caught it.

**The all-time tournament boards count finished weeks only**, since a placing in a week still being played is not a result yet. The page now says so rather than leaving the totals looking short. Place is `RANK()` over each week's whole field, ordered the way the live board is (score, then who posted first), so a player's record matches what they saw.

## Smaller

- The metric bar scrolls, so it carries a right-edge fade that clears at the end of the scroll. Training (4 tabs, fits) gets none.
- `/stats` and `/ranks` link to each other; Play links to both.
- `app-ui.css` changed, so the cache-buster went `?v=w8` → `?v=w9` across 24 pages.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` clean; **196/196 tests pass** (9 new).
- All 17 board tabs driven in a real browser against real Postgres — correct rows, no console errors.
- `is_me` confirmed against the API: lands on the signed-in player's row (rank 2, not the top row), and flags nothing when signed out.
- Tournament career verified against Postgres with three players over two closed weeks — wins, podiums and average finish all correct, including a player dropping off the podium when a fourth entrant arrived; the no-rounds case returns nulls, not NaN.
- 13 pages swept at `--sab` 0 and 48: no horizontal overflow, no page errors.

Split the monolithic 1,215-line `contracts/sharibo/src/lib.rs` into focused submodules (types, errors, constants, circle, admin, views, crypto, storage) while keeping `lib.rs` as the crate root that declares modules, re-exports public types, and holds the `#[contract]` struct. author: argj92
body:
## Summary
Indexing and duplicate detection were already fully automatic (background worker rescans every `scan_interval_minutes`, recomputes duplicate groups each cycle). Metadata title/year guessing was — and still is — on-demand per file via the existing "Guess title/year" button; left that as-is since it needs network access for TMDB and shouldn't run unattended by default.

What was missing was any way to actually browse and play what's indexed. This adds:

- **Library section**: each tracked root's video files shown as a collapsible folder tree (same `.section`/`.subsection`/`.group` patterns the rest of the UI already uses), with an inline `<video>` player per file.
- **`GET /play/{file_id}`**: streams the file via FastAPI's `FileResponse`. Range requests work out of the box (verified manually — the browser's `<video>` element issues Range requests and gets `206 Partial Content`, so seeking/scrubbing works), no extra plumbing needed.
- **Hidden-folder convention**: a folder is left out of the Library view — but stays fully scanned/synced/deduped/protected like any other tracked folder — if its name starts with `.`, or if it contains an empty `.mediavault-hide` marker file. This is enforced server-side in `/play/` itself, not just the listing: requesting a hidden file's id directly still 404s.

Playback streams the raw file with no transcoding, so it's limited to whatever your browser can decode natively — mp4/mov generally fine, mkv/avi/wmv often won't play. Called out in both the UI (shown under the player) and the README rather than failing silently.

## Test plan
- [x] `tests/test_browse.py` — 12 new unit tests covering the hidden-folder rules (dot-prefix, marker file, nested markers, root-level marker) and tree building (grouping, missing/placeholder files, non-video extensions).
- [x] Full suite: 61 passed.
- [x] Manual pass against a real running instance (`mediavault web`) with a small fixture library:
  - Library section renders the correct folder tree and video count, correctly excluding a dot-prefixed folder and a folder with a `.mediavault-hide` marker (including a nested marker).
  - Clicking Play issues a Range request to `/play/{id}` → `206 Partial Content`.
  - Direct `curl` to `/play/{id}` for a hidden file → `404` even though the id exists; for a visible file → `200`.
  - Verified this coexists cleanly with the just-merged "edit root role/mode in place" change (both features render correctly together).

author: drewwoods
body: glRasterPos3f mapped the clip-space coordinates to the viewport without dividing by w. That only works when w = 1, as under glOrtho; under glFrustum or gluPerspective the raster position lands in the wrong place. The coordinates are now divided by w first. The raster position is valid only inside the clip volume, -w <= x, y, z <= w. The check this replaces tested only lower bounds on the undivided coordinates, so it accepted some positions outside the volume and rejected some inside it, such as any with clip z < 0 (the near half of the depth range). A rejected position kept the previous one, so the next glBitmap drew at a stale spot. The position now carries a validity flag, and glBitmap ignores a bitmap at an invalid position, including its xmove/ymove advance, as the spec requires. glWindowPos3f sets the flag as well. A valid position lies inside the viewport, so it is never negative, which keeps the guarantee #495 added for the CGNSPLOT crash. Known gaps, each marked with a TODO: - glDrawPixels doesn't check the flag yet and still draws at the last valid position. - glWindowPos3f invalidates negative coordinates, keeping #495's check, although the spec never invalidates a window position. - GL_CURRENT_RASTER_POSITION_VALID isn't queryable. See https://drewwoods.github.io/gl4es-ab/01-rasterpos for an A/B demonstration as well as the reproducer source code. Each arrow is a glBitmap placed with glrasterpos3f at its point's coordinates, so it should sit on the point:

author: tgvashworth
body:
Stacked on #2717 (→ #2714 → #2712 → #2711 → #2710). Review only the top commit until those merge.

Closes #2700

## What changes

- **Edit battle** gets two fields in its "After the game" section: "Territory staked" (assets a participant holds now) and "Territory goes to" (a participant, or "Stays with its holder"). The label comes from the asset type's own name, and reads "Asset" when the assets on offer are of more than one type. Only the arbitrator can open Edit battle, so only they can set these. A gang's report never moves the stake.
- **Saving** transfers the `CampaignAsset` through `CampaignOperation.transfer` under the campaign lock. The LOST/GAINED events name the battle. Their shared mark is kept on `Battle.stake_transfer_mark`, so saving again moves nothing, and a repeated submit is refused by the battle's existing revision check.
- **Corrections**: if the arbitrator later changes the stake or where it goes, the earlier transfer is reversed first. This happens only if the gang it went to still holds the asset. Otherwise the save is refused: "Old Ruins cannot move back: the gang it went to no longer holds it. Transfer it on the campaign page."
- **Read-only display**: the battle page, and both gangs' Mission results (editor) and receipts, show "Territory staked: Old Ruins · Goes to Rust Kings" and "Held by …". The holder is read live from the asset, so both reports always name the same gang.

## Migration

`n26/core/migrations/0077_battle_stake.py` — three nullable `AddField`s on `Battle` (`stake` FK CampaignAsset SET_NULL, `stake_awarded_to` FK Gang SET_NULL, `stake_transfer_mark` UUID). Generated with makemigrations; depends on `0076_founding_activity_label_spend_built_in_tp`, the single n26 leaf on main. No other open PR adds migrations. Announced in the board's migrations room.

## Tests

`n26/tests/test_battle_stake.py`: one transfer after two saves; a repeated submit moves nothing; "stays" and "goes to its holder" move nothing; only assets participants hold are offered; a bystander's asset is refused; a correction reverses the transfer; a correction after it changed hands is refused; the gang owner gets 404 on Edit battle and sees the stake read-only; both editors and both receipts name the live holder.

Full `n26` suite: 7949 passed.

> **Overview**
> **Battles** can record a staked campaign asset and which participant receives it. Edit battle adds stake fields for the arbitrator; saving runs a one-time `transfer` (tracked via `stake_transfer_mark`) and linked ledger events, with reversal on correction only while the asset is still with the awarded gang. Battle and post-battle UIs show read-only stake outcome via `BattleStake` / `battle_stake`.

The editor is split into HTMX-refreshed **Mission results** and per-model modules, with client-side credit/counter previews and coordinated autosave.

author: lesnik512
body:
## What

The `adr-check` recipe now fetches the shared test into a temp dir inside the repo (`.adr-check.XXXXXX`, removed on exit) and runs it with `--noconftest -o addopts=` in addition to `--rootdir=.`.

## Why

The pilot recipe (#55) put the file in `mktemp -d`, outside the repo. That broke in chat-app: `pytest-alembic`'s `pytest_collect_file` calls `path.relative_to(config.rootpath)` and raises `ValueError` for any path outside the root. Any plugin that assumes collected files live under rootpath has the same problem, so the fix is to keep the file inside the repo rather than to disable one plugin.

Inside the repo, pytest finds `pyproject.toml` as the ini file and would apply the repo's `addopts` (coverage gates with `--cov-fail-under`) to a one-file run, and would load a root `conftest.py` if one exists. `-o addopts=` and `--noconftest` remove both; the shared test needs neither. The temp dir is dot-prefixed so the scanner does not walk it.

Same change is applied to the 23 open rollout PRs, so the recipe stays identical across repos.

## Verified

- Here: 9 passed against `.github` `main`, no temp dir left behind.
- chat-app (the failing case): 9 passed with `pytest-alembic` installed; exit 1 with the file and citation named when a broken citation is planted; temp dir removed on both paths.

author: roschaefer
body:
`preview:up` ended when the build hook accepted the request, so it reported success before the preview served the new values, and a failed or skipped build went unnoticed until someone opened the preview. Steps that must only happen once the new deploy is live, such as retiring the credentials the previous deploy still uses (see #260), had nothing to wait for.

The build hook does not report which deploy it starts, so the build gets a unique title and the script finds that deploy through the Netlify API, then polls it until it is ready or has failed. The API calls go through `netlify api` with the user's own session, the same way the Infisical calls use theirs, so no Netlify credential is stored anywhere, which keeps the reasoning of #269.

`preview:up` now requires the Netlify CLI and `netlify login`, and checks the session before it creates anything.

## Before merge

- [x] **Test run:** `infisical run --env test -- pnpm run preview:up` on a pushed branch. It should log the deploy's states and end with "Preview live at …" once the deploy is ready.

## Samtycke (LEK 9 kap. 28 §)
- Vercels besöksstatistik laddades statiskt på alla 35 öppna sidor innan någon frågats. Nu laddas den först efter ja.
- Rutan frågar om två syften var för sig (statistik, annonser) med Neka alla / Godkänn alla på första nivån, lika stora, inget förkryssat. Gamla svar räknas som inget svar.

## Gallring (GDPR art. 5.1 e) — körd i driften
- `leads-avidentifiering`: intresseanmälningar avidentifieras sex månader efter senaste kontakt.
- `konton-oanvanda`: konton oanvända i två år blir en uppgift (raderas aldrig automatiskt, bokföringen ska stå kvar i sju år).

Rättslig grund per behandling, biträdena med land, överföringen till USA, lagringstid per sort, barnens uppgifter, ett avsnitt skrivet för eleven, rättigheterna med IMY, AI och automatiska beslut, incidenter. Kontaktformuläret, felrapporterna och drift-agenten står nu med.

Registret över behandlingar (art. 30), konsekvensbedömningen (art. 35), incidentrutinen och -loggen (art. 33), biträdena, gallringsjobben, hur en begäran om utdrag eller radering hanteras, och listan över det som bara kan göras för hand. Timbanken (Fas 22) står med efter att main mergats in.

author: shaullavo
body:
Establish zustand as the single state management library across web and TUI, and restrict raw `useSyncExternalStore` to sources zustand cannot own (DOM events, renderer events, mutable objects).

## Summary

This plan standardizes state management by:
- Converting hand-built module stores to zustand throughout the codebase
- Replacing raw `useSyncExternalStore` calls with `useStore(store, selector)` where the source is a zustand store
- Keeping `useSyncExternalStore` only for external sources (DOM, renderer events) in dedicated `use-*` hooks
- Adding a lint gate to enforce these patterns going forward

## Changes

- **AGENTS.md**: Added three new rules to the React section:
  - State outliving a component must be a zustand store, read with `useStore(store, selector)` in React
  - Selectors return primitives, held references, or use `useShallow` for derived objects
  - Raw `useSyncExternalStore` only for sources zustand cannot own, inside `use-*` hooks

- **plans/199-one-store-library.md**: Comprehensive plan document with:
  - Rationale for zustand (already in ~80 web files, works without React for client-core and TUI)
  - Survey of 40+ locations across web and TUI organized in sections A–F:
    - **A**: Hand-built module stores → zustand (8 rows, web)
    - **B**: zustand stores currently read via raw `useSyncExternalStore` (4 rows, web)
    - **C**: TUI stores and subscribers (7 rows, TUI)
    - **D**: Snapshots deriving per read that need memoization (6 rows)
    - **E**: Stays on `useSyncExternalStore` (rule 3 sources)
    - **F**: Looked at, no change needed
  - Execution order and proof requirements per row
  - Gate: lint rule to enforce patterns after implementation

- **plans/README.md**: Added Plan 199 to the index

## Implementation Notes

- No second state library; if zustand is ever replaced, it replaces all of it
- TUI gains zustand as a dependency, pinned to the version client-core uses
- Proof includes render count measurements for TUI (C2 must show workspace no longer re-rendering per chat event), store tests where behavior changes, and lint gate enforcement
- Execution order prioritizes high-impact rows (A6 last in group A, C4 first in TUI, C2 hottest path)

author: linardsb
body:
## Summary

Every `ci.yml` run since at least 2026-09-11 has failed, including the Dependabot PRs, #404 and #405. Two jobs are red:

- **Backend:** the `pip-audit` step reports 20 known vulnerabilities in 7 packages.
- **Container image scan (Trivy):** 3 HIGH or CRITICAL findings in the same packages.

The first commit changes only `uv.lock`. It bumps each package to the fix version `pip-audit` names:

| Package | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| aiohttp | 3.14.1 | 3.14.3 |
| anyio | 4.12.1 | 4.14.2 |
| cryptography | 49.0.0 | 50.0.0 |
| httpcore2 | 2.7.0 | 2.12.0 (`httpx2` 2.12.0 requires this exact version) |
| httpx2 | 2.7.0 | 2.12.0 |
| pip | 26.1.1 | 26.2 |
| soupsieve | 2.8.4 | 2.9.0 |

The lock also gains `httpx2-jsfetch`. It is only installed when `sys_platform == 'emscripten'`, so the app never installs it.

Merge this before PR B (#405), so that #405 and #404 can go green.

## Second commit: Trivy db-image suppressions

With the app image clean, Trivy's `db` step runs again. It had been skipped since 2026-08-31, because the `app` step failed first.

The `db` step flags 7 HIGH vulnerabilities in the Go standard library compiled into `/usr/local/bin/gosu` (Go v1.24.6). `gosu` comes with the digest-pinned `pgvector:pg16` base image. The CVEs are CVE-2026-33818, -39821, -56853, -56858, -56859, -56860 and -56862.

The rationale is the same as for the 20 existing entries: `gosu` switches user at container start and takes no network input. The new entries are added to `.trivyignore` and mirrored in `docs/dependency-debt.md`, with a review date of 2026-12-31.

Known issue, not fixed here: Trivy only enforces an expiry written as `exp:YYYY-MM-DD` on the entry line. The file's `# expires:` comments are documentation only, so none of these entries ever lapses.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pip-audit --strict` with the CI ignore flags: "No known vulnerabilities found" (observed locally).
- [x] `make check-full` exit 0: pytest 8492 passed, 0 failed; vitest 780 passed; flag audit 0 errors (observed locally).
- [x] CI run 36345484858 at 83e7e675: Backend green (pip-audit passes), Trivy `app` step green, `db` step red on the 7 gosu CVEs above.

author: steveraysteveray
body:
Closes #380.

The quantity kind and unit requested in #380 were added earlier (#855, #1489). This PR adds the remaining pieces from that issue, plus one classification gap:

- Reciprocal `rdfs:seeAlso` between `quantitykind:AbsorbedDose` ↔ `quantitykind:DoseEquivalent`, and `quantitykind:AbsorbedDoseRate` ↔ `quantitykind:DoseEquivalentRate`.
- A `dcterms:description` for `quantitykind:DoseEquivalentRate`, which had none.
- `quantitykind:DoseEquivalentRate qudt:organizedUnder quantitykind:SpecificPower`, mirroring `AbsorbedDoseRate` (and the non-rate dose kinds under `SpecificEnergy`). `organizedUnder` rather than `specializationOf`, so Gy/s and Sv/s are not asserted commensurable with each other or with W/kg.

Not included: the "Effective dose rate" altLabel suggested in #380. Effective dose is a distinct radiological-protection quantity (tissue-weighted sum of equivalent doses), so labelling dose equivalent rate with it would introduce the confusion the `unit:SV` description warns against.

Related follow-up: #1545 (`KermaRate` uses `specializationOf` where the other dose kinds use `organizedUnder`).

body: ## Description The template loaded its 8 font families through `next/font/google`. That already served the fonts from the site itself at runtime, but it downloaded them from Google on every `next build`. When that download misbehaved, the build failed, for this repo and for every charity site built from it (#163). The fonts are now committed to the repo and loaded with `next/font/local`, so a build makes no request to Google at all. ## Type of Change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [x] Test addition/update - [x] CI/CD or tooling change - [x] Documentation update ## Related Issue(s) Fixes #163 ## Changes Made - **`src/fonts//`:** 9 latin woff2 files (269 KB), with each family's SIL OFL licence. No npm dependency was added. - Open Sans, Raleway, Faustina, Montserrat and Cinzel: one variable file each, from `@fontsource-variable/*` 5.3.0. This is the same single file per family that the Google loader served. - Lato (400, 700), Cantata One (400) and Fauna One (400): static files from `@fontsource/*` 5.3.0. They have no variable build. - The first version used one static file per weight (25 files). Every file is preloaded, and Lighthouse performance fell from 85–89 to 78–80. With 9 files the page preloads what the Google version did. - **`src/lib/fonts.ts`:** `next/font/local` with the same 8 export names, `--font-*` variables and `display: 'swap'`, plus metric-adjusted fallbacks. It covers every weight used before. `layout.tsx` and the CSS needed no change. - **`scripts/check-drift.mjs`:** a new rule fails on `next/font/google` or any `fonts.googleapis.com` / `fonts.gstatic.com` reference in `src/`. Comments are ignored. - **Tests:** - `__tests__/lib/fonts.test.ts` was rewritten. It forbids `next/font/google`, and for each export checks the variable, that every weight the Google config had is covered, and the declared sources. It also checks every file exists and is real woff2, and that each family has its licence. - 3 drift-rule cases were added, a pass case plus two that must fail. - **Docs:** `AGENTS.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `TEMPLATE_USAGE.md`, `TESTING.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` no longer describe a Google Fonts build dependency, or say to comment out font imports when a build fails. ## Testing Performed ### Automated Testing - [x] `pnpm run lint`: all linting checks pass (0 errors; the 2 `` warnings are pre-existing). - [x] `pnpm test`: 34/34 suites, 397/397 tests. - [x] `pnpm run build`: builds successfully. - [x] `pnpm run test:e2e`: 53 passed. Run on the first version. Also passing: `format:check`, `tsc --noEmit`, `check:site-config` and `check:drift`. **No-network proof:** - The build succeeded with every proxy pointed at a dead port. - The same build with `main`'s `fonts.ts` failed with `Error while requesting resource … fonts.googleapis.com`. - `out/index.html` preloads 9 font files, and `out/` has 0 references to Google font hosts. **Mutation checks:** - Removing the new drift check makes 2 of its 3 tests fail. The third, the pass case, still passes. - Narrowing a variable font's weight range fails the fonts test. ## Breaking Changes None. The same fonts, weights and CSS variables are served from the site as before. ## Additional Notes The Single Page template gets the same change in FreeForCharity/FFC-IN-FFC_Single_Page_Template#479. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_017vrGmawc7kDH9s833Shica

The "Einsatz abschließen?" dialog now has an opt-in checkbox, **"PDF erstellen und per E-Mail senden"**, that does it in one go:

1. The incident closes, so the PDF is final and has no "Zwischenstand" footer.
2. The usual section dialog opens. Its button reads **"PDF ERSTELLEN & MAILEN"**.
3. After saving, the OS mail program opens a new message with the PDF attached. The subject is prefilled as `Einsatzbericht <Einsatznummer> · <Stichwort> · <Beginn>`, and any blank part is dropped.

No recipient is prefilled. The subject deliberately leaves out the Einsatzort: a subject is never encrypted, sits in mail server logs and shows on lock screens. The body carries no names.

## Changes

- **`IMailComposer`** (AppLogic): a new platform hook, following the `IIncidentPdfExporter` pattern.
  - The desktop implementation is `OsMailComposer`. Android gets `NoopMailComposer`, so the checkbox never shows there, just as PDF export doesn't.
  - It is wired as a nullable constructor parameter through `CompositionRoot`, `HomeViewModel` and `IncidentWorkspaceViewModel`.
- **`IncidentMail`**: builds the subject and body.
  - Control, format (bidi, zero-width) and line/paragraph-separator characters are collapsed to spaces. Einsatzdaten may come from a sync peer or from a handed-over file.
- **`ConfirmDialogViewModel` / view**: an optional checkbox (`OptionLabel`, `IsOptionChecked`). It starts unticked, and existing callers are unchanged.
- **`PdfExportOptionsViewModel` / view**: the confirm button label is now configurable.
- **`IncidentWorkspaceViewModel`**:
  - `RunExportAsync` now returns the written path.
  - `RunExportAndMailAsync` composes the mail and reports the outcome in the export status line.
- **`OsMailComposer`** (desktop). `mailto:` cannot carry an attachment, so it attaches per OS:
  - **Windows:** Simple MAPI `MAPISendMailW` (`MapiMail`), on its own STA thread. `DllImport` is pinned to System32, and no new package is added.
  - **Linux:** `xdg-email --attach`, called through `ArgumentList` with no shell.
  - **macOS:** Mail.app via `osascript`. The script is fixed, and the values arrive as argv behind a fixed first operand, so a value can never be read as `-e`.
  - **Fallback:** when attaching fails (the new Outlook has no MAPI, `xdg-utils` is missing), a plain `mailto:` opens and the folder holding the PDF is shown. The status then reads "E-Mail geöffnet – PDF bitte anhängen".
  - A launch still running after 5 s counts as success, because classic Outlook and a freshly started Thunderbird only return once the compose window closes. This keeps the export dialog from being held busy.
- **Hardening from a security review.** `xdg-email` re-decodes backslash escapes under dash's `echo`, and its Thunderbird route decodes the attach path with `echo -e`. A crafted Stichwort or file name could therefore inject a hidden To/Bcc. The fixes:
  - no backslash ever reaches `xdg-email`;
  - an attachment path containing `' " , \ %` takes the `mailto:` route;
  - only an existing, absolute `.pdf` path is ever handed on.

  Each case has a test that replays the attack.
- **Changelog:** `changelog.d/+close-incident-mail-pdf.added.md`.

### Screenshots

Before: the plain confirm, unchanged for every other caller.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c53c3ee2-3875-4585-b8b6-8d58242d359a)

After: close dialog with the mail option, shown ticked.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e0b43e8-868f-4b11-a564-2b2789e300e8)

### Not yet verified by hand

- **Windows MAPI:** check classic Outlook and Thunderbird (attached), and the new Outlook (expect the `mailto:` fallback).
- **macOS:** check that Mail.app opens with the PDF attached.
- **Linux:** check a real Thunderbird or Evolution compose window. Unit tests cover argument building, the path guards, the fallback order and the timeout.

- [x] Commits are cryptographically signed (SSH or GPG) and show as **Verified** on GitHub — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/CodeForFire/lagebuch/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#signing-your-commits)

- [x] Changes under `src/` add **one** changelog entry in `changelog.d/` — English, one sentence, no PR link (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md#changelog-entries))
- [x] UI changes include before/after screenshots

author: sarah86
body:
Follow-up to #1. This commit was pushed after #1 was merged, so it isn't in `main` yet.

## Problem
After listening to a page, selecting another page (or pressing Stop / Listen again) switched the button to **"Try again"** even though nothing had failed. Pressing it again worked.

## Cause and fix
- **Spurious error:** stopping playback cleared the old audio element's `src`, which fired its `error` handler and set the status to `error`. Handlers are now detached before the source is cleared, and each handler ignores events that don't belong to the current audio.
- **Mobile (iOS Safari):** `play()` was only called after the TTS request returned, seconds after the tap, so Safari could block it. A retry then worked because the audio came from cache quickly. One audio element is now reused for all playback, unlocked with a short silent clip during the Listen tap, so later `play()` calls (including chunk-to-chunk and auto-play to the next page) are allowed.

## Testing
- `tsc -b` and `vite build` pass.
- Headless Chromium with `/api/tts` mocked:
  - Reproduced the bug on the old `main`: after page 1 finished, selecting page 2 showed "Try again". With this fix it shows "Listen".
  - Auto-play still plays through every page.
  - A 3-chunk page plays all 3 chunks, both from the network and from cache.
- Not tested on a real iPhone/Safari.

author: undeemed
body:
Closes #116

**What now works:** when the OS kills the trainer (OOM, `kill -9`, laptop sleep), the watcher moves the task type from TRAINING back to READY within one poll. It also adds a `training` event: "Training stopped without finishing (exit unknown). Approve again to retry." The dashboard's Activity log shows that event and the task type reads **Ready to train**, so Approve works again.

## How
- **`graduate/router/consent.py`** (ayaangazali's file: **one call site plus one import**): after `Popen`, it saves `trainer: {pid, started}` in the registry entry.
- **`graduate/watcher/__init__.py`**: `watch()` calls `reap()` on every poll. A TRAINING entry with a `trainer` record goes back to READY when the process is gone, is a zombie (the router never reaps its child), or has a different start time (a reused pid). `started()` uses `ps -o stat=,lstart=`, so it works on macOS too. No new daemon and no new dependency.
- **`graduate/registry.py`**: `transition()` drops `trainer` on every state change, so a stale pid can't outlive its TRAINING.
- **`scripts/demo.sh --use-checkpoint`**: after it `pkill -9`s the consent-started job, it waits for the watcher's READY before `graduate train --use-checkpoint`. Without that wait, the watcher could reset TRAINING in the middle of that command.
- **Start time within 2 s:** on this host, `ps` printed the same process's `lstart` as 19:28:27 from one environment and 19:28:28 from another. The first real run caught this, so start times are compared as epoch seconds with a 2 s window. A reused pid starts much later.

**Contract note:** `trainer` is a new optional TaskType field. `graduate/contracts.md` is untouched. The field and the §1 actor line are proposed on #11 for ayaangazali's call.

## Tests (commands and raw output)
File paths in the output are shortened to repo-relative ones (or `$GRADUATE_CHECKPOINT`, as in SUBMISSION.md); nothing else is edited except where noted.

### 1. Fake trainer through the consent path, `kill -9`, READY within one watcher poll: fails on main
`tests/test_dead_trainer.py` POSTs `/api/consent/write-migration` with `TRAIN_CMD` set to `sh -c 'echo $$ > trainer.pid; exec sleep 60'`. It runs the real `watch()` loop for exactly one poll with the trainer alive (still TRAINING), then `kill -9`s it and leaves it a zombie, as the router does. After one more poll it asserts READY, no `trainer` record, and the event text. A second test gives a live pid a different start time (a reused pid) and expects READY.

Main's code with only the new test file:
```
$ git stash push graduate scripts  # main code, new test only
$ python -m pytest -q tests/test_dead_trainer.py::test_killed_trainer_returns_to_ready_within_one_poll

tests/test_dead_trainer.py:68: AssertionError
=========================== short test summary info ============================
FAILED tests/test_dead_trainer.py::test_killed_trainer_returns_to_ready_within_one_poll - AssertionError: assert 'TRAINING' == 'READY'
  
  - READY
  + TRAINING
1 failed in 0.44s
```
This branch:
```
$ python -m pytest -v tests/test_dead_trainer.py

tests/test_dead_trainer.py::test_killed_trainer_returns_to_ready_within_one_poll PASSED [ 50%]
tests/test_dead_trainer.py::test_reused_pid_counts_as_dead PASSED        [100%]

============================== 2 passed in 0.48s ===============================
```

### 2. Real reproduction on this host (`GRADUATE_OWNED_BACKEND=local`, Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B LoRA, the real trainer)
Router `uvicorn graduate.router.app:app --port 4196` and `python -m graduate.watcher` ran in a scratch dir with `registry.example.json` and 3 chat records for `write-migration`. The trainer got `kill -9` after its first loss row, mid-run. As on the Mac in the issue, the log ends with the `resource_tracker` warning and no traceback.
```
$ curl -s -X POST localhost:4196/api/consent/write-migration
{"task_type":"write-migration","state":"TRAINING","records":3,"log":"data/write-migration.train.log"}
$ jq ".task_types[\"write-migration\"] | {state, consent, trainer}" registry.json
{
  "state": "TRAINING",
  "consent": true,
  "trainer": {
    "pid": 871735,
    "started": 1790537435
  }
}
$ ps -o pid,stat,lstart,rss,args -p $(jq .task_types[\"write-migration\"].trainer.pid registry.json)
   PID STAT STARTED                      RSS COMMAND
871735 Rsl  Sun Sep 27 19:30:35 2026 3376708 .venv/bin/python3 -m graduate.registrar.train write-migration
$ cat data/write-migration.loss.jsonl
{"step": 1, "loss": 2.3295, "secs": 11.6, "peak_rss_mb": 4388}
$ jq .task_types["write-migration"].state registry.json   # after >= 1 watcher poll with the trainer alive
"TRAINING"
$ kill -9 871735   # mid-run: 1 loss rows written
READY 1.07 s after the kill (POLL_SECS=1.0)
$ ps -o pid,stat -p 871735
   PID STAT
871735 Zs
$ tail -n 3 data/write-migration.train.log
{"step": 1, "loss": 2.3295, "secs": 11.6, "peak_rss_mb": 4388}
multiprocessing/resource_tracker.py:396: UserWarning: resource_tracker: There appear to be 1 leaked semaphore objects to clean up at shutdown: {'/mp-covazg04'}
  warnings.warn(
$ curl -s localhost:4196/state | jq "{task: .registry.task_types[\"write-migration\"] | {state, consent, model, trainer}, events: .registry.events[:3]}"
{
  "task": {
    "state": "READY",
    "consent": true,
    "model": null,
    "trainer": null
  },
  "events": [
    {
      "ts": "2026-09-27T19:31:02Z",
      "kind": "training",
      "task_type": "write-migration",
      "text": "Training stopped without finishing (exit unknown). Approve again to retry."
    },
    {
      "ts": "2026-09-27T19:30:35Z",
      "kind": "training",
      "task_type": "write-migration",
      "text": "Training started on this machine with 3 runs."
    },
    {
      "ts": "2026-09-27T19:30:35Z",
      "kind": "consent",
      "task_type": "write-migration",
      "text": "You approved training write-migration on this machine with 3 runs."
    }
  ]
}
```
Dashboard at the same moment: Activity shows the event, and Write a migration reads **Ready to train**.

__omp_shell("[dashboard after kill -9](https://github.com/ayaangazali/jelly/blob/92538881850658f63989c6d443bcc29cf3fef334/docs/screens/issue-116-dead-trainer.png?raw=true)")

### 3. A normal training run still ends GRADUATED
`PORT=4196 scripts/demo.sh --offline --auto-approve` (stub upstream, zero OpenAI calls). The live local training job ran 326 s with the watcher's `reap()` polling every second. There was no false reset, and the job graduated:
```

== 1/6 restore the staged 4-of-5 ledger from backups/stub-corpus

== 3/6 consent: fix-failing-test is READY
training job started, log: data/fix-failing-test.train.log
== 4/6 waiting for the live training job to graduate fix-failing-test

Your model: its first passing session after graduation (a failed session is never counted as savings), graduated by the live training job.
== checks
demo ok: backups/demo-20260927T193409Z/demo.log
```
Registry events for the task type (newest first):
```
2026-09-27T19:40:30Z graduated: fix-failing-test graduated: fix-failing-test-v1, trained on 5 runs in 326.4 s.
2026-09-27T19:35:03Z training: Training started on this machine with 5 runs.
2026-09-27T19:35:03Z consent: You approved training fix-failing-test on this machine with 5 runs.
```
