author: yannickmonney
body:
## Summary

Organization deletions before #3240 (0.5.0–0.5.8) removed a few tables and left every other org-keyed app row behind. That included the organization's automations and their enabled schedules. The minutely scan kept claiming each due occurrence and started a run for an organization that no longer existed, and it would do so indefinitely (#3022). This PR fixes it in two layers:

1. **The scan never runs a schedule of a deleted organization** (`backend/domains/automations/triggers.ts`).
   - Each row the scan reads now carries an `orgMissing` flag (`NOT EXISTS "organization"`).
   - Such a schedule is skipped before anything else is read (no claim, no run).
   - Each page disables the skipped schedules with one conditional `UPDATE … SET enabled = false`. The write re-checks that the row is still enabled and the organization still missing, and it returns the rows it changed.
   - One summary line per scan names what that write disabled.
   - It is logged exactly once: a disabled schedule never enters a page again, and an overlapping scan that lost the write reports nothing.
   - `ScheduleScanResult.orphaned` counts them.
2. **Migration `0125_rows_of_deleted_organizations.sql` removes what those deletions left behind.** It works the way the teardown cascade does:
   - It walks the same catalog as `listOrgOwnedTables`: every `app` base table with an `org_id` column.
   - It deletes child tables before the tables they reference. The order is byte order ("C"), and on the real schema it is identical to `orderChildrenFirst`'s (checked on a scratch copy).
   - It keeps `ORG_TEARDOWN_KEEPS` (`audit_logs`, `audit_chain_heads`, `audit_integrity_progress`, `organization_tombstones`).
   - A row is stranded when no `"organization"` row carries its `org_id`.
   - It is guarded with `to_regclass('"organization"')` for a fresh database, the 0120 pattern. App migrations run before Better Auth creates its tables.
   - It is idempotent and safe during a rolling deploy. Triggers are deleted before the runs they reference, so a claim the old image's scan makes during the migration is waited for, and its run is deleted too.

`backend/MIGRATION.md` (organizations row) and `tests/manual/reference/automation.md` (a new automated row) record both.

Closes #3022

## Decisions for the reviewer

- **A deleted organization under an active legal hold keeps every row.** The teardown has refused to delete a held organization since 0.5.8 (#3162). Legal holds exist since 0.5.0, though, so on 0.5.0–0.5.7 an organization could be deleted while held, and the rows it left are exactly what the hold preserves. A released hold does not count. Such an organization's schedules are still disabled by the scan. Its rows stay until someone releases the hold. If you would rather delete held rows as well, it is one `NOT EXISTS` clause to drop.
- **The keep list is written into the migration**, because a shipped migration is frozen. It matches `ORG_TEARDOWN_KEEPS` as of this PR.
- **Migration number.** `0123` is taken on main (#3519) and `0124` is claimed by the open #3533 (#3532 also still claims `0123`), so this PR takes `0125`. Please re-check at merge time. The integration lane finds the file by its slug, so renumbering needs no code change.
- **Cost.** The migration runs one DELETE per org-keyed table (96 today), each an anti-join against `"organization"`, which means a sequential pass over the large tables. This is a one-time cost at the boot that applies it, the same kind of cost as the `0076`/`0077` dedups.
- **`org_id` holds only organization ids.** Before relying on "no `organization` row means stranded", I swept every write into the 96 tables, in current code and in all v0.5.x tags. Every INSERT binds `org_id` to an organization id resolved from a session, REST key, token or existing row. No table is deployment-wide, and no migration seeds rows.

## Verification

- `bunx vitest run --project server` on `triggers.scan.test.ts`, `triggers.webhook.test.ts`, `backend/jobs/` and `backend/domains/organizations/`: 12 files, 95 tests passed. After rebasing onto the current main, the scan, webhook and organizations files passed again: 5 files, 68 tests. The two new scan cases and the updated result shapes fail against the unfixed scan (5 of 10 red).
- `bunx oxlint --type-aware` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed TypeScript files: clean. Opengrep (`tools/opengrep/run.sh`) on the changed files: 0 findings. `bun run lint:manual`: ok.
- Scoped `tsc` over the changed files (except the 54k-line `integration-check.ts`, whose only change is two imports and two lane entries): exit 0.
- The migration applies cleanly to a fresh database after every other migration, where the guard returns early. The harness's boot migrations exercise the same path on each run. Applied twice to a seeded scratch database: live org untouched, dead org removed except the ledger, held org kept, released-hold org removed, second pass unchanged.
- **Real Postgres (local; no CI workflow runs `backend:integration`).** Two new lanes, both registered:
  - `checkDeletedOrgSchedules`: a deployed, due schedule of a non-existent organization
    - starts no run and ends up disabled;
    - is not claimed (the cursor is unmoved and no skip is stamped);
    - is named in one line across two scans;
    - does not stop the live schedule beside it from being claimed.
  - `checkOrphanedOrgRowsBackfill`: re-applies the file inside a rolled-back transaction. At boot the guard returns before any DELETE, so this lane is the only place the DELETEs run. Results:
    - the dead organization's rows are gone, across a cascade (a table with no org id), SET NULL and NO ACTION foreign key;
    - the audit row and the tombstone stay;
    - a held dead organization and the live organization keep every row;
    - a second pass changes nothing.
  - `ITEST_LANES=checkAutomations,checkAutomationTriggerDelivery,checkDeletedOrgSchedules,checkOrphanedOrgRowsBackfill`: **36/36 checks passed across 4/4 lanes**. This filtered run includes the existing fairness (205 schedules), overlapping-scan and schedule-fire probes.
  - Regression proof: with only `triggers.ts` reverted, `checkDeletedOrgSchedules` reads `runs=1 (want 0), enabled=true (want false), claimed=true`.
- **Pre-existing, not from this branch:** `checkOrganizationLifecycle` fails 6 checks with the same output on `origin/main`. The lane renames org A to "Life A renamed" and later confirms the deletion with "Life A", so the teardown answers `400 ORG_CONFIRM_NAME_MISMATCH`, and every check after it that assumes the deletion happened fails. It needs its own fix.

## Not in scope

- Slug-keyed leftovers of pre-#3240 deletions (knowledge corpus rows, blobs, the config tree). They live outside the app database, and a new organization may have taken the same slug since.
- `app_realtime.outbox`. The teardown clears it, but `listOrgOwnedTables` does not walk it, and hints older than an hour are reclaimed anyway.
- The webhook and event doors. Their trigger rows go with the cascade and this backfill, and neither can fire without an outside caller or an event in that organization.

author: andylizf
body:
`space-board.spec.ts` knocked #1872 out of the merge queue (run 36341262532). In each failing attempt the review of a freshly created space returned 200, and the very next request, `POST /tasks` into that space, got 400 "Space must be approved before creating tasks". It failed on the first attempt and on both retries.

`POST /admin/spaces/{id}/review` left its commit to `get_db`'s teardown, which FastAPI runs after the response has been sent. A client that publishes into the space as soon as it hears "approved" can arrive before that commit and still read the space as `PENDING`. #1833 fixed the same ordering for `POST /spaces` and `POST /tasks`; this commits in the review route the same way.

## Tests

A new case in `backend/tests/integration/test_a_create_commits_before_its_response_is_sent.py` drives the review through the real app and checks the commit lands before the response starts. On main it fails with `['response.start', 'commit']`; here it passes.

The race does not show up on its own on a local stack, so the e2e comparison widens it: a local-only `asyncio.sleep(0.3)` before the teardown commit in `get_db`, not part of this PR. `space-board.spec.ts`, retries off, excluding the one test in which a member joins a task (joining provisions a project repository, which needs the Forgejo that CI starts):

| | repeats | "Space must be approved" |
|---|---|---|
| main, no sleep | 20 | 0 (160/160 passed) |
| main, 0.3 s sleep | 5 | 5 |
| this branch, 0.3 s sleep | 20 | 0 (40/40 task creations after a review succeed) |
| this branch, no sleep | 20 | 0 (160/160 passed) |

With the sleep, this branch then fails one step later in the same test: approving a task through `PATCH /tasks/{id}` also commits after answering, so the board opened next can miss the task. In the spec that step is followed by a full page load, which is far longer than the gap, and it has not failed in CI. It is left to the systemic fix #1833 describes (running `get_db`'s exit before the response) rather than patched here.

author: andrewlampert
body:
﻿## What
`load_all_from_db()` creates a temp directory, exports the save's tables into it as CSVs, and reads them into memory - but never cleaned that directory up. Found while auditing for other instances of the leaked-stream/temp-file pattern flagged by Codex review on #2: this machine's Temp folder had **163 leftover `hc09_bridge_load_*` directories**, one per historical "Load Save File" / team switch, going back who knows how long.

## How
- `_finish_load()` reads every CSV fully into memory before returning, so nothing downstream ever touches the directory again afterward - it's safe to delete immediately, the same way `save_to_db()` already deletes its own temp directory. Wrapped in `try/finally` so cleanup happens even if the load fails partway through.
- Removed the now-pointless `_load_tmp_dir` bookkeeping field - it was written but never read anywhere.
- Also hardened `save_to_db()`'s existing cleanup with the same `try/finally` for symmetry, since it currently only deletes its temp dir on the success path (no evidence this has leaked in practice - 0 leftover `hc09_bridge_save_*` dirs found - but the failure mode is the same shape).

## Testing
Verified against a real save file (`BLUS30128-CAREER-QUICKSAVE`, 2,366 players): both load and save round-trip correctly, and the temp-dir count stays at 0 after each. Cleaned up the 163 pre-existing leaked directories as part of this fix (620KB total on this machine - small per-leak, but unbounded over time and every user who's used this feature has some amount of this sitting in their Temp folder).

author: deadbytee-del
body:
## Summary

This continues the big block-system redesign from the previous PR (#12) with the remaining high-value items:

- **MiniMessage-formatted text**: `send styled message` / `broadcast styled message` actions using real Adventure `MiniMessage` (`<gradient:...>`, `<red>`, `<bold>`, etc.), not just plain text.
- **LuckPerms integration**: give a permanent permission/group, or check group membership — all as a soft dependency that safely no-ops if LuckPerms isn't installed. Auto-added to `plugin.yml`'s `softdepend` whenever a project actually uses it.
- **Persistent player data**: save/read a value on a player that survives server restarts (`PersistentDataContainer`), separate from normal in-memory variables.
- **Unsafe/Advanced category**: raw Java statement/expression/class-reference blocks as a clearly-labeled (red) escape hatch for anything the friendly blocks don't cover yet — no coercion, no type checking.
- **Lists + for-each**: `create list with`, `length`, `is empty`, `get`/`set` index, `for each item in list`, all backed by `java.util.List<Object>`.
- **Logic XOR** block.
- **Fixed the variable system**: fields were silently `double`-only (a real, pre-existing bug once typed sockets allowed non-numeric values into `set variable`/`get variable`). Now every variable is `Object`-typed, so one variable can hold a number, string, boolean, list, or player — with safe coercion at every consumption site (arithmetic, comparisons, `if`/`while` conditions) and value-aware equality (`Objects.equals`, numeric-aware for `==`/`!=` so `10` and `10.0` compare equal).
- **Pre-build validation**: before generating code, Quint now scans the whole workspace for a block sitting disconnected from any event/command, or a required socket nobody filled in, and reports a plain-English list instead of a cryptic Java error (or a plugin that silently does less than it looks like).
- **Dependency manager**: Plugin Settings now has depend/softdepend fields written into `plugin.yml`.
- Vendored `adventure-text-minimessage.jar` (per Minecraft version) and `luckperms-api.jar`, wired into both the CheerpJ (browser) and native (Electron) compile classpaths.

## Test plan

author: malibio
body:
Closes #2905.

## What was wrong

ADR-038's contract allows at most one clarification per intent. The guard found the current intent by scanning back for the last assistant message that did not start with the composed-clarification opener. A clarification Stage 2 asked in its own prose carried no opener, so:

1. it was not counted, and
2. it was read as the intent *resolving*, which dropped any earlier `route_clarify` from the window. Clarifications could alternate forever.

## What this does

**Each assistant turn records how it ended**, structurally, and the guard reads that record instead of reply text.

- `AiChatTurnOutcome` (`Acted` / `Clarified` / `Replied`) is persisted on each assistant `AiChatMessage` and seeded back into `AgentSession::prior_turns` from history.
- `AgentTurnResult::outcome()` derives it from what the turn did: a composed clarification is `Clarified`; **a successful write** is `Acted`; anything else, including a turn that only read, is `Replied`.
- The intent boundary is the last `Acted` turn. A `Replied` turn stays inside the intent, so a prose question can no longer erase an earlier clarification.
- **The intent is already clarified** when it holds a composed clarification, **or at least two turns that did not write.** One such turn is as likely an answer ("hi" → "Hello!") as a question; counting it alone suppressed the first genuine clarification of any chat that opened with conversation or a lookup. Two in one intent is the loop the contract stops. The cost: an intent clarified only in prose can ask twice.
- The duplicate-entity guard disarms only for records a **composed** clarification asked about. A read-only answer that linked the record stays in the intent but asked nothing.
- When the intent is already clarified and Stage 2 replies in prose **with no tool call at all**, it is put back once with the contract stated (`ALREADY_CLARIFIED_NUDGE`). The prose is dropped from history so the model does not re-read its own question. The nudge never fires after a tool call, so a turn whose search answered the user is not pushed to call another tool.
- `route_clarify`'s Stage-2 description now says to clarify through it, never in a plain reply (tool-selection guidance, per ADR-064). The detection does not depend on it being followed.

### Why only a write closes an intent

The first version counted any tool call as acting. The routing eval showed why that fails: Stage 2 searched and then asked in prose, twice, so each search closed the intent and nothing was on record by the scored turn. Structurally, "searched, then showed results" and "searched, then asked about them" are identical, so reads cannot close an intent.

The cost is on the other side: a conversation that has only read keeps its intent open. With the two-turn rule above, that costs a clarification or a re-prompt only from its third non-writing turn, which errs toward acting over asking again — the direction ADR-038's contract prefers over looping.

## A deleted test

`an_unanswered_clarification_is_not_treated_as_already_clarified` was removed. It pinned two things:

- **A clarification still awaiting its answer is not a prior one.** That state cannot occur any more: `run_turn` writes the `PriorTurn` record only after a turn ends, and the guard reads it only inside the next turn, whose user message *is* the answer.
- **One clarification must not disable the guard for the rest of the chat.** Still pinned, by `the_clarification_contract_re_arms_on_a_new_intent` (clarified → armed → acted → re-armed).

## Verification

- Unit tests: the erasure case, prose counting (one non-writing turn does not count, two do — threshold pinned both ways), outcome derivation (read-only → `Replied`, failed write → `Replied`), the re-prompt fires / does not fire after a tool call / does not fire after a single earlier reply / fires once, two search-then-prose turns count, a linked read-only answer does not disarm the duplicate guard, and the daemon round-trip. Each new test was checked to fail with its fix reverted.
- `bun run test:changed` passes.
- **Routing eval, targeted** to the two scenarios this rule can reach (the only ones with prior turns in their chat), 5 reps, E4B, isolated daemon, no other model loaded:

  | Scenario | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `clarification-then-fallthrough` | 0/3 | **5/5** |
  | `instance-not-schema-invoice` (control) | — | 5/5 |

  Re-run on the final two-turn rule: again **5/5** and **5/5**. The re-prompt fired on all 5 scored turns in both runs: each pass came through the new path, not a lucky first reply. The run reused a database where the model's search finds two plausible trackers, which is what produced the search-then-ask turns that failed before the write-only rule.

The full routing suite was not re-run. Its other scenarios start in a fresh chat, where no prior turn exists for the guard or re-prompt to read; the only change they see is the `route_clarify` description. Rewording that fixture's scenarios into the developer-workflow domain is #3189, which is sequenced after this merges.

## After merge

Update ADR-038's "What the agent loop does today" clarification-contract bullet: the contract is enforced from the persisted turn outcome; only a successful write closes an intent; the intent is clarified by a composed clarification or two non-writing turns.

author: memtomem
body:
Refs #169 (diagnostics only; the issue stays open).

## What
When `tests/smoke-hardening/60-viewer.sh` fails, a cleanup entry dumps to stderr:
- every viewer capture (`view-*.out`, last 120 lines, through `cat -v`);
- every stream's record and marker lines (`grep -an debate-round`, through `cat -v`, where `\x1e` shows as `^^`).

It runs from the part's cleanup, so it covers every assertion. It replaces the earlier per-assertion dump for line 100. On a pass it prints nothing.

## Why
The flake has now shown two signatures:
- **Line 100** (case 1): 5 `<!-- debate-round` markers shown. Seen locally several times, and once on hosted macOS.
- **Line 167** (case 3, continuing a finished debate): 2 `attempt failed` lines where no attempt failed. Seen on hosted macOS in run 36358715094, attempt 1.

The hosted macOS tally is 2 of 5 runs. Locally it did not reproduce in 132 runs of case 1, under CPU load or alongside the unittest suite.

## Evidence
- **Forced failure** (the expected value at line 167 temporarily set to 9): the log holds 4 capture headers and 6 stream headers, each starting its own line. An earlier draft glued headers onto captures that end without a newline; that is fixed.
- **Normal run:** 147 assertions passed, and no dump was printed.
- `shellcheck -S error` is clean.

## Also: a test race in wait57 (60-viewer.sh:667)
A hosted macOS run (#163) failed `wait57 ignore`: after printing `bounded=1`, bash reported the TERM-ignoring child it had just killed (`Killed: 9`). That job was left to be reaped at exit, and `wait57` captures stderr with stdout. The case now does `{ kill -9 "$pid" && wait "$pid"; } 2>/dev/null`. Measured with a minimal copy: the old form printed `Killed` 30 times in 30 when the shell outlived the kill; the new form 0 in 30. This is a harness race, not a viewer bug.

author: cirwel
body:
## What changed

- **`src/http_routes/access.py`: the trusted-network bypass.** This is the set of callers that skip auth in local posture on REST and the dashboard WebSocket.
  - **Built-in networks:** now loopback plus the RFC1918 private ranges only. `100.64.0.0/10` is removed. It is the CGNAT range Tailscale assigns from, and some ISPs also use it for carrier-grade NAT.
  - **`UNITARES_TRUSTED_NETWORKS`:** a new `extra_trusted_networks()` reads comma-separated CIDRs or addresses. Each entry is parsed **strictly**:
    - A bare address is a /32 or /128.
    - An entry that doesn't parse is logged and skipped. That includes a CIDR with host bits set, such as `203.0.113.7/8`, which is likely a typo for one host. It is never masked into a wider network.
    - The value is cached per raw string, so a changed setting is re-read on the next request, and warnings are logged once per value.
  - **Catch-all warning:** any setting that trusts every caller is honoured but logged, because it switches local-posture auth off. The check collapses the built-in ranges, the listed ranges, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 entries projected into IPv4 into one union per address family. It warns when that union covers a whole family, or when an IPv6 range contains `::ffff:0:0/96`.
  - **IPv4-mapped peers:** on a dual-stack bind, a peer written `::ffff:a.b.c.d` is also matched against the IPv4 ranges, both built-in and listed.
  - **Public OAuth listener:** still never trusted, whatever the setting says.
- **`src/services/mcp_transport_service.py`:** both uvicorn listeners now set `forwarded_allow_ips` to `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS = "127.0.0.0/8,::1/128,::ffff:127.0.0.0/104"`, where it was `"127.0.0.1"`.
  - **Why:** the bypass trusts all of loopback. A same-host reverse proxy that uvicorn did not recognise, such as one on `127.0.0.2`, `::1` or `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, would pass its public callers through on its own loopback trust.
  - **In `_is_trusted_network`'s docstring:** that this only covers proxies that set `X-Forwarded-For`. Header-less forwarders, and proxies on a trusted non-loopback address, still pass callers through. The docstring points to `UNITARES_REST_STRICT` or a bearer for those.
- **Config:**
  - `scripts/ops/com.unitares.governance-mcp.plist` gains `UNITARES_TRUSTED_NETWORKS`, empty, with a comment giving the reference deployment's `100.64.0.0/10`.
  - `.env.example` gains the same, commented. It is not added to Compose, on purpose: a Compose install publishes on `127.0.0.1`, and tailnet traffic reaches the container through the bridge gateway, which is already RFC1918.
- **Docs:**
  - `docs/FLAGS.md` is regenerated.
  - `docs/integration/MCP_CLIENTS.md` names the setting.
  - `docs/install/cross-machine-surface.md` records the reversal of its earlier "correct as a constant" row.
  - The `dashboard.py` comment and `open-decisions-packet-v0.md` no longer describe the tailnet as built-in trust.
  - The `unitares-dashboard` skill is re-attested.
- **Tests:**
  - **New `tests/test_trusted_networks.py`:**
    - defaults, and the CGNAT range refused by default;
    - adding a tailnet, several entries, bad entries and host-bits entries;
    - catch-alls, including split, mapped, cross-family and built-in-completed ones;
    - parse-and-log once per value;
    - IPv4-mapped peers;
    - the public listener;
    - a same-host proxy on every loopback form, run through `ProxyHeadersMiddleware`.
  - **Changed:** `test_ws_auth_align.py` and `test_rest_posture_decoupled.py` list the tailnet before asserting it is trusted, and the latter no longer uses the operator's own tailnet IP. `test_mcp_transport_service.py` pins both listeners to the constant.

## Why

The operator, when I asked whether to keep the Tailscale range: "are you asking me if outside users should inherit my tailscale address by default?" No, they shouldn't. The range was built into every install's default auth bypass, so a fresh install trusted callers from one operator's network layout. This is the same fresh-install leakage as #2499, #2523 and #2552, but in an auth decision. The review rounds then surfaced the dual-stack and same-host-proxy cases, which this PR also closes.

## Validation

- The five auth, transport and OAuth test files pass locally: 157 passed.
- `ruff`, `flag_catalog.py --check`, `check_fleet_identity_leak.py`, skill freshness and the proposal length ratchet are all clean.
- CI is fully green on `4069d32`.

## Review history

`access.py` is on the second-family list. Every finding below was fixed in this PR. The last round was clean from both families:

- **Codex:** P2s on IPv4-mapped peers, and on the catch-all union four times: split, mapped, cross-family and built-ins. Also a P2 on the proxy allow-list covering `127.0.0.2`. Codex found no issues on `622b9fc` and again on `4069d32`.
- **Claude, fresh-context subagents:**
  - P3s: strict parsing, stale prose, the catch-all union, the parse cache test, and the zone-suffixed `::1`.
  - One P2: the same-host proxy riding mapped-loopback trust.
  - CLEAN on `ed1b59f` and on `4069d32`.
- All records were posted via `review.sh record --emit`. The `review` check passes.

## Risk and rollout

- **Breaking for any deployment whose callers come over a tailnet**, including the reference deployment. Set `UNITARES_TRUSTED_NETWORKS=100.64.0.0/10` in the running LaunchAgent plist (or the environment) **before** deploying. Otherwise tailnet callers get 401 on REST and on the dashboard WebSocket.
- **`X-Forwarded-For` is now applied from every loopback peer.**
  - Previously only `127.0.0.1` counted. Now `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1` and `::ffff:127.0.0.0/104` do too.
  - A local process that sends the header can only replace its loopback trust with the named address's own trust. It gains nothing it didn't already have.
- **Not affected:**
  - Strict posture: a bearer or `UNITARES_REST_STRICT` already disables the bypass.
  - `/mcp`, which never had a network bypass.
  - Loopback and LAN callers.
- **Rollback:** revert, or set the variable.

## Reviewer focus

- **RFC1918 stays built in.** Compose needs `172.16.0.0/12` for the bridge gateway, and the other ranges keep the existing LAN behaviour. Narrowing them is a separate call.
- **#2549 interaction:** #2549's decision 7.3 reuses this list to decide which model endpoints count as "local". With this change, a tailnet-hosted model counts as local only when its range is listed, which matches 7.3's "Tailscale is not part of UNITARES setup".

- [x] The PR is one reviewable topic and links its issue or decision context.
- [x] Tests cover changed behavior, or this is documentation/configuration only.
- [x] User-facing behavior and compatibility notes are documented.
- [x] No credentials, private telemetry, or unrelated generated files are included.
- [x] Version, release, migration, and deployment steps are called out when applicable.

body:
Fixes #159823

## What Problem This Solves

Session reads in the Gateway protect a session key with the caller's current sharing predicate and retained read lifetime — `sessions.files.list`, `sessions.files.get`, `sessions.branches.list`, `progressCard.get` and `sessions.messages.subscribe` all go through `retainSessionScopedRead`. `sessions.diff` never did: the handler loaded the checkout diff and answered without ever binding the caller to the session. On the Gateway configuration #159823 reproduces against — operator roles configured, two identified profiles — that means

1. another person's **draft** session returns its diff to any identified operator who knows the key, through the real checkout reader, with real file changes, and
2. a read admitted while the session was visible keeps serving after the session is made a draft, is reassigned, or the caller's authority is revoked **during** the asynchronous diff.

### Real checkout-diff trace, base vs this head

Same probe, same script, real Gateway dispatcher + real session store + real `gateway.roles` policy + a real git checkout containing one committed file with one uncommitted edit. The reader is a separate profile with `operator.read`; the session belongs to another profile. Re-run on the exact head below.

On `origin/main` (`3ef1f6e8572c990abf187facdc066cf85582edcd`):

```text
TRACE visibility=shared -> {"ok":true,"files":[{"path":"note.txt","additions":1,"deletions":0}]}
TRACE visibility=draft  -> {"ok":true,"files":[{"path":"note.txt","additions":1,"deletions":0}]}   <-- another person's draft
```

On this head (`00b4a987c97`):

```text
TRACE visibility=shared -> {"ok":true,"files":[{"path":"note.txt","additions":1,"deletions":0}]}
TRACE visibility=draft  -> {"ok":false,"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Session \"agent:main:trace-diff\" was not found."}
```

The visible session still gets the same real diff payload; the draft now gets the same non-disclosing hidden-session response as its sibling reads.

Precedent: `#159823` is the tracked remainder of the closed `#144169`. `#155184` (merged) introduced `retainSessionScopedRead` and put `sessions.files.list` / `sessions.files.get` / `sessions.branches.list` / `progressCard.get` / `sessions.messages.subscribe` on it; `#136900` established the boundary predicate the exact-key reads use for callers that have an operator boundary.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-diff.ts` retains the scoped read through the existing `retainSessionScopedRead` owner, asserts it immediately before `respond`, and releases it in `finally` — the same composition `sessions-files.ts` and `progress-card.ts` use. `allowMetadataChanges: true` matches `sessions.branches.list`: the diff payload is derived from the checkout, the baseline and the session identity, so a concurrent label or activity update must not fail a working read, while visibility, caller authority and session identity must still hold when the response is built.

The guard is applied where a caller class actually has a boundary, using the predicate the exact-key reads already use (`hasOperatorBoundary` from `src/gateway/operator-role-policy.ts`, the expression `sessions-read-by-key.ts:123` pairs with `createSessionListEntryFilter`): configured operator roles, or a narrow session grant. A Gateway **without** `gateway.roles` keeps exactly the access it has today, per the reviewer's recommendation on the previous revision and #159823's own reproduction, which is scoped to "a Gateway with operator roles enabled".

No new option, configuration, persistence, validator, helper, or RPC surface. Production LOC is `+24/-6` in one file. The RPC's request/result schema, registered scope (`operator.read`) and error shapes are unchanged.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

<details>
<summary>Reviewer response: what changed for the 5fdea4bc review</summary>

That review raised two P1s. Both are addressed in this revision:

- **"Preserve the no-roles diff access contract (P1)."** Done as recommended: the retained read is now gated on `hasOperatorBoundary`, so an identified caller on a Gateway without `gateway.roles` keeps today's access. The behavior-preserving case below ("keeps a caller without an operator boundary on its existing access") asserts the per-method outcome and passes on both the base and this head.
- **"Prove rejection after authority changes during diff loading (P1)."** Done: the in-flight case is now parameterized over the three authority-chain changes the review named — `visibility`, `reassignment` (same key, new session id and lifecycle revision), and `authority` (the requester's live authority is revoked). Each case asserts that **nothing** reaches the caller while the read is still open, then observes the outcome the Gateway actually produces: the hidden-session refusal for a visibility change or a reassignment, and a transport-level rejection (`Gateway requester authority changed`, no response emitted at all) when authority is revoked. On the base all three observed the diff instead, so they are genuine RED -> GREEN cases.

The earlier P1 about the security-sensitive scope entry was resolved by removing that file from the PR entirely.

One difference remains and I am not hiding it: for a caller with **no** operator boundary, `sessions.diff` serves another person's draft while `sessions.files.list` refuses it. That divergence is pre-existing on `main` and this PR neither widens nor narrows it; the no-boundary case above pins it explicitly so a future decision is visible. Closing it means aligning `retainSessionScopedRead`'s no-boundary behavior for all of its consumers, which is an owner-level change beyond this repair.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Scope note and remaining gap</summary>

While verifying this defect I found a second, distinct omission in the same family and deliberately did **not** fix it here: `sessions.diff` is absent from `SESSION_READ_METHODS` in `src/shared/session-method-scopes-base.ts`, so a session-scoped caller (`operator.sessions.read`) cannot call the RPC at all, while `sessions.files.list`, `sessions.files.get`, `sessions.branches.list`, `sessions.describe` and `chat.history` all admit that grant. Measured on `origin/main` through the same dispatcher:

```text
caller=operator.sessions.read  sessions.diff       -> ok=false  {"code":"FORBIDDEN","details":{"code":"MISSING_SCOPE","missingScope":"operator.read"}}
caller=operator.sessions.read  sessions.files.list -> ok=false  {"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Session \"…\" was not found."}
```

Adding that entry **widens a caller permission** and the file is covered by this repository's security-sensitive guard (`security-sensitive-changed`), which is why it was split out of this PR; `#159823` is itself scoped to "the remaining diff handler". It is a one-line addition next to `sessions.files.list` / `sessions.files.get` and I can add it in a follow-up or here on request.

The issue also names `board.get` and `session.discussion.info` as unvalidated follow-ups; I did not revalidate or touch them, so they are not asserted as defects here.

</details>

## User Impact

- On a Gateway with operator roles, another person's draft session no longer returns a diff payload — through either the local-checkout reader or the stored-repository reader — including when the session becomes a draft, is reassigned, or the caller's authority is revoked while the diff is computed.
- **No change for Gateways without `gateway.roles`**: an identified caller keeps the read it has today.
- Visible sessions are unaffected: the real checkout trace returns the same payload before and after, a shared session still serves its diff, a metadata-only update (rename/activity) during the read still serves the diff, and a session with no row still returns the existing `unknown_session` result.
- No rendered markup, styling, copy, storage, migration, or upgrade steps. No UI source changes.

## Evidence

author: jselvalugo
body:
Replaces #67 (same commits, head 2fccf3e) under a new branch name, with the owner's approval. #67's preview database branch still recorded this PR's pre-renumber migration 0036, so every Netlify deploy preview there failed with "migration 0036_custom-field-show-in-list has been modified after being applied". A new branch gets a fresh preview database from the main one (`docs/runbooks/netlify.md`, second case). No code changed.

## Summary

Owner requests (2026-09-27): once in the University, a popup always prompts the user to acquire DenialDesk University, stating how long it is and that access starts at $299; and the courses are locked until access is purchased.

- **Access record:** `university_access`, one row per practice (migration 0037). RLS + FORCE with the shared tenant policy. A practice session may read only the state columns (migration 0038) and insert/update only the `requested_*` columns, so it can never grant itself access or read the operator's note or revoke reason. The operator grants and revokes through `src/domain/platform/university-access.ts` with the new `withTenantAsPlatform` helper (owner privileges; the tenant policy is defense in depth only, so every statement names the practice explicitly). Customer practices only; one active grant at a time; a row is revoked once.
- **Prompt (locked practices):** `AccessPrompt.tsx`, a native `<dialog>` that opens on every visit to `/university`. It shows what the program is and its length computed from the catalog (5 courses, 16 lessons, about 25 minutes, 12 Wiki articles today). It shows "Access starts at $299.00" (`UNIVERSITY_ACCESS_FROM_CENTS`, business content in integer cents), that the courses unlock for the whole practice once confirmed, and the courses disclaimer. Close, Escape, backdrop, and "Browse the catalog" dismiss it; nothing is remembered.
- **Requests:** "Request access" records the request on the practice row (audited `university.access_requested`) and confirms inline. Later visits show "Access requested on <date>" while the request is pending. A repeat within a minute, or a request from a practice that already has access, writes nothing. After a revoke the practice can request again, and the operator sees it as a new pending request. No follow-up is promised.
- **Lock:** the catalog shows "Locked" with no course links, and course and lesson routes redirect to `/university`. Lesson completion refuses through `completeLessonIfUnlocked`, tested for locked, granted, and revoked practices. The Wiki is not gated.
- **Operator console:** the practice page has a "DenialDesk University" panel (Not requested / Requested / Access granted + order reference / Revoked + reason) with "Grant access" and "Revoke access". Both are audited (`operator.university_access_granted` / `_revoked`), and the panel shows only the latest outcome.
- Migration 0038 also adds `university_access` to `purge_demo_practices()`.
- Copy in the `university` (`access.*`) and `operator` (`university.*`) namespaces in English, Spanish, and Portuguese.
- Spec section "Access" in `docs/specs/denialdesk-university.md`, project state, and owner item **OA-044** (pricing terms, how a practice pays, who watches for requests).

## Requirement IDs

R-7.2.4 (tenant isolation of the new table), R-7.5.1 (request, grant, and revoke are audited), R-7.4.8 (nothing in URLs), §11 (accessible modal: labelled, described by its body, focus-contained, keyboard-dismissable), R-11.1 (three languages). The paid offer itself has no requirement ID; it is an owner request recorded in the spec.

## SOC 2 controls touched

CC6.1 (RLS, column-level privileges, operator-only grant), CC7.2 (three audit events), CC8.1 (migrations 0037–0038, spec, tests), CC2.3 (customer-facing offer wording).

## Data-classification impact

Internal. `university_access` holds tenant and user IDs, timestamps, an optional operator order reference, and a revoke reason; no PHI. Audit rows add actor, practice, and the price shown.

## New dependencies

None.

## Test evidence

On the merged tree (base through #69 included, merge commit 2fccf3e), against PostgreSQL 16 and a production build:

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`: clean.
- `pnpm test`: 825 passed.
- `pnpm test:integration`: 365 passed (39 migrations). `university-access.test.ts` covers:
  - Locked by default.
  - Request is one row per practice and audited.
  - App role can't set grant columns or read the note.
  - Unfiltered cross-practice read and update see nothing.
  - Operator grant unlocks; repeat grant refused.
  - Revoke needs a reason, happens once, and locks; re-request after revoke is pending; re-grant re-opens.
  - Customer-only grants.
  - Requested-only revoke refused.
  - Completion guard for locked, granted, and revoked practices.
  - The repeat-request window.
  
  `demo-purge.test.ts` seeds an access row.
- `pnpm test:e2e` (university, operator, shell, patients) on a freshly migrated database: 49 passed.
- CI on 2fccf3e (in #67): lint/types/unit, integration, end-to-end, container build, and secrets scan all green.

## Reviewer-agent results

- **reviewer:**
  - Prompt commit: 3 blocking items fixed.
  - Gate commit: 4 blocking items (re-request after revoke, operator visibility of re-requests, double status banner, untested completion lock) fixed in 606d3fa, and the follow-up review confirmed all four with no new blocking findings.
  - Optional items applied: request audit on the row id, logged failures, list markup, Portuguese "clínica", dismiss label.
- **security-reviewer:** approve, no Critical/High. Medium items fixed (real cross-practice read test; accurate helper docstring). Low items fixed (operator functions moved to the platform domain, customer-only grants, revoke once, operator-only columns hidden, repeat-request window). Needs a human: whether the Netlify database role is superuser/BYPASSRLS, and sign-off on the new owner-role helper (R-15.9).
- **compliance-checker:** 2 blocking wording items fixed on the prompt commit. Its concern about showing a price for free content is resolved by the lock. Needs a human: OA-044 (terms, payment, request owner) and OA-038 (the "University" name).

## Checklist

- [x] Synthetic data only; no PHI in code, fixtures, logs, or snapshots
- [x] No legal deadline, rate, or threshold outside `rules/` (the price is a business value)
- [x] Spec and roadmap checkboxes updated
- [x] IAM / branch protection / audit-logging changes called out for human sign-off:
  - New audit actions `university.access_requested`, `operator.university_access_granted`, and `operator.university_access_revoked`.
  - New `withTenantAsPlatform` database helper (owner role, operator writes only).
  - Column-level grants on `university_access`.
  - No IAM changes.

author: mrhodlx
body:
Keep derived address keys as wipeable bytes; encode WIFs only on demand (#546 B2)

Every derived address row built its private key as a WIF string and a hex
string, even while private values were hidden. Strings cannot be erased,
so a 2 x 10 view held 40 key strings per account for the whole session.
The row already had the key as bytes and zeroed them, keeping only the
strings ("the row keeps its strings").

Rows now keep that byte copy (and the non-secret network) and no key
text. hodlRowWif encodes a WIF only where one is shown or exported:

- The address table encodes a row's WIF only while private values are
  revealed, and a virtualized table only for the rows on screen. Hidden,
  the cell masks the fixed WIF length (every compressed WIF is 52
  characters) instead of encoding the key to measure it.
- The recovery sheet encodes the WIFs it prints.
- Nothing read row.privHex; it is gone.

Wiping the bytes:

- Wipe zeroes the wallet's row keys, but only once no key tab, shown
  result or Key Manager entry still holds that result. The Key Station
  and a tab committed from it share one result (hodlCloneDerivedKey), so
  zeroing on one tab's Wipe would leave the other rendering zeroed keys.
- pagehide and a persisted pageshow zero every derived wallet's row
  keys, shared ones included.
- The Key Manager reset (Journal lock, unlock, create, wipe) already
  zeroes every byte array its pending keys reach. A key detached from a
  station can share its result with one still shown, so the reset now
  skips results a station still shows.
- The Ignored-keys copy is JSON; it now leaves byte arrays behind (it is
  read only for identity, and JSON would turn key bytes into plain
  numbers no wipe reaches).

Contract: while a wallet's private values are hidden, no derived address
row holds a private key as text; every WIF shown or exported is unchanged;
Wipe and page teardown zero the key bytes of rows nothing still shows.

Initial red on f2ab995:

  node --test test/secret-clear.test.mjs
  -> 5 fail: rows hold their private keys as text; Wipe leaves the row
     key bytes in memory; pagehide leaves them; the Ignored copy keeps
     them; a Key Manager reset zeroes keys the Key Station still shows.
     (The reveal test fails on the missing hodlRowWif, a new function;
     its expected WIFs come from @scure/bip32 and an independent
     Base58Check encoder.)

Green after: secret-clear 39/39. npm run build && npm test: 1569 pass,
1 fail (browser harness: no browser on PATH), 0 skipped with bitcoind on
PATH. Browser suite (Chromium): 99/103, the same 4 failures as rock in
this environment.

Equivalence, rock's built page vs this one in Chromium: five Key Station
wallets (12 and 24 words, with and without a passphrase, BIP44/49/84/86,
mainnet and testnet, accounts 0, 3 and 7, up to 120 rows virtualized).
The hidden view, the revealed view, every scroll window of every table
and the private recovery sheet are byte-identical, and the hidden view
carries no WIF.

Fault injection, each reverted, each caught by its own test: rows
keeping the WIF text, Wipe ignoring shared results, Wipe never zeroing,
pagehide skipping the rows, the Ignored copy keeping bytes, and the Key
Manager reset walking shown wallets.

Still text after this: the seed phrase and passphrase, which start as
text in their inputs, and the wallet-level secrets (seed hex, root xprv,
single-key WIFs), which are the next B2 step.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_0144Dr81BKQUUtKnh4bLcLxq

@timechainb this touches the private-value reveal and the address-table rendering, with no visual change.

### Follow-up after review: 792e3c7

Astra's NACK: a derivation's rows are local variables until it commits, so a stopped, wiped, hidden, failed or declined derivation left its row keys unzeroed.

Each key derivation now records the row keys it makes and zeroes those no station shows when it ends. Invalidation (Wipe, pagehide, persisted pageshow) zeroes them at once. A stopped derivation's account node, and an imported account key's node, are now wiped in a finally.

Contract: once a key derivation has stopped, failed or been declined, or the page has invalidated it, no row key it made holds a nonzero byte. A committed derivation's keys, and every key a station shows, are kept.

Initial red on a922da3: node --test test/secret-clear.test.mjs -> 10 fail, each on the bytes. Green after: 49/49. npm test 1571 pass, 1 fail (no browser on PATH), 8 skipped. Chromium browser suite 99/103, the same 4 failures as rock. The equivalence run is byte-identical again. Fault injection: 7 weakenings, each caught.

Known remaining gap (planned for B2 step 2): results the station drops on an edit, a re-derive or a tab delete are not zeroed.

body:
## Summary

Fixes #12628.

`ck_tile::Alibi` defaults to `LogMaxSadOprndSize = 16`, which computes the ALiBi distance with a 16-bit `sad_u16`. With that default, the fwd (non-trload), bwd, pagedkv and batch_prefill FMHA kernels return wrong results whenever `seqlen_q` or `seqlen_k` exceeds 65536.

This PR passes `32` at those eight call sites, matching what `fmha_fwd_splitkv_kernel.hpp` and the trload branch of `fmha_fwd_kernel.hpp` already do. Only the template argument changes (plus clang-format re-alignment of the continuation lines). Results for sequence lengths up to 65536 are unchanged.

## Test plan

Ran `tile_example_fmha_fwd` / `tile_example_fmha_bwd` with CPU validation (`-v=1`) on gfx950 (MI350X), ROCm 7.1, bf16, hdim 128, b=1, h=2, s_q=16, `-bias=a`. The build included only the ALiBi bf16 d128 instances (`--filter`), with separate builds for `FMHA_FWD_ENABLE_APIS` = `fwd`, `pagedkv_prefill` and `batch_prefill`.

| kernel | before (s_k = 65536 / 65537 / 70000) | after (s_k = 1024, 65536, 65537, 70000, 131072) |
|---|---|---|
| fmha_fwd, mask 0 and 2 | valid / fail / fail | all valid |
| fmha_fwd_pagedkv (`-page_block_size=128`), mask 0 and 2 | valid / fail / fail | all valid |
| fmha_batch_prefill (`-mode=1 -page_block_size=16`), mask 0 and 2 | valid / fail / fail | all valid |
| fmha_bwd, mask 0 | valid / fail / fail | all valid |

These runs used CK at c56c6750d, where the eight sites are identical to develop. The diff applies cleanly to develop @ 973351c.

- [x] gfx950 validation as above
- [x] New gtest cases `TestCkTileFmhaFwdLongSeqlen/Alibi` and `TestCkTileFmhaBwdLongSeqlen/Alibi` (seqlen_k 65537 and 70000, hdim 128, masks `0` and `b`): all 14 fail without the fix and pass with it (fp16 and bf16, gfx950). The existing `Alibi` suites still pass.
- [x] Same fix verified end to end through Flash-Attention's CK backend (fwd and bwd, 40-case seqlen scan)
- [ ] CI on other architectures

author: creed1759
body:
## Summary

This PR resolves four issues across `@lumen/types`, `@lumen/server`, and `@lumen/react`.

---

### Close #172 — FeeLimitRule: enforce maximum transaction fee in the policy engine

The fee sponsor wraps and pays fees for user transactions, but the policy engine previously had no visibility into the inner transaction fee. A client could construct a transaction requesting an arbitrarily high max fee (e.g. 100 XLM), which the sponsor would pay on fee-bump.

**Changes:**
- `packages/types/src/policy.ts`: added `FeeLimitRule` interface (`type: 'fee_limit'; maxFeeStroops: number`) and added it to the `PolicyRule` union.
- `packages/types/src/index.ts`: exported `FeeLimitRule` from the package.
- `packages/server/src/policy/engine.ts`: imported `FeeLimitRule`; implemented `evaluateFeeLimit()` which reads `transaction.fee` in stroops and returns `{ approved: false, reason: 'Transaction fee exceeds maximum allowed fee limit' }` when it exceeds `maxFeeStroops`; wired into the `evaluateRule()` switch.
- `packages/server/src/validation.ts`: added `FeeLimitRuleSchema` (Zod: `type: 'fee_limit'`, `maxFeeStroops: positive int`) and included it in the `PolicyRuleSchema` discriminated union.

---

### Close #173 — Dispatch balance.low webhook event via WebhookDispatcher in SponsorMonitorService

`SponsorMonitorService` previously sent a raw HTTP POST to an optional `SPONSOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` on low balance, but did not use the server's `WebhookDispatcher`. Subscribers registered via `POST /webhooks` with event `balance.low` never received notifications.

**Changes:**
- `packages/server/src/fee-sponsor/monitor.ts`: added `webhookDispatcher?: WebhookDispatcher` to `SponsorMonitorOpts`; stored it on the service; in `checkBalance()`, when `isLow` is detected, calls `this.webhookDispatcher?.dispatch('balance.low', { sponsorPublicKey, balance, threshold })`.
- `packages/server/src/server.ts`: passes `webhookDispatcher` when constructing `SponsorMonitorService` so all registered `balance.low` subscribers receive events.

---

### Close #182 — Export useTransactionHistory from @lumen/react index

`useTransactionHistory` existed in `packages/react/src/use-transaction-history.ts` but was not re-exported from `packages/react/src/index.ts`, making it unreachable to library consumers.

**Changes:**
- `packages/react/src/index.ts`: added `export { useTransactionHistory }` and `export type { Transaction, UseTransactionHistoryResult }` from `./use-transaction-history.js`.

---

### Close #183 — Add useSessionKey React hook to @lumen/react

Session keys allow pre-authorizing temporary keypairs with a spend cap and time limit for gasless, prompt-free interactions. `@lumen/react` had no dedicated hook for managing the session key lifecycle.

**Changes:**
- `packages/react/src/use-session-key.ts`: new `useSessionKey(walletId, durationSeconds?)` hook exposing:
  - `sessionKey` — active session `{ publicKey, expiresAt }` or `null`
  - `createSession(durationSeconds?)` — generates a session keypair via `client.createSessionKey()` and stores state
  - `revokeSession()` — clears the active session
  - `isExpired` — boolean, true when `Date.now() >= expiresAt`
  - `timeRemainingSeconds` — live countdown ticking every second via `setInterval`
  - `isLoading` and `error` state
- `packages/react/src/index.ts`: exported `useSessionKey` and `SessionKeyState`.

---

## Testing

No new tests added per task instructions. Pre-existing build errors (unrelated workspace linking issues) were not introduced by this PR.

author: nickvigilante
body:
## Summary

Ghostty sends `TERM=xterm-ghostty` to every remote host it SSHes into. Most remote hosts' terminfo databases don't have an entry under that exact name, and on a host running a shell that does live redraw (oh-my-zsh + `zsh-autosuggestions` + `zsh-syntax-highlighting` + a dynamic prompt), the unresolvable `TERM` makes `zle`'s redraw logic misbehave -- producing garbled/duplicated keystroke echo. Confirmed reproducing over SSH into gandalf from Ghostty; not reproduced from Warp (which sends `TERM=xterm-256color`), and not reproduced SSHing from Ghostty into a host running a plain default shell (no live-redraw widgets to trip the bug).

## Changes

- Add `SetEnv TERM=xterm-256color` to the existing `Host *` block in `home/dot_ssh/create_config`, so every SSH session requests a universally-supported `TERM` regardless of destination.
- Deliberately scoped as a blanket `Host *` rule rather than naming specific hosts, to keep internal homelab hostnames out of this public repo (existing convention -- see `~/.ssh/config.local`, sourced from a private Bitwarden note).

## Notes

- Ghostty 1.4.0+ (currently a tip/nightly build) has a proper fix via `shell-integration-features = ssh-terminfo`, which installs the real terminfo entry per host instead of overriding `TERM`. That's a local Ghostty config change, not something this repo manages -- worth revisiting once that's in a stable release.
- `~/.ssh/config` uses chezmoi's `create_` semantics (create once, never overwritten after), so this change will only take effect automatically on newly-bootstrapped machines. Already-provisioned machines need the same `SetEnv TERM=xterm-256color` line added to their existing `~/.ssh/config` by hand.

## Testing

- `pre-commit run --files home/dot_ssh/create_config` passes, including the "chezmoi templates render + shell syntax" check.

---

body:
Fixes #41 (BUG-009). Version **2.25.2** (patch).

## Problem
When Whisper transcription failed, `WhisperClient` set its error to `Whisper API error (HTTP n, model m): ` + the first 300 characters of OpenAI's response body. That body is a JSON error object, so the New Bug / New Feature dictation line showed raw JSON — including the masked key fragment OpenAI echoes — and no next step. The terminal mic tooltip and the Settings self-test used the same string.

Reproduced with a fake key: HTTP 401, `{"error": {"message": "Incorrect API key provided: sk-fake-****…", "code": "invalid_api_key", …}}`.

## Changes
- `TranscriptionFailure` (end of `WhisperClient.swift`, pure): HTTP status + OpenAI `error.code`/`type` → problem, next step, tag `(HTTP 401 · invalid_api_key)`. Covers bad key, no credit, rate limit, unavailable/forbidden model, region, too large/short, other 4xx, 5xx, non-JSON bodies, offline, timeout. Only snake_case codes reach the tag; the body is never displayed or logged.
- `WhisperClient.errorOpensSettings` → `DictationController.opensSettings` → **Open DDE Settings** button in `DictationStatusView`.
- `DDESettingsWindow`: the DDE Settings window opener, moved out of `MarkViewApp` so the menu and the intake sheet share one window.
- Docs: BUG-009 resolution, architecture notes, test tables, todo, lesson.

Example: *OpenAI rejected the API key. Check or replace the key in DDE Settings. (HTTP 401 · invalid_api_key)* [Open DDE Settings]

body:
## Summary

Fix production tutorial links that redirect from `/openshell/latest/tutorials/*` to the retired `/openshell/latest/get-started/tutorials/*` tree and return 404. The docs snapshot sync updates pages and navigation but never synchronizes `redirects`, so obsolete production rules survive both stable and dev publishes.

## Related Issue

No issue required: a localized documentation publishing bug. Searches of open and closed issues and PRs found no existing fix for redirect synchronization. #3713 addresses separate navigation/slug problems (including invalid `about/run-an-agent` redirect destinations), but does not change this sync path.

## Changes

- Synchronize redirects with their owning mutable snapshot, replacing removed rules as well as adding/updating rules. A versioned source takes precedence over its destination when determining ownership; unversioned aliases to a versioned destination follow that version. `dev` owns shared fallback rules.
- Update `latest` rules only when stable promotion succeeds, preserving other versions and preventing an older maintenance release from rolling back current routing. Keep version-specific rules before shared wildcards.
- Document channel ownership and manual repair, and update the docs contributor skill.

Audited 115 published navigation URLs, checking both the default unversioned paths and explicit `/latest` paths. Exactly 10 returned 404: each of the following with and without `/latest`:

| Page | Path below `/openshell[/latest]` |
| --- | --- |
| Tutorials landing | `/tutorials` |
| Run Pi with OpenRouter | `/tutorials/run-pi-with-openrouter` |
| First Network Policy | `/tutorials/first-network-policy` |
| GitHub Push Access | `/tutorials/github-push-access` |
| Microsoft Graph Provider Refresh | `/tutorials/microsoft-graph-provider-refresh` |

These also affect 11 authored MDX links: the home Tutorials card; the Pi link in Run Your First Agent; links in provider profiles, sandbox overview, policy overview, network rules, and the first network policy tutorial; and four cards in the currently orphaned tutorials index. The four tutorial sidebar entries are affected too. The canonical versioned Pi URL under `/v0.1.1/tutorials/run-pi-with-openrouter` returns 200.

After merging, repair production with a `latest` snapshot sync and publish using the updated automation. Retain the source SHA, release version, display name, and availability recorded on `docs-website`. Republishing `docs-website` without syncing will retain the stale redirects. A local replay against the actual production configuration and v0.1.1 source removed all four obsolete rules and installed the correct tutorial aliases without changing the version entries. This PR does not publish production.

## Testing

- [x] `mise run pre-commit` passes.
- [x] Unit regression tests: all 29 docs snapshot tests pass; all three new cases fail against the original implementation. They cover both `latest` and `stable`, deleted redirects, repeated syncs, other-version preservation, wildcard ordering, and older maintenance releases.
- [x] `mise run test` passes (complete Rust, Python, TypeScript, and tooling suite).
- [x] `mise run python:typecheck` and all 29 docs tests pass after the final type annotation correction.
- [x] `mise run docs`: zero errors, three warnings.

author: google-labs-stitch[bot]
body:
## Summary

Fixes WebRTC file transfer stalls caused by race conditions during backpressure buffer draining.

When checking `bufferedAmount` prior to awaiting `bufferedamountlow`, if the data channel buffer drains fast or completes during listener registration, the system missed the `bufferedamountlow` event and file transfers stalled indefinitely.

This PR introduces:
1. **Immediate Buffer Recheck**: Attaches the `bufferedamountlow` listener and immediately re-evaluates `bufferedAmount` before awaiting event resolution. If `bufferedAmount <= targetThreshold`, the listener is removed and the promise resolves immediately.
2. **Polling & Channel State Fallback**: Implements a safety timer polling fallback (25ms in JS, 20ms ticker in Go) that periodically re-checks `bufferedAmount` and validates `readyState === 'open'`. If the channel closes, the wait rejects cleanly with an error instead of hanging indefinitely.
3. **Zero Memory Leaks**: Guarantees cleanup of event listeners (`removeEventListener`) and intervals across all resolution/rejection paths.
4. **Unit Test Suite**: Adds 5 comprehensive test cases covering immediate resolution, event resolution, immediate recheck during attachment, polling fallback on missed events, and channel closure handling.

## Verification

- **JS Unit Tests**: `npm test` passed 30/30 tests across 4 test suites (`Gaze Web Receiver Test Suite`, `Gaze Web Sender Test Suite`, `WebRTC Buffer Backpressure Suite`, `Service Worker Stream Cleanup & RFC 6266 Tests`).
- **Go Unit & Integration Tests**: `go test -v ./...` passed all tests.
- **Go Build Verification**: `npm run build:go` succeeded without errors.

author: esoinila
body:
#251 batch 6 is long methods, and only where an existing test already pins the exact output, so an extraction can be proven not to change behaviour. Two of the candidates had such a test and are extracted here. The rest are skipped, and each skip says whether it was missing that test or had control flow that can't be cut verbatim.

## What was extracted

| method | was | is | extracted into | oracle |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|
| `HavenInterior.BuildComplex` | 625 | **129** | 13 named steps in the new partial `HavenInterior.Build.Steps.cs` (605) | every docked haven frame in `EveryFrameHashesTheSameTests` |
| `UndergroundComplex.AddRoomsAlong` | 322 | **34** | `LayTheColumn` (137) · `CarveTheRecesses` (131), same file | the luna B1–B13, phobos B1 and titan B1 frames plus the Hive fingerprint sequences |

`HavenInterior.Build.cs` goes from 705 to 209 lines.

**How each extraction was done:**
* **Statements are unchanged and in their original order.** Each helper's body is a run of the original method, character for character. A check on disk found every non-blank line of each base file in the output: **0 missing, 0 changed.** The only new lines are the calls, the signatures, the braces, docblocks, and three `return <list>;` lines for the steps that create a list.
* **Side effects happen in the same sequence.** The lists (`walls`, `doors`, `labels`, `consoles`, `hatches`, and the `column` array) are passed by reference, and each step appends to them exactly where the original statements did. Three steps create a list (`SetTheTables`, `HangTheBackdrops`, `FitTheGallery`) and return it at the spot where the original declared it. `CarveTheRecesses` returns exactly what `AddRoomsAlong` returned.
* **One statement moved.** In `BuildComplex` the `hatches` list is now allocated one statement earlier, before the ring's vertex loop instead of after it. That only creates an empty list, so nothing observable changes.
* **Nothing else changed.** No literal, seed string, iteration order or static field was touched. The steps are private static methods of the same partial class. `LayTheColumn` and `CarveTheRecesses` take only the locals their own statements read (worked out from their code), and the build reports 0 warnings.

## The oracles are live: each one fails on a deliberate reorder

For each extraction I made a small reorder, watched the pinned ledger fail, then reverted the change. `SPACESAILS_REPIN` was unset for these runs, and the ledger files were never touched.

* **`BuildComplex`.** I swapped two step calls (`LayTheBar` before `LayTheImmigrationDesk`). Result: `EveryFrameHashesTheSameTests.EveryCaseDrawsTheFrameThatWasPinnedOnTheOldCode` went RED.
* **`AddRoomsAlong`.** I reversed the side loop inside `LayTheColumn`. Result: `EveryFrameHashesTheSameTests` plus three `EveryFrameLeavesTheSameFingerprintTests` cases went RED (`AHiveFloorWithAPatrol × AHandOnTheWarpSlider / SteadyFrames`, `ACaptainInAChair × APlannedRoute`).

With the extractions exactly as committed, every ledger passes and the ledger diff is empty:
```
$ git diff --stat origin/our-own-ship-has-compartments -- tests/SpaceSails.Client.Tests/Ledgers/
(nothing)
```

## The gate: exactly which runs happened

**Per commit, targeted:**
* **`BuildComplex`.** Core: the static-field law and the size gate, 6 tests. Client: the four ledgers plus every haven / docked-bar / walls-hung / observation-walk / T-walk / eighth-seat / ride-down class, 127 tests.
* **`AddRoomsAlong`.** Core: the static-field law, the size gate and 208 fire-code / recess / lane / underground / floor guards, 214 tests. Client: the four ledgers, 43 tests.

**Full Release suites, once, on the PR tip:**
```
Passed!  - Failed:     0, Passed:  2395, Skipped:     0, Total:  2395 - SpaceSails.Client.Tests.dll (net10.0)
Passed!  - Failed:     0, Passed:  5176, Skipped:     0, Total:  5176 - SpaceSails.Core.Tests.dll (net10.0)
```
These counts are higher than #1303's because this branch was cut from a base that had gained tests since. CI is the merge gate, not these numbers.

(The `AddRoomsAlong` commit message says "322 → 7 lines". That miscounts: the method is **34** lines including its comments, as the table above says.)

## Skipped, and why

* **`UndergroundComplex.CarveBins` (332): the structure can't be cut verbatim.** Its placers (good offices, hall, park, lift) all call the local function `TakeTheBin`, which captures `bins`, the collision segments, the furniture list and `walls`. Moving any placer out would mean turning that closure into parameters or a delegate. That is a rewrite of how it runs, not a cut of its statements.
* **`UndergroundComplex.CarveRefuges` (169): the structure can't be cut verbatim.** It has four early `return refuges;` statements through its middle. Extracting a block that contains them means rewriting the returns (`return;`, or a flag), which is not verbatim.
* **The second `UndergroundComplex.LiftPanel` (226): the structure can't be cut verbatim.** It is a decision ladder with five early returns, and the final stop reads about twelve flag locals. Any helper would have to hand those flags back as a new tuple. That is a rewrite.
* **`TransferPlanner.Solve` (253): no oracle.** `TransferPlannerTests` checks bounds (a plan is found, Δv under a ceiling, arrival under the capture speed), determinism (the same request twice gives the same numbers), and failure messages. Nothing pins the numeric result over a seeded set, and the brief made that the condition.
* **`Map.Surface.Reevers.StepReevers` (413): the structure can't be cut verbatim.** The method is one 312-line per-Reever `foreach` that uses `continue` and writes the frame's `caught` flag. Cutting the loop body out would mean rewriting both. The pack-shove block after the loop could move verbatim, but that is about 30 lines of a 413-line method, and the Reever property and replay tests are not the byte-exact end-to-end pin the brief asked for.
* **`Map.Vault.cs`: no byte-exact oracle.** It is three methods (149, 185 and 333 lines). Eleven guards read the save and restore halves side by side, and the round-trip tests check behaviour rather than pinning the output. By the brief's rule, it stays as it is.

body:
Adds the main Christian and US national holidays, plus one monthly observance theme per month. Each one appears in two places:

- **Visitor hero themes on `/events`**: gradient, heading, badge, floating emojis and confetti, chosen from the theme picker.
- **Coordinator presets on `/coordinator/settings/styling`**: one-click `primary_color`/`secondary_color` pairs for `/c/$slug` and the embed.

There are no database changes. Existing saved choices keep working: the `eh:holiday-theme` and `eh:christmas-variant` keys, the four original ids, the Christmas Emerald/Ruby/Alternate hero, and all 12 original preset hex values are unchanged.

## Themes added

**Christian holidays** (Christmas kept as-is)
| Theme | Date rule | Presets |
|---|---|---|
| Epiphany ⭐ | January 6 | Star of Bethlehem, Magi Gold |
| Ash Wednesday & Lent 🙏 | Easter − 46 days, through the Saturday before Palm Sunday | Lenten Violet, Ash & Stone |
| Palm Sunday 🌿 | Easter − 7 | Palm Fronds, Olive Branch |
| Good Friday ✝️ | Easter − 2 | Solemn Black, Passion Crimson |
| Easter 🌷 | First Sunday after the first full moon on or after Mar 21 (Anonymous Gregorian algorithm) | Easter Lily, Sunrise Service |
| Pentecost 🔥 | Easter + 49 | Tongues of Fire, Holy Spirit Dove |
| All Saints' Day 😇 | November 1 | Saints' Gold, Candlelight |
| Advent 🕯️ | 4th Sunday before Christmas (a Sunday between Nov 27 and Dec 3) through Dec 24 | Advent Purple, Rose Sunday |

**National and widely observed holidays** (Halloween and Thanksgiving kept as-is)
| Theme | Date rule |
|---|---|
| New Year's Day 🥂 | January 1 |
| Martin Luther King Jr. Day 🕊️ | 3rd Monday in January |
| Valentine's Day 💝 | February 14 |
| Presidents' Day 🎩 | 3rd Monday in February |
| St. Patrick's Day ☘️ | March 17 |
| Mother's Day 💐 | 2nd Sunday in May |
| Memorial Day 🇺🇸 | Last Monday in May |
| Father's Day 👔 | 3rd Sunday in June |
| Juneteenth ✊🏿 | June 19 |
| Independence Day 🎆 | July 4 |
| Labor Day 👷 | 1st Monday in September |
| Columbus Day / Indigenous Peoples' Day 🧭 | 2nd Monday in October |
| Veterans Day 🎖️ | November 11 |

Each of these has two presets.

**Monthly observances** (one theme and one preset per month)
| Month | Observance | Source | Preset |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jan | National Blood Donor Month (first proclaimed for January 1970) | [American Red Cross](https://www.redcross.org/about-us/news-and-events/news/Resolve-to-Give-during-National-Blood-Donor-Month.html) | Blood Donor Red |
| Feb | American Heart Month (Proclamation 3566, proclaimed every year since 1964) | [American Presidency Project](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/proclamation-3566-american-heart-month-1964) | Heart Health |
| Mar | Women's History Month (Pub. L. 100-9, 1987) | [womenshistorymonth.gov](https://womenshistorymonth.gov/About.html) | Suffrage Purple & Gold |
| Apr | Earth Month (Earth Day, Apr 22) | [US EPA](https://www.epa.gov/history/epa-history-earth-day) | Earth Month |
| May | Mental Health Awareness Month (Mental Health America, since 1949) | [Wikipedia summary of MHA history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_Health_Awareness_Month) | Green Ribbon |
| Jun | National Country Cooking Month + National Iced Tea Month (combined, as requested) | [National Today (Country Cooking)](https://nationaltoday.com/national-country-cooking-month/), [TeaTime Magazine (Iced Tea)](https://teatimemagazine.com/june-is-national-iced-tea-month/) | Sweet Tea & Biscuits |
| Jul | Park and Recreation Month (NRPA, since 1985) | [NRPA](https://www.nrpa.org/events/july/) | Great Outdoors |
| Aug | National Back to School Month | [DoD Work-Life campaign](https://www.dcpas.osd.mil/sites/default/files/August-DoD%20Work-Life%20Health%20and%20Wellness%20Campaign.pdf) | School Bus & Apple |
| Sep | National Hispanic Heritage Month (Sep 15 – Oct 15, law since 1988) | [hispanicheritagemonth.gov](https://hispanicheritagemonth.gov/) | Fiesta Colors |
| Oct | National Breast Cancer Awareness Month (ACS, since 1985) | [American Cancer Society](https://www.cancer.org/cancer/latest-news/our-impact/turning-awareness-into-action-40-years-of-breast-cancer-awareness-month.html) | Pink Ribbon |
| Nov | National Native American Heritage Month (first designated 1990) | [nativeamericanheritagemonth.gov](https://nativeamericanheritagemonth.gov/About.html) | Earth & Sky |
| Dec | Universal Human Rights Month (UN Human Rights Day, Dec 10) | [United Nations](https://www.un.org/en/observances/human-rights-day) | Human Rights Blue |

Choices that need your call:
- **February:** I picked American Heart Month over Black History Month. It has an annual presidential proclamation and works well as a heart-health visual. Valentine's Day is also red and hearts, so the Heart Month palette leans toward health (🏃🥗🚴).
- **September:** Hispanic Heritage Month is the most widely recognized observance, but it runs Sep 15 – Oct 15, and the date shown says so. The runner-up was National Preparedness Month (FEMA).
- **December:** December's observances are thin because the month is dominated by holidays that already have themes. Universal Human Rights Month was the most established option that also works visually.
- **Iced Tea / Country Cooking:** these come from food-holiday calendars, not an official proclamation. They are included because you asked for them.

Federal holiday rules are from [OPM, 5 U.S.C. 6103](https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/). Moving Christian dates were checked against the [USCCB 2026 liturgical calendar](https://www.usccb.org/resources/2026cal.pdf): Ash Wednesday Feb 18, Easter Apr 5, Pentecost May 24.

## Tone for religious and solemn days
- Good Friday has a dark, subdued hero with no confetti. Its emojis are cross, candle, praying hands, book and dove, with no bunnies or eggs.
- Ash Wednesday & Lent has a stone and violet hero with no confetti.
- Easter leads with ✝️🕊️🌷🌅. The egg appears only as the last of six emojis.
- Palm Sunday, All Saints', Advent, MLK Day, Memorial Day, Veterans Day, Breast Cancer Awareness Month, Mental Health Awareness Month and Human Rights Month get a short, slow, sparse "muted" confetti burst.

## UI
- **Styling page:** tabs for Coming up (the default), Christian holidays, National holidays, Monthly observances and Seasonal.
  - Every holiday shows its next date, its rule, and a Now / Tomorrow / In N days badge.
  - Each group marks its soonest holiday as "Next up".
  - A line at the top names the current look.
- **Theme picker:** Default, then three "Coming up" shortcuts, then a submenu per group. The Christmas variant submenu is unchanged.
- All date logic lives in `src/lib/holiday-dates.ts`: pure functions at UTC midnight, independent of time zone and DST.

## Contrast (WCAG AA)
- The embed prints event dates in the brand color, and `/c/$slug` draws a white icon on it.
- Every **new** preset's primary color meets 4.5:1 on white.
- Six of the **original** presets don't: Golden Harvest #f59e0b is 2.15:1, Playful Pumpkin 1.92, Golden Elegance 2.94, Classic Red & Green 3.30, Classic Trick-or-Treat 3.56 and Winter Frost 4.10.
- Changing those hex values would silently drop coordinators who already use them, because `findPresetByColor` matches on the exact hex. Instead, the embed now sets `--ehx-brand-text: readableTextColor(brand)`, the same hue darkened just enough to pass AA. This also covers any custom color. The saved color itself is untouched.

## Bugs fixed along the way
1. **The intro confetti never used the visitor's theme.** The theme is in localStorage, so the hydration render always had `theme = null`, and the mount effect captured that. Every visitor got the default colors, and a Good Friday visitor would have got a full burst. It now reads the theme when the burst fires. I found this through the new "Good Friday fires no confetti" check.
2. **The `/events` top bar was dark text on dark heroes**, including the existing Halloween theme. It now turns light when the generic hero is dark. The

body:
Refs #1197

Stacked on #1253 (the L3 Runs landing page) — this PR shows only the
admin-view sections and views work on top of it; diff will shrink once
#1253 merges.

## What this adds (design.md §6 L4 row)
- Admin view: a "Waiting on the owner" section (owner sign-in holds and
  lost runs — no admin can act on them) alongside "Needs a decision",
  per the owner's H-3 answer.
- Everyone/Mine (H-4): the Admin view defaults to Everyone, with a Mine
  option that narrows via the server's existing `owner=me` filter.
  Picking a saved view never resets it — that is who is asking, not
  something a view remembers — and the Saved view select now correctly
  shows the picked view's own name in that case too, rather than
  falling back to "View · Custom".
- Saved views (H-8): localStorage, up to 10, "Save view" names the
  current URL. Four built-in views (Default, Failed this week, Killed,
  By workspace) ship alongside whatever the browser has saved. The
  Saved view select always shows a label ("View · <name>", falling back
  to "View · Custom" when the URL matches none of them).
- Group by Workspace or Title (H-6): a display-only option, saved in
  the URL, that replaces the time sections with one section per
  workspace/title — Needs a decision / Waiting on the owner keep their
  own fixed sections regardless. Section ids come from React's own id
  generator, so two group titles that would slugify the same never
  collide.

## Changed
- `ui/src/app/components/screens/runs.tsx` — wires the new section,
  the owner query param, saved views state, the group-by branch, and
  `applySavedViewOwner` so a saved-view pick keeps the current
  Everyone/Mine.
- `ui/src/app/components/screens/runs/runs-model.ts` — a `waitingOwner`
  bucket in `sectionRuns` (attention `by=owner`), `isTopQuiet` updated,
  `nonAttentionRuns` for the group-by path.
- `ui/src/app/components/screens/runs/runs-filters.ts` — `scope` and
  `group` added to the URL-driven filter state, plus
  `applySavedViewOwner` and `matchesSavedView` (the latter ignores
  `owner` when deciding which Saved view option is picked, in the
  Admin view only — `applySavedViewOwner` reapplies the current
  Everyone/Mine onto a picked view's own search, so an exact-string
  match against the stored view would otherwise miss and show
  "View · Custom" right after a real pick).
- `ui/src/app/components/screens/runs/runs-groups.ts` (new) — pure
  Workspace/Title regrouping.
- `ui/src/app/components/screens/runs/runs-saved-views.ts` (new) —
  built-in views + localStorage persistence, tolerant of a corrupted
  entry.
- `ui/src/app/components/screens/runs/runs-filter-bar.tsx` — Whose
  runs (Admin view only), Group by, Saved view + Save view controls,
  the save form prefilled with "My view" and its own "Save"/"Cancel".
- `ui/src/app/components/wardyn/copy/runs-landing.ts` — the new canon
  strings (design.md §2.1), plus the saved-view option/custom-sentinel
  and save-form strings.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Unreleased entry for the Admin view's sections,
  Everyone/Mine, saved views and Group by.
- Tests: `runs-model.test.ts`/`runs-filters.test.ts` extended (the
  latter now also covers `matchesSavedView`), `runs-groups.test.ts` and
  `runs-saved-views.test.ts` new (corrupted localStorage entry
  included), `runs.test.tsx` gained two cases (a stray `?owner=me` in
  the User view, and group-by section id collisions). `ui/e2e/
  runs-admin.spec.ts` now covers the design row (owner sign-in with no
  button, Mine narrows, a saved view survives a reload, Group by Title)
  plus the review-round fixes (the Saved view select never blanks,
  reads its own name right after a Mine pick rather than falling back
  to Custom, and picking a view keeps Mine).

Also merged in L3's two review-fix rounds (focus loss, lease-ended
glyph/count, the label-stripping pass) as they landed on
`feat/1197-l3-runs-page`; each merge is its own commit
(`--no-ff --signoff`). The real conflicts (in `runs.tsx` and
`runs-model.test.ts`) were resolved by keeping both sides' behaviour —
this PR's own attention-bucket and filter logic alongside L3's
lease-ended and de-labelling changes — rather than either side
overwriting the other.

## Gates (all green at this head)
- `pnpm typecheck` — exit 0
- Touched-scope vitest (`runs/` + `runs.test.tsx`) — 7 files / 95
  tests, exit 0; every new/changed rule proven red (reverted the
  matching logic, confirmed the pinning test failed) then green again
- `e2e.sh runs-admin runs-landing runs admin-run-monitor` — 4 spec
  files, 49 tests, 0 failed, 0 flaky, exit 0 (also proven red: reverted
  `matchesSavedView` and re-ran `e2e.sh runs-admin` alone, reproducing
  the review's own "View · Custom after a real pick" defect exactly)
- `make dco` — exit 0
- identity check: clean

## UNVERIFIED
- No live axe-core scan (same substitution L3 used: direct WCAG
